summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones, through his company Comstock Resources Inc., is aggressively pursuing shale gas assets in Louisiana's Haynesville play, considering it the best for low-cost hydrocarbons. This strategy involves potential acquisitions exceeding $1 billion, including rumored talks with Chesapeake Energy Corp. and the recent acquisition of Covey Park Energy LLC, as Jones doubles down on natural gas despite a glut in the market and a significant drop in Comstock's share price.

title: How To Invest In An Oil Contango
summary: This article explains contango and backwardation in oil futures markets and how they impact traders. It provides strategies for investors to navigate a contango market, such as constantly monitoring the futures curve, investing directly in oil companies or energy ETFs, and employing a hybrid model using different ETFs.

title: Drilling Down: Top 10 drilling rig companies in Texas and their customers
summary: This article identifies the top 10 drilling rig companies and their top customers in Texas, based on exclusive data from Enverus as of November 26, 2019. It highlights Helmerich & Payne as the leading operator with 117 horizontal rigs and notes that Exxon Mobil leads in rig count among customers. The article also discusses the impact of low oil prices on the industry and the overall U.S. rig count.

title: New Vaca Muerta concessions awarded to YPF, Vista
summary: Neuquén province has granted new concessions in the Vaca Muerta shale formation to Vista Oil and Gas and YPF. Vista will invest US$32mn in its Águila Mora block, while YPF will invest US$60mn in its Loma Amarilla Sur block, both focusing on horizontal well development. These awards mark a continued push by companies to expand shale development into the northern parts of the Neuquina basin.

title: Oklahoma tornadoes: Oklahoma energy companies contribute millions to relief efforts
summary: Several prominent Oklahoma energy companies, including Chesapeake Energy Corp., Devon Energy Corp., and Continental Resources Inc., have collectively pledged over $7 million towards relief efforts following this week's deadly tornadoes. Companies like Continental and ConocoPhillips are also facilitating additional donations and matching employee contributions. These contributions aim to support organizations like the American Red Cross and the OK Strong Disaster Relief Fund to aid affected families and communities.

title: Exxon Mobil found not guilty in climate change accounting case
summary: A New York judge found Exxon Mobil not guilty in a lawsuit accusing the company of deceiving investors about the cost of climate-change regulations. The judge stated that the New York Attorney General's office failed to prove that Exxon Mobil made material misstatements to investors, emphasizing that it was a securities fraud case, not a climate change case. Despite the ruling, the Attorney General maintained that Exxon Mobil misled investors and vowed to continue fighting to hold companies responsible for actions impacting financial health.

title: Exxon Mobil wins lawsuit over climate change risks
summary: Exxon Mobil won a lawsuit filed by the New York Attorney General's office, which alleged the company duped investors about the financial impact of climate change regulations. A state judge ruled there was no proof of material misstatements that misled reasonable investors, emphasizing the case was about securities fraud, not climate change itself. The lawsuit had sought significant restitution to shareholders and was seen as a test case for how investors perceive energy companies' futures in a warming world.

title: Exxon to Export First Oil from Guyana in Early 2020
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and Hess Corp are set to export the first crude oil from Guyana in early 2020, marking a significant milestone for the Latin American nation. A consortium including these companies and CNOOC Ltd has discovered over 6 billion barrels of recoverable oil and gas, with production expected to reach 750,000 bpd. The Liza project, Guyana's first crude grade, will be processed by Exxon at its refineries, while Hess eyes spot sales and CNOOC plans shipments to China.

title: Natural Gas Boom Fizzles as a U.S. Glut Sinks Profits (Published 2019)
summary: A decade after being heralded as the fuel of the future, the U.S. natural gas industry is experiencing a bust due to a significant glut in supply, leading to sinking profits and company write-downs. Chevron's $10 billion to $11 billion asset write-down, mainly in shale gas holdings, highlights the industry's over-optimism and the current oversupply situation. This market downturn is exacerbated by the falling costs of renewable energy and growing international gas production, suggesting a potentially prolonged slump.

title: Exxon Mobil scores win in New York climate change lawsuit
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp won a significant victory in a New York climate change lawsuit, with a judge ruling that the company did not defraud investors by hiding the true cost of climate change regulation. The judge found that the New York State Attorney General's case lacked sufficient evidence to prove investors were misled. This ruling represents the first major decision in several climate change lawsuits against oil companies.

title: Transocean Rig to Mobilize in Caribbean
summary: Transocean has secured a one-year contract for its Development Driller III semisubmersible rig to operate offshore Trinidad and Tobago. The contract is expected to commence in the second quarter of 2020 and contribute approximately $91 million to Transocean's backlog. The rig, capable of ultra-deepwater drilling, is currently contracted to ExxonMobil Corp.

title: Satellite observations reveal extreme methane leakage from a natural gas well blowout
summary: Satellite observations using the Tropospheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) revealed a major methane leak from a natural gas well blowout in Ohio in 2018. The leak, which lasted 20 days, emitted an estimated 120 ± 32 metric tons of methane per hour, a rate twice that of the Aliso Canyon event in 2015. This single event's total methane emission was comparable to a significant fraction of annual anthropogenic emissions from several European countries, highlighting the importance of satellite monitoring for unexpected large-scale greenhouse gas releases.

title: News Content Hub - Industry leader: Quintin Kneen, President and CEO, Tidewater Inc
summary: Quintin Kneen, President and CEO of Tidewater Inc., is aggressively reshaping the company's fleet, management, and IT infrastructure to prepare for a market recovery and further industry consolidation. He has implemented significant organizational changes, including management shakeups and board reductions, and is focusing on cost-efficiency, technology leverage, and cultural transformation to improve decision-making and generate cash flow. Tidewater is also actively managing its fleet, including scrapping older vessels, acquiring new ones, and divesting non-returning assets, while considering strategic mergers to strengthen its market position.

title: Natural Gas Extraction Opportunities in the Mississippian Barnett Shale
summary: The Barnett Shale in North-central Texas is becoming a major source of natural gas, offering low-cost extraction opportunities due to advancements in technology. Despite senior companies moving to other regions, smaller E&P firms are finding success by re-working existing wells and utilizing established infrastructure. The US is set to become a net energy exporter by 2020, with rising global demand for natural gas, particularly from countries like China.

title: Year in Review: 2019 Was A Pivotal Year for American Oil and Natural Gas
summary: 2019 proved to be a pivotal year for the American oil and natural gas industry, marked by record production and export achievements that reshaped global energy markets. The U.S. became a net exporter of petroleum products and solidified its position as the world's leading oil and natural gas producer. These advancements have not only driven significant economic growth and job creation but also contributed to substantial reductions in emissions and considerable savings for American families.

title: Oil Boom Begins in Guyana as Exxon Produces First Liza Crude
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. and its partners have produced the first commercial crude from Guyana's offshore Liza field, signaling a significant economic boost for the small South American nation. Output from the first phase is expected to reach 120,000 gross barrels of oil per day in the coming months, with the initial cargo set to be sold soon. This development positions Guyana to potentially produce 750,000 barrels per day by 2025.

title: TGS finaliza construcción de gasoducto en Vaca Muerta
summary: Transportadora Gas del Sur (TGS) has completed the construction of a 150 km gas pipeline and an conditioning plant in Vaca Muerta, Neuquén, Argentina. This infrastructure will allow for the capture and transport of up to 60 MMm3/d of unconventional gas from the Neuquén basin to the national transportation network. The project, completed in record time, is deemed crucial for accelerating the development of gas production in Vaca Muerta, with companies like Pluspetrol, YPF, Pampa Energía, Total, Shell, GyP, and Tecpetrol already injecting gas into the new system.

title: ABB committed to serving Bartlesville
summary: ABB has reaffirmed its long-term commitment to Bartlesville by acquiring its facility near Bison Road for $17 million and an additional 18 acres for future expansion. This move reinforces their satisfaction with the Bartlesville operation's performance. The Bartlesville Development Authority supported this growth by offering no-cost land for expansion that generates quality employment and sales tax revenue.

title: Exxon Wins U.S. Suit Over $2 Million Ukraine-Sanctions Fine
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. won a lawsuit challenging a $2 million fine imposed by the U.S. Treasury Secretary for alleged violations of Ukraine-related sanctions. A U.S. District Judge ruled that Exxon was not given sufficient notice that its 2014 contracts with a Russian ally would violate the sanctions. The sanctions were put in place after Russia annexed Crimea.

title: Energy stocks surge, as crude oil prices spike on Middle East tensions
summary: Energy stocks experienced a broad surge in premarket trading on Friday as crude oil prices spiked due to Middle East tensions following a U.S. airstrike. The SPDR Energy Select Sector ETF saw a 1.4% gain, with major components like Exxon Mobil Corp., Occidental Petroleum Corp., and Chevron Corp. all rising. This rally in energy stocks contrasted with a broader market downturn, as S&P 500 futures sank and crude oil futures shot up significantly.

title: Fiserv and ExxonMobil will Enable Consumers to Fill Up by Asking Alexa to Pay at the Pump
summary: Fiserv and ExxonMobil announced a partnership to allow consumers to pay for fuel at over 11,500 Exxon and Mobil stations using Amazon Alexa. This new voice-activated payment method, powered by Fiserv's digital commerce technology and Amazon Pay, will be available later in 2020 and demonstrated at CES 2020. It aims to provide a frictionless and secure transaction experience for consumers in Alexa-enabled vehicles or using other Alexa mobility devices.

title: Mobil SA se queda con la mayoría de Sierra Chata
summary: Mobil Argentina SA, a subsidiary of ExxonMobil, has acquired Total Austral SA's stake in the Sierra Chata area, becoming the majority shareholder with 54.45%. This move makes Mobil a key partner with Pampa Energía SA in the Vaca Muerta shale and tight gas project. The acquisition involved an initial payment of $33.64 million and strengthens Mobil's presence in Argentina's unconventional energy sector.

title: Imperial Oil, Canada's Exxon Subsidiary, Ignored Its Own Climate Change Research for Decades, Archive Shows
summary: Imperial Oil, Exxon’s Canadian subsidiary, publicly denied climate change for decades while its own research recognized the reality and dangers of global warming. Archival documents reveal that Imperial Oil started commissioning environmental studies in the 1960s and by the 1990s, internal researchers had analyzed ways to reduce carbon footprints, yet the company leadership chose to obfuscate the science and focused on new business opportunities from a warming Arctic. This strategy of denial and delay was employed despite understanding the severe environmental impact of their operations and the necessity of transitioning to sustainable energy.

title: Cenovus sets bold sustainability targets
summary: Cenovus Energy Inc. announced ambitious environmental, social, and governance (ESG) targets for 2030, focusing on climate & greenhouse gas emissions, Indigenous engagement, land & wildlife, and water stewardship. The company aims to reduce emissions intensity by 30% and hold absolute emissions flat by 2030, with a long-term ambition for net-zero emissions by 2050. These targets are integrated into Cenovus's strategy to enhance business resilience and foster long-term sustainability.

title: The 10 Biggest Carbon-dioxide Emitting Firms In The World
summary: This article identifies the ten largest corporate emitters of carbon dioxide globally, responsible for a significant portion of greenhouse gas emissions since 1965. It details each company's emissions, origin, and some of their initiatives or controversies related to climate change. The article also highlights the impact of investor pressure in driving companies towards decarbonization efforts.

title: Understanding the Emissions Challenge
summary: Integrated oil companies are facing increasing pressure to reduce emissions from investors and regulators. This article assesses their efforts, highlighting that while many have adopted targets, Scope 3 emissions (90% of total) remain largely beyond their control. Investments in renewable power generation and increasing natural gas production are identified as the most impactful strategies for reducing full-cycle emissions.

title: District Court Overturns OFAC Fine Against Exxon
summary: A U.S. District Court overturned a $2 million OFAC fine against ExxonMobil for contracts signed by Igor Sechin of Rosneft, arguing OFAC failed to provide fair notice of its sanction interpretations. The decision highlights the importance of clear guidance from OFAC and urges companies to seek clarification when regulations are unclear. The ruling suggests OFAC may need to be more explicit about when interpretive guidance for one sanctions program applies to others.

title: Activists cheer BlackRock's landmark climate move but call for vigilance
summary: BlackRock, the world's biggest asset manager, announced a significant shift in its investment strategy, divesting $500m from coal-related businesses due to climate risks. Environmentalists hailed this as a major breakthrough but urged continued vigilance and further action, emphasizing that these initial steps are just the beginning of necessary changes in the financial sector to combat climate change. Activists and financial experts alike called for BlackRock to leverage its substantial shareholder power to push for immediate, concrete climate actions from companies it invests in.

title: There Is a Fund for Everything. But Why?
summary: The article discusses the proliferation of niche thematic Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) that aim to profit from specific trends like cannabis, pet care, or even adult obesity. While fund managers use these to stand out in a bull market, experts question their necessity and highlight their complexity, higher costs, and increased risk compared to broad-index funds. The piece advises caution, suggesting these funds are best suited for a small portion of a risk-taker's portfolio rather than as core holdings.

title: Oklahoma Oil Rig Explosion Wrongful Death Trial Begins in Oklahoma
summary: A wrongful death trial has begun in Oklahoma against National Oilwell Varco (NOV) following a January 2018 oil rig explosion that killed five men. Families of the victims claim NOV was primarily responsible due to a failure in providing proper operational oversight, a charge NOV disputes, attributing fault to another company, Red Mountain Operating, LLC. The families have already reached settlements with several other companies involved in the incident.

title: Pizza Inn Express Opens Inside Exxon Station in Arkansas
summary: Pizza Inn Express has opened a new location inside a renovated Exxon station in Danville, Ark., offering specialty pizzas, sandwiches, wings, and appetizers. Owned and operated by David Blackmon, this marks his fourth Pizza Inn Express location, with Blackmon Oil Co. also contributing STEM grants to local high schools. Rave Restaurant Group, the parent company of Pizza Inn Express, and ExxonMobil, are expanding their presence in the U.S. with this new opening.

title: Exxon, Chevron earnings bring worries about oil prices to the forefront
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. are facing increased scrutiny from Wall Street as they prepare to report fourth-quarter earnings, amidst negative sentiment for the energy sector and declining oil prices. Both integrated energy giants are scheduled to report earnings and conduct conference calls with analysts on Friday.

title: Exxon Mobil closes at lowest since October 2013
summary: Exxon Mobil shares reached their lowest closing price since October 2013, driven by falling oil prices stemming from the widening coronavirus outbreak. The decline was also impacted by a regulatory filing from Exxon indicating weaker fourth-quarter results due to issues in its chemicals and refining segments, leading analysts to lower their outlooks for the stock.

title: Pemex Claims Ownership of Lion's Share of Zama Field
summary: Mexico's state oil company Pemex is claiming the majority ownership of resources in the Zama offshore field, conflicting with Talos Energy Inc.'s interpretation. This dispute adds to tensions between the Mexican government and the private sector, as both companies vie for operator status of the significant oil field. The resolution of this issue, which could impact Mexico's energy production and revenue, is expected to be determined through technical means and discussions with the Energy Ministry.

title: Exxon Mobil and Chevron Help Fuel Investor Revolt
summary: Weak earnings reports from Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp., following Royal Dutch Shell Plc's earlier debacle, are contributing to investor dissatisfaction in the oil majors. The energy sector's weighting in the S&P 500 Index has fallen to a four-decade low, highlighting increasing vulnerability for these companies and a lack of investor confidence. The results suggest a prolonged challenge for these large oil companies to regain shareholder trust.

title: Exxon Mobil’s stock drops to decade low after Goldman says it’s time to sell
summary: Exxon Mobil's stock fell to its lowest point in a decade after Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta recommended selling due to concerns about the oil giant missing its investment return targets. The stock dropped 2.2%, making it the biggest loser in the Dow Jones Industrial Average on Monday. This decline marked the 13th fall in 14 days for Exxon Mobil's shares.

title: Martinez Named to Top Latinos Leaders in Corporate America
summary: Alumna Maria Martinez ’01, MBA ’06, was recognized by Latino Leaders Magazine as one of the top Latino Leaders in Corporate America, serving as the Vice President of Human Resources & Administration at Murphy Oil Corporation. She is noted for her leadership in global HR programs and her community involvement with organizations like the Greater Houston Women’s Chamber of Commerce. Martinez credits her two degrees from the University of St. Thomas for providing a strong foundation for her professional success.

title: All eyes on Exxon and Chevron after BP pledges to go carbon neutral
summary: BP's commitment to go carbon neutral by 2050 intensifies pressure on U.S. oil giants Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. to similarly expand their climate efforts beyond operational emissions. While European peers are investing in low-carbon energy, Exxon and Chevron remain focused on their core oil and gas businesses, viewing climate change as a technology problem yet to be solved, and prioritizing higher returns. This stance puts them at odds with shareholder groups and an increasingly climate-conscious investment landscape.

title: A Canadian Energy Company Bought an Oregon Sheriff’s Unit
summary: A Canadian energy company, Pembina Pipeline Corp., funded a specialized unit within the Coos County Sheriff’s Office in Oregon for nearly four years to handle security concerns related to its proposed Jordan Cove Energy Project. This unit, established to monitor opposition and acquire riot control equipment, highlights an unusual partnership between a public law enforcement agency and a private corporation. Critics argue this arrangement biases law enforcement and raises constitutional questions regarding free speech and public safety.

title: ExxonMobil, Canada enter landmark settlement in NAFTA arbitration
summary: ExxonMobil and Canada have reached a multi-million-dollar settlement in a long-running NAFTA arbitration case. The dispute, which lasted 16 years, concerned the amount of money the energy giant was required to spend on research.

title: Westlake Chemical agrees to report plastic pellet spills under activist shareholder pressure
summary: Westlake Chemical Corp. has agreed to publicly report its plastic pellet spills due to pressure from the activist shareholder group As You Sow. This decision follows similar commitments from other major plastics producers like Exxon Mobil, Chevron Phillips Chemical, and Dow Chemical, and comes after Formosa Plastics settled a major lawsuit over a plastic pellet spill for $50 million. Westlake will include this data in its 2020 sustainability report, which will be published in 2021.

title: See Where 'X' Marks The Spot For XLE
summary: The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) experienced a poor start to 2020, being the worst-performing sector in January, largely due to sliding oil prices and concerns over the coronavirus outbreak. Despite being in bear market territory and nursing an 11% loss, some market observers believe a rebound could be possible given that energy is one of the least expensive sectors. The article discusses technical support and resistance levels for XLE, including its late-2018-through-2019 lows at $54 and 2010 lows at $49.

title: USA Compression Partners Cuts 2020 Capex
summary: USA Compression Partners LP (USAC) has reduced its 2020 capital expenditures and equipment orders due to the industry downturn, forecasting spending of US$110-120 million and acquiring 56,000 hp of compressors, down from US$150 million and 132,000 hp in 2019. Despite "strong headwinds" in the energy industry, CEO Eric Long anticipates stable cash flows from long-term, high-horsepower contracts and sees continued opportunities in chemical, LNG export, and power generation sectors.

title: JPMorgan Will Stop Lending to Coal Companies
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced it will cease doing business with coal companies and restrict financing for Arctic drilling projects. The bank plans to phase out existing coal company loans by 2024 and will only fund new coal-powered plants that include carbon capture technology. This move comes as JPMorgan also committed $200 billion in financing for clean and renewable energy companies by 2025.

title: NRG eyes private option despite earnings turnaround
summary: NRG Energy, despite a significant earnings turnaround in 2019 ($4.4 billion from $268 million in 2018), is struggling with a lagging stock price, leading CEO Mauricio Gutierrez to consider taking the company private. This move echoes competitor Calpine's 2018 privatization and could allow NRG to escape public market scrutiny and potentially re-engage in ventures like renewables. The company's financials proved strong last year, buoyed by high wholesale electricity prices during an August heat wave, but its share price remains a concern for executives.

title: Guyana holds crucial election ahead of expected oil boom
summary: Guyana is holding a crucial election that will determine which party oversees an anticipated oil boom, with over eight billion barrels of oil and gas discovered offshore. The election comes at a pivotal moment as economic forecasts predict an 86% GDP growth for 2020, but concerns remain about potential resource curse, corruption and the terms of the deal with ExxonMobil. Indigenous leaders are also campaigning to ensure that the country's wealth benefits all its citizens and to address long-standing issues of poverty and land rights.

title: Santos Contracts Valaris Rig for Van Gogh Phase 2
summary: Santos Ltd. announced a final investment decision for the Van Gogh Infill Development Phase Two Project offshore Western Australia, contracting the Valaris MS1 mobile offshore drilling unit. The project involves drilling three new horizontal dual-lateral production wells and subsea tieback into existing infrastructure, with first oil expected late next year. This follows the successful Phase One, which delivered higher reserves for lower costs.

title: Exxon calls for stricter methane regulations
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has called for strengthening methane emissions regulations, publishing its internal guidelines as a model for industry and governments. The company's CEO, Darren Woods, hopes this framework will assist other operators in reducing the sector’s methane emissions, as investor and consumer pressure mounts despite the Trump administration's rollback of Obama-era standards. Exxon's move follows similar actions by European oil and gas firms and highlights a growing industry sentiment that voluntary reductions are insufficient.

title: Colorado hits Suncor with record air pollution violation penalties over its Commerce City refineries
summary: Colorado has issued record air pollution violation penalties against Suncor Energy for its Commerce City refineries. The penalties include significant fines and require millions of dollars to be invested in improving community air quality and reducing emissions. This action follows previous apologies from Suncor executives and ongoing legal challenges from Colorado communities regarding the refinery's impact.

title: U.S. shale producers deepen spending, output cuts as oil prices slump
summary: U.S. shale producers are rapidly deepening spending and output cuts in response to a sharp decline in oil prices, triggered by OPEC's decision to flood a market already suffering from reduced demand due to the coronavirus. Major shale independents like Diamondback Energy Inc. and Parsley Energy Inc. have announced significant reductions in drilling and well completions to maintain cash flow, leading to a sharp drop in their share prices and impacting oilfield service firms. Analysts predict that U.S. oil production growth will be near zero compared to 2019, with further reductions in spending expected as investors are less willing to finance the sector than in previous downturns.

title: In Conflict of Interest, Interior Secretary Met With Halliburton Lobbyists
summary: The article exposes potential conflicts of interest involving former Interior Secretary David Bernhardt and Halliburton Energy Services. Despite a recusal agreement due to his past legal work for Halliburton, Bernhardt met with lobbying groups representing the company. These meetings raise concerns about the spirit, if not the letter, of ethical guidelines regarding government officials and their previous private sector clients.

title: Crude Oil Continues To Crater As Short Crude ETFs Gain
summary: Crude oil prices are crashing due to a price war between Saudi Arabia and Russia, exacerbated by diminished demand from the coronavirus pandemic. Analysts predict oil could fall to $20 or even $10 a barrel, leading to significant gains for inverse crude oil ETFs such as SCO, DTO, and DNO. Goldman Sachs and Rystad Energy have drastically cut their oil demand forecasts for 2020.

title: Coronavirus causes ConocoPhillips to temporarily cancel flights for workers to North Slope fields
summary: ConocoPhillips has canceled flights for hundreds of workers to Alaska's North Slope for two weeks to prevent the spread of COVID-19, asking critical personnel to extend their rotations. Other oil companies like BP are continuing screenings for workers, while the virus has led to plunging oil prices and a slowdown in the North Slope oil patch. All companies are implementing measures like social distancing and health screenings, with no confirmed cases on the North Slope at the time of the report.

title: Exxon notifies contractors, vendors of spending cuts over coronavirus
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is notifying its contractors and vendors of impending near-term cuts in capital and operating expenses due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to announce these reductions once finalized, indicating a need to significantly lower costs in the current unprecedented environment. Exxon has already begun reducing production at its Baton Rouge refinery and cut 1,800 contract workers, with expectations to also delay a $30-billion liquefied natural gas plant in Mozambique.

title: Oil crash leaves Exxon, Chevron dividends safe -- for now
summary: In the wake of a significant oil market crash driven by a Saudi Arabia-Russia price war and the COVID-19 pandemic, the dividends of ExxonMobil and Chevron are under threat but still considered safe "for now." Both companies have seen their stock prices plummet, leading Chevron to cut capital spending and halt share buybacks to conserve cash. Analysts believe the companies will prioritize dividend payments as long as possible due to their strong balance sheets and the importance of dividends to their investor base.

title: Oil Storage So Full That Traders May Stow It on Pipe Networks
summary: The US oil glut is growing so rapidly that storage facilities are nearing capacity, leading pipeline operators to worry that traders might use pipelines for temporary storage to await better prices. Plains All American Pipeline LP is requiring proof of buyers for crude shipments to prevent this, while Colonial Pipeline Co. has warned clients that unreserved fuel will be sold off. This situation highlights rising concerns about overwhelming storage capacity and the impact of the Covid-19 outbreak on demand.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | A Top Occidental Petroleum Executive Is Out as Company Grapples With Oil Rout
summary: A top executive at Occidental Petroleum Corp., Oscar Brown, has been "forced out" of the company amid challenges from an ill-timed acquisition, declining crude prices, and substantial debt. Brown, who was a key lieutenant to CEO Vicki Hollub and instrumental in the Anadarko Petroleum acquisition, served as senior vice president over strategy, business development, and supply chain. The $38 billion Anadarko deal included a costly $10 billion investment from Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway.

title: Rockets target US oil company site in southern Iraq
summary: Three rockets landed near the site of US oilfield service company Halliburton in Basra, southern Iraq, marking the first such attack since last summer against US oil companies in the region. No damage or casualties were reported, and a rocket launcher was later found with unused missiles. Oil production and export operations were unaffected, and the area was largely empty due to foreign personnel evacuation amidst the coronavirus crisis.

title: Rockets target US oil company in Iraq’s Basra province
summary: At least three rockets targeted the site of the American oil field service company Halliburton in Iraq's Basra province, marking the first such attack on US energy interests in recent months. While no casualties were reported and oil production was unaffected, the incident fuels tensions, with pro-Iran militias in Iraq having previously pledged to target US interests. Security forces found a rocket launcher and defused unused rockets nearby.

title: Just in: Exxon Mobil delays FID for the Rovuma LNG project in Mozambique
summary: Exxon Mobil has delayed the final investment decision (FID) for the Rovuma LNG project in Mozambique, previously scheduled for later in the year, as part of broader spending cuts. The oil and gas supermajor reduced its 2020 capital budget by 30%, or $10 billion, to $23 billion, and aims to cut operating expenses by 15% in response to low energy prices and collapsing demand caused by the coronavirus pandemic. These cuts primarily affect Permian Basin operations and will also delay some Guyanese field development activities.

title: Exxon Mobil cuts spending plans, reduces expansion budget as coronavirus hits oil demand
summary: Exxon Mobil has significantly reduced its 2020 capital spending by 30% to $23 billion, in response to the coronavirus pandemic's impact on oil demand and prices. This cut is deeper than most rivals, with major impacts on U.S. shale production and deferred investment decisions on projects in Mozambique and Guyana. Despite the spending cuts, the company has maintained its shareholder dividend.

title: Guangdong pushes forward on Exxon Mobil project in Huizhou
summary: Guangdong provincial government and Exxon Mobil Corporation held a video conference to discuss the construction of the Huizhou ethylene project. Both parties expressed their commitment to pushing the project forward despite the global economic impact of the pandemic. Exxon Mobil stated it would not change its investment plans in China and its development strategy in Guangdong.

title: Exxon raises $9.5 billion to load up on cash while debt market still open to new deals
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp raised $9.5 billion in new debt to bolster its finances, taking advantage of still-open debt markets amid investor confidence gradually returning. The oil producer secured the debt at a lower borrowing cost compared to a month ago, selling five different bonds with durations ranging from five to 31 years. This move is part of a broader trend of highly-rated U.S. companies raising cash due to economic uncertainty from the coronavirus pandemic.

title: ‘Gigantic impact’: Chesapeake Energy’s complex legacy
summary: Chesapeake Energy, once a fracking pioneer and a significant contributor to Oklahoma City's development, is grappling with overwhelming debt and a collapsed petroleum market. The company recently executed a one-for-200 reverse stock split to avoid delisting from the NYSE, signaling its struggle for survival amidst a complex legacy that includes both economic impact and environmental concerns. The article delves into the company's boom-and-bust history, the controversial leadership of co-founder Aubrey McClendon, and the broader implications of its trajectory for the energy industry and local communities.

title: ConocoPhillips Cuts Oil Output, Spending Again
summary: ConocoPhillips announced significant cuts to its planned spending and oil production, along with the suspension of its share repurchase program, in response to the collapse in oil prices due to coronavirus impact. The company plans to reduce spending by 35%, operational capital expenditures by $1.6 billion, and cut oil production by approximately 225,000 barrels per day across its Canadian and U.S. operations. These measures follow similar actions by other major oil and gas producers grappling with drastically reduced demand and low crude prices.

title: Oil prices dip below zero as producers forced to pay to dispose of excess
summary: US crude oil prices plummeted to negative values for the first time in history, reaching -$38 a barrel, as an oversupply due to the coronavirus crisis overwhelmed storage facilities. Producers were forced to pay buyers to take crude, highlighting the severe impact of reduced demand. While prices rebounded slightly on Tuesday, the long-term outlook remains uncertain, with calls for a shift towards sustainable energy sources.

title: Oil plunges below zero for first time; Marathon refinery remains open
summary: Oil futures plummeted below zero for the first time in history, reaching negative $37.63 per barrel for May delivery, due to a severe collapse in demand from the coronavirus pandemic and a lack of storage capacity. While an international standard for oil also fell, the Detroit Marathon Petroleum Corp. refinery continued operations, monitoring the market as other global markets reacted to the unprecedented plunge. Simultaneously, the broader stock market saw declines, with the S&P 500 down 1.8%, though some tech companies gained.

title: Exxon Mobil starts building $10 billion China petrochemical complex: Xinhua
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has commenced construction of its $10 billion petrochemical complex in Huizhou, China. This facility includes a 1.6 million tonnes per year ethylene plant and is notable as one of the few mega petrochemical projects in China wholly owned by a foreign investor. The project was announced by state news agency Xinhua.

title: Eaton adds Lori J. Ryerkerk to its board
summary: Eaton (NYSE: ETN) has appointed Lori J. Ryerkerk, chairman, president, and CEO of Celanese Corp. (NYSE: CE), to its board of directors, effective April 22, 2020. Ryerkerk brings extensive experience from the energy industry, including previous roles at Shell Downstream Inc., Hess Corp., and ExxonMobil. She succeeds Todd M. Bluedorn, who served on Eaton's board for 10 years.

title: ExxonMobil starts building $10 billion China petrochemical complex
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has begun construction on its $10 billion petrochemical complex in Huizhou, China. This facility, which includes a 1.6 million tonnes per year ethylene plant, marks one of the few mega petrochemical projects in China wholly owned by a foreign investor.

title: Trump orders Chevron to halt oil production in Venezuela
summary: The Trump administration ordered Chevron to stop oil production in Venezuela by December 1, as part of efforts to pressure the Maduro regime. This move, while having limited financial impact on Chevron, deals a significant blow to Venezuela's oil industry. Chevron, which has a long history in Venezuela, will be allowed to maintain a limited presence for essential operations.

title: What's Driving the Multi Pad Drilling Market Size? Prominent
summary: This article discusses the multi-pad drilling market, highlighting its growth potential, key trends, and competitive landscape. It segments the market by application (onshore, offshore) and pad size, providing regional analysis with a focus on North America, Western Europe, and Asia Pacific as key growth areas. The report profiles major players such as ExxonMobil, Devon Energy, and Chevron, offering an overview of global market trends and opportunities.

title: U.S. oil plunges 25%, Brent falls below $20 a barrel
summary: U.S. crude oil plunged 25% and Brent crude fell below $20 a barrel due to a lack of available storage and weak fuel demand caused by the coronavirus pandemic. Global fuel demand is down 30% and roughly 85% of worldwide onshore storage was full last week. Retail investment vehicles like the United States Oil Fund LP are shifting holdings to later-dated contracts to avoid similar losses experienced a week prior.

title: What Traders Should Know About the Oil Crash
summary: This article explains the oil crash of April 2020, detailing how global events like the pandemic and price wars led to negative oil futures prices. It offers advice to traders on navigating this volatile market, including understanding risks, considering green energy with caution, and exploring sympathy plays. The piece emphasizes the importance of research, a strong trading plan, and caution in unprecedented market conditions.

title: Exxon Posts Historic Loss on Rout With Chevron in Retreat
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. reported its first loss in at least three decades, amounting to $610 million, and plans to cut hundreds of thousands of barrels of daily output. Meanwhile, Chevron Corp. slashed $2 billion from its spending plan and accelerated supply curbs, highlighting the financial impact of the coronavirus pandemic on oil giants. These actions reflect the historic falloff in oil demand and the need for significant cost-cutting measures.

title: Chesapeake Energy preparing bankruptcy filing
summary: Chesapeake Energy Corp is preparing a potential bankruptcy filing due to a severe rout in energy prices and significant debt obligations. The company is in early discussions with creditors about debtor-in-possession financing, potentially totaling $1 billion, to sustain operations during bankruptcy proceedings. Chesapeake faces looming debt maturities and interest expenses exceeding $1 billion this year, and has seen its credit rating cut deep into junk territory by Moody's Investor Service.

title: Exxon reports historic loss, closes 75% of Permian rigs
summary: Major U.S. oil producers like Exxon Mobil, ConocoPhillips, and Chevron reported historic losses in the first quarter due to the coronavirus pandemic's impact on global oil demand. Companies are cutting spending and production, particularly in the Permian Basin, and expect the recovery to be slow, with low prices persisting through the end of the year.

title: Exxon Mobil eyes Irving property sale
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is looking to sell off about 100 acres of surplus land surrounding its Irving headquarters, including a 35-acre parcel for which it is seeking new office zoning. The energy firm's plan involves rezoning part of the Las Colinas land for offices, indicating a strategic move to divest non-core real estate assets in a popular corporate area. This comes as Irving's planning and zoning commission is set to consider the request.

title: Value Tilt – Don’t Give Up on Your Small-Cap Value Strategy
summary: This article argues against giving up on a small-cap value investing strategy despite recent underperformance. The author, Dr. Jim Dahle, explains the rationale behind factor investing in small value stocks, including risk and behavioral biases, and presents data indicating historical long-term outperformance. He discusses why now, given the undervaluation and underperformance of small-cap value, is a good time to stick with or even implement such a tilt, cautioning that it is a long-term decision.

title: Shell to divest natural gas wells in Pennsylvania
summary: Royal Dutch Shell is set to sell its natural gas assets in Tioga County, Pennsylvania, to National Fuel Gas Co. This sale will further expand National Fuel's presence in the state, positioning it as one of the top shale producers. The article notes this transaction while also referencing a broader trend of declining natural gas production and optimism from other Marcellus producers for 2021.

title: Halliburton lays off 1,000 at Houston headquarters
summary: Halliburton has laid off 1,000 employees at its Houston headquarters due to record low crude prices and a "dramatic business downturn." This action follows earlier furloughs and is part of broader global reductions, bringing the company's workforce down from 55,000 to about 50,000 worldwide. The company has also implemented significant cost-cutting measures, including executive pay cuts and a reduction in its capital budget, to navigate the challenging market conditions.

title: Tankers Round the Cape as Glut Snarls Ports
summary: Due to a global oil glut caused by the coronavirus pandemic, supertankers are undertaking unusual, longer voyages around South Africa's Cape of Good Hope to delay cargo delivery as storage fills up and generate profit from contango market conditions. These rare detours, which avoid the Suez Canal, also capitalize on historically low fuel prices and offer a way for suppliers to manage an oversupplied market. The extended routes highlight the significant impact of the current market disruption on the global shipping industry.

title: Rio Grande LNG and BND amend lease, amid global oil and gas market uncertainty
summary: The Port of Brownsville (BND) and NextDecade’s Rio Grande LNG project have amended their lease agreement, linking its start to a financial investment decision (FID) for the first phase, with a deadline in May 2021 and a possible extension. This amendment comes amidst global oil and gas market uncertainty and delays experienced by several other LNG projects in Texas due to the COVID-19 pandemic and oversupply. The project faces local opposition and legal challenges, with environmental groups welcoming the FID delay.

title: Kevin O'Leary: If you're worried about dividend cuts, it's 'time to use actively managed ETFs'
summary: Kevin O'Leary suggests that actively managed ETFs are a valuable tool for investors concerned about dividend cuts and market volatility, particularly in an uncertain market environment. He highlights O'Shares FTSE U.S. Quality Dividend ETF (OUSA) as an example of an actively managed fund that focuses on companies with high-quality balance sheets and lower likelihood of cutting dividends. O'Leary emphasizes that in these times, quality really matters and active management can help cherry-pick sound investments.

title: Chesapeake Energy considers bankruptcy after losing more than $8B in first quarter
summary: Chesapeake Energy Corp. announced it is considering bankruptcy after posting a net loss of $8.3 billion in the first quarter of 2020, largely due to low commodity prices and depressed demand caused by COVID-19. The company also disclosed that executive bonuses were cut, while a new quarterly bonus program was created for rank and file employees. While bankruptcy is an option, the company is also exploring other strategic alternatives to restructure its debt and align its capital structure.

title: Midland-based Propetro, makes dramatic employee layoffs
summary: Propetro Holding Corp. laid off 150 workers and plans to cut up to 28% of its hydraulic fracturing fleets, representing a 9.5% staff reduction, in response to the oil price drop and Covid-19. The company also announced compensation reductions for its board and management and approved a short-term stockholder rights plan to protect its capital structure and ensure fair treatment for shareholders during potential takeovers.

title: Unravelling the climate footprint of U.S. liquefied natural gas
summary: This article examines the significant climate footprint of U.S. liquefied natural gas (LNG), particularly from the Permian Basin, challenging its portrayal as a clean energy source for Europe. It highlights high levels of methane emissions and flaring, which compromise the climate benefits of replacing coal, and discusses the EU's proactive stance on methane emissions. The piece also points out the complexities and inconsistencies in measuring and comparing methane emissions across different gas-producing regions globally.

title: Chevron Buys More Marcellus Shale
summary: Chevron has expanded its Marcellus shale holdings by purchasing drilling rights for an additional 228,000 acres, following its 2011 acquisition of Atlas Energy. This move aims to secure more gas-rich land amidst a booming U.S. natural gas sector, despite environmental concerns and falling domestic gas prices. The acquisition is estimated to be worth $1.6 billion.

title: Chevron Nigerian Rig Fire Finally Burns Out
summary: A natural gas fire on a Chevron Corp. rig off the coast of Nigeria, which killed two people, finally stopped burning after 46 days. Though the fire is out, Chevron acknowledged the possibility of gas flowing from the well and is drilling a relief well to permanently plug the site. The Nigerian government attributes the explosions, which occurred on January 16 and killed a man from India and another from France, to a "gas kick" or buildup of gas pressure.

title: Exxon, Chevron face shareholders as oil faces uncertain future
summary: Exxon Mobil and Chevron are facing shareholder meetings amidst a global oil crash caused by the coronavirus pandemic, raising questions about the future of oil demand and climate change policies. Despite the challenges, analysts believe these U.S. oil giants are well-equipped to weather the storm due to their strong balance sheets and diversified operations, potentially allowing them to redefine themselves and acquire struggling rivals. However, shareholder resolutions regarding independent board chairmen and differing outlooks on future oil demand highlight ongoing debates within the industry.

title: Exclusive: Chevron to cut up to 15% of staff amid restructuring
summary: Chevron Corp plans to cut 10% to 15% of its global workforce, representing about 4,500 to 6,750 jobs, as part of a restructuring effort to align with projected activity levels amid a sharp drop in oil prices and demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This move follows a 30% reduction in its 2020 spending and previous voluntary job cuts. Most of the reductions are expected to occur this year, with additional severance and benefits offered to affected U.S. employees.

title: BlackRock says voted to split CEO, chairman roles at Exxon Mobil
summary: Top fund manager BlackRock Inc. announced it voted in favor of splitting the CEO and chairman roles at Exxon Mobil Corp. and against the reelection of two directors due to concerns over the company's approach to climate risks. Exxon shareholders rejected the proposals, with the independent chairman proposal failing to pass. BlackRock, the second-largest institutional owner of Exxon, cited a lack of independent leadership and insufficient progress on climate-related financial disclosures.

title: BlackRock votes to split CEO, chairman roles at Exxon Mobil
summary: Top fund manager BlackRock Inc. announced it voted in favor of splitting the CEO and chairman roles at Exxon Mobil Corp. and opposed the re-election of two directors due to concerns over Exxon's approach to climate risks. BlackRock, a significant shareholder, highlighted the need for independent leadership and greater urgency in addressing climate-related financial disclosures. This move came despite Exxon shareholders rejecting all four shareholder resolutions.

title: Chevron plans sweeping job cuts with 6,000 employees at risk
summary: Chevron Corp. announced plans to cut its global workforce by 10 to 15 percent, affecting about 6,000 non-gas station employees, in response to the Covid-19 pandemic and record-low oil prices. The job cuts are part of an effort to streamline operations, achieve $1 billion in operating expense savings, and may signal similar actions among other major oil companies. This move follows broader job losses within the energy sector, particularly in oilfield services and North American independent producers.

title: ExxonMobil’s delayed FID on Mozambique project should come next year -official
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp's final investment decision (FID) on its $30 billion gas project in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province, which was postponed due to the coronavirus and oil price slump, is now expected in 2021. The project, known as Rovuma LNG, is seen as crucial for Mozambique's economic transformation, despite facing challenges from militant Islamists in the region. Other major oil companies like Total and Eni are also involved in projects in the area.

title: Oil Traders Fret Over Rising Inventories, Questionable Production Cuts
summary: Oil prices experienced volatility due to rising inventories and debates over production cuts among top producers like OPEC+. The extension of current cuts, particularly the 9.7 million barrels per day agreement, is crucial for market stability, as failure to do so could lead to a selling spree, while extending cuts could have longer-term bearish effects on shale production forecasts. Investors can gain exposure to oil through ETFs such as IEO, USOU, and GUSH, with OILK offering an actively managed strategy for WTI crude oil futures.

title: Oxy Starts Returning Staff to U.S. Gulf of Mexico after Storm
summary: Occidental Petroleum Corp has begun returning staff to its Gulf of Mexico facilities after Tropical Storm Cristobal moved away. The company plans to fully restaff by Tuesday and resume production once safe. This move follows other energy companies preparing to restart oil and gas production in the region after evacuations and shutdowns.

title: Chesapeake’s fate marks the end of an era in U.S. shale
summary: Chesapeake Energy Corp., once a pioneer in shale drilling, is facing bankruptcy, signaling the end of an era for U.S. shale and potentially the largest corporate casualty in the industry. The company's financial struggles, exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic and years of debt, highlight the broader challenges faced by many North American energy explorers. This situation underscores the unraveling of the shale model established by Chesapeake and its late co-founder Aubrey McClendon, leaving an uncertain future for smaller operators and the industry as a whole.

title: Vaca Muerta Shale Oil and Gas Field
summary: The Vaca Muerta field in Argentina is a significant shale oil and gas development, encompassing conventional and unconventional resources. Various companies, including YPF, Total, Shell, and ExxonMobil, are involved in its exploration and production, with projects aimed at increasing shale gas and oil output. Future plans include further development of blocks and a natural gas liquefaction facility to support continued growth.

title: ‘Google of oil and gas’ files for bankruptcy
summary: Chesapeake Energy Corp., once the second-largest natural gas producer in the country and a pioneer of the fracking boom, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. The company's filing follows a decade of struggling with debt and the legacy of its late founder, Aubrey McClendon, exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic. Despite efforts to reduce debt by $20 billion and lay off thousands of workers, the company was unable to remain solvent.

title: Chesapeake Energy files for bankruptcy, as details emerge of wine cellars and botox
summary: Chesapeake Energy, a key player in the U.S. shale revolution, filed for bankruptcy protection due to heavy debt and a drop in oil and gas prices. The restructuring will wipe out $7 billion in debt, and the company has secured additional financing to continue operations at a reduced capacity. Details emerging from the company's past finances reveal extravagant spending under former CEO Aubrey McClendon, including wine cellars and botox treatments.

title: Exxon Mobil resists write-downs as oil, gas prices plummet
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is notably resisting writing down the value of its U.S. shale assets despite plummeting oil and gas prices, setting it apart from its peers. Other major energy companies like BP PLC, Hess Corp., Occidental Petroleum Corp., Chevron Corp., and Royal Dutch Shell PLC have all taken significant impairments totaling billions of dollars due to the coronavirus-induced economic slowdown and lower energy prices. This stance has even led to an SEC complaint filed by some accountants, suggesting Exxon should recognize the diminished value of its shale driller XTO Energy.

title: Investors pressure Exxon, Chevron to disclose long-term oil price forecasts
summary: Climate-conscious investors, including the New York State Common Retirement Fund and California State Teachers’ Retirement System, are intensifying pressure on Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. to reveal their long-term crude price forecasts. These investors argue that the lack of transparency prevents them from adequately scrutinizing how the oil giants' investment strategies align with the global shift towards clean energy, especially given the market uncertainties exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic. European counterparts like BP and Royal Dutch Shell have already adjusted their forecasts, leading to significant writedowns, highlighting the financial risks of potentially over-optimistic price assumptions and the creation of "stranded assets."

title: Duke Energy, Dominion Energy cancel contested Atlantic Coast Pipeline
summary: Duke Energy and Dominion Energy have canceled the multi-state Atlantic Coast Pipeline project, citing escalating costs and regulatory uncertainties. This decision comes despite a recent U.S. Supreme Court victory regarding a critical permit, due to continued opposition and delays. The $8 billion natural gas pipeline was designed to cross West Virginia and Virginia into North Carolina.

title: Chesapeake Energy transformation of OKC came with a price
summary: Chesapeake Energy's extensive investment in Oklahoma City, spearheaded by founder Aubrey McClendon, dramatically transformed the city with developments like a sprawling campus and upscale shopping districts. However, this civic transformation coincided with a ballooning company debt that eventually led to Chesapeake filing for bankruptcy. Despite the company's financial struggles and McClendon's death, his legacy of civic impact, particularly on areas like the Boathouse District, continues to be recognized.

title: Total’s CEO Pouyanne plots successful course while competitors stumble
summary: Total SA has successfully navigated the recent oil market downturn and the coronavirus pandemic, avoiding the financial troubles faced by competitors like Royal Dutch Shell Plc and BP Plc. CEO Patrick Pouyanne's strategic cost-cutting, dividend management, and significant investments in clean energy have positioned the company as a stable investment. Total's strong balance sheet, low breakeven point, and advanced diversification into renewables make it an attractive option despite industry-wide challenges.

title: Flaring of Natural Gas in Guyana: Why Is It Happening, and How Can It Be Minimized?
summary: ExxonMobil's Liza field offshore Guyana is flaring significant amounts of natural gas due to equipment problems with gas reinjection. This practice wastes a valuable resource and contributes to carbon dioxide emissions. The author suggests that ExxonMobil should adhere to its environmental standards, improve gas compression systems, diligently monitor for methane leaks, and ensure efficient flaring when necessary, possibly by bringing gas onshore for domestic use to benefit Guyana's energy sector.

title: Exxon vs Chevron Which Is The Smartest Buy
summary: The article compares ExxonMobil (XOM) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) amidst the shale bust, evaluating which company presents a smarter investment. It highlights Chevron's stronger resilience due to more modest capital investment plans and lower debt-to-equity ratio, contrasting it with Exxon's aggressive spending that has strained its balance sheet and dividend. The analysis suggests Chevron is better positioned to weather the industry's downturn.

title: News Content Hub - Former LNG facility to be converted to UK’s largest LPG storage terminal
summary: Flogas Britain is converting a former National Grid LNG facility in Avonmouth, Bristol, into the UK's largest LPG storage terminal through a £40M investment. This project aims to store 34,564 tonnes of LPG to supply commercial and residential customers not connected to the UK's gas grid. The conversion, spearheaded by TGE Gas Engineering GmbH, is expected to be completed and operational by H2 2022, securing LPG supply and promoting a lower-carbon future as part of the UK's Clean Growth Strategy.

title: Energy Transfer’s CEO preparing for Dakota Access battle
summary: Energy Transfer CEO Kelcy Warren is preparing for a legal battle after a judge ordered the Dakota Access pipeline to shut down by August 5th for further environmental reviews. Despite the order, the company announced its intention to continue operating and accepting oil while appealing the ruling, a move that has drawn both strong criticism and support. This decision follows a series of setbacks for the U.S. pipeline industry, though Energy Transfer believes the judge exceeded his authority and is challenging the ruling in court.

title: Fracking Firms Fail, Rewarding Executives and Raising Climate Fears
summary: As U.S. oil and gas companies rapidly face bankruptcy due to a global price war and reduced demand, concerns are rising over abandoned wells left to leak planet-warming pollutants and cleanup costs burdening taxpayers. Despite these financial collapses, millions of dollars have been paid out in executive compensation, drawing criticism from financial analysts. Companies like MDC Energy, Whiting Petroleum, Chesapeake Energy, and Diamond Offshore Drilling compensated executives shortly before or during bankruptcy proceedings, highlighting a controversial trend in the industry.

title: Giveaways created a poverty sinkhole. Then the virus hit
summary: Property tax exemptions offered to oil companies in Louisiana have exacerbated poverty and health disparities in communities surrounding refineries, particularly impacting Black neighborhoods in Shreveport. The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted these long-standing issues, revealing significantly higher mortality rates among Black residents in these areas due to underlying health conditions linked to pollution and a lack of public services resulting from the tax giveaways. Local efforts to reform these tax incentives, such as the Industrial Tax Exemption Program (ITEP), are facing ongoing challenges despite some initial successes in regaining local control over property tax revenue.

title: Are Traders Ready to See Oil Prices Go to $0 Again?
summary: Oil traders are contemplating the possibility of oil prices dropping to $0 again, reminiscent of the April 2020 lows caused by the coronavirus pandemic. While prices have rebounded due to supply cuts and easing lockdowns, the risk of renewed declines exists if COVID-19 cases surge and demand falters. The article discusses leveraged ETFs like GUSH for those betting on price increases and DRIP for those on the bearish side.

title: Membrane Technology Could Cut Emissions and Energy Use in Oil Refining
summary: New membrane technology developed by researchers from Georgia Tech, Imperial College London, and ExxonMobil could significantly reduce carbon emissions and energy consumption in crude oil refining. Currently, heat-based distillation is energy-intensive, accounting for nearly 1% of global energy use. The novel polymer membrane aims to replace some of these conventional processes by separating hydrocarbon mixtures with pressure rather than heat, showing promising results in laboratory tests for recovering gasoline and jet fuel from crude oil.

title: Texas FLNG Bunkering Project Proposed for Galveston
summary: Pilot LNG LLC has proposed the Galveston LNG Bunker Port, a floating liquefaction (FLNG) project on Pelican Island, to develop the Gulf Coast’s first dedicated LNG bunker terminal. The project aims to provide LNG marine fuel to the busy Houston Ship Channel area, reducing emissions and fuel costs for shippers. Pilot LNG expects to make a final investment decision in the latter half of 2021, with operations slated to begin in 2024.

title: Prepara a tu pyme para el comercio exterior
summary: This article highlights the low percentage of Colombian SMEs involved in exports and introduces the "Fábricas de Internacionalización" program launched by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism, along with ProColombia. The initiative aims to foster an export culture and expand the export base among micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises. It addresses the challenges faced by SMEs, such as the lack of dedicated foreign trade departments and offers tailored support to help them overcome these barriers and achieve internationalization.

title: Exxon has topped North Texas’ biggest-companies list for 3 decades. Now there’s a challenger to the throne
summary: For the first time in 30 years, Exxon Mobil Corporation is at risk of losing its position as North Texas' largest public company by revenue. Due to the significant downturn in the oil and gas industry caused by the pandemic and an oil price war, Exxon's revenue is projected to fall to $176 billion in 2020. This opens the door for companies like McKesson Corp., a pharmaceutical distributor whose revenue reached $231 billion in its most recent fiscal year, and potentially AT&T, to claim the top spot previously held by the oil giant.

title: BlackRock Punishes 53 Companies Over Carbon Emissions, 191 On Watchlist
summary: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, has taken action against 53 companies for climate inaction, including ExxonMobil and Chevron, after joining the Climate Action 100+ pact. An additional 191 companies are on a watchlist, facing voting action next year if they fail to improve their climate risk disclosures. This move signifies BlackRock's commitment to integrating sustainability into its investment strategy and ensuring long-term shareholder value.

title: Chevron Deal for Oil and Gas Fields May Set Off New Wave of Mergers (Published 2020)
summary: Chevron's acquisition of Noble Energy for approximately $5 billion marks the first major deal since oil prices crashed four months prior, signaling a potential wave of consolidation in the U.S. oil industry. The pandemic-induced decline in oil demand has pressured highly indebted companies like Noble, creating an opportunity for larger entities like Chevron to expand their assets. Experts anticipate further bankruptcies, mergers, and acquisitions as stronger players consolidate within the struggling sector.

title: Stuck with coal pits the world needs, but few want
summary: Major mining companies like BHP Group are struggling to sell lucrative thermal coal assets, despite strong demand in Asian markets, due to increasing investor pressure to divest from fossil fuels. This trend highlights a growing conflict between the profitability of coal mines and the environmental concerns of investors, pushing companies to consider selling at lower valuations or spinning off their coal operations. The situation for coal producers could serve as a warning to other resource companies about the rapid devaluation of assets not aligned with the Paris climate accord.

title: Jeff Bezos net worth 2020 as billionaire, American business magnate and Amazon.com CEO break stock record in one single day for Bloomberg World's Billionaires ranked list history
summary: Jeff Bezos gained $13 billion in a single day, marking the largest one-day jump for any individual in the history of the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Amazon.com Inc. shares increased by 7.9% due to the rise in internet shopping, contributing to Bezos's net worth reaching $189.3 billion in 2020. His former wife, Mackenzie Bezos, also saw a significant increase in her wealth, and other tech figures like Mark Zuckerberg experienced growth during the lockdown period.

title: Eni seeks to sell assets in Norway, Congo
summary: Eni SpA is reportedly looking to divest assets in Norway and the Republic of Congo due to the slump in oil prices and an industry-wide push to cut spending. In Norway, its subsidiary Var Energi AS aims to sell the Jotun floating production, storage and offloading vessel, valued at around $1 billion. In Congo, Eni is working with advisors to sell a package of operated assets, with the company also pursuing an ambitious carbon-reduction program.

title: Eni seeks to sell assets in Norway, Congo
summary: Eni SpA is looking to sell assets in Norway and the Republic of Congo due to the oil slump and a company-wide push to reduce spending and pursue a carbon-reduction program. In Norway, its majority-owned Var Energi AS plans to sell the Jotun FPSO, valued at about $1 billion, while in Congo, Eni is working with advisers to sell a package of operated assets. The move comes as crude prices are down significantly and energy producers are offloading marginal activities.

title: Jeff Bezos is now personally worth more than the market valuation of Exxon, Nike, and McDonald’s
summary: Jeff Bezos's net worth surged by $13 billion in a single day, marking the largest daily jump recorded by the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. His fortune now stands at $189.3 billion for 2020, exceeding the market capitalization of major corporations like Exxon Mobil, Nike, and McDonald's. This increase is attributed to a 7.9% rise in Amazon shares amid optimism about online shopping trends during an economic downturn.

title: Jeff Bezos' Net Worth Jumps $13 Billion USD in Single Day
summary: Jeff Bezos' net worth increased by $13 billion USD in a single day, setting a new record for the highest individual increase since 2012, driven by a 7.9% surge in Amazon's stock price. This boost pushed his total fortune to $189.3 billion USD in 2020. His ex-wife, Mackenzie Bezos, also saw her net worth rise by $4.6 billion USD, making her the 13th-richest person globally.

title: Precision Drilling second-quarter loss surges as pandemic weakens demand for oil
summary: Precision Drilling Corp. reported a significant surge in its second-quarter loss to $48.9 million, up from $13.8 million a year earlier, with revenues plummeting 47% to $189.8 million due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on oil demand and prices. The company expects a muted third-quarter rebound and aims to reduce 2020 cash outflows by up to $150 million through further cost-cutting and capital expenditure reductions. CEO Kevin Neveu stated these actions have financially and competitively positioned the company for an eventual industry recovery.

title: Equinor second quarter 2020 results
summary: Equinor reported adjusted earnings of USD 0.35 billion and USD 0.65 billion after tax for Q2 2020, significantly down from 2019, primarily due to low commodity prices caused by the Covid-19 pandemic. Despite financial challenges, the company maintained stable operations, implemented cost reductions, and saw strong trading results in volatile markets. Equinor reaffirmed its commitment to strategic development as a broad energy company aiming for a low-carbon future, while also progressing competitive projects and delivering a cash dividend of USD 0.09 per share.

title: The 2010 Enbridge oil spill reshaped the Kalamazoo River and provided a cautionary tale
summary: The 2010 Enbridge oil spill, the second-largest inland oil spill in U.S. history, dramatically impacted the Kalamazoo River but led to extensive cleanup efforts costing $1.21 billion. A decade later, the river's ecosystem shows signs of recovery and improved recreation, yet the incident remains a critical cautionary tale concerning pipeline safety and the environmental risks of tar sand oil. The disaster also sparked important discussions about infrastructure, regulation, and the reliance on Canadian tar sand oil, emphasizing the need for ongoing vigilance to prevent future spills.

title: Reliance overtakes Exxon to become world's No 2 energy firm
summary: Reliance Industries Ltd has surpassed Exxon Mobil Corp to become the world's second-largest energy company after Saudi Aramco, driven by investor interest in its digital and retail ventures. The Indian conglomerate, led by Mukesh Ambani, saw its market value climb to US$189 billion, while Exxon's declined amid a global plunge in fuel demand. This shift reflects Ambani's strategic pivot towards technology and retail, successfully attracting significant investments into its Jio Platforms unit.

title: BP, Total not to bid for BPCL; investors weigh inflexible locations, labour laws with mkt access
summary: BP Plc and Total of France are unlikely to bid for Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL) due to concerns over inflexible refinery locations and tough labor laws in India, despite the access to a rapidly growing fuel market. Russian energy giant Rosneft, Saudi Aramco, and Reliance Industries are seen as potential bidders for the government's 52.98% stake, considering the high price tag of around $10 billion and the lucrative fuel retailing network. The sale of BPCL is crucial for the Indian government to meet its disinvestment target.

title: Total writes off $9.3B in oilsands assets, cancels Canadian oil lobby membership
summary: French energy giant Total announced it is writing off $9.3 billion in oilsands assets in Alberta, including stakes in the Fort Hills and Surmont projects, and canceling its membership in the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers (CAPP). The company cited a "misalignment" with CAPP's public positions on climate change and its own carbon reduction targets, stating that high-cost oil reserves to be produced beyond 20 years are now considered "stranded." This decision follows similar writedowns by other companies and is seen by environmental groups as a sign of the oilsands' diminishing appeal.

title: Valero swings back to profit in 2nd quarter
summary: Valero Energy Corp. reported a $1.3 billion profit in the second quarter of 2020, a significant rebound from a $1.9 billion loss in the first quarter, despite revenues falling 64 percent year-over-year due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company slashed operating expenses and maintained its target to cut capital spending by $400 million to adapt to reduced fuel demand.

title: E&E News: Judges toss $20M fine for Exxon refinery complex
summary: A federal appeals court has overturned a $20 million penalty against Exxon Mobil stemming from a 2012 refinery fire, ruling that the company cannot be held liable under the Clean Air Act because it lacked the intent to release hazardous chemicals. The court found that prior rulings by the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas did not adequately establish intent. This decision could significantly impact how environmental violations are prosecuted, particularly regarding accidental releases.

title: Exxon, Chevron report massive losses
summary: Exxon Mobil and Chevron, the leading U.S. oil companies, reported significant losses in the second quarter of 2020, primarily due to the dramatic drop in oil demand and prices caused by the coronavirus pandemic. Exxon posted its first consecutive quarterly loss in over 30 years, losing $1.1 billion, while Chevron reported an $8.3 billion loss, its worst performance in at least three decades. Both companies responded by cutting spending, production, and laying off employees, though they affirmed plans to maintain shareholder dividends amidst a projected long recovery period for oil prices.

title: Move over Aramco, Apple is now world’s most valuable company
summary: Apple Inc. has surpassed Saudi Aramco to become the world's most valuable company, with its market capitalization reaching $1.817 trillion after a 10% jump on Friday. This shift comes as Apple has benefited from an accelerated move to digital services during the pandemic, while Aramco has faced challenges including a disappointing IPO and plunging crude prices. Apple's valuation now stands higher than Aramco's $1.76 trillion, highlighting the growing strength of tech companies amid global changes.

title: Ivanhoe Mines and Franco-Nevada Look Favorable Ahead of Earnings
summary: This article highlights the favorable positions of Ivanhoe Mines and Franco-Nevada ahead of their earnings reports, despite a general decline in S&P 500 profits and U.S. GDP due to the coronavirus pandemic. It discusses how certain sectors, particularly tech and metals/mining, have thrived, with specific attention given to Ivanhoe's copper production and Franco-Nevada's performance as a gold royalty company, both benefiting from rising metal prices and strategic market conditions. The author also touches on the broader market sentiment, gold's performance, and other economic indicators.

title: Energy transition to be topic in presidential race
summary: The 2020 presidential race is expected to prominently feature the topic of energy transition, with Democratic nominee Joe Biden advocating for renewable energy and reduced fossil fuel dependence, while President Trump supports the oil and gas industry. Industry experts note that energy transition has always been a constant throughout history, driven by innovation and technology in response to societal needs and environmental concerns. The debate centers on the pace and scope of this transition, with some predicting rapid change and others a more gradual shift spanning decades.

title: Utilidad de Ecopetrol, con todo y coronavirus, fue de $ 158.000 millones
summary: Ecopetrol reported a net profit of 158,000 million pesos in the first half of the year, despite the impact of the coronavirus pandemic and low oil prices. The company maintained production above 700,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day and plans investments between $11 billion and $13 billion for 2020-2022, with 80% destined for Colombia. Although the second quarter saw a significant drop in net profit and sales, Ecopetrol is focusing on capital discipline, cash protection, and efficient costs, while advancing with unconventional exploration projects.

title: BP Reports $17.7 Billion Loss, Cuts Dividend
summary: BP PLC announced a $17.7 billion loss and cut its dividend for the first time in a decade, signaling a major strategic shift. The energy giant plans to pivot away from oil and gas, increasing low-carbon investments to $5 billion annually by 2030 and aiming for a 40% reduction in oil and gas production from 2019 levels, while significantly boosting renewable energy capacity.

title: From International Oil Company to Integrated Energy Company: bp sets out strategy for decade of delivery towards net zero ambition | News and insights | Home
summary: BP announced a new strategy to transform from an international oil company into an integrated energy company, focusing on low-carbon energy solutions and customer experiences. The company plans a ten-fold increase in low carbon investment by 2030, targeting 50GW of renewable generating capacity and a 40% reduction in oil and gas production. A new financial framework includes a resilient dividend and a commitment to share buybacks, aiming for long-term value for stakeholders while pursuing net-zero ambitions.

title: Se derrumbó la utilidad de Ecopetrol en el segundo trimestre, cayó un 99,3%
summary: Ecopetrol's profit plummeted by 99.3% in the second quarter due to low oil prices and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The company reported a profit of only 25 billion, with sales of key products decreasing significantly. President Felipe Bayón highlighted the swift financial and operational adjustments made, focusing on capital discipline, cash protection, and cost efficiency.

title: Shell eligió a TGS para construir una nueva planta de gas en Vaca Muerta
summary: Shell Argentina has contracted Transportadora Gas del Sur (TGS) to build a new gas treatment plant in Vaca Muerta for its Bajada de Añelo block. TGS will provide midstream services including dehydration, filtering, regulation, and gas measurement with a capacity of up to 1 million cubic meters per day. This agreement solidifies TGS's presence in the Neuquén basin and allows Shell to focus on drilling and optimizing its development projects.

title: Chris Carr named Member of the Board of Directors at Hilton
summary: Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc. announced the appointment of Chris Carr, Chief Operations Officer of sweetgreen, to its board of directors, effective immediately. Mr. Carr will serve on the Nominating and ESG committee of the board and previously held various roles at Starbucks and ExxonMobil.
