He also serves on the board of REI and as a Trustee for Howard University and the University of San Diego.

title: Exxon Mobil to Suspend 401(k) Match in October
summary: Exxon Mobil announced it will suspend its 401(k) match beginning in October 2020 as a cost-cutting measure due to the COVID-19 pandemic and global oversupply. The move impacts thousands of employees and follows the company's Q2 2020 loss of $1.1 billion. This decision aligns with a trend observed across other plan sponsors during the pandemic.

title: Exxon halts contributions to employee retirement plan
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is suspending the company's contribution to its U.S. employee retirement savings plan starting in October due to cost-cutting measures amid the pandemic. This decision follows back-to-back quarterly losses and significant reductions in project outlays and operating expenses. The United Steelworkers union has expressed opposition and is assessing options to protect members' benefits.

title: EOG Resources loses $909M in second quarter
summary: EOG Resources reported a loss of $909 million in the second quarter of 2020, a significant drop from an $848 million profit in the same period last year, due to the global pandemic's impact on oil demand and prices. The company's revenue declined by over 80 percent, but EOG announced measures to reduce spending, cut operating costs, and improve capital efficiency to maintain production at lower oil prices. Despite the losses, EOG generated positive free cash flow and began restarting production as crude prices recovered.

title: ExxonMobil hires Noble Corp. drillship for Guyana drilling
summary: ExxonMobil has contracted Noble Corp.'s drillship, Noble Sam Croft, for a six-month drilling program in Guyana, starting in the fourth quarter of 2020. This deal is part of a Commercial Enabling Agreement signed in February 2020, bringing all four of Noble's high-specification HHI drillships under contract with ExxonMobil in the Guyana-Suriname basin. The Noble Sam Croft will commence its work for ExxonMobil after completing its current contract with Apache in Suriname in mid-November 2020.

title: BP walks away from the oil supermajor model it helped create
summary: BP is divesting from its oil supermajor model, a concept it helped create, under new CEO Bernard Looney. The company plans to significantly decrease oil and gas output, cut dividends by half, and invest up to $5 billion annually in renewable energy. This strategic shift puts BP, along with other European majors like Shell and Total, on a different path from US counterparts Exxon Mobil and Chevron, who continue to prioritize fossil fuels.

title: Stena drillship arrives on ExxonMobil’s well location in Guyana
summary: The Stena Carron drillship has arrived at the Kaieteur Block offshore Guyana to commence drilling operations for the Tanager-1 well for ExxonMobil. This well is the first in a potential multi-well drilling campaign by ExxonMobil in the region, targeting high-impact Upper Cretaceous prospects over the next 6 to 12 months. Westmount Energy holds indirect interests in the Kaieteur Block, and views this campaign as a potential source of "transformational value changes."

title: Phillips 66 Plans to Shut Facilities, Pipelines Amid Renewables Shift
summary: Phillips 66 announced its intention to close or convert certain facilities and associated pipelines as part of a shift towards renewable fuels. The company plans to shut down its carbon plant in Rodeo and Santa Maria refining facility by 2023, converting its Rodeo refinery into a renewable fuels plant. This move aligns with other U.S. refiners who are also converting facilities to produce renewable fuel, particularly to supply the California market.

title: Phillips 66 Is Building the World's Largest Renewable Fuels Plant
summary: Phillips 66 is converting its crude oil refinery in Rodeo, California, into the world's largest renewable fuels plant, which will produce over 800 million gallons of fuel annually from materials like used cooking oil, fats, greases, and soybean oil. This move comes despite low oil prices, signaling a continued demand for cleaner fuels, particularly in California which has a low-carbon-fuel standard. The transformed facility, dubbed "Rodeo Renewed," is expected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 50% and sulfur dioxide by 75%, starting operations as early as 2024.

title: LNG 101: The Complex Process of Financing Massive LNG Projects
summary: This article discusses the complex and lengthy process of financing massive LNG projects, highlighting how Total SE secured $14.9 billion for its Mozambique LNG project amidst the Covid-19 pandemic. It explains that such projects typically involve multiple sponsors, a syndicate of lenders including export credit agencies and commercial banks, and long-term supply agreements to mitigate risks. The financing process can take up to two years and is influenced by various factors such as project costs, host country, and market conditions.

title: Collaborating to Benefit Communities
summary: ConocoPhillips actively engages with communities to foster open dialogue and build mutually beneficial relationships, exemplified by its Citizens Advisory Committee (CAC) in Texas's Eagle Ford region. The CAC, composed of local leaders and company employees, discusses industry matters, environmental concerns, safety practices, and community involvement. ConocoPhillips also utilizes "Leadership Roundtables" to communicate with elected officials and address local issues, demonstrating a commitment to being a responsible community partner.

title: One carbon capture project stalls as another advances
summary: The Petra Nova carbon-capture project, the world's largest, has been mothballed by NRG Energy due to low oil prices making it unprofitable. This highlights the reliance of such projects on demand for CO2 from the oil sector for enhanced oil recovery. Conversely, another DOE-funded carbon-capture project, Cal Capture, is proceeding in California, planning to sequester CO2 from a gas-fired power plant rather than use it for oil production.

title: The sound science of cleaner energy: Jenny Seagraves
summary: This article highlights Jenny Seagraves, an ExxonMobil scientist, and her journey into science, driven by imagination. It details her team's meticulous four-year process of developing OASE® Sulfexx™ with BASF, a technology that efficiently removes hydrogen sulfide from natural gas, illustrating the importance of testing and retesting in scientific innovation. Seagraves emphasizes that creativity and breakthrough innovation arise from collaboration and a willingness to set aside biases to solve challenges.

title: Carr to Succeed Milton at ExxonMobil
summary: ExxonMobil Fuels & Lubricants President Bryan Milton is set to retire on September 1, 2020, after 34 years of service. His successor, Ian Carr, who most recently served as senior vice president of ExxonMobil's Fuels business, has been named vice president of ExxonMobil by the board. Milton was instrumental in combining the company's refining and marketing operations in 2018.

title: Phillips 66 to reconfigure California refinery for renewable fuels
summary: Phillips 66 announced plans to convert its Rodeo, California crude oil refinery into a renewable fuels plant, utilizing cooking oil and food wastes to produce motor fuels. This initiative is part of a broader trend among U.S. refiners to transition existing facilities to renewable fuel production, driven by California's low carbon fuel standard. The project, estimated to cost up to $800 million, aims to produce 680 million gallons per year of renewable diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel starting in 2024, and includes shutting down associated carbon and refining facilities.

title: Phillips 66 closing its Nipomo Mesa refinery. What will happen to the workers?
summary: Phillips 66 announced it is closing its Santa Maria Refinery on the Nipomo Mesa by 2023, impacting 110 employees, as the company shifts towards renewable fuels. The company plans to convert its San Francisco refinery into the world's largest renewable fuels plant. While employees will retain their jobs until 2023 and the company hopes to offer opportunities at other facilities, local officials are concerned about the loss of high-paying jobs in the area.

title: Oil giant taking stake in nuclear fusion startup
summary: Chevron Corp., the second-largest U.S. oil and gas company, has made a Series A investment in Zap Energy, a Seattle-based startup developing commercially scalable nuclear fusion reactors. This investment by Chevron’s Future Energy Fund marks its tenth and aligns with its strategy to explore breakthrough technologies for decarbonization and energy transition. Nuclear fusion is highlighted as a promising low-carbon energy source compared to conventional nuclear fission.

title: Gaurdie Banister Jr. elected to Dow Board of Directors
summary: Dow (NYSE: DOW) announced that Gaurdie Banister Jr., former president and CEO of Aera Energy LLC, has been elected to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Mr. Banister brings extensive global business and leadership expertise, along with a strong background in engineering and the energy sector, to Dow's board. He will serve on the Environmental, Health, Safety and Technology and the Compensation and Leadership Development committees, further strengthening the board's industry leadership and diversity.

title: Shale driller Chaparral Energy files for bankruptcy due to pandemic woes
summary: Chaparral Energy Inc, an Oklahoma oil and gas producer, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection due to the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on oil prices. This marks the second time the company has sought bankruptcy protection, previously doing so during the 2014-16 oil price slump. The filing follows warnings from the company about its ability to continue as a going concern amidst a historic plunge in commodity prices.

title: Brazil: Total Launches Phase 3 On the Giant Mero Field Development| Total.com
summary: Total and its partners have approved the investment for the third phase of the Mero project in Brazil's deep offshore, targeting a liquid treatment capacity of 180,000 barrels per day by 2024. This decision aligns with Total's strategy to develop giant projects in Brazil's deep-offshore, aiming for competitive production costs and a target of 150,000 barrels per day in Brazil by 2025. The Mero field, part of the Libra Consortium, has significant oil resources estimated at 3 to 4 billion barrels.

title: California refiners shift production to renewable diesel
summary: California petroleum refiners Phillips66, Global Clean Energy, and Marathon Oil are converting their facilities to produce renewable diesel from plant oils and animal fats, driven by subsidies for climate-friendly fuels and low petroleum prices. This shift is expected to intensify competition for cheap feedstocks, potentially impacting industries like soap and detergent that also rely on animal fats. The new entrants will join established companies in supplying renewable diesel to California, which mandates reductions in the carbon intensity of transportation fuels.

title: Newpek LLC leaves Texas and sells oil and gas holdings
summary: Newpek LLC, a Texas-based company under Mexico-based Alfa, has divested all its oil and gas assets in Texas, including operations in the Eagle Ford Shale and Edwards Shale. This transaction, valued at an implied US $88 million, allowed Newpek to cancel its obligations and resulted in an extraordinary gain of US $58 million for Alfa in Q3 2020 EBITDA. The move is part of Alfa's strategy to unlock value by divesting oil and gas assets outside of Mexico, leading Newpek to close its Texas administrative office and relocate functions to Monterrey, Mexico.

title: Exxon Limits Guyana Output Due to Gas Injection Issues
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has limited output at its Guyana offshore project to 100,000 barrels-per-day due to ongoing issues with natural gas reinjection. Mechanical problems with gas compressing equipment are preventing full reinjection, prompting Exxon to reduce production to avoid excessive flaring of natural gas. The company aims to restore full capacity of 120,000 bpd once the gas handling system is fully commissioned.

title: Salesforce, Amgen, and Honeywell Int’l will join Dow Jones Industrial Average
summary: Salesforce, Amgen, and Honeywell International are set to join the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) before trading opens on August 31, 2020. These companies will replace ExxonMobil, Pfizer, and Raytheon Technologies. The changes are a response to Apple's 4:1 stock split, which would have reduced the index's information technology weighting, and are intended to maintain the index's level.

title: A julio, Ecopetrol contrató con proveedores locales más de $1,8 billones
summary: As of July, Ecopetrol contracted over $1.8 billion with local suppliers, including $806 million directly and an additional $1 trillion through 'local export' where local suppliers sell to other Ecopetrol regional operations in Colombia. Despite international oil price fluctuations and the COVID-19 pandemic, Ecopetrol continues to engage with local businesses across all regions where it operates, supporting regional growth and competitiveness. The company's strategy also encourages its allies to contract with local providers, totaling $1.4 trillion in contracts and local exports by June 2020.

title: Salesforce to replace Exxon in Dow Jones Industrial Average index next week
summary: Salesforce.com Inc, Amgen Inc, and Honeywell International Inc are set to replace Exxon Mobil Corp, Pfizer Inc, and Raytheon Technologies Corp in the Dow Jones Industrial Average index starting August 31. This change follows Apple Inc's stock split, which would have reduced the index's weight in the information technology sector.

title: Salesforce to replace Exxon in Dow Jones Industrial Average index next week
summary: Salesforce.com Inc, Amgen Inc, and Honeywell International Inc are set to join the Dow Jones Industrial Average index on August 31, replacing Exxon Mobil Corp, Pfizer Inc, and Raytheon Technologies Corp. This change follows Apple Inc's stock split, which prompted a rebalancing of the index's representation in the information technology sector.

title: Dow kicks out Exxon, Pfizer, Raytheon in biggest shake-up since 2013
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average is undergoing its biggest reshuffling in seven years, with Exxon Mobil Corp., Pfizer Inc., and Raytheon Technologies Corp. being replaced by Salesforce.com, Amgen Inc., and Honeywell International. This change reflects the declining influence of commodity companies and the rising dominance of technology firms, a trend amplified by Apple's stock split which reduced the sway of computer and software companies in the price-weighted index. The exclusions highlight a significant shift in the US economy and stock market, particularly the underrepresentation of technology in the Dow compared to other indexes.

title: Exxon kicked out of Dow Industrials
summary: Exxon Mobil, Pfizer, and Raytheon Technologies were removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average, making way for Salesforce.com, Amgen, and Honeywell International. This reshuffling, the biggest in seven years, reflects the increasing dominance of technology companies and the declining influence of commodity firms in the American economy, a trend amplified by the 2020 pandemic. The changes were prompted by Apple's stock split, which reduced tech's sway in the price-weighted index, leading the Dow's handlers to seek greater technology representation.

title: Enel X y Enex instalan puntos de carga rápida en estaciones de servicios Shell
summary: Enel X and Enex have partnered to install rapid charging points for electric vehicles at Shell service stations in Chile. Three out of ten planned charging stations are already operational in Santiago, with a goal to expand the "ElectroRuta Enel X" project to 1,200 chargers nationwide, creating the largest road charging network in Chile. These 50kW chargers can simultaneously charge two vehicles in 25-40 minutes, providing over 250 kilometers of autonomy.

title: Texas energy corridor shuttering plants as Hurricane Laura set sights on Gulf Coast
summary: As Hurricane Laura bears down on the Gulf Coast, major oil and chemical facilities in Texas and Louisiana are shutting down operations. This includes approximately 30% of the U.S. Gulf Coast refining capacity, leading to a surge in gasoline prices due to concerns about destruction comparable to Hurricane Harvey in 2017. However, analysts note that current high gasoline inventories and lower refinery utilization rates due to the pandemic might mitigate the impact of supply disruptions.

title: Exxon Mobil dropped from the Dow after nearly a century, replaced by Salesforce
summary: Exxon Mobil, a Dow Jones Industrial Average member since 1928, is being removed from the blue-chip index and replaced by Salesforce.com. Drug company Pfizer and Raytheon Technologies are also being replaced by Amgen and Honeywell respectively. These changes, effective August 31, were prompted by Apple's stock split and aim to better reflect the American economy.

title: Big Oil, meet Big Green
summary: The term "Supermajor" is increasingly shifting from large oil companies to major renewable energy producers like NextEra Energy, Iberdrola SA, and Ørsted A/S, whose valuations now exceed traditional oil giants such as Royal Dutch Shell and BP. This transition is driven by the economic downturn affecting oil stocks and the rising attractiveness of renewable projects due to falling costs and climate targets, prompting oil majors to invest heavily in green energy or face acquisitions. Experts predict a reallocation of capital from fossil fuels to renewables is essential for meeting net-zero emissions targets.

title: Exxon yanked from Dow after nearly a century
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. was removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average after more than 90 years, a symbolic move reflecting the oil industry's recent struggles, including falling oil prices and climate concerns. This change saw SalesForce.com Inc., Amgen Inc., and Honeywell International Inc. replace Exxon, Pfizer Inc., and Raytheon Technologies Corp. While Exxon maintains its focus on shareholder value, critics argue the company is failing to adapt to a changing energy market.

title: Exxon Mobil replaced by a software stock after 92 years in the Dow is a 'sign of the times'
summary: Exxon Mobil, a Dow component for 92 years, has been replaced by software company Salesforce, marking a significant shift in the index. This change, alongside Amgen and Honeywell International replacing Pfizer and Raytheon Technologies, reflects the declining prominence of the energy sector and the corresponding rise of technology stocks. The move is seen as a "sign of the times," highlighting the faltering energy industry against a backdrop of strong tech growth.

title: Exxon Mobil Exits: The Dow Drops Its Oldest Member
summary: Exxon Mobil, once the Dow Jones Industrial Average's longest-tenured member, is being removed from the influential index, effective August 31, 2020. This change is driven by Apple's stock split, which necessitates a rebalancing of the Dow. While symbolic, the move underscores Exxon's diminished stature compared to tech giants and highlights the struggles of oil companies amid climate concerns and shifting market dynamics.

title: YPF: una empresa argentina que tenemos que fortalecer
summary: The article argues that YPF, Argentina's state-owned oil company, is crucial for the country's development, especially concerning Vaca Muerta, but suffered during the Macri administration due to misguided strategies and decreased investment. It highlights YPF's unique history and emphasizes the necessity for current measures to strengthen the company as a key driver for economic growth and exports in Argentina. The author contrasts YPF's strategic role with other international and national oil companies and underscores its importance for Argentina's energy security.

title: Oklahoma Corporation Commissioners decide electric territorial disputes, leaves natural gas cap on, for now
summary: The Oklahoma Corporation Commission addressed two electric territorial disputes, ruling in favor of a cooperative in one case and an investor-owned utility in another. They also voted to temporarily keep a proration formula that caps natural gas production from the state's most productive wells. Commissioners indicated that the continued necessity and methodology of this natural gas proration will be re-evaluated.

title: Exxon Presses for Guyana Approval of Third Offshore Project
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is urging Guyana's new government to approve its third offshore oil project, Payara, which has been under review amid political uncertainty. The project, which is part of the Stabroek block operated by a consortium including Hess Corp and CNOOC Ltd, aims to develop over 8 billion barrels of recoverable resources. Guyana's new president, Irfaan Ali, has expressed concerns about the Production Sharing Agreement's generosity and plans to implement stricter local content and labor rules.

title: What Dow Changes Mean For ETF Investors
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is undergoing a significant shakeup, with Exxon, Pfizer, and Raytheon Technologies being replaced by Salesforce, Amgen, and Honeywell. These changes are designed to diversify the index and better reflect the American economy, particularly after Apple's stock split impacted the technology sector's weighting. For ETF investors tracking the DJIA, such as through DIA, these adjustments will inevitably alter portfolio returns and exposure.

title: Quién es Ricardo Darré, el nuevo CEO de YPF
summary: Ricardo Darré will assume the role of CEO of YPF on July 1st, succeeding Daniel González. An industrial engineer from ITBA, Darré has a three-decade career in the oil industry, having worked for Schlumberger and most recently as managing director of Exploration and Production for Total in Houston. His role will focus on operational management and production, complementing Miguel Ángel Gutiérrez's responsibilities for government relations.

title: Global offshore industry is struggling, Nigeria is not immune
summary: The global offshore oil industry is facing significant struggles, with major drillers filing for bankruptcy due to low drilling contracts and debt, a situation that also impacts Nigeria. Nigeria, whose deepwater assets contribute significantly to its oil production, is seeing a sharp decline in rig counts, indicating reduced exploration and production activities. This poses a challenge for the country's oil production targets and highlights the need for a more stable regulatory environment to attract investors.

title: Amgen Joins Dow Jones Industrial Average as the Benchmark Index Revamps to ‘Better Reflect’ the U.S. Economy
summary: Amgen, Salesforce, and Honeywell have been added to the Dow Jones Industrial Average, replacing Pfizer, Exxon Mobil, and Raytheon Technologies. This revamp aims to better reflect the U.S. economy's shift towards innovative technologies. Amgen's inclusion marks the first biotech stock in the index, highlighting the growing significance of the biotech industry.

title: Spared from Hurricane Laura’s wrath, Gulf Coast refineries begin to restart operations
summary: Several Gulf Coast refineries, including Motiva Enterprises and Exxon Mobil, have begun restarting operations after sustaining minimal damage from Hurricane Laura. While Valero and Citgo also reported minimal or no visible damage to their refineries in Port Arthur and Lake Charles respectively, Citgo expects a delayed restart due to high winds damaging its facility. Power outages and worker availability in Louisiana are cited as potential challenges for a quick return to normal operations.

title: Big Oil Faded. Will Big Tech?
summary: This article questions whether Big Tech companies, currently dominant, face a similar fate to Big Oil, specifically Exxon Mobil, which was once the world's most valuable company but has since declined. The author draws parallels between the economic and political influence of past oil superpowers and current tech giants, suggesting that while Big Tech seems invincible now, history shows that even dominant industries can lose relevance due to changing global dynamics and a failure to adapt.

title: “Humiliation”: Exxon dumped out Dow Jones Industrial Index after nearly 100 years
summary: ExxonMobil has been removed from the influential Dow Jones Industrial Index after nearly a century, marking a significant decline for the oil giant. This "corporate humiliation" reflects a long-term erosion of value and investor shift away from fossil fuels towards renewables due to climate change concerns and the impact of COVID-19. The move is seen as a major milestone signaling the potential "beginning of the end" for Big Oil's dominance.

title: PetroChina and Ovintiv end joint venture deal, agree to split Alberta assets
summary: PetroChina Canada Inc. and Ovintiv Inc. have mutually terminated their eight-year joint venture in Alberta's Duvernay shale assets, agreeing to split the acreage and production equally. PetroChina Canada will create a new operating team to manage its share, with Ovintiv continuing operations until PetroChina is ready. This move signifies a major step in PetroChina's upstream capabilities in Canada.

title: REFILE-Exxon Mobil offers voluntary redundancy for Australian employees
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced a voluntary redundancy program for its Australian employees across various cities to navigate "unprecedented" market conditions. This move follows earlier reports that the U.S. oil company was preparing significant spending and job cuts to preserve its shareholder dividend amidst quarterly losses. An Exxon spokesman in Australia declined to comment on the percentage of staff targeted for reduction.

title: Statement for Partners, Customers, and Suppliers - AUGUST 2020
summary: Braskem Idesa issued a statement to address allegations related to Ethylene XXI and its contract with Pemex. The company refutes claims of irregular payments, asserting that its contract with Pemex resulted from a transparent international public auction and that various audits found no irregularities. Braskem Idesa also highlighted its significant investment in Mexico's petrochemical sector and its ongoing commitment to finding solutions for ethane supply issues.

title: Imperial Oil shuts down production at Kearl after pipeline spill
summary: Imperial Oil has halted production at its Kearl oil sands site in Canada following a leak in the Polaris diluent pipeline, which supplies ultralight oil needed for blending bitumen. The spill, estimated at 90 cubic meters, occurred near Fort McMurray, and the timing for restarting production is currently unknown. This outage is expected to remove a significant amount of oil from the market and has also impacted operations at Husky Energy’s Sunrise oilsands facility.

title: Exxon weighs global job cuts after unveiling Australian lay-off
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is considering global job cuts following a voluntary layoff program initiated in Australia. The decision comes as the oil major faces a historic collapse in fuel demand due to the coronavirus pandemic, leading to reduced capital spending and consecutive quarterly losses. The company is evaluating efficiencies on a country-by-country basis to "right-size" its business.

title: -Exxon weighs global job cuts after unveiling Australian lay-off plan
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced that it is assessing worldwide job cuts due to the global coronavirus pandemic's impact on fuel demand, following an announcement of voluntary layoffs in Australia. The company stated that job cuts will continue globally into 2021, driven by a historic collapse in fuel demand and back-to-back quarterly losses. Despite a previous ambitious spending plan, Exxon has slashed capital spending and is evaluating workforce reductions "business by business and country by country."

title: ExxonMobil Unit Shuts Oil Sands Mine After Pipeline Spill
summary: ExxonMobil's Imperial Oil shut down its Kearl oil-sands mine in northern Alberta after a spill from a pipeline supplying diluent to the operation. This disruption, caused by a leak in Inter Pipeline Ltd.'s Polaris system, adds to the challenges faced by Canadian crude producers already struggling with infrastructure limitations and reduced demand. The shutdown directly impacts Imperial Oil and could affect other producers like Husky, BP, and Cenovus, though Imperial is pursuing mitigation steps.

title: Mars crude on pace to average premium to WTI MEH
summary: Mars crude is projected to average a premium to WTI MEH for the first quarter since 2015, driven by stronger demand and tighter supply of sour crude along the US Gulf Coast. This shift reverses the traditional sweet/sour spread, with Mars crude showing significant strength in Q2 and August 2020. The increased demand for sour crudes is attributed to the resilience of deepwater production compared to shale plays during the COVID-19 pandemic and continued global sanctions and OPEC+ cuts impacting sour crude supply.

title: Pullback Brings Stocks Closer to Fair Value
summary: The market experienced its largest single-day decline since June 11, primarily driven by a sell-off in the technology sector, which was deemed overvalued. While the overall market remains overvalued, this pullback has brought stock valuations closer to fair value. The energy sector, in contrast, appears significantly undervalued, offering potential opportunities for long-term investors.

title: CORRECTED (OFFICIAL)-PDVSA, Eni weigh options to transfer oil from idled facility amid risks
summary: Venezuela's state-run PDVSA and Italian energy firm Eni are exploring ways to offload approximately 1.3 million barrels of Corocoro crude from an idled floating storage facility (FSO) off Venezuela's eastern coast. The facility has been inactive for over a year due to U.S. sanctions, leading to worsening operational issues and environmental risks, including a substantial lean and a seawater leak in the engine room. While Eni states the situation is stable and plans to use a dynamic-positioning vessel for unloading, any transfer for export would require authorization from the U.S. Treasury Department due to sanctions against PDVSA.

title: Pipeline Spill Forces Temporary Shutdown at Kearl Lake Tar Sands/Oil Sands Mine
summary: Imperial Oil's Kearl Lake mine has temporarily shut down following a diluent pipeline spill from Inter Pipeline Ltd.'s Polaris system. The spill disrupted the supply of diluent crucial for transporting sticky bitumen, forcing a halt in oil sands production as companies already face financial struggles. The incident occurred shortly after ExxonMobil, which owns Imperial Oil, had identified Kearl Lake as a potential site for permanent closure due to scaling back its rebuilding plans.

title: ConocoPhillips Drops Request for Oil and Gas Flaring in West Texas After Challenge from Clean Air Groups
summary: ConocoPhillips has withdrawn its request for flaring permit extensions at 41 oil and gas sites in West Texas following a challenge from clean air advocacy groups. The company cited "operational changes" that made the extensions unnecessary, after the groups objected to the permits due to concerns about air quality and public health impacts from the released pollutants. This decision is seen by environmental advocates as a victory that underscores the need for stricter oversight from the Texas Railroad Commission on flaring activities.

title: Marathon Petroleum to represent refinery owners in 2022 USW contract talks: official
summary: Marathon Petroleum Corp. will lead negotiations with the United Steelworkers union (USW) for the 2022 national agreement covering U.S. refinery and chemical workers, replacing Royal Dutch Shell Plc. This change reflects the evolving landscape of the U.S. refining industry, where independent companies like Marathon now operate a larger share of refineries compared to major energy companies. The national bargaining agreement sets pay and benefits for approximately 30,000 workers, with the current contract expiring on February 1, 2022.

title: Hess makes another oil discovery off Guyana
summary: Hess Corp. announced another oil discovery off the coast of Guyana, its 18th find on the Stabroek Block. The company struck oil at its Redtail-1 well and also found more oil next to its Yellowtail-1 discovery at Yellowtail-2. These discoveries are expected to add to the estimated recoverable resource of over 8 billion barrels of oil equivalent in the Stabroek Block.

title: Why Suncor Energy, Continental Resources, and Occidental Petroleum Stocks Crashed Almost 10% Today
summary: Suncor Energy, Continental Resources, and Occidental Petroleum stocks plummeted by nearly 10% today after Saudi Arabia announced a price cut for crude oil, causing Brent crude and WTI prices to fall significantly. These oil companies are particularly vulnerable due to their substantial debt loads and unprofitability, with some having faced losses since late 2019 even before the pandemic's impact. The recent downturn in oil prices following a period of flatlined prices since April further heightens uncertainty for their future.

title: ExxonMobil Hits Its 18th Oil Discovery Offshore Guyana
summary: ExxonMobil announced its 18th oil discovery offshore Guyana at the Redtail-1 well, adding to the Stabroek Block's estimated recoverable resource of over 8 billion barrels of oil equivalent. This discovery, along with additional reservoir intervals found at Yellowtail-2, reinforces the significant exploration potential in the block. ExxonMobil, in partnership with Hess and CNOCC, continues to develop these projects, with future FPSOs planned to significantly increase production capacity in Guyana.

title: Using Foreign Funds to Correct for a Sliding Dollar
summary: The dollar has recently been in decline relative to other foreign currencies, primarily due to low interest rates and a shift in the Fed's monetary policy. This can have varying implications for investors' portfolios depending on their holdings. Foreign stock and bond funds, particularly unhedged ones, can benefit from a weaker dollar, while U.S. companies with significant foreign revenue may also see improved profits.

title: Exclusive: -Exxon downsizes global empire as Wall Street worries about dividend
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp faces a projected $48 billion shortfall through 2021 due to ill-timed investments and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to deep cuts in staff and projects. The financial strain has raised concerns among Wall Street investors about the sustainability of Exxon's once-sacrosanct dividend. The company is undertaking a worldwide review to cut expenses, including staff reviews and benefit reductions, while analysts believe a dividend cut is increasingly likely amidst falling oil prices and weakened demand.

title: Exxon Refinery Wage and Hour Lawsuit Results in $4M Settlement
summary: ExxonMobil, PBF Energy Ltd., and Torrance Refining Co. agreed to a $4.4 million settlement in a class action lawsuit filed by workers. The lawsuit alleged that the companies denied meal and rest breaks and miscalculated payroll for employees working 12-hour shifts. The settlement is expected to cover 335 workers, with each potentially receiving approximately $9,500.

title: Veronica Foley Is Precision Drilling’s ‘Key to Success’
summary: Veronica Foley, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary at Precision Drilling, is honored for her role in successfully defending the company against a major Fair Labor Standards Act lawsuit and securing shareholder approval for a critical executive compensation plan. Foley's strategic decision-making and leadership during these challenging times for Precision Drilling, and the oil and gas industry as a whole, have earned her significant recognition, including the 2020 Houston Corporate Counsel Business Litigation of the Year award. The article also highlights her personal journey and professional philosophy as an in-house counsel.

title: Talos Says Its Gulf of Mexico Acreage Unaffected by Trump's Order
summary: Talos Energy confirmed that its operations in the Gulf of Mexico are unaffected by President Trump's executive order extending a moratorium on oil and gas operations in other parts of the Gulf and Atlantic. The company stated that 100% of its federal waters assets are in the Central and Western Gulf of Mexico Planning Areas, which are not subject to the order. Talos also highlighted the significant economic contributions of the U.S. Gulf of Mexico oil and gas industry.

title: CORRECTED-ANALYSIS-LNG investments vanish in 2020 as coronavirus slashes oil and gas prices
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has led to an unprecedented halt in new liquefied natural gas (LNG) export project approvals in 2020, a first in at least two decades. The dramatic drop in oil and gas prices has forced companies to delay investment decisions and write down existing assets, with only a few North American projects still remotely considered for approval, primarily Sempra Energy's Costa Azul. While this creates challenges for smaller developers, the delay is seen as potentially positive for oil majors with large LNG portfolios, contributing to higher prices by 2025 as demand eventually recovers.

title: Entergy Recognized as a Top U.S. Utility in Economic Development for 13 Years
summary: Entergy has been recognized by Site Selection magazine as a top U.S. electric utility in economic development for the 13th consecutive year. This recognition highlights Entergy's significant role in fostering economic growth, contributing to nearly $18.2 billion in capital investment and creating over 5,463 new jobs in its service territory in 2019 alone. Over the past 13 years, Entergy has supported projects totaling $153 billion in capital investment and close to 100,000 jobs.

title: Oil Companies Admit to Contributing to Climate Change — and Blame You
summary: In a landmark 2018 federal court hearing in San Francisco, five major oil companies (Chevron, ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips, Royal Dutch Shell, and British Petroleum) acknowledged the scientific consensus that human activity, including the burning of fossil fuels, is the dominant cause of global warming and sea-level rise. While admitting their contribution to greenhouse gas emissions, the companies deflected direct responsibility, arguing that the blame lies with consumers' energy use. Judge William H. Alsup confirmed the court's acceptance of the vast scientific consensus during the proceedings, highlighting the historic nature of these admissions in legal record.

title: Imperial ramps up Kearl oil sands mine output after diluent pipeline restored
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. is resuming normal production at its Kearl oil sands mine after its main diluent supply pipeline was restored following a leak. The company had halted operations at the 240,000 barrels per day facility after a leak was detected in the Polaris pipeline in late August. Analysts estimate that the two-week production loss will reduce Imperial's third-quarter output from Kearl.

title: Eastern Med’s Prolific Natural Gas Resources Looking Rock Solid with Eni’s 4 Tcf Discovery
summary: Eni SpA and BP plc announced a significant natural gas discovery of an estimated 4 Tcf offshore Egypt in the Nidoco NW-1 well within the Abu Madi West Development Lease, expanding the Great Nooros Area's potential. This new find, located in the Eastern Mediterranean, further solidifies the region as a prolific natural gas resource area. Eni, with its partners, plans to quickly evaluate development options, leveraging existing infrastructure to bring the resources to market.

title: Imperial Oil Restarts Oilsands Output from Kearl After Pipeline Leak
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. has restarted production at its 220,000 b/d Kearl oilsands mine after Inter Pipeline Ltd. repaired a leak that had halted operations. The leak, which occurred in a 238,000 b/d Inter Pipeline conduit called Polaris, spilled an estimated 550 barrels of bitumen and disrupted the supply of condensate essential for bitumen processing. The full production impact of the outage is still being assessed by Imperial Oil, a company 70% owned by ExxonMobil.

title: Top Comcast exec to become lead independent director at JPMorgan Chase
summary: Comcast Corp. executive Steve Burke has been appointed as the lead independent director of JPMorgan Chase & Co. Burke will be succeeding former ExxonMobil CEO Lee R. Raymond in this role. This move brings a prominent media executive into a key leadership position at one of the largest financial institutions.

title: Exclusive: -EQT bids for Chevron U.S. shale-gas assets in Appalachia - sources
summary: EQT Corp., the largest U.S. natural gas producer, has reportedly placed a $750 million bid for Chevron Corp.'s Appalachia shale gas properties and a pipeline stake. Chevron is currently evaluating bids for these assets, which it had previously taken an $8.17 billion charge to write down their value. This potential acquisition comes as EQT views Appalachia shale as a "buyer's market" and an opportunity for consolidation.

title: LGI Homes expands neighborhood in Baytown area
summary: LGI Homes has expanded its Joseph’s Cove community near Baytown, offering new homes starting in the $190,000s in the Barbers Hill ISD. The Woodlands-based builder is providing seven floor plans for homes ranging from 1,300 to 2,300 square feet. The community is located conveniently near major employers like Exxon Mobil Baytown.

title: Wall Street-Backed Exchange Launches as Rival to NYSE, Nasdaq
summary: A new exchange, Members Exchange (MEMX), backed by major Wall Street firms and BlackRock Inc., launched on Monday to compete with NYSE and Nasdaq. MEMX aims to offer a low-cost alternative, initiating trading with seven stocks and planning to expand to all U.S. exchange-listed securities by September 29. This launch follows years of dissatisfaction among banks and trading firms regarding fees charged by existing major exchanges.

title: ExxonMobil Expands Agreement with Global Thermostat, Sees Promise in Direct Air Capture Technology
summary: ExxonMobil and Global Thermostat have expanded their joint development agreement to advance direct air capture technology, which removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Following a 12-month technical evaluation, the companies see promising signs that this technology can be scaled. Both companies emphasize the importance of CO2 capture for decarbonization and achieving climate goals, leveraging their research networks to further develop and scale the technology.

title: R&D Council of NJ Announces 2020 Thomas Edison Patent Award Winners
summary: The Research & Development Council of New Jersey announced the 2020 Thomas Edison Patent Award winners and special individual honorees. Awards will be presented on November 12, 2020, to 14 companies and institutions, recognizing innovations from biomaterials to water-efficient toilets. Special awards will be given to Dr. Roger Perlmutter of Merck for the Chairman's Award, Dr. Joachim Messing (posthumously) for the Science and Technology Medal, and Dr. Dawood Farahi for the Educator of the Year Award.

title: Petra Nova is closed: What it means for carbon capture
summary: The Petra Nova carbon capture project, one of the world's largest, is offline due to low oil prices, prompting reevaluation of carbon capture project revenue streams. While its economics are cautionary, carbon capture remains important for decarbonization strategies, especially with federal tax credits like 45Q. Developers are exploring dedicated storage options and CO2 pipeline networks to de-risk future projects from oil price volatility.

title: General Electric, Shell looking for exits as energy transition accelerates
summary: General Electric (GE) and Royal Dutch Shell are shifting away from fossil fuel assets to expand their renewable energy footprints due to changing market dynamics and investor pressure. GE will focus on wind power generation, while Shell plans to build an end-to-end power business encompassing solar, wind, and storage, aiming for net-zero emissions by 2050. This strategic pivot reflects the decreasing cost of renewables and increased consumer demand, making such moves financially rational.

title: Reporter Russell Gold Warns Against a ‘Failure of Imagination’ in the Energy Sector
summary: Energy reporter Russell Gold discusses the "failure of imagination" in the energy sector, particularly in the context of PG&E's bankruptcy and the broader challenges faced by oil and gas companies in adapting to climate change. He emphasizes the importance of making energy reporting tangible to mainstream readers by connecting it to everyday consumer choices and highlights the differing approaches of European and U.S. oil majors to the energy transition. Gold expresses optimism about the future of energy, believing that existing technology and market forces can drive a significant shift towards a carbon-free electricity system within the next two decades.

title: New York sets minimum 3-year term for new load management programs to drive more energy storage
summary: New York's Public Service Commission has mandated a minimum three-year term for new dynamic load management (DLM) programs, aiming to incentivize energy storage development. This move addresses the previous bias towards short-term, low-capital solutions by providing longer-term contracts for capital-intensive projects like battery storage. The initiative is designed to help New York achieve its goal of procuring 1,500 MW of energy storage by 2025, while also accommodating other demand response resources.

title: BlackRock, Vanguard, Transamerica roll out latest ESG funds
summary: BlackRock, Vanguard, and Transamerica have launched new funds that incorporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) screens, catering to the increasing investor demand for sustainable investing options. These new ESG-focused funds, while slightly more expensive than traditional index funds, aim to provide targeted exposure to ESG objectives. By applying these screens, they alter the composition of standard indexes, leading to differences in holdings and potentially performance compared to their non-ESG counterparts.

title: BlackRock, Vanguard, Transamerica roll out latest ESG funds
summary: BlackRock, Vanguard, and Transamerica have launched new ESG funds to meet the growing investor demand for sustainable investing options. These funds apply ESG screens to traditional indexes, resulting in slightly higher costs and altered stock compositions compared to their non-ESG counterparts. For example, BlackRock's iShares ESG Screened S&P 500 ETF (XVV) removes companies like Exxon and Chevron from the standard S&P 500 index.

title: Athlete-turned-CEO wins Rainmaker race
summary: Jill Evanko, CEO of Chart Industries, won ExxonMobil's 2020 Power Play award for "Rainmaker" due to her dedication to clean energy and diversity. Evanko emphasizes the importance of diverse perspectives in driving innovation and transitioning to cleaner energy solutions, particularly in the evolving LNG industry. She believes her varied career background and athletic experience have provided her with a broad perspective to lead strategic transformation and advocate for greater inclusion in the sector.

title: Oil Refining
summary: Air Products offers extensive services and technologies to the oil refining industry, focusing on enhancing safety, efficiency, and environmental performance. They provide essential industrial gases like hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen, along with applications for gas separation, purification, and on-site generation. The company also emphasizes its leadership in low-carbon-intensity hydrogen production and carbon capture solutions to support refinery decarbonization efforts.

title: Oil and Gas
summary: Air Products offers over 50 years of experience and industrial gas services and technology to support the oil and gas industry. This includes nitrogen supply for well completion, large-scale nitrogen generation for enhanced oil recovery, and a range of gas supply options like bulk delivery, on-site generation, and temporary emergency services. The company provides a comprehensive network, service teams, and production technology to meet the diverse needs of the oil and gas sector.

title: Canadian government commits C$320 million to aid offshore oil industry
summary: The Canadian government has pledged C$320 million ($238.56 million) to support its offshore oil industry, which has been significantly impacted by reduced demand due to the coronavirus pandemic. Natural Resources Minister Seamus O'Regan announced the funds are intended to preserve jobs and can be utilized for maintenance, upgrades, and environmental services. This aid, however, falls short of the industry's full requests, which included government stakes in major projects and tax incentives.

title: BP Says Oil Is On The Ropes. Is It Really?
summary: BP and Shell are spearheading a significant shift among European oil giants by pledging to eliminate greenhouse gas emissions, reduce spending on traditional oil and gas projects, and invest heavily in renewables. This move has been met with mixed reactions in Houston, the U.S. energy capital, where some view it as a necessary evolution for economic growth while others remain skeptical about the quick demise of the oil industry. Despite these efforts and predictions of peak oil by 2030, the financial market has not yet responded positively to BP's new direction, and there's ongoing debate about whether these initiatives are genuine transformations or merely strategic asset divestments.

title: Insurer must represent Phillips 66 in trucker’s wrongful death lawsuit
summary: A federal court ruled that Canal Indemnity must defend Phillips 66 in a wrongful death lawsuit after denying the insurer's claims of a pollution exclusion. The lawsuit was filed by the family of a trucker, Elwyn Webb, who died of cancer allegedly caused by benzene exposure from the fuel he hauled. The court determined that Phillips 66 qualifies as an "additional insured" and that the pollution exclusion did not apply because the injury resulted from direct exposure to gasoline, not a dispersal or escape of pollutants.

title: Comunidad mapuche denuncia a YPF por contaminación y derrames en su territorio
summary: A Mapuche community, Lof Newen Kura, has filed a new complaint against YPF with the Environmental Crimes Prosecutor's Office in Neuquén, accusing the company of ongoing contamination and spills in their ancestral territory. They report over three thousand wells in their area and highlight recurrent incidents of hydrocarbon and chemical spills, which have led to animal deaths and economic hardship for the community. Despite prior acknowledgments of spills and recommendations for company closures, the community states that governmental control and remediation efforts have been insufficient.

title: ExxonMobil launches flagship PV and 2W service centres
summary: ExxonMobil Lubricants has launched flagship Mobil Bike Care Elite and Mobil Car Care Elite service centers in India in association with independent workshop owners. These centers will offer premium bike and car servicing experiences, providing expert maintenance recommendations, detailed inspections, and best-in-class quality lubricants. The initiative, starting in Bangalore and Delhi, aims to expand nationwide, enhancing customer engagement and providing trustworthy comprehensive car and bike care services.

title: ExxonMobil to Proceed with Payara Development Offshore Guyana
summary: ExxonMobil has received government approvals and made its final investment decision to proceed with the Payara field offshore development in Guyana. This marks the third project in the Stabroek Block, expected to commence production in 2024 with a capacity of 220,000 barrels of oil per day. The $9 billion development aims to target an estimated resource base of about 600 million oil-equivalent barrels, significantly increasing investment in the Guyanese economy and supporting local employment.

title: Insight: Nigeria's pioneering gas flaring plan risks going down in flames
summary: Nigeria's ambitious plan to eliminate gas flaring by 2030, a critical step towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions and providing much-needed electricity, is facing significant hurdles. Delays, a lack of commercial viability for many flare sites, and a "lack of trust" from potential bidders are undermining the government's efforts. Experts warn that without substantial investment and a more robust approach, Nigeria's pioneering initiative could fail, impacting both its climate goals and economic development.

title: Randall Ebner to Retire as General Counsel for Exxon Mobil Corporation; Craig Morford Elected as General Counsel and Corporate Vice President
summary: Randall Ebner, Exxon Mobil Corporation's vice president and general counsel, will retire on November 1, 2020, after over 40 years of service. Craig Morford, currently deputy general counsel, has been elected to succeed him. Morford brings extensive experience from the United States Department of Justice and private industry to his new role.

title: U.S. oil refiner Marathon Petroleum cuts 12% of staff because of pandemic
summary: Marathon Petroleum Corp, the largest U.S. oil refiner, is reducing its workforce by 12%, or 2,050 jobs, due to a continued decline in fuel consumption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The company expects to incur a charge of up to $175 million to third-quarter earnings as a result of these job cuts and refinery closures. This move is part of a broader trend of cost-cutting and layoffs across the oil industry amid weak prices and a global glut of fuel.

title: Exxon Mobil signals bigger-than-expected loss in third quarter
summary: Exxon Mobil is anticipating a larger-than-expected loss in the third quarter due to the ongoing pandemic-driven downturn in the energy sector. The company indicated potential earnings ranging from a loss of 68 cents to a profit of 7 cents per share, with the midpoint loss of 30 cents significantly wider than analysts' estimates. If this occurs, it would mark Exxon's third consecutive quarterly loss, a first in at least 36 years, despite expected boosts from higher crude prices and the chemicals business.

title: RBC announces new restrictions on financing coal, oil developments
summary: RBC, Canada’s largest bank, has announced new restrictions on financing for certain fossil fuel developments, including new coal-fired power generators, thermal coal mines, and mountaintop removal coal mines. The bank will also require special committee approval for financing Arctic oil exploration and will not fund drilling in Alaska’s Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. While environmental groups praised the move for the Arctic refuge, critics note that RBC remains a major financier of fossil fuels overall.

title: Suncor Energy to cut staff by up to 15% over next year and a half
summary: Suncor Energy has announced plans to cut up to 15% of its workforce over the next year and a half due to the global pandemic, economic slowdown, and slumping oil prices. The Calgary-based company, which had 13,000 employees at the end of 2019, will implement the first 5% of layoffs within six months. This decision reflects a broader trend in the energy sector towards efficiency and cost reduction, prompting concern from Alberta's Premier about the economic emergency while the NDP leader criticized corporate tax cuts.

title: Oil loses 4% after Trump gets coronavirus and economies wobble
summary: Oil prices fell more than 4% on Friday, marking a second weekly decline, after U.S. President Donald Trump tested positive for COVID-19, causing market jitters. The drop was also attributed to a weak U.S. unemployment report and rising global crude output threatening the market's recovery. Both Brent and U.S. crude benchmarks saw significant weekly losses as increased supply from OPEC members and U.S. energy firms further weighed on prices.

title: Noble Energy shareholders approve $4.1 billion sale to Chevron
summary: Noble Energy shareholders have approved the company's $4.1 billion sale to Chevron Corp, making Chevron the second-largest U.S. shale oil producer and expanding its international natural gas reserves. The all-stock deal also includes $8 billion in debt assumed by Chevron and represents the first major energy deal since the global fuel demand was impacted by the coronavirus pandemic. Despite the deal's approval, only 60% of shareholders voted in favor of merger-related executive payouts, following recommendations against "excessive" executive payments.

title: How NextEra Overtook ExxonMobil As The Largest U.S. Energy Company
summary: NextEra Energy surpassed ExxonMobil in market capitalization, highlighting a significant shift in the U.S. energy sector. This divergence is attributed to NextEra's aggressive investment in renewable energy and strong financial performance, contrasted with ExxonMobil's struggles due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on energy demand. The article details how NextEra's strategy, particularly its focus on wind and solar power, has led to exceptional returns, positioning it as a leading energy company.

title: Extent of contamination from former Regina refinery site still unknown 45 years after shutdown
summary: The Saskatchewan Ministry of Environment admits it still does not know the full extent of contamination from an Imperial Oil refinery in Regina that closed 45 years ago. Critics lambaste the government's voluntary approach to environmental oversight, arguing it has allowed Imperial Oil to dictate assessment timelines, leading to significant gaps in understanding the site's impact on human health and the environment. Property owners have filed a class-action lawsuit, alleging Imperial Oil and the City of Regina concealed information about the contamination, which has stalled due to roadblocks and lack of funds.

title: Exxon to cut 1,600 jobs across Europe as oil rout weighs
summary: U.S. oil giant Exxon Mobil announced plans to reduce its European workforce by up to 1,600 employees across its affiliates by the end of 2021 as part of a global review. This decision comes as the COVID-19 pandemic has severely impacted demand for its products and caused crude prices to tank, forcing oil majors to cut jobs and spending. Exxon previously announced voluntary layoffs in Australia, indicating global job cuts would continue into 2021.

title: Payara Field Development Project, Stabroek Block, Guyana
summary: The Payara Field Development Project is the third oil field to be developed in the Stabroek Block offshore Guyana, operated by Esso Exploration and Production Guyana (EEPGL), a subsidiary of Exxon Mobil. With an estimated investment of approximately $9 billion, the project is expected to commence production in 2024 and produce up to 220,000 barrels of oil per day. The development involves 41 wells tied to the Prosperity FPSO, similar to previous Liza developments in the block.

title: Wind and solar producer tops Exxon as most valuable U.S. energy company
summary: NextEra Energy, a wind and solar power producer, eclipsed ExxonMobil to become the most valuable U.S. energy company with a value of $143.8 billion. This milestone highlights the significant shift towards clean energy, contrasting with Exxon's declining value and stock performance. NextEra's growth is driven by high profit margins and investor confidence in renewable energy, despite government policies favoring fossil fuels.

title: Equinor committing to the Sea Cargo Charter – for more transparent reporting of shipping activity to reach decarbonisation targets
summary: Equinor has joined the Sea Cargo Charter, an initiative by major companies like Shell and Total, to enhance transparency in reporting shipping activity's climate alignment. This commitment aims to drive decarbonization efforts in the maritime industry, which accounts for 2-3% of global greenhouse gas emissions. By collaborating and disclosing environmental performance, Equinor and its partners seek to meet the UN's International Maritime Organization ambitions and achieve their own maritime climate targets for 2030 and 2050.

title: ExxonMobil Loses $225 Billion In Market Cap Against Chevron
summary: ExxonMobil's market capitalization has significantly declined, losing $225 billion against Chevron, leading to its replacement by NextEra Energy as the largest U.S. energy company. While both companies faced a tough decade, Chevron's strategic decisions and fewer missteps allowed it to better maintain its value and dividend payments compared to ExxonMobil's costly acquisitions and struggles. Despite ExxonMobil's brief bounce back, its enterprise value remains comfortably ahead of Chevron and NextEra, indicating its total asset value.

title: Petronas spuds keenly watched Suriname wildcat
summary: Petronas has started drilling a highly anticipated wildcat well in Suriname, hoping to join other companies in making significant discoveries in the region. The Malaysian giant is using the semi-submersible Maersk Developer for this exploration effort.

title: Personnel Moves: ExxonMobil VP and General Counsel To Retire
summary: Randall Ebner, VP and General Counsel for Exxon Mobil Corp., is retiring, and Craig Morford will succeed him. This article also details several other significant personnel changes across various companies in the Dallas area, including new hires and promotions at Dallas Area Habitat for Humanity, DuWest Realty, Augustine Agency, OneDay, Imaginuity, Fermata Energy, HudsonLake, and Agents National Title Insurance.

title: Northern Lights is innovating for the future of carbon transport and storage
summary: The article details the Northern Lights project, a partnership between the Norwegian government, Equinor, Shell, and Total, focused on scaling carbon capture and storage (CCS) across Europe. Microsoft has joined the project as a technology partner to integrate its digital expertise and explore the use of the Northern Lights facility as part of its own carbon capture projects. The initiative aims to create a permanent storage solution for CO2 in the North Sea and develop a new business ecosystem around carbon management to achieve a net-zero carbon future.

title: Argentine gas companies plan to invest US$400mn in pipeline expansions
summary: Argentine gas companies Transportadora de Gas del Norte (TGN) and Transportadora de Gas del Sur (TGS) are planning to invest around US$400mn to expand pipeline capacity from the Vaca Muerta formation and southern provinces. The companies are in discussions with gas regulator Enargas regarding details like fee collection and loan repayment. The government plans to utilize equipment acquired in 2015 for previous expansion efforts to reduce investment costs.

title: U.S. oil majors pitch more campaign cash to Democrats as frack battle looms
summary: U.S. oil majors Chevron Corp and Exxon Mobil Corp have increased their campaign donations to Democrats for the current election cycle, amidst a looming battle over fracking and concerns about renewable energy policies. This shift comes despite the vast majority of oil and gas donations still favoring Republican candidates and conservative causes. The article highlights the strategic donations by energy companies as Democratic challenger Joseph Biden gains ground with an agenda focused on renewable energy and an end to new fracking permits on federal lands.

title: ConocoPhillips Adopts Paris-Aligned Climate Risk Framework to Meet Net-Zero Operational Emissions Ambition by 2050
summary: ConocoPhillips has adopted a comprehensive Paris-aligned climate risk framework to guide its management of climate-related risks and stakeholder expectations through the energy transition. The company has set an ambition to achieve net-zero operational emissions by 2050 and revised its greenhouse gas emissions intensity reduction target to 35-45% by 2030. This strategy also aims to meet global energy demand sustainably and deliver competitive returns by focusing on cost of supply and utilizing a scenario-based strategic planning process.

title: ConocoPhillips to Buy Shale Rival Concho for $9.7 Billion
summary: ConocoPhillips has announced its acquisition of Concho Resources Inc. for $9.7 billion in an all-stock deal, signifying the largest U.S. oil transaction since the beginning of the pandemic. This acquisition expands ConocoPhillips' presence in the Permian Basin and makes the combined entity the largest U.S. oil independent producer. The move reflects a broader trend of consolidation in the U.S. oil industry as companies navigate low prices and weak demand.

title: HPE Office Project Tops Out in Springwoods Village in North Houston
summary: Construction has topped out on Hewlett Packard Enterprise's new campus in Springwoods Village, North Houston, a joint venture between Patrinely Group, USAA Real Estate, and CDC Houston. The campus, set for completion in Spring 2022, will consist of two five-story buildings totaling 440,000 square feet and will be the fifth major corporation in the master-planned community. The development emphasizes a high-quality, walkable, mixed-use environment and aims for LEED Silver certification.

title: HP Enterprise campus in north Houston reaches construction milestone
summary: Construction has topped out on Hewlett Packard Enterprise's new campus in Springwoods Village, north Houston. The campus features two five-story buildings totaling 440,000 square feet and is expected to open in Spring 2022. This milestone was celebrated by the Patrinely Group, USAA Real Estate, and CDC Houston joint venture, highlighting their continued confidence in CityPlace as a significant mixed-use destination.

title: ConocoPhillips to buy Concho Resources for $9.7 billion in 2020's top shale deal
summary: ConocoPhillips announced its acquisition of Permian-focused driller Concho Resources for $9.7 billion, marking the largest shale deal of 2020. This all-stock, low-premium transaction reflects a trend of consolidation within the energy sector as companies grapple with weak crude prices and high debts amid the Covid-19 pandemic. The acquisition will significantly expand ConocoPhillips' presence in the Permian Basin and position it as the largest U.S. independent oil producer.

title: ConocoPhillips Doubles Down On The Permian Basin And Fracking With Concho Acquisition
summary: ConocoPhillips announced its acquisition of Concho Resources for $9.7 billion in an all-stock transaction, marking the largest U.S. shale-focused deal of 2020. This acquisition significantly expands ConocoPhillips' Permian Basin holdings, aiming for annual cost savings and a strong asset base below $30 per barrel WTI. The move signals strong confidence in the future of U.S. shale despite industry headwinds and political uncertainties.

title: Chevron and Exxon boost campaign donations to Democrats
summary: Chevron Corp (CVX.N) and Exxon Mobil Corp (XOM.N), the two largest US energy firms, have increased their share of campaign donations to Democrats in 2020, according to recent filings. This represents a strategic shift for these oil giants, as Joe Biden leads in the polls, leading them to diversify political contributions beyond their traditional Republican support. Despite this, the majority of fossil fuel donations still overwhelmingly favor Republican and conservative groups.

title: Exxon Mobil, after Trump's fundraising remarks, says its CEO and Trump had no phone call
summary: Exxon Mobil clarified that no phone call occurred between its CEO, Darren Woods, and then-President Donald Trump, despite Trump's remarks at a rally where he implied he could easily raise significant campaign funds by calling oil and Wall Street executives. Trump had created a hypothetical scenario of calling the head of Exxon to solicit $25 million for his campaign. The clarification came as Trump was trailing his Democratic rival, Joe Biden, in both opinion polls and fundraising during the 2020 election campaign.

title: Exxon Turns to Academia to Try to Discredit Harvard Research
summary: ExxonMobil is attempting to discredit a 2017 Harvard research paper that concluded the company misled the public about climate change. Exxon's Vice President of Research and Development published a comment in Environmental Research Letters alleging methodological flaws, but the original Harvard authors, Supran and Oreskes, published a reply refuting these claims and citing new documents that further support their initial findings. This ongoing dispute highlights Exxon's consistent efforts to challenge criticisms of its climate history.

title: Exxon Mobil to workers: Job cuts are coming
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced job cuts due to low oil prices and the impact of COVID-19 on global fuel demand, forcing delays in major projects. CEO Darren Woods stated these are difficult times requiring tough decisions to make the organization more efficient. This move follows similar struggles among other U.S. energy producers and comes after Exxon slashed its capital spending budget.

title: |‘Tenuous’ stability emerges as oil-field services firms cut losses
summary: |Oil-field services giants like Halliburton, Schlumberger, and Baker Hughes are seeing losses shrink in the third quarter of 2020, signaling a "tenuous" stability for the sector after significant cost-cutting and job losses. Despite this improvement, the recovery is expected to be slow, with oil demand potentially remaining below pre-pandemic levels until 2023 due to the ongoing impact of COVID-19. Analysts and CEOs note a slight increase in drilling activity and stable crude prices around $40 per barrel, but warn that the rebound remains fragile.

title: U.S. oil giant Exxon set to announce layoffs in Canada
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is nearing the completion of workforce appraisals in the United States and Canada and plans to announce job cuts, as disclosed by its chief executive in an email to employees. The company has faced significant financial losses, including nearly $1.7 billion US in the first half of the fiscal year, and is implementing cuts to increase competitiveness amidst a COVID-19 induced decline in oil demand. Despite these measures, the CEO stated that further reductions are necessary due to ongoing significant headwinds.

title: ExxonMobil plans to Layoff 1,600 staff
summary: ExxonMobil announced plans to lay off an unspecified number of employees globally, with a specific focus on 1,600 in Europe, as low oil prices force the company to delay major projects. CEO Darren Woods defended the company's focus on fossil fuels, despite a significant drop in stock value and industry-wide struggles. The company, which normally produces about 500,000 barrels of crude per day, is making efforts to increase efficiency while maintaining its long-term investment strategy in traditional energy sources.

title: Exxon Mobil 'very close' to disclosing US job cuts
summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods announced that the company is "very close" to completing workforce appraisals in the U.S. and Canada, with job cuts expected to be unveiled soon. These reductions are part of a plan to increase competitiveness and respond to a "devastating impact" on oil demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic, which has significantly strained the company's finances and dividend obligations.

title: Alberta to scrap oil production limits in December with demand for heavy oil poised to rise
summary: The Alberta government announced it will cease setting monthly oil production limits in December, opting instead to extend its regulatory authority to curtail production through December 2021 without actively imposing limits. This decision is based on sustained lower production levels and aims to stabilize the resource sector for investor confidence while retaining the ability to reintroduce limits if storage capacity becomes an issue. Canadian oil prices are expected to strengthen in 2021 as demand for heavy oil rises and Mexican heavy crude exports to the U.S. Gulf Coast decline.

title: Stock Wars: ExxonMobil Vs. NextEra, A Battle Of Old Vs. New In Energy
summary: This article examines the shift in the energy sector with NextEra Energy Inc. surpassing ExxonMobil in market capitalization, highlighting a battle between old fossil fuel companies and new clean energy providers. It compares the financials and stock performance of both companies, noting ExxonMobil's declining value and NextEra's significant growth, especially in the context of increasing clean energy investments.

title: ExxonMobil Deploys QR Codes And NFC Tags for Streamlined Mobile Payment at the Pump
summary: ExxonMobil is implementing QR codes and NFC tags at over 11,500 U.S. stations to enable streamlined mobile payments with Apple Pay and Google Pay. This system leverages Apple App Clips for iPhone users without the ExxonMobil app and provides a web-based solution for Android users, enhancing contactless payment options at the pump. The initiative is part of ExxonMobil's ongoing efforts to innovate and offer secure, convenient payment methods, building on prior contactless payment solutions like "Alexa, Pay for Gas."

title: Cenovus and Husky combine to create a resilient integrated energy leader
summary: Cenovus Energy Inc. and Husky Energy Inc. are combining in an all-stock transaction valued at $23.6 billion, including debt, to form a new integrated Canadian oil and natural gas company. The merger is expected to generate $1.2 billion in annual synergies, largely within the first year, enhance free funds flow, and support an investment-grade credit profile. The combined entity will become the third-largest Canadian oil and natural gas producer and the second-largest Canadian-based refiner and upgrader, with a focus on ESG leadership and achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.

title: Rival Canadian Company Agrees To Buy Husky Energy In $2.9B Deal
summary: Cenovus Energy Inc. has agreed to acquire Husky Energy in a $2.9 billion deal, combining two major Canadian oil companies. This consolidation comes as the oil sector faces significant challenges due to the coronavirus pandemic, leading to a global decline in fuel demand. Husky Energy, which owns Wisconsin's only oil refinery in Superior, had previously cut capital spending on the refinery's rebuild following a 2018 explosion.

title: Exclusive: GM, Ford knew about climate change 50 years ago
summary: A monthslong investigation by E&E News reveals that scientists at General Motors and Ford Motor Co. knew as early as the 1960s that car emissions caused climate change. Despite this internal knowledge, both companies engaged in decades of political lobbying to undermine efforts to reduce emissions and invested heavily in gas-guzzling vehicles while financially supporting groups that cast doubt on climate science. The transportation sector, largely driven by cars and trucks, remains the leading source of planet-warming pollution in the United States today.

title: Focus: Chevron bets on Middle East gas riches and reconciliation
summary: Chevron is strategically shifting its natural gas focus to the Middle East, betting on regional reconciliation to capitalize on growing demand for cleaner fuels. This move, highlighted by their acquisition of Noble Energy and its stake in Israel's Leviathan field, signifies a pivot away from U.S. shale and an investment in an area with significant gas reserves despite existing political risks. The company aims to supply gas to Europe and Asia, where demand for natural gas as a complement to renewables is projected to rise.

title: France’s Engie Delays Finalizing U.S. LNG Deal With NextDecade Over Emissions Concerns
summary: French energy company Engie SA has indefinitely postponed a long-term deal to purchase liquefied natural gas (LNG) from NextDecade Corp.'s proposed Rio Grande LNG facility in Texas. The delay is due to concerns from the French government regarding hydraulic fracturing (fracking) and its environmental implications, which are not aligned with Engie's goals for reducing emissions and transitioning to carbon-neutral solutions. While NextDecade plans to use carbon capture technology to reduce on-site emissions, critics argue this does not address emissions from the fracking process itself, complicating the future of the multi-billion dollar project.

title: BP Posts Fifth Straight Quarterly Loss
summary: BP PLC reported its fifth consecutive quarterly loss, struggling with reduced demand and lower refining margins exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic. Despite oil prices stabilizing at around $40 a barrel in the third quarter, they remained significantly lower than the previous year. This loss follows a difficult second quarter where BP halved its dividend and cut jobs.

title: How NextEra became America’s most valuable energy company
summary: NextEra has emerged as America's most valuable energy company, surpassing traditional oil giants, by strategically transitioning towards natural gas and renewables. This shift, driven by declining costs for wind and solar and government mandates, has proven highly prescient and profitable. The company's focus on utility operations and significant investments in renewable energy infrastructure have solidified its leading position in the evolving energy landscape.

title: Exxon Mobil to keep dividend flat for first time since 1982
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced it would keep its fourth-quarter dividend flat at 87 cents per share, marking the first time since 1982 that the U.S. oil producer has not raised its shareholder payout. The decision comes amidst sharp declines in energy prices and demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to projected full-year losses for the company. While the dividend is maintained for now, analysts express doubts about its long-term sustainability if demand doesn't fully recover.

title: Imperial Oil commissions cogeneration unit at Strathcona refinery
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. has commissioned a new cogeneration unit at its Strathcona refinery in Alberta, aiming to enhance energy efficiency and reduce provincial greenhouse gas emissions. The unit generates approximately 41 Mw/day of electricity, covering 75-80% of the refinery's power needs and decreasing GHG emissions by about 112,000 tpy. This is Imperial's third cogeneration unit in Alberta, contributing to broader emissions reductions across its operations.

title: Guyana a low-cost oil supplier, as world still needs almost 50 percent oil and gas energy – Hess
summary: Hess Corporation views Guyana as a crucial low-cost oil supplier, anticipating that oil and gas will continue to constitute nearly 50% of the world's energy mix for the next three decades, even with a global push for renewable energy. The company highlighted Guyana's advantageous operating costs in the Stabroek Block, enabling a breakeven price under US$40 per barrel Brent.
