Hess also announced that the Payara Field development, the third project in the Stabroek Block, has been approved and is targeted for first oil in 2024, contributing to the consortium's goal of producing over 750,000 gross barrels of oil per day by 2026.

title: Exxon to cut 14,000 jobs as pandemic hits oil demand
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced plans to cut approximately 15% of its global workforce, amounting to about 14,000 jobs, due to the severe impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on energy demand and prices. This includes deep white-collar staff reductions in the United States, following more than $10 billion in budget cuts this year. Other major oil companies like Royal Dutch Shell, BP, and Chevron are also implementing significant workforce reductions.

title: Job cut nation: Exxon Mobil to lay off 1,900 US employees
summary: Exxon Mobil announced it would lay off about 1,900 employees in the United States, primarily from its Houston, Texas office, due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on energy demand and prices. The company has been cutting costs, promising to shed over $10 billion in project spending and reduce operating expenses by 15 percent, after significant losses earlier in the year. Despite the layoffs and financial challenges, Exxon confirmed it would maintain its quarterly shareholder dividend payments.

title: ExxonMobil to cut 14,000 global jobs as Covid-19 pandemic hurts energy demand
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced plans to cut approximately 14,000 global jobs, including contractors, which accounts for about 15% of its workforce, due to the severe impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on energy demand and prices. The job cuts are part of a global reorganisation and come after the company reported significant losses in the first half of the year. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other major energy companies like Royal Dutch Shell, BP, and Chevron.

title: Devon’s Permian Oil Output Climbs, Anadarko Growth Eyed as Natural Gas Prices Climb
summary: Devon Energy Corp. has increased its full-year 2020 oil production forecast and reduced exploration costs, largely due to strong performance in the Permian Basin's Delaware sub-basin. The company also announced a merger with WPX Energy Inc. and is considering resuming activity in the Anadarko Basin due to improved natural gas prices. Despite net losses totaling $92 million in Q3 2020, Devon generated $223 million in free cash flow, improved its cost structure, and plans to deliver improved output with less capital.

title: Dwindling Oil Demand: 14,000 ExxonMobil staff to lose jobs
summary: ExxonMobil is set to cut its global workforce by 15%, equating to about 14,000 employees and contractors, over the next two years. This decision comes as the COVID-19 pandemic has severely impacted global crude oil demand and prices, leading major oil producers like Shell, Chevron, and BP to also announce significant job reductions. The cuts are part of CEO Darren Woods' efforts to curtail spending and address the company's recent quarterly losses.

title: Convert to Natural Gas
summary: This article from National Fuel Gas Company promotes converting to natural gas for WNY Residences. It highlights the benefits of natural gas, including its affordability, efficiency, reliability, environmental advantages (less pollution), and its ability to add value to homes. The company provides options for both new and existing customers to convert.

title: BW Energy Buys Two Borr Drilling Rigs for Gabon Offshore Developments
summary: BW Energy has acquired two jack-up drilling rigs, "Atla" and "Balder", from Borr Drilling for $14.5 million to develop its Hibiscus/Ruche satellite field offshore Gabon. This conversion approach is expected to reduce capital investments by approximately $100 million and significantly lower CO2 emissions compared to newbuild platforms. The strategy also aims to decrease the cash-break even oil price for the development to about $25 per barrel Brent and the overall production cost for the Dussafu license to $11 per barrel.

title: Exxon’s climate fix is algae. Experts say it won’t work
summary: Exxon Mobil has invested in algae-based biofuels for over a decade, promoting it as a solution for climate change and reduced emissions, particularly for commercial transportation. However, experts and critics largely dismiss this as "greenwashing," arguing the technology is too expensive and impractical for large-scale fuel production, especially compared to Exxon's continued massive investments in oil and gas extraction. The company's spending on algae research pales in comparison to its advertising budget, and other major oil companies are pursuing different renewable strategies.

title: Underwater Pioneer Lad Handelman Dies at Santa Barbara Home
summary: Lad Handelman, a pioneer in deep-water diving and offshore oilfield construction, passed away at his Santa Barbara home on October 26. He began his career as an abalone diver and went on to found California Divers, which evolved into Oceaneering International. Handelman was also known for his philanthropic efforts, including marine preservation and support for those with spinal injuries, and despite a debilitating accident, continued to lead his company and contribute to various causes.

title: U.S. assures Eni repairs to Venezuela oil facility not barred by sanctions
summary: The United States has informed Italian oil company Eni SpA that its efforts to repair a tilting floating crude facility, Nabarima, in Venezuela and offload its oil would not be penalized by U.S. sanctions. This assurance comes after concerns of a potential environmental disaster due to the FSO's instability. Eni plans to proceed with repairs and offloading once approval from Venezuela's state oil company, PDVSA, is secured.

title: Nine takeaways from BP's shock closure of its Kwinana refinery
summary: BP's unexpected decision to close its Kwinana oil refinery after 65 years will significantly impact Western Australia's economy, particularly workers and related industries, though BP itself is expected to fare well. The closure, driven by low refining margins, will reduce 400 staff jobs to 60 as the site converts to an import terminal, and will force businesses reliant on Kwinana's products to find new suppliers. While fuel prices are not expected to rise, the move highlights the uncertain future of Australia's remaining refineries and raises questions about national fuel security.

title: US regulators accuse Singapore energy trader of Iran sanctions breach
summary: US authorities have sanctioned a Singapore-based energy trader, Jiaxiang Energy Holding, accusing it of breaching restrictions on trade with Iran by purchasing oil worth millions of dollars. Five Chinese companies were also sanctioned for facilitating payments for these banned petroleum sales. The US government asserts that these actions are part of its commitment to targeting revenue sources the Iranian regime uses to fund terrorist groups and oppress its people, operating under its secondary sanctions regime.

title: TransAlta to stop mining coal at Highvale near Edmonton, stop using coal in Canada
summary: TransAlta Corp. announced it will cease operations at its Highvale thermal coal mine near Edmonton by the end of 2021 and accelerate its switch to natural gas at all Canadian coal-fired plants, four years ahead of schedule. This move will result in hundreds of job losses at the mine, Canada's largest, as the company responds to rising carbon taxes and aims for significant greenhouse gas emission reductions. The decision was not influenced by a recent investment from Brookfield Asset Management but by the changing economics of coal power in Alberta.

title: Hundreds of coal mining jobs to end as TransAlta switches to natural gas
summary: TransAlta Corp. announced it will end operations at its Highvale thermal coal mine by the end of 2021, four years earlier than planned, as it transitions to natural gas for all its Canadian coal-fired plants. This decision will result in hundreds of job losses, though 40 to 50 people will remain for reclamation work expected to last about 20 years. The company cites the economics of producing power from coal with the carbon tax as a primary driver for the accelerated transition.

title: Colombia Inches Closer to Becoming Second South American Nation to Use Fracking
summary: Colombia is moving forward with hydraulic fracturing (fracking) pilot projects, with contracts for four projects in the Middle Magdalena and Cesar Ranchería basins to be awarded by the end of November. This initiative aims to assess the technical, operational, and environmental aspects of fracking in the country, potentially making Colombia the second South American nation after Argentina to use the technique commercially. Companies like ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips, and Ecopetrol SA have expressed interest, with drilling expected to begin by late 2021 to inform a definitive government policy.

title: ConocoPhillips bets on crude-by-rail, despite progress on pipeline expansions
summary: ConocoPhillips is investing in crude-by-rail with a 10-year agreement for a new 50,000 bbl/day diluent recovery unit (DRU) at Hardisty, despite current pipeline expansions. This project, a joint venture between Gibson Energy and USD Group, aims to process diluted bitumen (dilbit) into DRUbit™, making rail transport safer and more cost-effective. While crude-by-rail exports have recently fallen due to narrow differentials, this investment anticipates a future increase in heavy oil production and rail demand, with the DRU expected to be operational by mid-2021.

title: Enbridge Wins Natural Gas Pipeline Duel with TC Over Traffic to LNG Canada
summary: Enbridge Inc. has secured a victory in a pipeline dispute with TC Energy Corp. after the Canada Energy Regulator (CER) approved a C$25 million ($19 million) flow meter for Enbridge’s Westcoast network. This approval allows Enbridge to relay up to 1.2 Bcf/d into the supply artery for the Shell-led LNG Canada project, solidifying its position to serve the first Canadian liquefied natural gas export terminal on the Pacific coast. The CER's decision favored open competition in the Montney Shale region and dismissed TC's demand for an inquiry into the effects of Enbridge's gain on Western Canadian pipeline traffic and tolls.

title: Tim McKay says conditions right for consolidation as Canadian Natural reports $408M profit
summary: Tim McKay, president of Canadian Natural Resources Ltd., believes conditions are ripe for further merger and acquisition activity in the Canadian oil and gas sector. The company reported a third-quarter profit of $408 million and plans to increase investment in natural gas drilling. This strategy serves as a hedge against oilsands operation costs and addresses lower oil prices experienced earlier in the year.

title: Kirby gets energized by alternative energy
summary: Kirby Corp, traditionally associated with fossil fuels, is shifting its business focus towards alternative and clean energy solutions due to "demand destruction" from COVID-19 and a growing emphasis on decarbonization and ESG factors. The company plans to expand its involvement in transporting alternative fuels, building electric-powered fracturing units, and supporting offshore wind projects to generate new revenues and maintain growth despite declines in traditional markets.

title: Shell to Close Gulf Coast Refinery
summary: Royal Dutch Shell will close its 53-year-old Convent refinery in Louisiana, a move affecting approximately 675 employees. This shutdown is part of Shell's broader strategy to reduce its global refining portfolio from 14 to six integrated oil refining and chemical plants by 2025, focusing on sites strategically positioned for a low-carbon future. The decision comes amidst a trend of refinery closures in the U.S. and a decline in global demand and profits due to Covid-19.

title: Ralph Cunningham Obituary - Houston, TX
summary: Ralph S. Cunningham Sr. passed away on November 7, 2020, at the age of 80 in Houston, Texas. He was a distinguished chemical engineer with a long career in the energy industry, holding executive positions at companies like Exxon and Huntsman Corporation, and serving on several company boards. Cunningham was remembered for his brilliant mind, compassionate heart, deep faith, generosity, and strong devotion to his family and various organizations.

title: TD's Ambitious Climate Action Plan
summary: TD has unveiled an ambitious Climate Action Plan aiming for net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from its operations and financing activities by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement. The plan includes establishing GHG baselines, working with clients on interim reduction goals, and creating a Sustainable Finance and Corporate Transitions Group. TD also committed to not providing financial services for new oil and gas exploration within the Arctic Circle.

title: Comstock Ramps Haynesville Activity in Anticipation of Higher Natural Gas Prices
summary: Comstock Resources Inc. is increasing its activity in the Haynesville Shale, adding two drilling rigs and accelerating well completions, in anticipation of higher natural gas prices. The company aims to capitalize on increased LNG exports and a recovery in natural gas prices following a warm winter and low production levels. Despite a challenging third quarter with a net loss due to hedging, Comstock expects to boost capital spending and production to take advantage of improved market conditions in early 2021.

title: Terrestrial Energy / Company Begins Testing Of IMSR Fuel Salt
summary: Terrestrial Energy USA and Argonne National Laboratory have initiated detailed testing of the Integral Molten Salt Reactor (IMSR) fuel salt, a crucial step for the Generation IV advanced nuclear power plant's licensing applications. This testing program supports broader confirmatory evaluations of the IMSR's fuel, components, and systems. Terrestrial Energy aims to deploy the 195-MW IMSR, which operates at high temperatures and uses low-enriched uranium, in the late 2020s, with a joint technical review already underway by Canadian and US nuclear safety commissions.

title: ExxonMobil’s Failure to Go Green Could Worsen Its Financial Future
summary: ExxonMobil is facing significant financial difficulties, including substantial quarterly losses and removal from the Dow Jones Industrial Average, primarily due to its reluctance to embrace renewable energy like its competitors. While other major oil companies are investing in green alternatives, Exxon has stubbornly maintained its focus on fossil fuels, despite falling oil prices and increasing pressure from investors and policymakers concerned about climate change. This resistance to change is putting the company's long-term financial future at risk and has led to a rethinking of how oil companies are valued.

title: Rising Market Cap Fuels Acquisition Ambitions For US Renewable Energy Firms
summary: The rising market capitalization of US renewable energy firms like NextEra Energy is fueling their acquisition ambitions, allowing them to use stock to purchase competitors. This trend highlights the growing momentum in the renewable energy sector compared to traditional energy giants. The article also touches upon the potential for similar developments in India, despite differences in capital market access for renewable developers.

title: Awarding Bacalhau drilling and well services contracts
summary: Equinor, on behalf of its partners ExxonMobil and Petrogal Brasil, awarded drilling and well services contracts for the Bacalhau field in Brazil to Baker Hughes, Halliburton, and Schlumberger. These contracts, totaling an estimated USD 455 million, aim to ensure safe and efficient operations and will significantly contribute to local content in Brazil, with an average of 74% local content. The Bacalhau field is a key asset for Equinor in Brazil, with a final investment decision planned for 2021 and first oil production expected in 2024.

title: Bayer’s shady PR firms: FleishmanHillard, Ketchum, FTI Consulting
summary: This article exposes the "shady" tactics of PR firms like FleishmanHillard, Ketchum, and FTI Consulting, which have represented Bayer/Monsanto, the tobacco industry, and the oil industry. It details instances of deception, including creating "watch lists" of influential individuals, impersonating journalists, and orchestrating campaigns to discredit critics and promote glyphosate and GMOs. The article highlights how these firms, despite their controversial histories, continue to be hired for image rehabilitation and crisis management by major corporations.

title: Woodside sticks with Pluto-2 plan to save costs, time
summary: Woodside Petroleum is moving forward with its $16 billion Pluto-2 LNG production train plan, asserting it will save 30% in capital costs and offer the quickest route to market. This decision rejects suggestions to process gas from the Scarborough field at the existing North West Shelf plant, which Woodside deems less cost-efficient. The company will detail its cost savings and emissions reduction targets in an upcoming investor briefing.

title: SOCAR-KBR JV Nearly Done with ACE Platform Work
summary: The SOCAR-KBR joint venture is nearing completion of its engineering design work for the Azeri Central East (ACE) platform in the Caspian Sea. This $6 billion project, operated by BP, involves a new 48-slot production platform and is notable for fully utilizing KBR's Digital Twin technology throughout its design phases. The technology is expected to enhance efficiency during fabrication, commissioning, and operations, allowing for remote task execution.

title: Eni and HitecVision form Nordic renewable energy venture
summary: Italian energy company Eni and Norwegian private equity group HitecVision have established a joint venture named Vaargroenn to develop renewable energy projects in the Nordic region. The venture, 69.6% owned by Eni, aims to install 1 gigawatt of electricity capacity by 2030, initially focusing on offshore wind in Norway. This initiative is part of Eni's broader decarbonization strategy, building on their existing cooperation in oil through the Vaar Energi joint venture.

title: How One Firm Drove Influence Campaigns Nationwide for Big Oil (Published 2020)
summary: FTI Consulting, a global firm, designed and ran numerous influence campaigns nationwide for major oil and gas companies, often obscuring their involvement. These campaigns created seemingly grass-roots movements and websites like Texans for Natural Gas and the Arctic Energy Center to promote fossil fuels and counter climate activism. FTI also monitored environmental activists and created fake online personas, with former employees revealing that content from sites like Energy In Depth was directed by clients such as Exxon Mobil.

title: Woodside Stops Talks to Sell Offshore Project Stake to Chinese Firms over Diplomatic Row
summary: Woodside Energy halted discussions to sell stakes in a gas field and LNG project to Chinese companies due to the ongoing diplomatic tensions between Australia and China. CEO Peter Coleman expressed disappointment but hopes to revive talks once relations improve, noting that existing partnerships with Chinese companies in other regions remain unaffected. The diplomatic row has impacted various Australian exports but has not yet affected LNG shipments to China, according to research.

title: Sour China-Australia ties hit talks over LNG deal, says Woodside
summary: Australian LNG producer Woodside Petroleum halted talks with Chinese firms, including PetroChina, to sell stakes in a gas field and LNG project due to deteriorating diplomatic relations between China and Australia. CEO Peter Coleman expressed hope to restart discussions when the diplomatic spat subsides. The diplomatic row, triggered by Australia's call for an international inquiry into the coronavirus origin, has also led to China halting timber imports from Victoria and increasing customs inspections on other Australian products.

title: Double, double oil and trouble as layoff axe falls on Jurong Island
summary: US oil giant Chevron is reportedly planning to cut at least 10% of its jobs in Singapore, following Shell's announcement of 500 job cuts in the region. This move is part of Chevron's global strategy to reduce operating costs and capital investments by trimming 10-15% of its workforce. These layoffs reflect the ongoing challenges faced by big oil companies in Singapore amidst global economic shifts.

title: Former Alaska Governor’s New Company Aiming to Move North Slope LNG to Market
summary: Former Alaska Governor Bill Walker has launched a new company, Alaska Gasline & LNG LLC, to pursue the construction of a large volume pipeline for exporting North Slope natural gas. The company reportedly aims to acquire the state's proposed liquefied natural gas (LNG) project, which the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corp. (AGDC) took over in 2016. Walker is listed as the registered agent and an organizer for the newly incorporated company, which includes former Cheniere Energy executive Keith Meyer among its members.

title: Sasol wraps up $12.8B petrochemical complex in Lake Charles
Increasing capacity on Johan Sverdrup to half a million barrels of oil per day
summary: Equinor and its partners are increasing the daily production capacity of the Johan Sverdrup field to approximately 500,000 barrels of oil per day by the end of 2020, following positive test results. This expansion exceeds the original projections and highlights the field's high profitability, low CO2 emissions, and low operating costs. Further capacity increases are planned, with the full-field plateau production expected to rise to around 720,000 barrels per day.

title: 3 Oil ETFs to Buy That Are Gushing Higher: XOP XLE OIH
summary: This article recommends three oil ETFs (XLE, XOP, OIH) to buy, citing a recent rotation from growth to value stocks and positive vaccine news driving money back into the energy sector. It highlights the tumultuous year for oil prices and suggests that a recovery is underway, detailing the characteristics and appropriate trades for each ETF. The ETFs offer varying exposure to the energy market, from large-cap integrated oil companies to more volatile exploration and production firms and oil services companies.

title: Carbon Capture and Storage Market to See 48.39% Year-Over-Year Growth in 2020 Amid COVID-19 Spread | Technavio
summary: The global carbon capture and storage market is projected to grow by 39.94 million tons during 2020-2024, despite a decelerating CAGR of over 16% due to the impact of COVID-19. The report highlights market fragmentation with key players including Air Products and Chemicals Inc., Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises Inc., and Chevron Corp., and discusses the negative growth expected in 2020-2024 due to the pandemic's effect on energy demand and the utilities industry. It also provides a detailed analysis of the market's competitive landscape, growth drivers, challenges, and regional prospects.

title: Shell Takes Top Bid Spot for Offshore Lease Sale
summary: Shell Offshore Inc. secured the top bid position in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico Lease Sale 256, with $27.88 million across 21 high bids. The auction, organized by BOEM, generated over $120 million in high bids for 93 tracts, demonstrating the continued economic promise and value of the GOM basin. Industry leaders emphasized the long-term energy demand and the significant economic impact of offshore oil and gas activities.

title: Why climate change is getting the attention of world's wealthy investors
summary: Wealthy investors are increasingly focusing on climate change as a fundamental investment theme, driven by significant economic opportunities rather than political beliefs. Billionaires like Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk are leading the way, but this trend is also widespread among ultra-wealthy investors who see renewables becoming cheaper and creating vast capital investment opportunities. Despite concerns about short-term political uncertainties or the intermittency of renewable energy, experts believe the investment case for green technologies and addressing climate risk in portfolios remains strong, with potential for comparable performance to traditional investments.

title: China considers buyout of Exxon’s oil assets in Iraq
summary: Chinese state-owned oil companies, China National Petroleum Corp. and CNOOC Ltd., are reportedly considering acquiring Exxon Mobil Corp.'s 32.7% stake in Iraq's West Qurna 1 oil field for at least $500 million. This potential deal would mark Exxon's exit from the field, where it was once the dominant player. Geopolitical risks in Iraq present uncertainties to the potential agreement.

title: CNPC, CNOOC Weigh Deal for Exxon’s Iraq Oil Field Stake
summary: China National Petroleum Corp. and CNOOC Ltd. are considering purchasing Exxon Mobil Corp.'s remaining stake in Iraq's West Qurna 1 oil field, a deal estimated to be worth at least $500 million. This acquisition would signify Exxon's complete withdrawal from the project and further retreat of international oil majors from Iraq, driven by tough contractual terms, payment delays, and political instability.

title: How Does Saudi Aramco’s Production Compare to Its Peers?
summary: This article examines Saudi Aramco's crude oil and natural gas production in 2015, comparing it to other major oil producers like ExxonMobil, Chevron, Royal Dutch Shell, and BP. Saudi Aramco's production accounted for a significant portion of OPEC's total output, highlighting its influence within the organization and its leading position globally. The article also touches upon Saudi Aramco's plans for future natural gas supply expansion.

title: Graphical Representation of General Electric’s Business Model
summary: This article outlines General Electric's business model, highlighting its two main divisions: industrials and finance services, which contributed 91% and 9% respectively to its consolidated 2015 earnings. It details GE's industrial backlog, geographic reach, core strengths, and competitiveness, along with its 2016 operating EPS target. The company's strategic focus on technology, growth markets, and services is emphasized.

title: General Electric’s Mission, Vision, and Strategy
summary: General Electric (GE) is undergoing a strategic transformation to shift from a broad conglomerate to a focused industrial leader. This involves reshaping its portfolio by acquiring businesses like Alstom’s Power and Grid, spinning off entities like Synchrony Financial, and divesting non-strategic segments such as its appliance business. The goal is to achieve 75% of operating EPS from industrial businesses and return $50 billion to investors.

title: Suncor Energy taking operation of Syncrude by end of 2021
summary: Suncor Energy is set to become the main operator of Syncrude by the end of 2021, a move expected to generate $300 million annually in "synergies." This transition has received in-principle agreement from Syncrude's partners, and Suncor's CEO Mark Little believes it will enhance Syncrude's competitiveness by aiming for lower operating costs and higher utilization. Syncrude's managing director, Doreen Cole, also noted the deal would strengthen the company and region during challenging economic times.

title: Suncor agrees to begin operating Syncrude by end of 2021
summary: Suncor Energy Inc. has agreed to take over as operator of the Syncrude project by the end of 2021, pending formal approval from all joint venture owners. Suncor, which holds a 58.74% stake in Syncrude, believes this transition will enhance cost competitiveness and generate $300 million annually in synergies. The move follows Suncor's increased ownership in Syncrude and is expected to leverage existing bi-directional pipelines connecting their operations.

title: Suncor assuming operational control of Syncrude end-2021 & autonomous haulage will be in play
summary: Suncor, which owns 58.74% of the Syncrude Joint Venture, is set to become the operator of the Syncrude project by the end of 2021, a move expected to generate C$300 million in annual synergies by leveraging regional operational strengths. This transition will also put Suncor in a position to influence Syncrude's significant mining fleet operations, including the potential implementation of autonomous haulage systems, which Suncor has already extensively deployed at its other sites. The decision on the type of autonomous fleet for Syncrude will involve considering retrofitting existing Caterpillar trucks, purchasing new autonomous haulers, and integrating disparate fleet management and communication systems currently in use at both Suncor and Syncrude.

title: Imperial Oil set to end Syncrude services contract as Suncor becomes operator
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. will end its 14-year contract to provide business management services to Syncrude Canada Ltd. when Suncor Energy Inc. takes over as the operator of the oilsands mine and upgrader works at the end of 2021. Suncor, which holds a 58.74% stake in Syncrude, agreed in principle with partners Imperial (25%), CNOOC Oil Sands Canada (7.2%), and Sinopec Oil Sands Partnership (9%) to become the operator. Analysts are skeptical about Suncor CEO Mark Little's ambitious targets for Syncrude's operational reliability and reduced cash operating costs per barrel.

title: Imperial Oil set to end Syncrude services contract as Suncor become operator
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. announced it will relinquish its 14-year contract to provide operational, technical, and business management services to Syncrude Canada Ltd. by the end of 2021. This decision comes as Suncor Energy Inc., holding a 58.74% stake in Syncrude, is set to take over as the operator of the oilsands mine and upgrader. The transition is expected to improve efficiency through bidirectional pipelines connecting Suncor’s Base Plant and Syncrude’s operations, with Suncor anticipating annual cost-saving synergies of approximately $300 million.

title: How Fiserv Is Working With Google Pay And ExxonMobil To Go ‘Beyond the Buy Button’
summary: Fiserv is leveraging its Carat platform to integrate digital and physical commerce, exemplified by a new partnership with Google Pay and ExxonMobil. This collaboration allows consumers to activate gas pumps and pay directly from their cars using Google Pay, with ExxonMobil able to push offers post-transaction. Fiserv aims for Carat to be a leading omnichannel solution for various merchants, enhancing quick-purchase experiences across diverse channels.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Exxon Documents Reveal More Pessimistic Outlook for Oil Prices
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has significantly lowered its internal projections for oil prices for much of the upcoming decade, according to company documents reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. The oil giant cut its expectations for future oil prices for each of the next seven years by 11% to 17% during its financial-planning process this fall. This pessimistic outlook stems from an abundance of fossil fuels and advancements in renewable energy sources.

title: Exclusive: Exxon and Total in talks over Mozambique LNG resource-sharing deal - sources
summary: ExxonMobil and Total are negotiating a resource-sharing deal for their massive LNG projects in Mozambique to increase gas extraction from a shared field and reduce costs. The talks, which also involve the Mozambican government, aim to optimize development plans amidst falling oil prices and a worsening security situation in the region. Success in these negotiations is particularly crucial for Exxon's delayed Rovuma LNG project.

title: China confronts rig and offshore vessels off Malaysia
summary: A Borr Drilling rig, the 10,500-gt jackup Gunnlod, has become the center of a standoff in the South China Sea. Chinese and Malaysian naval vessels are confronting the rig as it works on a new gas discovery. This incident highlights ongoing geopolitical tensions in the region.

title: Borr Drilling faces challenging financial situation amid payment delays in Mexico
summary: Borr Drilling is facing a challenging financial situation in late 2020 and early 2021 due to a difficult market and significant payment delays from Mexico's Pemex for its five operating rigs. Despite previous assurances from Pemex, recent payment slowdowns have caused operational difficulties for Borr's joint ventures in Mexico. The company is actively negotiating with creditors to extend its liquidity runway, hoping to strengthen financial flexibility and attract new capital as the market recovers.

title: Thought Leaders - France 2021: Patrick Hebreard
summary: Patrick Hebreard, an expert in high-value energy arbitrations, shares insights from his career and discusses emerging trends in the energy market. With over 12 years in the energy industry at EDF and BP, he transitioned to consultancy and now advises on complex arbitration cases globally, highlighting the importance of industry experience. Hebreard also outlines his future goals, including developing Paris arbitration practice and mentoring the next generation of experts.

title: Exxon Mobil cuts billions in capital spending as oil and gas prices remain low.
summary: Exxon Mobil announced significant cuts to its capital spending plans over the next four years and will write off up to $20 billion in natural gas investments due to persistently low oil and gas prices exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to reduce capital expenditures to between $16 billion and $19 billion in the coming year, down from $23 billion in 2020, and anticipates annual spending of $20 billion to $25 billion through 2025. These measures aim to improve earnings, cash generation, and balance sheet capacity, while the company also committed to maintaining its dividend despite recent financial struggles.

title: Why ExxonMobil and Chevron Should Merge
summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron have both endured difficult business conditions in 2020 due to weak oil prices and the pandemic. Analyst Paul Sankey suggests a merger between ExxonMobil and Chevron could create a more resilient and efficient "mega-major" oil company, potentially named Chevron, allowing for cost reductions and stability for ExxonMobil's dividend. This comes as Chevron recently surpassed ExxonMobil in market capitalization for the first time.

title: Exxon tries to put the worst behind it with a $20 billion writedown
summary: Exxon Mobil announced a $17 billion to $20 billion writedown on natural gas properties, its largest ever, and plans to cut spending to a 15-year low next year. This move comes as the company attempts to protect a significant shareholder payout amidst the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on energy demand and prices. The writedown highlights a past miscalculation with the 2010 acquisition of XTO Energy and reflects a reduced outlook for oil and gas prices.

title: Exxon Mobil steps back from plan to increase spending, preparing to slash assets book value
summary: Exxon Mobil is reversing its prior strategy to increase spending for oil and gas production, instead planning to cut its capital expenditures and preparing for a significant write-down of asset book value. The Texas oil giant, having experienced over $2.3 billion in losses this year, expects to slash its assets by up to $20 billion in the fourth quarter and has revised its spending outlook for the next five years. This shift comes as a course correction for CEO Darren Woods, following the negative impact of the coronavirus pandemic on fossil fuel demand.

title: How wind and solar toppled Exxon from its place as America’s top energy company
summary: NextEra Energy, a company built on wind and solar farms, briefly unseated Exxon as America's most valuable energy company in early October, demonstrating the growing market ascendance of renewable energy. This shift, partly due to the pandemic's impact on oil majors, highlights NextEra's success in leveraging energy regulation changes and its dual business model of regulated natural gas utility and a deregulated renewables provider. Despite a mixed environmental record, NextEra's strategy offers a glimpse into a future where clean energy titans lead.

title: Zoom Founder’s Net Worth Has Plunged $7 Billion Since October As Explosive Pandemic Growth Slows
summary: Zoom founder Eric Yuan's net worth has dropped by $7 billion since October, with a $2.8 billion decrease on Tuesday alone, as the company's "explosive pandemic growth" slows. Despite beating analyst earnings expectations, concerns over higher costs and slimmer profit margins caused Zoom's stock to tank, although it remains up 500% for the year. Forbes estimates Yuan's current net worth at $18.2 billion, down from $25.1 billion, as shares have fallen nearly 30% from their October peak.

title: Is it Time for Investors to Buy the Dip in Exxon Mobil Stock?
summary: Exxon Mobil (XOM) has experienced significant revenue and net income losses in 2020 due to the pandemic, leading to a 45% year-to-date decline in its stock price and substantial debt. Despite these challenges, the company's efforts to reduce expenses and its commitment to maintaining its dividend could make it an attractive investment for long-term recovery and high-yielding returns, especially if it can restore net profits to previous levels. Additionally, XOM's high Schaeffer's Volatility Scorecard ranking suggests it could be a strong candidate for premium-buying options strategies.

title: ExxonMobil Shelves 2020 Bonuses
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has suspended employee bonuses for 2020 due to significant losses caused by the crude-market collapse, though top executives will still receive stock awards. The oil supermajor has faced a challenging year with crashing demand and prices, leading to job cuts and an expected asset write-down of up to $20 billion. Despite the company's struggles, the five highest-ranking executives will share restricted stock awards valued similarly to the previous year, despite a substantial drop in Exxon's share price.

title: Exxon Suspends Employee Bonuses After Oil-Market Collapse
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has suspended employee bonuses for the current year due to the significant collapse in the crude oil market, which led to a series of quarterly losses for the company. Despite this, the top five executives, including CEO Darren Woods, will still receive restricted stock unit awards. The company's board compensation committee justified this decision by citing challenging industry conditions and the impact on company earnings.

title: Exxon Writes Off Record Amount From Value of Assets Amid Energy Market Downturn
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced a record write-down of $17 billion to $20 billion in natural gas assets, primarily in the U.S., Canada, and Argentina, marking its largest-ever impairment. This move acknowledges past strategic errors and comes after a period where Exxon resisted such write-downs despite adjustments by rivals. The company continues to project long-term demand for oil, even as climate concerns mount.

title: ConocoPhillips to lay off 500 Houston workers, company says
summary: ConocoPhillips announced it will lay off approximately 500 workers in Houston as part of a workforce reduction tied to its upcoming acquisition of Concho Resources. The company stated these targeted reductions are necessary to align organizational capacity with future activity levels and maintain competitiveness. Impacted employees will receive advance notice, severance, and outplacement assistance, with severance notifications beginning in February.

title: America’s Greenest Energy Giant Isn’t Trying to Save the Planet
summary: NextEra Energy Inc. (NEE), despite its conservative political leanings and past opposition to certain green initiatives, has become the world's largest investor-owned generator of wind and solar power. The company's strategic investments and lobbying efforts position it to significantly benefit from the Biden administration's focus on zero-emissions electricity. NextEra's approach is driven by business interests rather than purely environmental motives, making it a prominent player in the U.S. clean energy transition.

title: Chevron tightens belt again with billions in spending cuts
summary: Chevron Corp announced significant cuts to its long-term capital and exploratory budget, reducing it to $14 billion-$16 billion through 2025 from a prior forecast of up to $22 billion. This move reflects the company's expectation of lower energy prices for years and a focus on capital discipline, despite recent acquisitions and in contrast to rival Exxon Mobil's projected spending increase. The 2021 budget details include $11.5 billion for exploration and production and $2.1 billion for refining, with a notable reduction in Permian basin spending.

title: Chevron Tightens Belt. Cuts Billions Off Long-Term Capex
summary: U.S. oil major Chevron Corp has significantly reduced its long-term capital and exploratory budget, cutting anticipated spending through 2025 by billions to between $14 billion and $16 billion, down from a previous forecast of up to $22 billion. This move reflects the company's strategy to preserve its dividend and adapt to expectations of sustained low energy prices. The reduction comes despite recent acquisitions and contrasts with rival Exxon Mobil's plans to boost expenditures.

title: Hydrogen's future as energy source remains murky despite home heating projects in Alberta and Ontario
summary: Pilot projects in Alberta and Ontario are exploring the use of hydrogen for home heating as a cleaner alternative to natural gas, but the commercialization of hydrogen as an energy source faces significant challenges. Analysts emphasize the varying environmental impact and cost of different types of hydrogen ("grey," "blue," and "green"), with "green" being the most environmentally benign but also the most expensive. Widespread adoption will likely depend on government support, infrastructure development, and improvements in cost-efficiency.

title: Suncor Energy: The Only Integrated Energy Loser This Week
summary: Suncor Energy (SU) was the sole integrated energy stock to decline this week, falling marginally by 0.43% to $34.52. Despite the minor dip, the stock has been on a strong uptrend since July 2017, rising approximately 23.0% and hitting a 52-week high of $35.18 last week. This week's movement appears to be a correction within its ongoing upward trend, with strong support at its 50-day moving average.

title: Tom Sullivan, longtime leader of RPM International and Cleveland philanthropist, dies at 83
summary: Tom Sullivan, former leader of RPM International and a prominent Cleveland philanthropist, passed away at 83. He was instrumental in growing RPM, founded by his father, through numerous acquisitions and was known for his significant charitable contributions alongside his late wife, Sandy. His legacy includes both business acumen in expanding RPM into a global company and deep philanthropic involvement in the Cleveland community, particularly with educational institutions and organizations aiding the poor.

title: 2021 ESG Trends to Watch
summary: This article outlines five key ESG trends for 2021, emphasizing the increasing maturity of ESG investing beyond hype and skepticism. It highlights the growing challenges for investors to align with Paris Agreement goals due to shrinking eligible opportunities, the surge in corporate ESG disclosures driven by new regulations, and the urgent need for investors to address systemic risks like social inequality and biodiversity loss, exacerbated by events like COVID-19. The article provides an overview of various aspects, including climate reality and financial implications for investors, the evolving understanding of ESG's pecuniary benefits, the impending biodiversity crisis, the "data deluge" of ESG reporting requirements, and investors' creative approaches to tackle social inequalities, including the rise of social bonds.

title: Lori Ryerkerk is D CEO’s CEO of the Year
summary: Lori Ryerkerk, CEO of Celanese Corp., has been named D CEO's CEO of the Year for 2020. The article highlights her trailblazing career, commitment to social responsibility, and efforts to advance diversity, inclusion, and corporate citizenship at the $6.3 billion company. It also touches on her experiences as a woman in a male-dominated industry and how motherhood shaped her leadership style.

title: Why We Named Lori Ryerkerk Our 2020 CEO of the Year
summary: D CEO named Lori Ryerkerk, CEO of Celanese Corp., as its 2020 CEO of the Year. Ryerkerk, an energy industry veteran, has made a significant impact since joining the $6.3 billion company in 2019, steering it through major business moves and expanding its diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. She is recognized for her authentic leadership and commitment to making a difference.

title: An underperforming Exxon Mobil faces a new climate threat: Activist hedge fund investors
summary: Exxon Mobil is facing a new climate threat from activist hedge fund investors and long-term impact investors focused on sustainability. A newly formed activist investor group, Engine No. 1, plans to seek four board seats at Exxon, supported by pension giant CalSTRS. The activists aim to overhaul Exxon's management and strategy due to its underperformance, significant decline in stock value, and perceived inaction on climate change, while also addressing concerns about the company's dividend.

title: Exxon faces proxy fight launched by new activist firm Engine No. 1
summary: A new activist investment firm, Engine No. 1, backed by the California State Teachers' Retirement System (CalSTRS), is challenging energy giant Exxon Mobil Corp to pivot towards clean energy, improve financial performance, and refresh its board. Engine No. 1, launched by hedge fund veterans, plans to nominate four directors with clean energy expertise to Exxon's board, citing the company's underperformance and governance issues. This proxy fight is seen as a significant move that could unite traditional and climate activists, especially given Exxon's recent financial struggles and its decision not to raise its dividend.

title: Malaysia’s CIMB announces coal financing phase-out by 2040 as Asia’s fossil fuel divestment drive accelerates
summary: Malaysia's CIMB Group Holdings has announced a comprehensive coal exit policy, committing to phase out financing for thermal coal mining and coal-fired power generation by 2040. This makes CIMB the first Malaysian bank, the first emerging markets bank, and the first Islamic financial institution globally to formalize such a progressive policy. The move highlights a growing trend of fossil fuel divestment in Asia, driven by increasing financial risks associated with climate change and the global energy transition.

title: Cheniere Loads First Cargo from Corpus Christi’s Third LNG Train Ahead of Schedule
summary: Cheniere Energy Inc. has loaded the first commissioning cargo from the third train at its Corpus Christi LNG export terminal, ahead of schedule. The train, with a capacity of 4.5 million metric tons/year, is expected to be fully in service in 1Q2021, bringing the terminal's total output to 15 mmty. This milestone comes as global natural gas prices are strong, making the arbitrage window for U.S. LNG exports highly profitable.

title: Chevron’s CEO says “action over pledges” will deliver higher returns, lower carbon
summary: Chevron's CEO, Mike Wirth, announced a focus on "action over pledges" to deliver higher returns and lower carbon, distinguishing the company from rivals with long-term emissions targets. Chevron, which has overtaken Exxon Mobil in market value, aims for capital efficiency and will continue to invest in less risky, quicker-to-produce operations rather than following European peers into renewables like wind and solar. The company's carbon goals are tied to reducing methane leaks and emissions intensity, allowing flexibility for future crude output growth.

title: Whitecap to buy TORC Oil & Gas for $552 million
summary: Canadian oil producer Whitecap Resources Inc. has agreed to acquire TORC Oil & Gas Ltd. in an all-stock deal valued at C$552 million, plus C$335 million in assumed debt. This acquisition is part of a broader consolidation trend in the Canadian energy sector, driven by reduced fuel demand due to the coronavirus pandemic. The transaction is anticipated to close by February 25.

title: Utility of the Year: NextEra Energy
summary: NextEra Energy was named Utility of the Year for its significant investments in green hydrogen, solar energy, and grid resilience, alongside expanding its renewables project pipeline. The company also showcased strong performance through its Florida Power & Light subsidiary amidst the pandemic and hurricane season, maintaining low residential bills and high reliability. Analysts highlight NextEra's leadership in renewable energy and its disciplined approach to M&A despite some unsuccessful bids.

title: S&P Global Platts Analytics Releases its 2021 Energy Outlook
summary: S&P Global Platts Analytics has released its 2021 Energy Outlook, forecasting a recovery in global GDP in the second half of 2021, which will lead to an upward revision in oil demand outlook despite short-term worsening conditions due to lockdowns. The report highlights a challenging year for refiners, increased volatility in petrochemical feedstocks, and mixed fortunes for natural gas and LNG. It also predicts accelerated growth for renewables and biofuels, though CO2 emissions are expected to rise year-on-year.

title: Exxon Mobil to cut 700 jobs in Houston
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced it will lay off over 700 workers in the Houston area as part of a larger global workforce reduction of about 15%, or 14,000 jobs, due to a collapse in oil demand caused by the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to cut costs and slash project spending, with the Houston jobs constituting part of 1,900 anticipated U.S. cuts. This move follows Exxon's previous announcement of a significant impairment to its natural gas properties.

title: Wall Street Is Now Betting on the Future of Water Supplies
summary: Wall Street is introducing futures contracts tied to the price of water, marking a first in US history. This move, led by CME Group, is a response to increasing water scarcity due to climate change, particularly affecting California. The contracts are intended to help manage risk and make water costs more predictable, primarily benefiting farmers rather than speculative investors.

title: Does Michigan really need Line 5?
summary: Line 5 is essential for Michigan, providing fuel for vehicles, heating homes, and supplying raw materials for manufactured goods. A shutdown would cause severe consequences for Michigan and Ohio, including a significant propane shortage, a shortfall in gas, diesel, and jet fuel, and risks to regional refineries and the Detroit Metro Airport. Replacing Line 5's capacity would require an impractical number of tanker trucks or rail cars, highlighting the pipeline's critical role in the region's energy infrastructure and economic stability.

title: Big oil companies eligible for millions from federal coronavirus bailout to clean up sites
summary: The Alberta government is allocating millions in federal coronavirus bailout funds to major oil and gas companies like Canadian Natural Resources Ltd and Cenovus for cleaning up aging sites. This initiative is part of a job-creation program aimed at addressing significant environmental liabilities, but critics question its effectiveness in creating new jobs and suggest the program is flawed. Regulatory experts propose that more aggressive measures like setting well closure timelines and requiring security deposits are needed to effectively tackle the growing inventory of inactive wells.

title: GM leads $23 million investment in on-demand vehicle maintenance service Yoshi
summary: General Motors is leading a $23 million Series B investment round in Yoshi, an on-demand car maintenance service. This marks GM's second investment in the Silicon Valley startup, bringing Yoshi's total funding to over $38 million. The funding will support Yoshi's expansion plans, which include potential EV charging services and integration with vehicle connectivity features like GM's OnStar.

title: Exxon's Suddenly Trouncing Chevron. Coincidence?
summary: ExxonMobil's stock has shown a notable outperformance against Chevron, a trend that began with the emergence of activist investor Engine No. 1 LLC. This surge is the sharpest relative outperformance in a decade, outside of the early COVID-19 market panic. The article suggests this activist campaign might already be yielding positive results for Exxon.

title: LNG Prices Rebound to 6-Year High
summary: LNG spot prices in Asia have rebounded to a six-year high, driven by colder weather, production outages, and shipping congestion. This surge, up 564% since April, is expected to persist into early 2021, boosting commodity traders but potentially leading some utilities to switch to cheaper fuels like coal. While the rally may not last past winter, it has significant short-term implications for global gas markets, drawing cargoes away from Europe and reducing the risk of U.S. cancellations.

title: JPMorgan Chase Board Member Lee Raymond to Leave
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced that Lee Raymond, its longtime lead independent director and former Exxon Mobil chief, will be leaving the board at the end of the year. Raymond has served on the board for over 30 years and recently faced a campaign to remove him due to climate-change concerns. He has been the lead independent director since 2001.

title: JPMorgan Chase Longtime Board Member Lee Raymond to Leave
summary: Lee Raymond, a longtime lead independent director at JPMorgan Chase & Co. and former Exxon Mobil Corp. chief, is leaving the bank's board at the end of the year. His departure follows a campaign by environmental groups and institutional investors seeking his removal due to climate-change concerns. Mr. Raymond had served on the board for over 30 years.

title: Former Exxon chief Lee Raymond to retire from board of JPMorgan Chase
summary: Lee Raymond, former CEO of ExxonMobil and a long-serving director at JPMorgan Chase, is retiring from the bank's board following pressure from environmental activists. While JPMorgan stated his retirement was unrelated to climate issues, activist groups view it as a win, urging the bank to now overhaul its fossil fuel financing. Raymond had been a director for 33 years and the lead independent director for 19 years.

title: Line 3: The time for delays and obstruction is over
summary: The author argues that after six years of review and legal challenges, it is time to move forward with the Line 3 replacement project. She highlights the economic benefits for Minnesota, including job creation and reliable energy infrastructure, and criticizes Governor Walz for what she perceives as obstruction. The article suggests that continued opposition to such infrastructure projects negatively impacts the state's economy and energy security.

title: Eastman joins pellet spill reporting, NGO targets broader effort
summary: Eastman Chemical Co. has agreed to public reporting of resin pellet spills, becoming the sixth plastics manufacturer to do so following an agreement with activist group As You Sow. This move is part of As You Sow's broader effort to increase transparency and accountability in the plastics industry regarding microplastic pollution, advocating for widespread adoption of spill reporting, in-transit reporting, and third-party audits. The initiative aims to address the estimated 10 trillion pellets lost annually, pushing for stricter regulations and industry standards.

title: Luego de dos décadas, Petrobras dejará definitivamente Argentina
summary: Petrobras, la petrolera estatal brasileña, anunció que planea cerrar sus oficinas en Argentina, Colombia y Uruguay como parte de un proceso de desinversión y reducción de tamaño. La empresa busca ahorrar US$13.5 millones en gastos corrientes y concentrar sus actividades comerciales internacionales en Róterdam, Houston y Singapur. Petrobras ya había vendido activos en Argentina previamente, incluyendo su refinería de San Lorenzo y la totalidad de sus operaciones en el país a Pampa Energía.

title: Exxon Mobil Corp. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) shares saw a modest gain of 0.80% on Wednesday, closing at $41.60, despite an overall positive trading day for the broader market. However, the stock underperformed some of its key competitors, such as Chevron Corp. and Honeywell International Inc., which saw slightly larger percentage increases. XOM remained significantly below its 52-week high.

title: Las 7 principales áreas productoras de gas natural de Colombia
summary: This article lists the top 7 natural gas producing areas in Colombia, based on average daily production in October as reported by the ANH. Most of the top fields are operated by Ecopetrol and located in the Casanare department, with Pauto Sur being the highest producer.

title: Exxon Mobil warns investors it’s heading toward a fourth straight quarterly loss
summary: Exxon Mobil is anticipating its fourth consecutive quarterly loss as it struggles to maintain its $15 billion-a-year dividend program. The Irving-based oil giant confirmed a regulatory filing indicating a write-down of up to $20 billion on its upstream assets, alongside smaller non-cash impairments in its refining business. This financial challenge highlights the company's reliance on debt to cover dividends and capital expenditures from operational cash flow.

title: Activist Wins Exxon Board Seats After Questioning Oil Giant’s Climate Strategy
summary: An activist investor, Engine No. 1, won two seats on Exxon Mobil Corp.'s board, marking a significant defeat for the oil giant and its CEO Darren Woods. This victory signals increased pressure on Exxon to address shareholder concerns regarding climate change. The final composition of the board was still unclear as of the preliminary vote count.

title: Beyond automation: Driving advances in autonomous drilling
summary: This article discusses the shift from mere automation to advanced autonomy in drilling operations to enhance efficiency and reduce costs in the challenging energy industry. It highlights that while automation streamlines repetitive tasks, autonomy enables systems to make independent decisions in dynamic environments, decreasing human oversight. The piece provides examples of autonomous directional drilling and automated stand drilling, detailing how these technologies improve performance, consistency, and safety while allowing human operators to focus on higher-level tasks.

title: Exxon Reveals Petroleum Product Emissions Data for First Time
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has for the first time released Scope 3 emissions data, detailing the emissions from customers' use of its petroleum products, totaling 570 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2019. While most major oil companies already publish this data, Exxon stated that it does not provide meaningful insight into the company's emission-reduction performance. The company prefers to focus on Scope 1 and 2 emissions, which are within its direct control, and reported a 3.2% reduction in its direct emissions in 2019 compared to 2018.

title: Canada’s oil sands hit record high production
summary: Canada's oil sands production reached a record high of 3.16 million barrels a day in November, fueled by the end of provincial government production curtailments in Alberta. This increase coincides with an 11-month high in global oil prices and is expected to continue rising, potentially reaching 3.3 million bpd by mid-2021. The Canadian Energy Regulator forecasts peak production of about 4.3 million bpd by 2039, mostly from existing facility expansions.

title: EIG Sells Share in Brazil-Bolivia pipeline, Eyes Petrobras' Assets
summary: EIG Global Energy Partners has sold a portion of the Brazil-Bolivia natural gas pipeline to Fluxys Belgium, removing a regulatory hurdle for EIG to bid for a larger stake in the same pipeline owned by Petrobras. EIG aims to invest billions in Brazil's growing natural gas industry, including acquiring pipelines, processing plants, and potentially production assets, and is also considering bids for Petrobras's mid-life offshore oil fields like Albacora and Marlim. The move aligns with Brazil's decreasing dependence on Bolivian gas imports due to new offshore discoveries and potential for future gas exports.

title: Suncor restarts Fort Hills oil sands mining operations
summary: Suncor Energy Inc. has restarted mining operations at its Fort Hills oil sands mine in northern Alberta, following a temporary halt due to a fatal vehicle collision involving two workers. The company emphasized safety during the slow restart process. The Fort Hills mine, which produced approximately 120,000 barrels per day in Q4 2020, had previously idled production due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: For first time, oil giant Exxon reveals full scope of emissions
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has for the first time disclosed the full scope of emissions from customers' use of its products, revealing that its 2019 Scope 3 emissions were equivalent to 730 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, comparable to Canada's total emissions. This disclosure follows pressure from investors for greater transparency despite Exxon's previous focus on Scope 1 and 2 emissions. While Exxon announced new targets to reduce emissions per barrel of crude, it has not committed to reducing absolute pollution levels.

title: Braskem Idesa Partially Restores Operations at Mexico Petrochemical Complex
summary: Braskem Idesa has partially restored operations at its Etileno XXI petrochemical complex in Mexico after its natural gas supply was cut by Cenagas in December. The shutdown was due to a dispute over ethane supply with Mexican state oil giant Pemex, which has been unable to meet its contractual commitments. Braskem Idesa is pursuing legal measures and is in negotiations to resolve the issue, with local officials urging a swift resolution due to job concerns.

title: Max Midstream agrees to pump $360 million into Calhoun Port's expansion plan
summary: Max Midstream is investing $360 million into a public/private partnership with the Calhoun Port Authority to deepen and widen the Matagorda Ship Channel by 2023. This expansion aims to provide an alternative export option for companies, enabling the port to accommodate larger vessels like Aframax and Suezmax. Max Midstream also secured a deal with Phillips 66 to connect the Gray Oak pipeline to the Calhoun Port, granting access to crude from the Permian and Eagle Ford basins.

title: Almost half of SA’s oil refining seen shut until 2022
summary: Nearly half of South Africa's oil refining capacity, primarily from plants owned by Glencore Plc and Petroliam Nasional Bhd, is expected to remain shut until at least 2022. This includes Astron Energy's Cape Town refinery and Engen's Durban plant, both closed due to accidents. The closures will significantly increase South Africa's reliance on fuel imports and are exacerbated by a pending clean-fuels policy and general industry struggles.

title: Almost half of South Africa’s oil refining seen shut until 2022
summary: Almost half of South Africa's oil refining capacity is expected to remain shut until at least 2022, according to energy consultant Citac. This closure, affecting plants owned by Glencore Plc and Petroliam Nasional Bhd, stems from accidents and will significantly increase the country's reliance on fuel imports. The entire South African oil refining industry faces challenges from accidents, a pending national clean-fuels policy, and reviews of operations by major stakeholders like Shell and Sasol.

title: Mozambique, Tanzania unite against rebel threats to LNG projects
summary: Mozambique and Tanzania are strengthening their cooperation to combat cross-border terrorism, especially ahead of a regional summit focused on addressing insurgency threats to nearly $60 billion in natural gas projects. Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi met with his Tanzanian counterpart John Magufuli to revive a joint commission on defense and security. This collaboration comes as insurgent attacks, linked to Islamic State, escalate in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province, impacting major LNG projects and displacing hundreds of thousands of people.

title: Enbridge defies Michigan’s demand to shut down Line 5 oil pipeline
summary: Enbridge Inc. has stated it will not comply with Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer's demand to shut down its Line 5 oil pipeline, which runs through the Straits of Mackinac. Enbridge argues that the pipeline is safe and Whitmer's order is based on inaccurate information and political motivations, while Michigan asserts that Enbridge has a history of violating easement terms and the pipeline poses environmental risks. Both parties have taken legal and public stances on the issue, with Enbridge pursuing permits for a tunnel project to house a replacement pipeline.

title: Venezuela refuels its territorial dispute with Guyana in area with massive offshore oil find
summary: Venezuela has escalated its long-standing territorial dispute with Guyana over the resource-rich Essequibo province, where ExxonMobil has discovered massive offshore oil reserves. Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro announced plans to "reconquer" the area, which Guyana maintains was awarded to it by the 1899 Arbitral Award. The renewed tensions are occurring after the inauguration of a pro-Maduro National Assembly and amid increased U.S. engagement with Guyana, while Venezuela continues to reject participation in International Court of Justice proceedings.

title: Oil and Gas Industry Fights New Regulations in Ventura County
summary: The oil and gas industry is fiercely resisting Ventura County's new environmental safety measures through lawsuits and petition drives, arguing the regulations will impact jobs and tax revenue. Companies like Aera Energy and California Resources Corporation face financial difficulties as communities move away from fossil fuels, and are challenging buffer zone requirements, pipeline mandates, and environmental impact reviews for older permits. The industry's lobbying efforts and petition drives have been met with counter-organizing from environmental groups and accusations of misinformation.

title: Investors flee Big Oil as portfolios get drilled
summary: The article details how Big Oil's financial might has been eroding for a decade, with a significant hit in 2020 due to collapsed fuel demand and oil prices. Investment firms and banks are increasingly wary of fossil fuels, with Goldman Sachs allocating more towards renewables, and major U.S. banks withdrawing funding for Arctic drilling. This shift is driven by both environmental concerns and the poor financial performance of the fossil fuel sector compared to growing competitive renewable energy.

title: Shell joins Equinor and YPF in Argentina block
summary: Shell has agreed to acquire a 30 percent non-operated interest in the CAN 100 block offshore Argentina from Equinor and YPF. This transaction, pending governmental approval, will result in Equinor and YPF each holding 35 percent equity in the block, with Shell holding the remaining 30 percent. The CAN 100 block, located in the North Argentinian Basin, covers an area of 15,000 km2.

title: Equinor, YPF partner with Shell offshore Argentina
summary: Equinor and YPF have partnered with Shell to farm down 30% non-operated interests in the CAN 100 block in the North Argentinian basin, offshore Argentina. After the transaction, which is pending governmental approval, Equinor and YPF will each hold 35% equity, with Shell holding the remaining 30% in the 15,000 sq km block. This agreement follows Equinor's farm-in to the CAN 100 block and agreement to take over operatorship in October 2019.

title: Exxon Was Hit Hard In 2020. How It Rebounds Could Shape Houston’s Future.
summary: ExxonMobil faced significant challenges in 2020, including low oil prices, the COVID-19 downturn, and workforce reductions in Houston, leading to three consecutive quarters of losses. Despite these setbacks and a global shift away from fossil fuels, energy experts believe ExxonMobil will rebound due to its strong financial position. The company's response to these challenges will profoundly impact Houston, an oil capital, affecting its economy and the community beyond just financial figures.

title: Population growth will sustain demand for fossil fuels, says Chevron CEO Michael Wirth
summary: Chevron CEO Michael Wirth believes global population growth will sustain demand for fossil fuels for decades, despite efforts to transition to cleaner energy. He highlights Chevron's commitment to address climate change through reducing carbon output, integrating renewables, and investing in new technologies like carbon capture. Wirth also discussed the industry's need for consolidation and Chevron's intent to work constructively with the new U.S. administration.

title: Exxon Mobil fails to encounter oil at Hassa-1 exploration well
summary: Exxon Mobil did not find commercially viable hydrocarbon resources at its Hassa-1 exploration well in the Stabroek block offshore Guyana, though hydrocarbons were encountered in other intervals. This failure highlights the inherent geological risks in frontier oil and gas exploration. Despite this, ExxonMobil remains committed to evaluating its offshore Guyana blocks and continues production from the Liza-1 well in the Stabroek block.

title: Durango’s Brennan Oil Co. switches gasoline supplier
summary: Brennan Oil Co., a 102-year-old family-owned business in Durango, has switched its gasoline supplier from Exxon Mobil Corp. to Marathon Petroleum Corp. The primary reason for the change was Marathon's more beneficial loyalty rewards program, which allows customers to earn points on both fuel and convenience store purchases. This move marks only the third change in suppliers for Brennan Oil Co., which previously used Texaco before its 22-year contract with Exxon Mobil.

title: Halliburton cut 15,000 jobs in 2020
summary: Halliburton, led by CEO Jeff Miller, announced 15,000 job cuts in 2020, a year described as "like no other." This significant reduction reflects broader trends of job losses within the energy sector during that period.

title: Justices divided in procedural battle between Baltimore, oil companies in climate fight
summary: The Supreme Court heard oral arguments in a procedural dispute between the city of Baltimore and several oil companies regarding the scope of appellate review for remand orders in climate change lawsuits. The justices appeared divided on whether federal appeals courts can review an entire case remand order when an appealable ground, such as the federal-officer removal statute, is present, or if review is limited only to that specific ground. The outcome of this case, involving statutory interpretation and concerns about potential loopholes, will impact other similar climate change litigations across the country.

title: Biden kills Keystone XL permit, again
summary: President Joe Biden revoked the Keystone XL pipeline permit on his first day in office, marking the second time a Democratic administration has scuttled the $8 billion project. This decision came despite appeals from Canadian officials and led to TC Energy, the developer, suspending the project and eliminating over 1,000 jobs. While environmental activists celebrated the move, it sparked criticism from Republicans and Alberta's premier, who threatened legal action and economic sanctions against the U.S.

title: Biden Revokes Keystone XL Pipeline Permit to Cross U.S. Border
summary: President Joe Biden revoked the Keystone XL oil pipeline's permit shortly after taking office, re-ending a project that had been revived under his predecessor, Donald Trump. This move marks one of Biden's initial significant environmental actions, canceling the cross-border pipeline and signaling a strong stance on climate change. Canadian Prime Minister Trudeau expressed disappointment but committed to working with the new administration.

title: There's Traditional Energy Funds. Then There's the MLPX ETF
summary: The Global X MLP & Energy Infrastructure ETF (MLPX) offers investors an alternative to traditional energy funds, providing exposure to midstream energy infrastructure MLPs and corporations. MLPX has demonstrated strong performance, being up over 30% in recent months and outperforming other energy indexes due to its midstream focus, tax efficiency, and high income potential. The fund benefits from recovering oil prices and the anticipated economic revival spurred by a COVID-19 vaccine.

title: Big U.S. oil drillers have federal permits to mute effect of any Biden ban
summary: Large U.S. oil companies have stockpiled permits for drilling on federal lands, which would significantly delay the impact of President Biden's proposed ban on new oil and gas permits. While bigger drillers are confident their existing permits could last for years, smaller independent operators are more concerned about the policy's potential "existential threat" given their limited resources and reliance on federal acreage. States that depend on revenue from federal drilling are also preparing opposition.

title: Magellan and Enterprise to develop Joint Houston crude oil futures contract
summary: Magellan Midstream Partners and Enterprise Products Partners announced an agreement to jointly develop a Houston-based crude oil futures contract. This initiative aims to address market interest for greater scale, flow assurance, and price transparency for physical crude oil delivery in the Houston area. The contract will specify West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil from the Permian Basin, deliverable at Magellan’s East Houston terminal or Enterprise’s ECHO terminal.

title: Iditarod Sled-dog Race Losing Exxon Support Amid Animal-rights Pressure
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced its decision to end its sponsorship of the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race after the 2021 event, citing economic concerns. This move is seen as a victory by animal-rights activists like PETA, who have long criticized the race as inhumane. The Iditarod organization, facing multiple sponsor withdrawals and a scaled-back race due to the pandemic, hopes to rebuild and reassess its partnerships.

title: Phillips 66 stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Shares of Phillips 66 (PSX) declined 0.65% to $72.08 on Monday, marking its third consecutive day of losses, despite a mixed trading session for the broader market. The stock remained below its 52-week high, yet it outperformed competitors like Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) which saw larger drops, while Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) rose.

title: BlackRock’s shift to ‘net-zero’ investments is accelerating, CEO Larry Fink says
summary: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink announced an acceleration in the firm's shift towards "net-zero" investments, urging companies in its portfolio to disclose their strategies for a carbon-neutral economy. This move reflects an intensifying reallocation of capital towards sustainable assets, with global investors pouring US$288-billion into sustainable funds from January to November last year. BlackRock emphasizes that companies failing to demonstrate progress in climate risk disclosure and transition plans could face divestment from its discretionary active portfolios.

title: BlackRock Is Turning Up The Heat On Oil Companies
summary: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager with $9 trillion in AUM, is increasing pressure on oil and gas companies to reduce carbon emissions and achieve "net-zero" goals by 2050. This move follows New York City's pension fund and the Rockefeller Foundation's announcements to divest from fossil fuels. While BlackRock faces criticism for existing fossil fuel investments, CEO Larry Fink asserts the firm will leverage its influence to drive a significant reallocation of capital toward climate-aligned businesses.

title: Exxon planning board changes under activist investor pressure - WSJ
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is reportedly planning to add new board directors and increase sustainability investments in response to pressure from activist investors. The company is in discussions with D.E. Shaw and could announce these changes along with its fourth-quarter results. This move follows years of underperformance and pressure from investor groups like Engine No. 1, which has formally nominated four directors to Exxon's board.

title: Activist investor Engine No. 1 nominates four potential Exxon Mobil directors
summary: Activist investor Engine No. 1 has nominated four candidates to Exxon Mobil's board of directors, arguing that the company needs a significant change in its existing strategy. This move indicates increasing pressure on Exxon Mobil to reassess its strategic direction.

title: Aramark Offshore Bags 5-year UKCS Catering Deal with Total
summary: Aramark Offshore has secured a new five-year contract with Total E&P to provide catering, cleaning, laundry, janitorial, maintenance, emergency response, and heli-deck services across six offshore platforms in the UK Continental Shelf. This deal expands Aramark's existing services and includes support for the Elgin Franklin shutdown in 2021. The financial details of the contract were not disclosed.

title: GM’s all-EV plan could shake the energy industry
summary: General Motors announced its plan to stop making gas-powered cars by 2035 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040, a move expected to transform the electric vehicle market and energy industry. This significant commitment will necessitate dramatic changes to the electric grid and put GM in direct competition with Tesla. The shift also marks a major policy turnaround for GM, which previously sided with the Trump administration against stricter emissions standards.

title: Exxon, Chevron CEOs discussed merger in early 2020-sources
summary: The CEOs of ExxonMobil and Chevron discussed a potential merger in early 2020, which would have been the largest merger ever. These confidential talks, which are no longer active, occurred as the energy sector faced significant pressure due to the COVID-19 pandemic and plummeting crude oil prices. Both companies declined to comment on the matter.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Exxon, Chevron CEOs Discussed Merger
summary: The CEOs of Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. discussed a potential merger last year after the pandemic significantly impacted oil and gas demand. While described as preliminary and not ongoing, such a combination could represent one of the largest corporate mergers in history. The discussions highlight the financial pressures faced by both companies due to crashing energy prices.

title: ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions to Commercialize Emission-Reduction Technology
summary: ExxonMobil has established a new business unit, ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions, to commercialize its low-carbon technology portfolio, initially focusing on carbon capture and storage (CCS).
