The company, with over 30 years of experience in CCS, plans to invest $3 billion in lower-emission solutions through 2025 and is advancing over 20 new CCS opportunities globally. These efforts aim to significantly reduce industrial emissions, supporting global climate goals.

title: Exxon Mobil to invest $3 billion in carbon capture and other projects to lower emissions.
summary: Exxon Mobil announced a $3 billion investment over the next five years into projects aimed at lowering emissions, focusing initially on carbon capture and storage. This move comes as the company faces increasing pressure from environmentalists, investors, and the Biden administration to address climate change, especially given its historical reluctance compared to European counterparts. Exxon is establishing a new business unit, ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions, to manage about 20 carbon capture projects worldwide.

title: BP sells 20% stake in Oman gas development to Thailand's PTTEP
summary: BP has announced the sale of a 20% stake in Oman's Block 61 gas development to Thailand's PTT Exploration and Production for $2.6 billion. Despite the sale, BP will retain a 40% interest and continue as the operator of the block, which includes the Khazzan and Ghazeer tight gas projects. This divestment is part of BP's global program while maintaining its commitment to Oman's significant energy projects.

title: CEOs of oil giants Exxon, Chevron discussed mega merger: Reports
summary: The CEOs of ExxonMobil Corp and Chevron Corp held preliminary talks in early 2020 about a potential mega-merger, which would have been the largest ever. These discussions, no longer active, highlight the immense pressure on the energy sector due to plunging oil prices during the COVID-19 pandemic. The potential merger would have faced significant regulatory scrutiny, particularly under the Biden administration, and sought synergies through major cost cuts.

title: Exxon defends dividend after posting first annual loss in decades
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has pledged to maintain its significant dividend despite reporting its first annual loss in 40 years, driven by challenging market conditions and activist pressure. While the company recorded a full-year loss, it returned to profit in the fourth quarter. CEO Darren Woods is implementing cost-cutting measures and capital spending reductions amid growing scrutiny over Exxon's environmental record and financial performance.

title: BPX Energy is bringing drilling rigs back to Texas
summary: BPX Energy, the U.S. shale oil business of BP plc, is reinstating drilling rigs in Texas. The CEO stated that the Denver-based division's Texas holdings have exceeded expectations. This move signals a renewed focus on drilling operations in the region.

title: Oil Companies Endure Brutal 2020, Warn of Slow 2021 Recovery
summary: Major oil companies like Exxon Mobil, BP, and Chevron reported significant annual losses in 2020, marking one of their worst performances in decades. The pandemic severely impacted demand for fossil fuels, and these companies are signaling that these challenges are expected to continue into 2021 with a slow recovery. This comes as investors increasingly shift capital towards renewable energy sources.

title: Exxon Mobil posts first annual loss in 40 years
summary: Exxon Mobil reported its first annual loss in 40 years for 2020, totaling $22.44 billion, primarily due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on energy prices and a significant writedown of its shale gas assets. The company responded by cutting up to 15% of its workforce and delaying projects, while also facing pressure from activist investors for strategic changes. Other oil majors like BP and Chevron also reported annual losses, highlighting the industry-wide struggles.

title: Exxon reports its largest losses in the oil giant's history
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. reported its largest ever losses, with $20.1 billion in the fourth quarter of 2020 and $22.4 billion for the full year, primarily due to the pandemic's impact on energy demand and oil prices. Other oil giants like BP and Chevron also faced significant losses, though crude prices have since risen. Exxon plans to cut $6 billion in annual spending by 2023, while facing pressure from activist shareholders to shift towards renewable energy.

title: Exxon Creates Carbon Capture Tech Branch
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has launched a new division, Low Carbon Solutions, to commercialize its carbon emission reduction technology. This move is part of the company's efforts to address climate change and reduce greenhouse gas emissions amid increasing pressure from investors and activists. The new unit will initially focus on carbon capture and storage in locations like the U.S. Gulf Coast and depleted North Sea gas fields.

title: Imperial Oil reports $1.15B loss on writedown, sees pandemic-related fuel demand cut
summary: Imperial Oil reported a $1.15 billion net loss in the fourth quarter of 2020, primarily due to a $1.17 billion non-cash charge related to Canadian unconventional natural gas assets it no longer plans to develop. The company's CEO, Brad Corson, attributed a significant portion of the loss and reduced revenue to sagging fuel demand caused by new community lockdowns due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite increased oil prices and strong production at its Kearl oilsands mine, Imperial Oil plans to maintain its current capital spending and dividend, disappointing some analysts.

title: Exxon Defends Dividend After First Annual Loss in Decades
summary: ExxonMobil (XOM) pledged to safeguard its dividend even after posting its first annual loss in 40 years, a stance that differentiates it from rivals who cut payouts. CEO Woods emphasized a willingness to sacrifice new projects to protect the dividend, highlighting the company's commitment to financial health even in a low oil price environment. The company's stock rose despite the news, indicating investor confidence in its dividend protection strategy.

title: The Drilldown: Imperial Oil has alternative plans in case Line 5 closes
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. is preparing contingency plans to transport oil from Western Canada to Ontario refineries if Michigan succeeds in closing Enbridge Line 5. The company reported a significant loss for its fourth quarter due to a non-cash charge on natural gas assets and decreased fuel demand from lockdowns. Internationally, Lebanon will receive fuel oil from Iraq to address power shortages, while France and the UK face criticism for insufficient action against climate change.

title: Billion-dollar baby: Amazon daily sales surpass new milestone
summary: Amazon.com Inc. achieved over $1 billion a day in revenue in 2020, reaching $386 billion for the full year, driven by the holiday shopping season and increased online shopping during the pandemic. The e-commerce giant's revenue surged by nearly 44% in the fourth quarter to over $100 billion, reflecting a significant shift towards online retail that analysts expect to continue. Despite CEO Jeff Bezos stepping down, strong analyst ratings and projected market dominance indicate continued growth for the company.

title: Oil companies’ losses in 2020 were staggering. And that was before the government focused on climate change.
summary: In 2020, major oil companies like ExxonMobil, BP, Chevron, and ConocoPhillips reported billions in losses due to a weakened market exacerbated by the pandemic, which caused oil prices and volumes to plummet. The severe financial downturn occurred even before the Biden administration signaled a strong focus on climate change and the growing momentum towards all-electric vehicles. These factors are now collectively raising significant concerns about the long-term viability of these once-dominant corporations.

title: What CEOs Are Saying About Covid-19, Leadership and More
summary: This article compiles statements from prominent CEOs, including leaders from Microsoft, Exxon Mobil, UPS, and Clorox Co., reflecting on how their businesses are adapting during the coronavirus pandemic. It covers topics such as the economic impact of Covid-19, leadership challenges, and the evolution of technology, highlighting strategic changes like simplification and efficiency improvements. The executives discuss the difficult decisions made to navigate the widespread disruption caused by the pandemic.

title: California Refinery’s Switch to Biofuels Not as Green As it Sounds
summary: A Phillips 66 refinery in Rodeo, California, announced plans to convert to processing biofuels, a move met with skepticism by environmental groups. While the company promotes "renewable diesel" from waste oils, critics point out the likely reliance on soybean feedstock, which drives deforestation in tropical regions. Concerns also include the significant fossil fuel use in the refining process, potentially leading to greenhouse gas emissions comparable to, or exceeding, those from crude oil refining, and a mysterious requirement to double crude oil tanker deliveries during the transition.

title: Exxon to close Australian refinery
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced the closure of its 72-year-old Altona refinery in Australia, converting it into a fuel import terminal due to low demand and economic unviability. This decision leaves Australia with only two operating refineries after BP Plc also decided to shut its Kwinana facility. The Australian energy minister expressed disappointment, noting that 300 jobs would be affected, but assured that fuel stockholdings would not be negatively impacted.

title: The 2020 Polar Endeavour Shipyard Project
summary: This article details the challenges faced during the 2020 Polar Endeavour shipyard project in Singapore, which was significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The crew and shoreside staff demonstrated exceptional teamwork and dedication to complete the required maintenance under strict travel restrictions and quarantine measures. Despite hurdles like reduced crew and limited shore access, the project was successfully completed, setting a precedent for subsequent tanker dry dock schedules.

title: Oil refineries are not national security assets: Kemp
summary: John Kemp argues that national governments' view of oil refineries as strategic national security assets is outdated, stemming from World War II-era concerns about blockades and fuel shortages. He contends that in modern warfare, which is much faster and more destructive, traditional blockades are ineffective and could quickly escalate into wider conflicts, making domestic refineries vulnerable targets rather than protective assets. Kemp suggests that relying on domestic refining capacity offers little real protection, especially since many countries still depend on imported crude, and these facilities would be high-value targets in any major inter-state conflict.

title: Celanese Corp. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Celanese Corp. (CE) stock rose 1.02% on Thursday, outperforming the mixed market performance of the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock closed $9.62 short of its 52-week high reached on January 6th. Trading volume for the day was below its 50-day average, and the company showed mixed performance against competitors like Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Eastman Chemical Co. (EMN), and Westlake Chemical Corp. (WLK).

title: U.S. Oil Majors Downgraded by S&P on Climate Risk, Earnings
summary: S&P Global Ratings downgraded the credit ratings of U.S. oil majors Exxon Mobil Corp., Chevron Corp., and ConocoPhillips. This move follows S&P's earlier warning and reflects increased industry risk due to climate change and weak earnings. The downgrades, occurring two weeks after a sector-wide report on climate challenges, saw each company's rating cut by one notch.

title: Dark money group pushing PRC reform tied to major oil company
summary: Exxon Mobil Corporation contributed at least $10,000 to a "dark money" group, "Committee to Protect New Mexico Consumers," which supported a successful referendum to reform New Mexico's Public Regulation Commission (PRC). This contribution, revealed through a lobbyist report, raises concerns about corporate influence on the agency that regulates them, especially as the group initially refused to disclose its donors. The reform changed how commissioners are selected and removed specific constitutional mention of other PRC oversight authorities, potentially benefiting energy companies.

title: New Mexico largest electric utility bankrolled dark money group in 2020 election
summary: New Mexico's largest electric utility, PNM Resources, Inc., was the sole funder of a dark money group called the “Council for a Competitive New Mexico” (CCNM) in the 2020 election, contributing almost half a million dollars. CCNM spent over $130,000 on mailers and robo-calls to support incumbents and attack opponents in five state senate Democratic primary races. This disclosure by the New Mexico State Ethics Commission highlights the utility's increasing involvement in state politics and raises suspicions about its potential funding of other dark money groups.

title: Exxon Mobil, Aramco Texas oil refineries temporarily shut down for unexpected mid-winter freeze
summary: Major oil refineries in Texas, including those operated by Exxon Mobil and Saudi Aramco's Motiva Enterprises, have temporarily shut down due to an unexpected mid-winter freeze. These closures are in response to unprecedented frigid temperatures and, in ExxonMobil's case, curtailment of natural gas supplies. Despite the shutdowns, some facilities are exporting electricity to the grid to support local power needs.

title: Oil production is rebounding at Argentina’s Vaca Muerta shale play
summary: Oil production at Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale play is exceeding pre-pandemic levels and is projected to increase further by the end of 2021, driven by a resurgence in unconventional oil exploration. In December, the region hit a record 124,000 barrels per day (bpd), with potential to reach 150,000 bpd. While oil output is strong, gas production declined due to lower seasonal consumption and reduced well activity in the gas zone.

title: CFO at Jerry Jones' gas company on rising prices due to Texas freeze: 'Like hitting the jackpot'
summary: Roland Burns, CFO of Comstock Resources Inc., a natural gas company controlled by Jerry Jones, reportedly described the rising natural gas prices during the deadly Texas winter storm as "like hitting the jackpot." This statement drew criticism as millions in Texas faced power outages and frigid temperatures. The storm caused gas production to plummet, leading to a surge in prices, from which Comstock benefited by selling gas at "super premium prices."

title: BlackRock puts muscle behind push for net zero
summary: BlackRock Inc. has intensified its commitment to net-zero emissions by pledging to hold companies accountable for their climate action. The financial giant will use its shareholder power to pressure companies to set carbon reduction targets and disclose net-zero plans by 2050, threatening to vote against directors who fail to comply. This marks a significant shift from BlackRock's previous hands-off approach, indicating a more aggressive stance on climate change integration into business strategy for its $8.7 trillion investment portfolio.

title: Why Texas Pacific Land Trust Has a Better Business Model Than Exxon and Chevron
summary: Texas Pacific Land Trust (TPL) is highlighted for its capital-light business model, which allows it to profit from oil and gas production without the heavy investment and debt typically associated with traditional exploration companies like Exxon and Chevron. TPL owns land in the Permian Basin and collects revenue from easements and a percentage of oil sales, while other companies bear the exploration and production costs. This approach has led to significant outperformance compared to its peers in the oil and gas sector over the last decade.

title: ExxonMobil to Sell U.K. Upstream Central and Northern North Sea Assets
summary: ExxonMobil has agreed to sell most of its non-operated upstream assets in the U.K. central and northern North Sea to HitecVision for over $1 billion, with potential for an additional $300 million in contingent payments. This divestment aligns with ExxonMobil's strategy to focus investments on more strategic, advantaged projects globally. The transaction includes 14 producing fields and is expected to close by mid-2021, while ExxonMobil maintains its significant downstream and marketing presence in the U.K.

title: Exxon to Sell Some North Sea Assets for More Than $1 Billion
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has agreed to sell most of its non-operated upstream assets in the U.K. North Sea to NEO Energy for over $1 billion. This move aligns with Exxon's strategy to concentrate on larger, newer oil and gas growth areas in Guyana, Brazil, and the U.S. Permian Basin. NEO Energy is an oil producer backed by Norwegian private equity firm HitecVision AS.

title: Exxon's Baytown refinery making slow progress restarting wastewater, sulfur units -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is facing slow progress in restarting the wastewater and sulfur recovery units at its 560,500-barrel-per-day Baytown, Texas, refinery. These units are crucial for environmental compliance, treating water used in fuel production and extracting sulfur from hydrogen sulfide. While the company acknowledges making progress in restarting operations, it refrains from discussing individual unit operations as a matter of practice.

title: Exxon Mobil's total reserves drop by a third after COVID-19 oil price drop
summary: Exxon Mobil's global oil and gas reserves decreased by a third in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on oil prices and demand. This reduction led to significant cuts in project spending, jobs, and a net annual loss of $22.4 billion for the company. The decline was primarily driven by oil sands in Canada and U.S. shale gas properties.

title: BP Introduces Price Match Program for Rewards Members
summary: BP is launching a new "Price Match" program for its BPme Rewards members. This program automatically compares BP and Amoco gas prices to competitors like Exxon, Mobil, Shell, Chevron, and Marathon within a certain radius, applying a cents-per-gallon savings to the member's next purchase if a lower price is found. The service is available through the BPme app for a monthly subscription fee of 99 cents, allowing members to save up to 5 cents per gallon per transaction, which can be stacked with other rewards.

title: Exxon Mobil's total reserves drop by a third after COVID-19 oil price drop
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp's global oil and gas reserves decreased by a third in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on oil prices and demand. Total reserves fell from 22.4 billion barrels to 15.2 billion, primarily affecting oil sands in Canada and U.S. shale gas properties. The company also reported a net annual loss of $22.4 billion for 2020 and plans to cut its global workforce.

title: Imperial Oil reports one-billion-barrel drop in bitumen reserves at end of 2020
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. announced a one-billion-barrel reduction in its oilsands bitumen reserves at the end of 2020, primarily due to "technical revisions" following a year of low oil prices and budget cuts. Its proved plus probable bitumen reserves decreased to 4.46 billion barrels from 5.45 billion barrels. This reduction aligns with a larger trend seen by its majority owner, Exxon Mobil Corp., which also reported a significant drop in worldwide proved oil and gas reserves.

title: Sempra CEO Says ‘Goal’ to Help in Mexico’s Infrastructure Needs
summary: Sempra Energy CEO Jeffrey Martin affirmed the company's commitment to supporting Mexico's infrastructure needs despite regulatory changes, viewing their role as a partner in the government's goals. Martin highlighted the importance of natural gas infrastructure and storage, especially after a recent energy crisis, and confirmed Sempra's continued investment in gas export projects and the $2 billion ECA LNG export terminal. The company reported strong full-year 2020 earnings and has a significant capital plan focused on infrastructure and renewable energy.

title: Kal Tire Mining Tire Group manages recycling of 501 large mining tyres for Imperial Oil Kearl
summary: Kal Tire Mining Tire Group successfully managed the recycling of 501 large mining tires from Imperial Oil's Kearl operation in Alberta. These tires were sent to Liberty Tire LLC for shredding into tire crumb, which is used in various products and fuel. Building on this, Kal Tire has also established a thermal conversion recycling facility in Chile, capable of processing 20 tons per day and converting scrap tires back into fuel oil, steel wire, and carbon black, advancing a circular economy for mining tires.

title: Eastman Chemical Co. stock rises Monday, still underperforms market
summary: Eastman Chemical Co. (EMN) stock rose 2.36% on Monday, closing at $111.84, although it still underperformed the broader market, as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both saw larger gains. The company's stock ended $2.57 below its 52-week high. Trading volume for EMN was 809,892, which was below its 50-day average.

title: ExxonMobil adds 'socially responsible' activist investor Jeffrey Ubben to board
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has appointed two new directors to its board, including activist investor Jeffrey Ubben and former Comcast CFO Michael Angelakis, amidst pressure from activist investors for board changes and a clearer energy transition strategy. While the move aims to refresh the board, one activist fund, Engine No. 1 LLC, still plans a proxy fight for additional board seats, pushing for more diverse expertise in the energy industry. The company also announced a new "low carbon solutions" business unit to invest in emission-lowering technologies like carbon capture and storage.

title: Exxon board adds activist after attacks on returns, climate
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. appointed climate-minded activist investor Jeff Ubben and former Comcast Corp. executive Michael Angelakis to its board following investor criticism over its environmental record and poor capital allocation. These appointments aim to appease shareholders amid a proxy battle with activist investor Engine No. 1 and follow moves by Exxon to address emissions targets and climate disclosure. The company's financial performance has dwindled, with a significant loss in 2020, intensifying pressure from investors for change.

title: TC Energy (TRP) Gets Approval to Acquire TC Pipelines for $1.68B
summary: TC Energy (TRP) has received approval to acquire TC PipeLines, LP (TCP) in a $1.68-billion all-stock deal. The transaction, expected to be effective on March 3rd, will result in TC Energy fully owning TC PipeLines, which will cease to be a publicly held master limited partnership. TC Energy had previously raised its offer for the acquisition due to investor allegations of an insufficient bid.

title: Exxon Mobil to Cut Jobs in Singapore as Big Oil Retrenches
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. plans to cut approximately 300 jobs in Singapore by the end of 2021, representing about 7% of its workforce in the city-state. This move is part of the company's global retrenchment strategy announced last year and follows similar job cuts by other major oil companies like Royal Dutch Shell Plc and Chevron Corp. in Singapore.

title: The latest on our clean air lawsuit against ExxonMobil
summary: A federal judge has issued a record-setting $14.25 million penalty against ExxonMobil for Clean Air Act violations, marking a significant victory after a decade-long legal battle initiated by citizen groups. This ruling reaffirms ExxonMobil's liability for releasing over 10 million pounds of dangerous contaminants and highlights the power of citizen enforcement suits in upholding environmental and public health standards when government regulators fall short. The penalty, while scaled down from an earlier ruling, remains the largest civil penalty ever imposed in a citizen-initiated Clean Air Act suit, emphasizing accountability for polluters.

title: Exxon Mobil to spend billions in low-carbon business line, CEO says
summary: Exxon Mobil plans to invest billions in its low-carbon business line, aiming to capitalize on four emerging tailwinds in the sector. CEO Darren Woods stated the company is focusing on these opportunities. This move comes amidst discussions of a potential megamerger with Chevron and a proxy fight with an activist investor.

title: ExxonMobil names two new board members
summary: ExxonMobil has appointed Michael Angelakis and Jeffrey Ubben to its board of directors, increasing the board to 13 members, 12 of whom are independent. These appointments are part of an ongoing refreshment strategy focused on diverse global business experience, capital allocation, and strategy development. Additionally, Neil Duffin, president of ExxonMobil Global Projects Company, announced his retirement after 41 years with the company, to be succeeded by Jon Gibbs.

title: Michael Angelakis and Jeffrey Ubben join ExxonMobil board of directors
summary: Exxon Mobil Corporation announced that Michael Angelakis and Jeffrey Ubben have joined its board of directors, increasing the board to 13 members, 12 of whom are independent. Angelakis, chairman and CEO of Atairos, and Ubben, co-founder of Inclusive Capital Partners, bring expertise in capital allocation and strategy development. Their appointments are aimed at strengthening ExxonMobil's board as it navigates complex transitions, focuses on increasing shareholder value, and plays a role in the energy transition.

title: Exxon to cut 7% of Singapore workforce amid 'unprecedented market conditions'
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp plans to cut approximately 7% of its workforce in Singapore, affecting about 300 out of 4,000 current jobs by the end of 2021. This decision comes due to "unprecedented market conditions" caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, which led to a historic annual loss for the company in 2020. The Singapore complex, home to Exxon's largest oil refining and petrochemical operations, will remain a strategic location despite the layoffs aimed at improving competitiveness.

title: ExxonMobil Seeks Minimum 30% Returns on New Projects
summary: ExxonMobil has set a target of at least 30% returns on new projects following reductions in capital spending, aiming to rebuild investor confidence. The company expects projects in Guyana and the Permian Basin to generate 10% returns even at oil prices of $35 a barrel or less. This strategy is intended to boost earnings, cash flow, and ensure dividend growth, despite significant debt and past cash burn.

title: Exxon and Macquarie in $11.7 million U.S. lawsuit over gas contract
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is suing Macquarie Energy in a Texas court to avoid paying $11.7 million for missed gas deliveries during last month's winter freeze in the central United States. Exxon argues that the massive storm and state emergency declarations constituted a natural disaster, allowing them to break the contract without penalty. Macquarie Energy, which stands to profit significantly from the record natural gas prices during the cold snap, had rejected Exxon's force majeure claim.

title: Exxon’s CEO sees golden opportunities in carbon capture
summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods views carbon offsets and carbon capture as significant money-making opportunities, especially through partnerships with venture funds. The company's new Low Carbon Solutions business aims to commercialize low-carbon technologies and would benefit from a government-set "transparent and explicit price on carbon." Exxon is looking to leverage external investments and its own capabilities to create a successful business while growing shareholder value in this space.

title: Line 5 'very different' from Keystone XL and Canada will fight hard for it: O'Regan
summary: Canada's Natural Resources Minister, Seamus O'Regan, stated that the federal government would vehemently defend the Line 5 pipeline against Michigan's efforts to shut it down, emphasizing that its operation is "non-negotiable." He distinguished Line 5 from the cancelled Keystone XL project, asserting that Line 5 is a crucial piece of energy infrastructure for both Canada and the U.S. and has operated safely for over 50 years. O'Regan expressed confidence that Enbridge and Michigan would reach an agreement to continue its operation.

title: Saudis bet on the end of fracking's glory days, pushing oil prices higher
summary: Saudi Arabia is making a high-stakes bet that the glory days of U.S. shale oil production are over, choosing to keep oil supplies tight through OPEC+ to boost prices. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman believes American shale producers will prioritize profits over growth and not flood the market, a strategy that has failed in the past. This decision has caused Brent crude to jump to a one-year high, but analysts warn it's a risky move as higher prices could eventually re-incentivize U.S. shale companies to increase output.

title: Feeling Aggressive? This Leveraged Oil ETF May Be for You
summary: Oil prices continue to rise, fueling the Direxion Daily Energy Bull 2X Shares (ERX) ETF, which has seen over 90% year-to-date gains. This surge is attributed to OPEC+'s decision to maintain supply curbs despite global economic recovery and the ongoing worldwide vaccine rollout. Investors looking for aggressive exposure to the energy sector might find ERX appealing, though its relative strength index indicates it is currently in overbought territory.

title: Cold weather played role in crude oil price increase in February
summary: Extreme winter weather, particularly in Texas, significantly contributed to the rise in crude oil and natural gas prices in February, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). The cold temperatures disrupted petroleum supply and increased demand for natural gas, leading to a notable price surge for both commodities. The EIA anticipates market rebalancing in the latter half of 2021 for crude oil and projects increases in U.S. electricity consumption and carbon dioxide emissions for 2021 and 2022.

title: BP set to close Kwinana Refinery in Australia this month
summary: BP is reportedly halting oil imports for its Kwinana Refinery in Western Australia, with plans to close the facility by the end of March 2021. The refinery, once the largest in the country, will be converted into an import terminal. This decision comes after BP deemed the refinery economically unfeasible due to regional oversupply and continuous lower refining margins.

title: Shell To Charter 10 New Dual-Fuel Crude Tankers
summary: Shell has announced agreements to charter ten new dual-fuel liquefied natural gas (LNG) powered crude tankers, with plans for half its long-term chartered crude tankers to run on LNG by 2023. These new vessels, built in South Korea, will feature advanced engines and design for high fuel efficiency and low methane slip, contributing to Shell's fleet decarbonization efforts. This move is significant for the global LNG-fueled fleet and the shipping sector's push towards cleaner fuels.

title: How Mississippi mud might stop La. from disappearing
summary: Louisiana is undertaking a massive $1.5 billion Mid-Barataria sediment diversion project to combat land loss by redirecting Mississippi River flow into Barataria Bay, aiming to build new wetlands. The project faces opposition from local fishers and Lieutenant Governor, who cite concerns about ecosystem harm from changes in salinity and polluted water, and suggest alternative coastal protection methods. Proponents argue it's a critical, long-term solution mirroring natural processes and is necessary given the accelerating rate of land disappearance.

title: What Is the Future of Gas Stations?
summary: This article discusses the evolving landscape of gas stations and convenience stores, emphasizing that despite the rise of electric vehicles, the demand for gasoline and in-store offerings will persist for the foreseeable future. The author highlights significant changes in the industry over the last 30 years and advises convenience store operators to embrace technology, leverage data, and adapt to changing market trends to ensure survival and shape the future of their businesses.

title: Activist Investor Seeks to Remove Ex-CEOs of IBM, Petronas, Caterpillar, MetLife from ExxonMobil Board
summary: Activist investor Engine No. 1 has named four directors it wants removed from ExxonMobil's board during the upcoming annual general meeting, including former CEOs from MetLife, Caterpillar, IBM, and Petronas. The fund argues these directors have "destroyed shareholder value" and appointed Wan Zulkiflee, former CEO of Petronas, is not relevant given Exxon's need for transformative energy experience. ExxonMobil, however, defended its board members, stating they bring valuable expertise from leading large, complex companies.

title: 21 Republican-led states sue Biden over Keystone XL rejection
summary: Twenty-one Republican-led states, including Texas and Montana, are suing President Joe Biden over his decision to revoke the Keystone XL pipeline permit. The lawsuit argues that Biden exceeded his authority by revoking the permit on his first day in office, citing a 2011 tax legislation provision related to presidential approval of the pipeline. Many of the same states also sued Biden last month over a climate executive order that increased the calculation of the "social cost of carbon."

title: N.L. hopes rise for future of Terra Nova field as Suncor and partners consider overhaul
summary: Newfoundland and Labrador is seeing increased optimism for the future of the Terra Nova oil field as Suncor and its partners consider an overhaul. The provincial government is willing to extend a deadline on a $175 million public money injection and potentially offer royalty relief to secure a long-term production plan. While no deal is finalized, discussions are ongoing among the seven partners, with the provincial energy minister expressing positive sentiment for the project's resumption.

title: How Qatari Investments Expand Globally
summary: Qatar, a small country rich in natural gas, has become a significant global investor through its Sovereign Wealth Fund (QIA). The country holds substantial shares in various international markets, companies, and financial institutions, with a focus on long-term investments and gaining political legitimacy. Its foreign direct investments reached $44.78 billion in 2019, with significant portions in the EU, the U.S., and the U.K., influencing sectors from automotive and finance to technology and real estate.

title: First Crude Cargo from Guyana to India Sets Sail
summary: The first crude oil cargo from Guyana, a new oil producer, has departed for India, the world's third-largest crude importer, aboard a vessel chartered by Trafigura. This move aligns with India's strategy to diversify its oil imports and reduce dependency on Middle Eastern crude after OPEC+ extended production cuts. The cargo of Liza light sweet crude is destined for India's Mundra port, arriving around April 8.

title: There’s $120 Billion at Stake in an Overlooked War in Mozambique
summary: An Islamic State-linked insurgency in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province is jeopardizing up to $120 billion in natural-gas investments, including projects by Total SE and Exxon Mobil Corp. Total halted work on its $20 billion project after an attack on Palma, the closest town to its site, despite recent assurances from the government. Exxon Mobil has also delayed its adjacent project, raising concerns about the viability of Africa’s largest private investment.

title: Grupo Ecopetrol anuncia compromiso y plan para lograr cero emisiones netas de carbono en 2050
summary: Grupo Ecopetrol has committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 for scopes 1 and 2, becoming the first oil and gas company in Latin America to set this ambitious goal. The company also aims for a 25% reduction in CO2e emissions by 2030 compared to 2019 levels and a 50% reduction in total emissions (scopes 1, 2, and 3) by 2050. This plan involves a comprehensive decarbonization strategy including efficiency improvements, renewable energies, natural climate solutions, hydrogen, and carbon capture technologies.

title: Chesapeake Agrees to $1.9M Fine for Wetlands Violations at Pennsylvania Oil, Gas Sites
summary: Chesapeake Appalachia LLC has agreed to pay a $1.9 million fine and implement a compliance program to address environmental impacts from failing to identify and protect wetlands at 76 oil and gas well sites in Pennsylvania. The settlement, a result of a voluntary disclosure by Chesapeake in 2014, requires the restoration of affected wetlands and streams. This agreement was reached with the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, and the U.S. Department of Justice.

title: Drillers Burned Off Gas at a Staggering Rate as Winter Storm Hit Texas
summary: During the winter storm in Texas, drillers in the Permian Basin were forced to burn off an estimated 1.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas in a single day, a fivefold increase from pre-crisis rates. This flaring occurred because pipelines froze and power plants went offline, leaving nowhere for the gas to go. Satellite analysis confirms this as one of the highest spikes in flaring ever observed in the region.

title: Can FuelCell Energy’s molten carbonate fuel cell help solve the CO₂ problem?
summary: FuelCell Energy (FCE) is developing a molten carbonate fuel cell (MCFC) that can capture CO2 from power plant flue gas while generating additional electricity. This technology offers an alternative to traditional, energy-intensive carbon capture methods, potentially reducing costs and allowing existing energy infrastructure to meet emissions demands. Despite challenges including financial losses and project setbacks, FCE is transitioning from an R&D company to a commercial provider, with investor interest growing due to its carbon capture and reversible hydrogen fuel cell solutions.

title: Exxon Mobil signals first profit in five quarters on price gains
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is poised to report its first profit in five quarters, driven by higher oil and gas prices which could boost earnings by up to $2.7 billion. Despite an estimated $800 million in damages from the February deep freeze, the company's financial outlook has improved. Refining remains a troubled sector, but the chemicals division is expected to see a significant profit increase over the previous quarter.

title: Exxon Sees Up to $800 Million Earnings Hit From Texas Freeze
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. anticipates a reduction of up to $800 million in its first-quarter earnings due to the severe Texas freeze last month. Despite this impact, the oil major likely returned to profit after four consecutive quarters of losses. Higher oil and natural gas prices, along with improved refining and chemical margins, are expected to boost earnings, offsetting the financial hit from the freeze.

title: Court Affirms Dismissal of NYC Climate Suit
summary: The Second Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of New York City's climate change lawsuit against major oil companies, ruling that the Clean Air Act governs domestic emissions and foreign policy concerns preclude judicial intervention in regulating foreign emissions. The court emphasized that federal common law displaces state law in this context, deeming global warming a "uniquely international problem of national concern" unsuitable for state nuisance law. This decision contrasts with other courts allowing state-level climate suits, highlighting ongoing litigation regarding climate change liability.

title: Six Ways Chevron Imperils Climate, Human Rights, and Racial Justice
summary: The article details six ways Chevron negatively impacts climate, human rights, and racial justice, including its failure to reduce emissions, foot-dragging on climate policy, greenwashing, and perpetuating racial injustice. It also highlights Chevron's support for the Burma/Myanmar military and its evasion of accountability in Ecuador, urging stockholders to hold the company responsible.

title: Fossil Fuel Companies Took Billions in U.S. Coronavirus Relief Funds but Still Cut Nearly 60,000 Jobs
summary: A new analysis by BailoutWatch reveals that dozens of fossil fuel companies received $8.2 billion in tax benefits through the CARES Act in 2020 but still cut nearly 60,000 jobs. This contradicts the stated intent of Congress to maintain employment, as companies like Marathon Petroleum ($2.1 billion in benefits, nearly 2,000 jobs cut) and NOV ($591 million, nearly 8,000 jobs cut) prioritized cash flow and shareholder rewards. The article highlights that these tax changes, while not explicitly targeting the oil industry, uniquely benefited them due to their volatile earnings.

title: ExxonMobil PESTLE Analysis - Detailed PESTEL Factors
summary: This article provides a detailed PESTLE analysis of ExxonMobil, examining the political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental factors influencing its operations. It highlights how these external forces impact the company's strategies, profitability, and resilience in the global oil and gas industry. The analysis covers aspects like government policies, global economic conditions, changing consumer preferences, technological advancements, regulatory frameworks, and environmental consciousness.

title: Exxon sues Energy Transfer over charges from pipeline dispute
summary: Exxon Mobil's XTO Energy shale unit has filed a breach of contract lawsuit against Energy Transfer LP over disputed payments related to the Dakota Access Pipeline. The suit claims Energy Transfer hit XTO with deficiency charges and revoked credits after Exxon shifted oil to other outlets following a U.S. court order to shut down DAPL. Exxon is seeking over $1 million in damages, return of revoked credits, and attorneys' fees.

title: World's biggest oil producers
summary: This article lists the top 10 oil-producing countries globally as of April 2021, detailing their daily output and recent production trends. It highlights the US as the leading producer, followed by Russia and Saudi Arabia, and discusses key factors influencing their production, such as the 2020 price collapse and OPEC agreements.

title: Occidental CEO Hollub opposes a carbon tax despite rivals' support for idea
summary: Occidental Petroleum CEO Vicki Hollub has voiced her opposition to a carbon tax, despite the backing it has received from major rival oil companies and some trade groups. Hollub argues that a carbon tax would negatively impact a significant portion of the industry, consumers, and particularly economically disadvantaged individuals. Meanwhile, Occidental is pursuing ambitious climate targets and is trying to make its low-carbon unit profitable.

title: MRC Global marks its centennial more with relief than revelry
summary: MRC Global, a leading distributor of pipe, valves, and fittings to the energy industry, is celebrating its centennial with a new CEO and a sense of optimism after a challenging year. The company recorded a significant loss in 2020 due to plunging oil prices and the pandemic but is now seeing improvements. They are also preparing for the industry's shift towards alternative energy sources.

title: Enbridge CEO says opposition to new pipelines adds value to those already in the ground
summary: The CEO of Enbridge Inc., Al Monaco, believes that opposition to new pipeline construction increases the value of existing pipelines, as North American energy demand is expected to rise. He specifically mentioned the $9.3-billion Line 3 replacement project, which is anticipated to be in service by Q4 this year despite challenges, and the ongoing legal battle over the Line 5 pipeline in Michigan. Monaco also noted that the company is progressing in the global energy transition with new businesses and aims for significant emissions reductions.

title: Terror attacks bring Mozambique gas projects to a halt
summary: Terrorist attacks in northern Mozambique, specifically the town of Palma, have halted natural gas projects worth approximately $60 billion. This disruption, attributed to Islamic State-backed terrorists, has resulted in numerous casualties and displaced over 100,000 people, causing a significant setback for the region's economic development and South African companies involved in the projects like Total and Sasol. The ongoing insurgency, which has been gaining momentum since 2017, is leading to increased security concerns and project costs, raising questions about stability and the future of these crucial energy initiatives.

title: Exxon says it may close down its oil refinery in Norway
summary: Exxon is considering closing its Slagen oil refinery in Norway and converting the site into an import terminal. The company cites falling demand for refined products, strong competition, and market overcapacity in Europe, exacerbated by Norway's high adoption rate of electric cars leading to decreased demand for road transportation fuels. A final decision timeframe is not yet clear.

title: This oil sands crude has lower GHG emissions intensity than the U.S. average
summary: Some oil sands crude, specifically that produced using paraffinic froth treatment (PFT), has a lower greenhouse gas emissions intensity than the average oil consumed in the U.S. This reduction is attributed to new technology and improved processes, with PFT effectively removing energy-intensive components before further processing. The overall emissions intensity of oil sands mining significantly decreased between 2017 and 2018, primarily due to the ramp-up of new projects like Suncor's Fort Hills.

title: COVID-19 surge complicates busy maintenance season for Canada's oil sands
summary: Canada's oil sands face challenges during their busy annual maintenance season due to a third wave of COVID-19, making workers reluctant to travel. Despite companies introducing rapid testing and travel assistance, finding skilled tradespeople is difficult with several oil sands sites fighting outbreaks. This could impact maintenance schedules crucial for regulatory compliance and safety, potentially affecting crude output.

title: Tegna shareholder says company has pattern of racial bias, insensitivity
summary: A major Tegna shareholder, Standard General, is calling for an investigation into alleged patterns of racial bias and insensitive behavior within the company. This demand follows media reports and an anonymous letter from a former employee detailing numerous incidents of discrimination. Tegna has acknowledged it's not perfect but claims significant progress in diversity, equity, and inclusion, dismissing Standard General's claims as an attempt to advance a proxy fight.

title: Exxon Mobil Will Keep Paying Its Dividend, And May Be Worth 30% More
summary: Exxon Mobil is committed to maintaining its dividend, offering a strong 6.15% yield. Based on historical dividend yield, P/E, and P/Sales multiples, XOM stock is estimated to be undervalued by approximately 30-34%, suggesting a target price significantly higher than its current trading value. While most analysts have more conservative short-term targets, the article argues for a long-term potential for significant returns, including dividend income.

title: US oil output climbs toward level not seen since pandemic’s start
summary: US crude oil production, particularly in the Permian Basin, is nearing pre-pandemic levels as higher prices and increased travel demand boost drillers' confidence. Output in the Permian Basin is projected to reach 4.466 million barrels a day in May, the highest in a year. Despite this recovery, experts suggest it will be challenging for US oil and gas production to return to its peak of over 13 million barrels a day due to producers prioritizing shareholder dividends over increased spending.

title: Can You Ship Wind Turbines by Train?
summary: This article highlights how railroads, particularly Union Pacific, efficiently and safely transport oversized wind turbine components across long distances. It emphasizes rail's advantages over truck transportation, such as safety, efficiency, reduced environmental impact, and avoiding complex road regulations. The piece also details the meticulous planning and specialized equipment involved in shipping these large components, underscoring the vital role rail plays in the growing wind energy market.

title: Exxon Mobil has agreed to reduce air pollution at refinery near Chicago - U.S. Justice Department
summary: Exxon Mobil has reached an agreement with U.S. and Illinois regulators to significantly reduce air pollution at its refinery near Chicago. The consent decree requires operational changes to its sulfur recovery plant and a payment of over $1.5 million in penalties, plus an estimated $10 million in improvements to reduce emissions. This action signals the Biden administration's commitment to cracking down on major polluters.

title: New York State Pension Fund Divesting From Oil Sands Companies Without an Energy Transition Plan
summary: The New York State Common Retirement Fund, with $248 billion in assets, announced it will divest over $7 million from seven oil sands companies lacking viable energy transition plans. This move aligns with the fund's goal to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040 and follows a prior divestment from coal companies. State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli highlighted the significant investment risks posed by companies in carbon-intensive industries without adaptation strategies.

title: Selling Its Alaskan Oil Business Was a Green Win for BP—Not the Planet
summary: BP's sale of its Alaskan oil business to Hilcorp, a private company, was touted as a move towards its net-zero emissions goal, allowing BP to significantly reduce its reported carbon footprint. However, critics argue that such divestment merely shifts emissions to less transparent operators, like Hilcorp and Ineos, who are not subject to the same public disclosure requirements and may even increase production and emissions from these older assets. This practice, often seen as "greenwashing," makes it harder to track global emissions and undermines the goals of climate accords, raising questions about whether significant strides towards environmental sustainability are truly being made.

title: Texas energy companies push back against Berkshire Hathaway’s $8 billion plan for backup power
summary: Texas energy companies are opposing an $8.3 billion plan by Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Energy to build 10 new natural gas power plants for emergency use, a proposal introduced as legislation following severe winter storm outages. Critics argue the plan, which would be funded by monthly charges on Texans' power bills, creates an unfair economic advantage and deviates from the state's deregulated electricity market. Despite the opposition, lawmakers and Berkshire executives are continuing discussions, with Berkshire Hathaway Energy having invested significantly in lobbying efforts.

title: Insight: Clean crude? Oil firms use offsets to claim green barrels
summary: Oil and gas companies are increasingly using carbon offsets and other methods to market their products as "cleaner" or "carbon-neutral." While proponents argue these credits fund clean energy, critics contend it's a public relations tactic that allows polluters to avoid meaningful emission reductions. The industry hopes to create a market for these purportedly cleaner fuels to command higher prices, despite a lack of uniform standards and the fact that most emissions occur after extraction.

title: Chemical Used in Many Oil Refineries Could Cause Mass Deaths If Leaked
summary: An investigation reveals that modified hydrofluoric acid (MHF), used in many oil refineries, poses a significant danger to nearby residents, with a potential leak causing mass casualties. Despite industry claims of safety, experts argue that MHF is nearly identical to deadly hydrofluoric acid (HF) and could form a flesh-eating vapor cloud. Community activists and local officials are pushing for a ban on these chemicals, highlighting past incidents and the inadequacy of current safety measures, particularly in earthquake-prone areas.

title: Tesla Runs on Faith, Exxon Runs on Discipline. Only One Is Right
summary: This article contrasts the leadership styles and visions of Elon Musk of Tesla and Darren Woods of Exxon Mobil regarding the future of energy. Musk is portrayed as a publicity-driven Technoking with diverse ventures, while Woods is presented as a low-profile, disciplined CEO. The piece suggests that despite their companies having "similar belief premiums," their approaches are fundamentally incompatible.

title: Exxon Mobil makes a pitch for capturing emissions and a carbon price.
summary: Exxon Mobil has proposed a $100 billion project to capture carbon emissions from industrial plants along the Houston Ship Channel and store them beneath the Gulf of Mexico. The company aims to profit from carbon capture but requires significant government support, including a carbon price or tax. This initiative, which Exxon discussed with policymakers, faces the challenge of incentivizing businesses to pay for carbon capture without a direct price on emissions.

title: Exxon proposes massive $100B CCS project
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has proposed a massive $100 billion carbon capture "innovation zone" near Houston to trap and store industrial emissions. The project aims to be a large-scale collaboration between government, industry, academia, and local communities, with a goal of capturing roughly 50 million metric tons of CO2 per year by 2030. This initiative aligning with the Biden administration's push for more carbon capture infrastructure, drawing parallels to the "Storing CO2 And Lowering Emissions (SCALE) Act."

title: Diverse workforce brought HPE headquarters to Houston, CEO says
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise CEO Antonio Neri stated that the primary reason for moving the company's headquarters to Houston was to tap into the city's diverse talent pool. Neri, an immigrant himself, believes that diverse companies perform better and sees Houston's demographics, as well as its educational institutions, as key assets for HPE's long-term growth and leadership diversity. Additionally, HPE's involvement in COVID-19 vaccine research using its high-performance computing systems was highlighted.

title: News - Braskem joins Cyclyx as Founding Member
summary: Braskem has joined Cyclyx International as a founding member, aiming to increase plastic recyclability from 10% to 90%. Geoffrey Inch, Braskem's Sustainability and Circular Economy Director, will also join the Cyclyx Executive Advisory Board. This partnership enhances Braskem's commitment to a Carbon Neutral Circular Economy and the development of certified circular polypropylene.

title: XI Technologies: Duvernay Overview
summary: This article from XI Technologies provides an overview of the Duvernay play, focusing specifically on the North Duvernay region around Fox Creek/Kaybob South. It analyzes asset ownership, highlighting Chevron, Shell (now Crescent Point Energy), and ExxonMobil as key players, and discusses the recent production history and liabilities associated with the play. The piece also promotes an upcoming webinar for those interested in learning more about analyzing regions within the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin.

title: NYC Sues Exxon, Shell, BP for Ads Calling Products ‘Cleaner’
summary: New York City has sued Exxon Mobil Corp., Royal Dutch Shell Plc, BP Plc, and the American Petroleum Institute, alleging deceptive advertising practices. The lawsuit claims the companies ran ads calling their products "cleaner" and "emissions-reducing" without disclosing their harmful effects on the climate. The city accuses them of systematically deceiving New Yorkers about the role of fossil fuels in climate change.

title: Does The Energy Sector and "ERX" Still Have Room to Run?
summary: The S&P 500 Energy index and the Direxion Daily Energy Bull 3X Shares (ERX) have shown significant strength in 2021, with ERX up 56%. Analysts suggest the sector still has room to run, supported by a bullish oil report from the International Energy Agency (IEA) and anticipated global demand growth despite potential fragility from rising COVID-19 cases. The IEA revised up global oil demand for 2021 and expects strong demand growth in the latter half of the year.

title: Shareholders Are Pressing for Climate Risk Disclosures. That’s Good for Everyone.
summary: Shareholders are increasingly demanding that companies disclose their climate change-related risks. Major corporations like BP, Exxon Mobil, Occidental Petroleum, and PPL Corporation have seen shareholder proposals accepted on this matter, and a record number of such proposals are expected this year. This trend, despite proposals often receiving limited initial support, signifies a growing investor focus on the financial implications of climate change.

title: $280MM ExxonMobil Cuba Lawsuit Can Proceed
summary: A U.S. judge has ruled that ExxonMobil can proceed with its $280 million lawsuit against two Cuban companies for assets seized after the 1959 Cuban revolution. The lawsuit, filed after the Trump administration allowed private claims for expropriated property in Cuba, seeks compensation for a refinery and other assets. The Cuban companies' attempt to dismiss the suit based on sovereign immunity was rejected for one company, and ExxonMobil can gather more evidence for the other.

title: Eastman Chemical Co. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Eastman Chemical Co. (EMN) saw its stock rise by 2.55% to $113.60 on Friday, outperforming the broader market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The company's stock closed just shy of its 52-week high and also outperformed competitors such as Exxon Mobil Corp., 3M Co., and FMC Corp. Trading volume for Eastman Chemical Co. exceeded its 50-day average.

title: NextEra Energy Is One of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies | TIME
summary: NextEra Energy has been named one of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies, following a period of significant growth and market outperformance. The utility company, which is the world's largest generator of wind and solar power, briefly surpassed ExxonMobil in market capitalization, demonstrating the profitability of renewable energy. NextEra is expected to invest tens of billions more in renewable energy by 2022, with 35% of its electricity already sourced from wind and solar.

title: CalPERS to back activist’s four director nominees in Exxon board fight
summary: The California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS) announced its support for Engine No. 1's four director nominees in their proxy fight against Exxon Mobil Corp. CalPERS, a major shareholder, cited ExxonMobil's long-term financial underperformance and the need for new expertise, particularly in clean energy, as reasons for its decision. This move adds significant weight to Engine No. 1's challenge ahead of Exxon's annual meeting.

title: The 5 Most Influential Oil Companies In The World
summary: This article identifies the five most influential oil companies globally, highlighting their revenue, net income, and market cap. It discusses their operations, strategies in response to climate goals, and regional dominance, noting that Chinese and European companies lead in revenue, while Saudi Aramco is the most valuable by market cap. The article also touches on the shift towards green energy for some major players and the broader implications of global climate targets on the oil and gas industry.

title: Avenir LNG’s duo meet off Malaysia ahead of Sardinian terminal launch
summary: Avenir LNG's two dual-purpose bunkering and supply vessels met offshore Malaysia as one prepares to commission the Higas small-scale terminal in Sardinia. The Avenir Advantage supplied LNG to the Avenir Accolade, which will now travel to Europe to launch the Higas terminal, marking the first such facility in Italy. This event marks a significant step for Avenir LNG's operations and the Italian LNG infrastructure.

title: East Lateral Xpress Louisiana Compressor Project Gets Green Light
summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) has granted a favorable environmental assessment for Columbia Gulf Transmission LLC's East Lateral Xpress project, designed to provide 725,000 dekatherms per day of firm natural gas transportation capacity to Venture Global LNG's Plaquemines facility. The project involves building two new compressor stations, Centerville and Golden Meadow, both equipped with Solar Titan 130 gas-fired turbine compressor units, along with new pipelines and ancillary facilities across several Louisiana parishes. It aims to enhance natural gas delivery through Columbia Gulf’s interstate pipeline system.

title: West Saturn to drill on the Bacalhau field in Brazil
summary: Equinor Brasil Energia Ltda has awarded Seadrill Management S PTE Ltd a four-year contract for drilling on the Bacalhau field in Brazil, contingent on a final investment decision. The contract, valued at USD 380 million, aims to drill six wells leading to production start in 2024 and includes performance elements for efficiency. The Bacalhau field is Equinor's deepest high-pressure field and will be the first greenfield pre-salt development by an international operator.

title: BP Execs Coy About Texas Freeze Impact on Gas Trading
summary: BP Plc reported an "exceptional" first quarter, largely due to its gas trading unit benefiting from the winter freeze in Texas, which caused natural gas prices to skyrocket. While executives remained tight-lipped about the exact figures, analysts estimate significant gains for BP, the largest physical gas supplier in the U.S., contrasting with some peers who expect losses from the same event. The company indicated it would provide more guidance on its trading unit's contribution to returns annually, starting next year, despite the secretive nature of these operations.

title: BP Seeks to Sell Electricity in Five States
summary: BP Plc is pursuing permission to become a retail electricity provider in Illinois, Ohio, Texas, California, and Pennsylvania, signaling a strategic shift into the power market. This move allows the oil and natural gas giant to leverage its existing power trading operations and branding, as the global energy sector moves towards electrification and renewable sources. This follows a trend among major energy companies, with Royal Dutch Shell Plc also aiming to be a leading power generator.

title: $380MM Brazil Drilling Contract Goes to Seadrill
summary: Seadrill Limited has secured a four-year firm contract, valued at approximately $380 million, for its West Saturn drillship to work on the Bacalhau field in Brazil for Equinor Brasil Energia Ltda. The contract's total value is contingent on the final investment decision by Equinor and its partners, Exxon Mobil Corp. and Petrogal Brasil. Seadrill plans to implement significant upgrades to the drillship, including a combined hydrogen and methanol injection system, to enhance efficiency and reduce fuel consumption by 10-15%.

title: ExxonMobil makes 19th oil discovery off Guyana's coast
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced its 19th oil discovery offshore Guyana at the Uaru-2 well in the Stabroek Block. This discovery further solidifies Guyana's importance to Exxon's future oil output plans. The consortium, including Hess Corp and CNOOC Ltd, has been developing this significant oil and gas block since production began in 2019.

title: Timeline: Looking back at departing Chesapeake Energy CEO Doug Lawler's time with the company
summary: This article provides a timeline of major events during Doug Lawler's tenure as CEO of Chesapeake Energy, from his appointment in 2013 to his departure in 2021. It highlights the company's efforts to reduce debt, its oil expansion, the Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing and subsequent emergence, and the renaming of Chesapeake Energy Arena. Lawler's time was marked by significant financial challenges and strategic shifts to keep the company afloat.

title: UAE Wealth Fund to Buy Share of Israeli Gas Field
summary: Mubadala, the UAE's sovereign wealth fund, plans to acquire a 22 percent stake in Israel's Tamar offshore natural gas field from Delek for $1.1 billion. This deal, the largest commercial agreement since the Abraham Accords, significantly advances the UAE's diplomatic and energy profile in the Mediterranean region. The acquisition faces geopolitical complexities, including Palestinian opposition and regional rivalries, while highlighting the broader growth of East Mediterranean energy production.

title: Stabroek partners find more oil at Uaru offshore Guyana
summary: ExxonMobil, Hess, and CNOOC have discovered more oil at the Uaru-2 well in the Stabroek block offshore Guyana, adding to the existing recoverable resource of over 9 Bboe. The Uaru-2 discovery enhances development opportunities and the company anticipates at least six projects online by 2027 with potential for up to 10 FPSOs. Production from Liza Phase 1 was curtailed due to a minor leak but is expected to return to nameplate capacity after repairs.

title: Enbridge CLO discusses ESG goals as energy sector creeps towards recovery
summary: The Canadian oil and gas industry is recovering in 2021 after a challenging 2020, driven by improving oil prices and increased efficiency. This recovery is coupled with growing pressure for ESG accountability from investors and stakeholders, leading companies like Enbridge to set ambitious environmental and social targets. In-house counsel are crucial in navigating the changing regulatory landscape, ensuring compliance with ESG commitments, and supporting safe economic recovery within the industry.

title: CrossAmerica to Acquire 106 C-Stores From 7-Eleven
summary: CrossAmerica Partners LP has agreed to acquire 106 convenience store properties from 7-Eleven Inc. for $263 million. These properties are part of 7-Eleven's divestiture process following its acquisition of Speedway from Marathon Petroleum Corp. The acquisition is expected to be immediately accretive to CrossAmerica's distributable cash flow.

title: Exxon posts a profit, snapping four-quarter loss streak
summary: Exxon Mobil reported a return to profitability in the first quarter of 2021, exceeding analysts' expectations for both earnings and revenue. This turnaround was driven by recovering oil prices and significant cost-cutting measures, ending a streak of four consecutive quarterly losses. The company is, however, facing ongoing pressure from activist investor Engine No. 1 regarding its board composition and strategy for a low-carbon future.

title: Canada's Imperial Oil swings to quarterly profit, helped by oil price recovery
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. reported a first-quarter profit of C$392 million, reversing a loss from the previous quarter, and raised its quarterly dividend by 23%. This turnaround was driven by higher crude prices and improved refining and chemical margins, despite lingering impacts of the pandemic on product demand. The company also achieved its highest first-quarter upstream production in 30 years.

title: Exxon Set to Lock Out Union Employees at Texas Oil Refinery
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is preparing to lock out union workers at its Beaumont, Texas refinery on Saturday after failing to reach a new labor agreement with the United Steelworkers. Despite the union's counteroffers and desire to continue negotiations, Exxon rejected their proposals. In response, the union plans to picket the refinery, asserting the lockout is illegal, rather than initiate a strike.

title: Exxon issued lockout notice at Texas oil refinery due to strike fears-manager
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp issued a lockout notice to union workers at its Beaumont, Texas refinery, effective Saturday, due to fears of a strike. The company stated this measure ensures it retains control of the facility and allows its skilled team to maintain safe operations. This action follows the union's failure to bring the company's contract proposal to a membership vote, and it would be the first worker lockout at the plant since 1988.

title: Exxon, Chevron generate most free cash flow in over a year
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. recorded their highest free cash flow in over a year, driven by rallying crude prices and increased demand for chemicals, despite losses in their refining sectors. Both companies covered their dividends, largely due to significant spending cuts, signaling a turn for the energy sector after a challenging period. Although profits met expectations, Chevron's stock fell as investors hoped for renewed share buybacks, and Exxon’s stock also declined despite blunted refining losses by chemical profits.

title: Record metals prices catapult mining profits beyond big oil
summary: Record-high metals prices, particularly for iron ore and copper, have propelled mining company profits beyond those of major oil producers for the first time in decades. The top five iron ore miners are projected to earn 13% more than the five biggest international oil producers this year, flipping a long-standing industry hierarchy. This shift indicates a broader inflationary trend in the global economy and highlights the increasing financial appeal of mining companies, partly due to their role in green technologies, compared to oil producers facing climate change concerns.

title: TTF, JKM Move Higher as Asia, Europe Compete for Natural Gas -- LNG Recap
summary: European and Asian natural gas prices increased due to competition for supplies, driven by cold European weather and rising JKM futures. European storage levels are low, exacerbated by reduced pipeline imports and concerns over Russian supply. The tight global gas market is also benefiting LNG shipping, with vessel rates climbing, while new LNG infrastructure projects and maintenance issues at existing plants in the US and Australia are also noted.

title: Worlds biggest oil producers
summary: The article details the world's top ten oil-producing countries as of May 2021, with the US, Russia, and Saudi Arabia leading. It discusses how the global pandemic and the Saudi-Russia price war impacted oil prices and production patterns. The piece also provides insights into each country's production volume, recent changes, and factors influencing their output.

title: Climate activists urge BlackRock, Vanguard to vote against Exxon directors
summary: Climate activist groups are pressing BlackRock and Vanguard, top shareholders in Exxon Mobil Corp, to vote against the re-election of CEO Darren Woods and lead independent director Kenneth Frazier. This push aims to support activist hedge fund Engine No. 1's proxy fight to secure board seats and influence Exxon's transition to cleaner energy, which activists argue is necessary given Exxon's poor returns on fossil fuels and lack of a clear climate strategy. BlackRock and Vanguard, both signatories of the Net Zero Asset Managers Initiative, have not commented on their voting intentions.

title: ConocoPhillips returns to profitability, plans to cut $5 billion of debt in 5 years
summary: ConocoPhillips reported its first profitable quarter since the global pandemic began, earning $1 billion in the first quarter of 2021 compared to a $1.7 billion loss a year prior. This return to profitability is attributed to higher crude prices, an increase in Cenovus Energy stock, and successful asset sales. The company also announced plans to reduce its gross debt by $5 billion over the next five years and sell its Cenovus Energy shares by the end of 2022 to fund share buybacks.

title: About
summary: This article commemorates the 100th anniversary of Barron's, reflecting on its history since its founding in 1921 by Clarence W. Barron. It highlights the publication's role in financial journalism, its founder's vision of scrutinizing Wall Street, and its coverage of significant economic and societal shifts over the past century. Additionally, it looks ahead to future reporting and celebrates Barron's legacy through awards and archived content.

title: Cheniere Logs Record LNG Cargoes Despite Winter Storm Uri
summary: Cheniere Energy Inc. reported record liquefied natural gas (LNG) cargo exports in the first quarter of 2021, despite disruptions caused by Winter Storm Uri. The company shipped 133 cargoes totaling 480 TBtu, an increase from the previous year, partly due to commissioning volumes from its Corpus Christi facility. Cheniere also highlighted a tightening global LNG market, strong demand for midterm agreements, and its debut in the carbon-neutral LNG market with a cargo delivered to Royal Dutch Shell plc.

title: Diamondback Sees No ‘Clear Signal’ to Boost Permian Output
summary: Diamondback Energy Inc. CEO Travis Stice stated that the company has no plans to increase oil output in the Permian Basin this year due to the control exerted by OPEC-plus over the market and the uncertain global oil demand recovery. Despite recent acquisitions, Diamondback will maintain pro forma fourth-quarter 2020 production levels through 2021. The company is also focusing on significant environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives to reduce gas flaring and greenhouse gas emissions, aiming for a 50% reduction in Scope 1 GHG intensity by 2024.

title: Exxon expects $200 mln in charges this year for job cuts
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp expects up to $200 million in charges this year related to job cuts as part of its cost-saving efforts, with total cash outflows estimated to be between $400 million and $600 million. The company's workforce reductions are expected to be "substantially complete" by year-end, leading to anticipated annual cost savings of $1 billion to $2 billion compared to 2019 levels. Exxon, which reported its first annual loss last year due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on energy demand, has been slashing costs and delaying projects.

title: Top 10 Leading Hot Melt Adhesive Manufacturers in the World
summary: This article identifies the top 10 leading hot melt adhesive manufacturers globally, detailing their company profiles, key achievements, and recent strategic moves. It highlights the advantages of hot melt adhesives over solvent-based ones and discusses the market's expected growth to USD 9,702.2 million by 2027, despite the initial impact of COVID-19 on the automotive and packaging sectors. The future of the market is seen as bright due to technological advancements and wide industrial applications.

title: Will Okla. disrupt Biden’s 100% clean energy goal?
summary: Oklahoma's strong reliance on natural gas for electricity generation poses a challenge to President Biden's goal of achieving 100% clean electricity by 2035, despite the state's significant wind energy production and efforts to reduce carbon emissions. While state leaders aim to foster renewables and cut emissions, they are not planning to abandon natural gas soon, setting up a potential conflict with federal climate policies. The February 2021 winter storm highlighted both the vulnerabilities of the power grid and the state's continued commitment to natural gas as a critical component of its energy mix alongside growing renewable sources.

title: Alberta temporarily tweaks environmental liability for oil sands mines
summary: Alberta has temporarily adjusted how oil sands mining companies calculate environmental liabilities for 2021. This change addresses the impact of wild oil price swings in 2020 which would have otherwise forced companies to pay billions in additional security. The province plans to implement a longer-term solution next year.

title: Exxon Outvotes Other Shareholders to Beat Back Net-Zero Resolution for Imperial Oil
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. shareholders, led by parent company ExxonMobil, voted to defeat a resolution for the company to adopt a net-zero carbon emissions target by 2050. While ExxonMobil owns 69.6% of Imperial, 58% of other shareholders voted in favor of the resolution, highlighting a rift. Imperial's CEO stated that such a long-term target is premature without clear, achievable steps, focusing instead on a 2023 emissions reduction goal.

title: How a Century of Moments Built MRC Global
summary: This article chronicles the 100-year history of MRC Global, a leading PVF distributor, tracing its evolution from Jerry McJunkin's initial company in 1921 to its current global presence. It highlights key moments like mergers, strategic acquisitions, and investments in technology like the Houston Operations Complex and the MRCGO e-commerce platform. The article emphasizes how the company has adapted to industry changes, customer needs, and economic cycles, positioning itself for future success under new leadership.

title: News Content Hub - Qatar bets billions on the future of LNG
summary: Qatar is making a significant investment in the future of LNG, planning to increase its liquefaction capacity by over 40%, invest in more than 100 LNG carriers, and integrate CO2 capture and sequestration (CCS) technology. This expansion is centered on the North Field East (NFE) project, with a second phase, North Field South (NFS), also planned, aiming to boost Qatar's total LNG production capacity to 126 million tonnes per annum. The country is also embarking on a massive shipbuilding program for LNG carriers and consolidating ownership of its initial LNG joint venture.

title: Wide Open Spaces, Part 4 - How Plains' Crane Terminals Help Move Permian Crude Oil to Market
summary: This article, part of the "Wide Open Spaces" series, explores the crucial role of Plains All American's crude oil terminals in Crane, TX, for balancing Permian crude oil delivery and offering destination optionality. It highlights how the interconnectivity of Plains' infrastructure, including gathering systems and long-haul pipelines, provides significant value. The piece also touches on the growth of Permian crude oil takeaway and storage capacity, raising questions about whether current storage is sufficient given expected production levels and operational needs.

title: Full-year US chemical results show an industry hit by COVID-19
summary: The article details how the COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted the top 50 US chemical producers in 2020, leading to a 10.1% drop in combined chemical sales and an even sharper decline of 15.6% in profits for those reporting operating income. Companies reacted by cutting capital spending, with some product demands like polyethylene seeing increases. The report also highlights changes in the ranking due to mergers, acquisitions, and new entrants.

title: Big Oil Is In Desperate Need Of New Discoveries
summary: Driven by a global pandemic, demand shocks, and a shift towards renewable energy, major oil companies like ExxonMobil and Shell saw significant reductions in their proven reserves in 2020. Rystad Energy warns that these reserves could run out in less than 15 years if new discoveries aren't made, a situation exacerbated by shrinking exploration investments and increasing climate activism.
