Both companies aim to integrate bio-based feedstocks like vegetable oils into current refining processes to create renewable diesel, sustainable aviation fuel, and renewable gasoline. This strategy allows them to leverage existing infrastructure and avoid costly refinery reconfigurations seen with some competitors, addressing criticism for a slower adoption of green technologies compared to European rivals.

title: Is Woodside the next South32?
summary: BHP is expected to announce the spin-off of its oil and gas assets to Woodside, similar to how it created South32 with its unwanted mining assets in 2014. The deal would allow Woodside to progress its Scarborough project and help BHP transition to a greener, mining-only focus, though complexities like decommissioning liabilities and deal valuation remain critical. Speculation also includes who will lead the newly enlarged Woodside.

title: EnLink Sees Oklahoma Declines Moderating as E&Ps Ramp Up, Permian Growth Continues
summary: EnLink Midstream LLC anticipates that the decline in natural gas and crude oil flows from its Oklahoma facilities will significantly moderate in the near future as higher commodity prices lead to increased drilling activity by exploration and production (E&P) operators. The company is simultaneously experiencing growth in its Permian Basin operations, where it plans to restart the Tiger processing plant and relocate another plant from Oklahoma to increase capacity. Additionally, EnLink is exploring decarbonization initiatives, including carbon capture and sequestration projects on the Gulf Coast.

title: Natural Gas ETFs Bounce on Supportive Short-Term Fundamentals
summary: Natural gas exchange-traded funds performed well on Monday as natural gas prices rebounded due to supportive short-term fundamentals like higher LNG demand and lower production. While peak summer demand may have passed, analysts suggest a potential downside near-term before storage trajectories provide support. Weather forecasts show continued above-normal heat for the coming week, influencing price movements.

title: Woodside, BHP Agree to Merge in $28B Deal, Creating LNG Giant with Estimable Deepwater GOM Portfolio
summary: Australia's Woodside Petroleum Ltd and BHP Group have agreed to merge their natural gas and oil portfolios in an all-stock transaction valued at $28 billion. This merger will create one of the world's largest energy companies, forming the biggest energy company listed on the Australian stock exchange and placing it among the top 10 global LNG producers. The combined entity will have a geographically diverse portfolio, including significant deepwater Gulf of Mexico assets, and aims to reduce carbon emissions with a target of net-zero by 2050.

title: Is Hollyfrontier’s acquisition of US refinery better than NNPC’s deal with Dangote?
summary: This article examines a viral social media claim comparing HollyFrontier's $2.6 billion acquisition of Sinclair Oil's vast refinery assets to NNPC's $2.76 billion purchase of a 20% stake in Dangote Refinery. The author investigates the details of both deals, highlighting the differing capacities and assets involved. The article concludes that the initial social media post is misleading due to a misrepresentation of the acquisition details for both companies.

title: Fossil Fuel Companies Are Quietly Scoring Big Money for Their Preferred Climate Solution: Carbon Capture and Storage
summary: Fossil fuel companies and other industrial sectors are quietly pushing for policies that allocate billions in federal funding for carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies, despite environmental advocates arguing that these funds would be better spent on proven renewable energy solutions. The bipartisan infrastructure legislation includes over $12 billion for direct carbon capture support, with potential for billions more, and industry lobbyists are pushing to expand existing tax credits for the technology. While some scientists acknowledge CCS could be useful for specific industrial processes or future direct air capture, environmentalists warn that significant funding risks prolonging the operation of polluting facilities and creating new dependencies on fossil fuels.

title: BHP may see 'no place for fossil fuels in a decarbonised world', so where does that leave Woodside?
summary: BHP's divestment of its petroleum business to Woodside raises questions about the long-term viability of fossil fuels. While the deal offers short-term financial gains for Woodside, analysts suggest BHP's move is driven by a belief that fossil fuels have no place in a decarbonised world and a desire to avoid future climate-related liabilities and investor pressure. This leaves Woodside, an expanded pure-play oil and gas company, facing renewed scrutiny over its long-term future in an increasingly climate-conscious investment landscape.

title: Enterprise AI for the Utilities Industry
summary: This article highlights how C3 AI addresses key issues across the utilities value chain using its powerful Enterprise AI platform and SaaS applications. It details how C3 AI solutions help prioritize asset maintenance, optimize AMI operations, reduce energy costs, and enhance customer service through AI/ML-driven CRM and energy management tools. The platform is designed for rapid integration and deployment, yielding significant business value for utilities.

title: Irving Oil partnering with TC Energy to reduce emissions from refinery
summary: Irving Oil announced a partnership with TC Energy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from its Saint John refinery, New Brunswick's largest emitter. The companies aim to decarbonize current assets, deploy emerging technologies, and explore the production of low-emission hydrogen and carbon capture. This initiative marks a significant step for Irving Oil amidst increasing pressure from stronger climate policies and public opinion.

title: Most flares from Texas Permian oil drilling lack permits -study
summary: A report by Earthworks claims that major oil producers like Exxon Mobil and Royal Dutch Shell are flaring gas in the Permian Basin without the required Texas state permits. The study found that between 69% and 84% of observed flares were likely unpermitted, despite industry claims of compliance and efforts to reduce flaring. Texas regulators, however, contend that Earthworks' analysis is flawed and based on incomplete data, as some unpermitted flaring is allowed under specific conditions.

title: Norway’s $1.4 trillion wealth fund takes aim at oil companies
summary: Norway's $1.4 trillion sovereign wealth fund is scrutinizing oil companies in its portfolio for insufficient emissions reductions, as the fund's operating guidelines are being reviewed. A government-commissioned report recommends updating the fund's mandate to better manage climate risk, potentially giving it more leverage to pressure greenhouse gas emitters and divest from those slow to cut carbon footprints. This move comes amid increasing investor activism against major oil companies and criticism that Norway has not been aggressive enough in using its fund to combat climate change.

title: ExxonMobil has poured millions into communities it's accused of poisoning. Now there's blowback
summary: ExxonMobil, facing accusations of poisoning communities near its refineries, has been channeling millions of dollars into these areas in Texas and Louisiana. Activists argue that these donations are merely "window dressing" to buy goodwill and distract from the environmental harm caused by the company's operations, a sentiment supported by legal battles and high pollution rates in these communities. Critics also suggest Exxon's financial contributions to academic institutions and its recent reduction in transparency for reporting donations raise concerns about its influence and commitment to addressing environmental concerns.

title: WATCH: Old Alabama TVA fossil plant's smokestacks demolished
summary: Six smokestacks at the decommissioned Colbert Fossil Plant in Tuscumbia, Alabama, were demolished by dynamite on August 25, 2021. The plant, operated by the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for over 60 years, is being dismantled as part of TVA's initiative to transition towards cleaner energy solutions, including new natural gas power generation facilities at the site. Video captured the implosion event.

title: Imperial Oil to produce renewable diesel at Strathcona refinery using locally grown crops
summary: Imperial Oil plans to build Canada's largest renewable diesel complex at its Strathcona refinery near Edmonton, utilizing blue hydrogen and locally grown crops to produce over one billion litres of low-carbon biofuel annually. This project, expected to reduce emissions from the Canadian transportation sector by an equivalent of three million tonnes per year, aims to meet growing customer demand for cleaner burning fuels and align with Canada's Clean Fuel Standard. The company anticipates a final investment decision next year, with production potentially starting in 2024, contingent on market conditions and government support.

title: Imperial to produce renewable diesel at refinery near Edmonton using locally grown crops
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. plans to build Canada's largest renewable diesel complex at its Strathcona refinery near Edmonton. The facility will use blue hydrogen and locally grown crops to produce up to 1 billion litres per year of low-carbon diesel fuel, potentially reducing annual CO2 emissions by 3 million tonnes from the Canadian transportation sector. The project's progression depends on market conditions and government support, with production possibly starting in 2024 to align with Canada's Clean Fuel Standard.

title: Imperial weighs renewable diesel complex at Strathcona refinery
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd., a majority-owned affiliate of ExxonMobil Corp., is considering building a renewable diesel production complex at its Strathcona refinery in Alberta, Canada. The proposed facility would produce approximately 3 million liters per day of renewable diesel using proprietary technology and locally sourced feedstocks, aiming to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 3 million tons per year. A final investment decision is contingent on government support, regulatory approvals, market conditions, and economic competitiveness, with production slated for 2024 if approved.

title: Imperial Oil outlines plan to produce plant-based renewable fuel
summary: Imperial Oil plans to build Canada's largest renewable diesel facility near Edmonton, converting vegetable oil into one billion litres of fuel annually. This initiative responds to increasing emissions-reduction goals and impending Canadian Clean Fuel Standard regulations. The project, expected to cost "hundreds of millions of dollars," hinges on government support and market conditions, with a final investment decision anticipated by mid-2022 and production by 2024.

title: Oil and gas firm Talos Energy picked to operate offshore carbon capture, storage project
summary: Talos Energy and partner Carbonvert have been awarded a lease by the Texas General Land Office to operate an offshore carbon capture and storage project in Jefferson County, Texas. This project aims to sequester 225-275 million metric tons of carbon dioxide and marks Talos's first step in building multiple CCS sites along the U.S. Gulf Coast. The agreement is currently in an exclusive negotiation phase with the GLO.

title: Big Energy Companies Are Tightening Their Purse Strings
summary: Global energy companies are curbing their spending despite high oil prices, a strategy that could benefit investors. The Alerian Energy Infrastructure ETF (ENFR), which holds C-corps and MLPs involved in energy transportation and storage, is highlighted as a potentially impactful investment. This continued fiscal discipline among midstream operators is leading to more stable earnings and improved shareholder returns, with ENFR showing strong year-to-date performance.

title: Exxon sting surfaces in climate litigation
summary: A secret recording of an Exxon Mobil Corp. lobbyist admitting to the company's obstruction of climate action has surfaced in climate change litigation against the oil giant. The recording, in which lobbyist Keith McCoy details how Exxon relied on "shadow groups" to deny scientific consensus on global warming, is being cited in a "friend of the court" brief in Minnesota’s climate lawsuit. This development is seen as a significant new data point, revealing an Exxon insider's admission of the company's historical and ongoing efforts to misrepresent climate science.

title: ExxonMobil Affiliate to Produce Renewable Diesel
summary: ExxonMobil's majority-owned affiliate, Imperial Oil Ltd., is developing a new complex at its Strathcona refinery in Canada to produce approximately 20,000 barrels per day of renewable diesel, aiming to significantly reduce emissions in the Canadian transportation sector. The project will utilize blue hydrogen and carbon capture and storage, reflecting ExxonMobil's commitment to low-carbon solutions and Canada's supportive fuel policies. This initiative could create 600 construction jobs, with production expected to begin in 2024.

title: P&G’s Board Must Be Accountable for Forest Destruction
summary: Ten months after Procter & Gamble's shareholders called on the company to address its impacts on climate-critical forests and Indigenous rights, P&G has failed to take meaningful action. This article details P&G's continued role in driving deforestation and human rights violations through its tissue and palm oil supply chains, and calls for investors to hold the Board of Directors accountable by voting against Angela Braly and James McNerney.

title: Venture Global, Cheniere Move Closer to Starting Up Louisiana LNG Projects
summary: Venture Global and Cheniere Energy are advancing their Louisiana LNG projects, with both Calcasieu Pass and Sabine Pass signaling potential startup by year-end. Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass is authorized to introduce feed gas, while Cheniere's Sabine Pass sixth train is expected to be fully operational in early 2022. These developments are poised to increase U.S. natural gas exports this winter to meet global LNG demand.

title: Exxon reducing Baton Rouge, Louisiana, refinery production on storm threat -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is cutting production at its Baton Rouge, Louisiana, refinery by 50% in anticipation of Hurricane Ida's landfall. The refinery, with a capacity of 520,000 barrels per day, is shutting down one of its two gasoline-producing catalytic crackers and some units in the adjoining chemical plant. This reduction is a precautionary measure to ensure safe operations during the hurricane and is partly due to expected difficulties in trucking products away from the complex.

title: Offshore oil and gas producer Beacon makes major final investment decision in Gulf of Mexico
summary: Beacon Offshore Energy has made its first final investment decision (FID) on the deepwater Shenandoah discovery project in the Gulf of Mexico. This decision could elevate Beacon Offshore Energy to become one of the top 10 offshore producers in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico. The project marks a significant milestone for the Houston-based oil and gas producer.

title: Borr optimism for the future after Q2 net loss
summary: Borr Drilling Limited reported a net loss of $59.9 million for Q2 2021, an increase from Q1, primarily due to a decrease in income from equity method investments. Despite this, the company expressed optimism for the future, citing significant contract wins, improved cash collections from Mexico operations, and a strategic sale of its IWS JVs. Borr Drilling anticipates having 17 rigs operating by year-end and all 23 delivered rigs working by the end of 2022, expecting to generate positive cash from operations.

title: First Look at Louisiana Offshore Oil Port Finds No Major Damage after Hurricane
summary: The Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP), the largest deepwater oil import and export terminal on the U.S. Gulf Coast, reported no major damage to its marine operations after Hurricane Ida. Despite the lack of major damage, operations remain offline as assessments continue and efforts to bring staff to onshore operations are hampered by power outages and debris. A full restart depends on further reviews and the resumption of operations by offshore oil producers and pipeline operators.

title: ExxonMobil Introduces EMRD™, a Renewable Diesel Process Technology to Enable High Yields from Bio-Feedstocks
summary: ExxonMobil Catalysts and Licensing LLC has launched EMRD, a new renewable diesel process technology designed to convert various bio-feedstocks, including vegetable oils and animal fats, into renewable diesel. This two-stage process, utilizing ExxonMobil’s BIDW™ catalyst, aims to achieve higher diesel yields and superior control compared to single-stage methods. ExxonMobil is also developing solutions to allow for the production of renewable jet fuel as a primary product.

title: Exxon taps US strategic oil reserve in aftermath of Ida’s wrath
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has been authorized by the U.S. Department of Energy to receive 1.5 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for its Baton Rouge refinery. This move aims to restart fuel production after Hurricane Ida shut down most oil production in the Gulf of Mexico. President Joe Biden stated the U.S. would use all available tools to increase gasoline availability and ease price pressures, as gasoline prices are expected to be the highest in seven years for the Labor Day weekend.

title: GOOD NEWS: MC students receive scholarships
summary: Midland College (MC) announced a new partnership with Ovintiv USA, Inc., which includes $8,000 in scholarships for Energy Technology students. The scholarships recognize students with GPAs over 3.0 who are also employed, highlighting Ovintiv's commitment to Permian Basin workforce development. Ovintiv, a North American oil and natural gas producer, is supporting MC's program that prepares students for careers in the oil and gas industry.

title: Chevron braces for activist challenge; meets Engine No.1 representatives- WSJ
summary: Chevron Corp is preparing for a potential activist challenge and has met with representatives of Engine No.1, the pro-environment fund that successfully won three board seats at Exxon Mobil. The oil major shared its plans to cut carbon emissions during these "cordial" talks and is considering adding an environmental expert to its board. Regulatory filings indicate Engine No.1 holds a stake in Chevron and has explored organizing other investors to purchase shares, suggesting interest in a second major campaign.

title: EXCLUSIVE Chevron looks to sell Texas' Eagle Ford Basin assets - document
summary: Chevron Corp is reportedly marketing its oil and gas assets in the Eagle Ford Basin, South Texas, for sale. The assets, valued between $1 billion and $3.8 billion depending on factors like undeveloped inventory, had a net production of 30,300 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2021. This divestment aligns with Chevron's strategy to streamline operations, focus on more economic projects, and diversify its business, following a trend of oil companies capitalizing on surging crude prices.

title: Putting Houston’s carbon capture and storage potential into perspective
summary: ExxonMobil is proposing a carbon capture and storage (CCS) hub in Houston, aiming to significantly reduce industrial emissions by capturing and storing CO2 deep beneath the Gulf of Mexico. This initiative could remove up to 100 million metric tons of CO2 annually by 2040, helping Houston achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. The article highlights CCS as a critical technology for meeting the Paris Agreement's climate goals and provides context for the scale of 100 million metric tons of CO2.

title: California Oil Industry Lobby Group Files for Bankruptcy
summary: The California Independent Petroleum Association (CIPA) has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after being ordered to pay over $2 million to the Center for Biological Diversity, youth groups, and the city of Los Angeles. This judgment stemmed from a retaliatory lawsuit CIPA filed against these groups, which a judge determined was intended to harass them for advocating for oil drilling protections. Activists express outrage, viewing the bankruptcy as an attempt by CIPA to evade accountability for its actions and continue its efforts against environmental protections.

title: Well of the Week – The first resource play with legs
summary: This article highlights the Pembina Cardium discovery well as a pivotal "Well of the Week," marking it as the first resource play with widespread development potential in the Canadian oil and gas industry. Discovered in 1953, the Cardium field represented a significant shift to conventional rotary drilling and, despite thinner pay sections, contributed substantially to Western Canada's oil and gas reserves. The write-up emphasizes its long-lived production profiles and its role as a trailblazer for subsequent large-scale resource play developments.

title: Schlumberger and Baker Hughes Bet On Green Energy Technologies
summary: Oilfield service giants Schlumberger and Baker Hughes are heavily investing in green energy technologies like hydrogen and carbon capture, projecting them to rival their traditional fossil fuel businesses by 2030. They anticipate significant growth in these sectors, with Schlumberger forecasting a potential $1.6 trillion in annual investments for energy transition by 2030-2040 and Baker Hughes expecting billions in annual orders from clean energy. This strategic shift highlights the increasing potential for net-zero transitions within the traditional oil and gas industry.

title: Oil-soaked birds found near oil spill at refinery in wake of Hurricane Ida
summary: Louisiana wildlife officials have documented over 100 oil-soaked birds near the Phillips 66 Alliance Refinery in Belle Chasse following an oil spill caused by Hurricane Ida's flooding. Efforts are underway to rescue and rehabilitate affected wildlife, including black-bellied whistling ducks, blue-winged teal, and egrets. The incident is part of a larger picture of numerous oil and chemical spills reported to the EPA and Coast Guard in the aftermath of the hurricane.

title: Why oil and gas stocks are a bargain
summary: Investors are warned they are missing out on an opportunity in oil and gas stocks due to a significant disconnect between depressed share prices and soaring commodity prices. The buoyant LNG market and robust crude oil prices are substantially increasing cash flows for producers, making these stocks appear to be a bargain despite general investor sentiment. This situation is highlighted as becoming "ridiculous" by market sources.

title: Gustavo Chaab, de YPF: "La Argentina tiene el potencial de exportar energía renovable"
summary: Gustavo Chaab, VP de Medioambiente, Salud y Seguridad de YPF, discusses how the company is transitioning towards sustainability while emphasizing Argentina's potential in renewable energy exports. He highlights YPF's four pillars of sustainability, the shift in the country's energy matrix towards renewables, and the projected job creation in the new energy sector. Chaab also details YPF Luz's role in electricity generation, particularly focusing on the high efficiency of wind power in Argentina and the future prospects of green hydrogen.

title: Chevron triples low-carbon investment, but avoids 2050 net-zero goals
summary: Chevron Corp pledged to triple its low-carbon investments to $10 billion through 2028, focusing on reducing its carbon emissions footprint. However, the company is not yet committing to a 2050 net-zero emissions target, citing concerns about realism and deliverability, a stance that diverges from European oil producers. The investment will be allocated across areas such as carbon capture, greenhouse gas reductions, renewable fuels, and hydrogen energy.

title: AFL-CIO’s Shuler to ExxonMobil: Locking out refinery workers risks deadly accident
summary: AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler has warned ExxonMobil that its lockout of 650 Steelworker members at its Beaumont refinery complex in Texas poses significant safety risks. Shuler emphasized that using temporary, ill-trained replacement workers instead of experienced union members increases the likelihood of dangerous industrial accidents, citing the tragic 2005 BP Texas City refinery explosion as a warning. The union is seeking a mutually agreeable end to the lockout, stressing that the dispute is not about wages but workplace safety for both workers and the community.

title: Landmark Legal Cases to Secure Clean Water and Clean Air as a Right For All
summary: Earthjustice highlights fifty years of landmark legal cases focused on securing clean water and clean air as a fundamental right. The article details significant victories, including those related to the Clean Air Act, Mercury & Air Toxics Standards, and the Clean Water Act, demonstrating how legal action holds polluters accountable and strengthens environmental protections across the nation and internationally. These cases range from local community protection to nationwide policy changes and international collaborations.

title: Chevron CEO Warns of High Energy Prices
summary: The CEO of Chevron, Mike Wirth, warns that high energy prices will persist for the foreseeable future as oil and natural gas producers are unwilling to significantly increase drilling. This reluctance stems from shareholder demands for immediate returns rather than reinvestment in new projects, despite market signals of rising commodity prices. Wirth notes that new dynamics, including government policy and capital constraints, are making it harder for the industry to access funding for new developments, potentially creating short-term risks for the global economy.

title: Exxonmobil investigates close-call incident on Hebron
summary: ExxonMobil is investigating a near-miss incident on its Hebron platform offshore Newfoundland, Canada, where a 3.6kg auxiliary hoist hook fell 5-6 meters. No injuries were reported, but the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Petroleum Board (C-NLOPB) deemed it a potential fatality risk according to its dropped objects prevention scheme calculator. All auxiliary crane operations have been halted as ExxonMobil investigates the root cause, with C-NLOPB oversight.

title: Increasing gas exports to supply tight European market
summary: Equinor and its partners have received permission to increase gas exports from the Oseberg and Troll fields on the Norwegian continental shelf to help supply the tight European market. Production permits for each field have been increased by 1 billion cubic meters (bcm) for the gas year beginning October 1st, aiming to boost gas supply through the fall and winter. This comes as Equinor is also ramping up production at Troll following the completion of its Phase 3 project, which will further extend gas deliveries for decades.

title: Shell Exits Permian Basin as ConocoPhillips Doubles Down
summary: Shell has sold its Permian Basin assets to ConocoPhillips for $9.5 billion, signaling Shell's shift towards value over volume and away from high-cost shale production. ConocoPhillips, meanwhile, is expanding its Permian footprint for the second consecutive year, acquiring 225,000 acres and 175,000 BOE/D. Shell plans to use the proceeds for share buybacks and balance sheet strengthening, while ConocoPhillips leverages the acquisition to consolidate its position as a major player in the dominant shale-oil play.

title: Suit claims BP trader sacked for raising Nigeria bribe concerns
summary: A former oil trader for British energy giant BP, Jonathan Zarembok, alleges he was fired for raising concerns about bribes being paid in Nigeria to secure local contracts. Zarembok claims BP paid "abnormally large" fees to a local agent and that the company's proposed reasons for these payments were a "sham." BP denies the allegations, stating that the payments were legitimate and thoroughly vetted, and that Zarembok's dismissal was due to an "irretrievably broken down" working relationship.

title: Royal Dutch Shell Sells Permian Basin Oil Holdings for $9.5 Billion (Published 2021)
summary: Royal Dutch Shell sold its Permian Basin oil holdings to ConocoPhillips for $9.5 billion in cash, marking a significant step for Shell toward cleaner energy production amidst investor and public pressure to reduce carbon emissions. This deal consolidates ConocoPhillips' position as a major player in the Permian Basin, which is seeing a recovery in American shale oil production and a wave of acquisitions. Shell's exit comes nine years after it acquired the field and developed it to produce about 200,000 barrels a day.

title: BP gambles big on fast transition from oil to renewables
summary: BP is embarking on a rapid transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy, selling off lucrative oil and gas assets to fund investments in clean energy despite current losses in its renewable ventures. CEO Bernard Looney aims to significantly cut BP's oil production while boosting renewable electricity generation by 2030, a strategy that has raised concerns among some executives and analysts about asset valuation and shareholder value. The company plans to offset declining oil and gas revenue with growing revenues from gasoline stations and electric vehicle charging, which they expect to be more stable than the volatile oil business.

title: Shell exits Permian with $9.5 bln Texas shale sale to ConocoPhillips
summary: Royal Dutch Shell announced the sale of its Permian Basin assets to ConocoPhillips for $9.5 billion in cash, marking its exit from the largest U.S. oilfield as it refocuses on clean energy transitions. ConocoPhillips' acquisition of 225,000 net acres strengthens its position in U.S. shale, while both companies made moves related to shareholder returns and greenhouse gas emission targets. The deal highlights a divergence between European and U.S. producers regarding future hydrocarbon investments.

title: Why We’re Bullish on Russia and Eastern Europe Right Now
summary: This article outlines why Russia and Eastern Europe, particularly the CEE region, present a bullish investment opportunity. It highlights Russia's positive real rates, strong oil and gas prices bolstering its economy, and its stock market's outperformance against the S&P 500, along with attractive valuations and dividend yields. The broader CEE region, including Poland, is also noted for its sustained growth and shared characteristics with other emerging markets.

title: As energy transition plays out, Shell exits Permian with $9.5 bln sale to ConocoPhillips
summary: Shell is selling its Permian Basin business for $9.5 billion in cash to ConocoPhillips as part of its strategy to shift towards renewable energy and meet its net-zero goals. ConocoPhillips will acquire 225k net acres with a current production of 175 thousand barrels equivalent per day, aiming to enhance its role in the energy transition with lower GHG intensity barrels and increasing its dividend. The deal, expected to close in Q4 2021, allows Shell to fund shareholder distributions and strengthen its balance sheet, while ConocoPhillips increases its divestment targets to help finance the acquisition.

title: Troll Phase 3 Project: Increasing Gas Exports to Supply Tight European Market
summary: Equinor and its partners have received permission to increase gas exports from the Oseberg and Troll fields by 1 billion cubic meters each for the upcoming gas year, aiming to supply the tight European market. This increase follows the completion of the Troll Phase 3 project, which started production on August 27 and is expected to reach plateau production by October 1, extending the Troll A platform's life beyond 2050. The Troll Phase 3 project is highly profitable with low CO2 emissions, leveraging existing infrastructure to recover an estimated 347 billion standard cubic metres of gas.

title: Exxon, Chevron conceal payments to some governments -watchdog
summary: U.S. oil majors Exxon Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp have reportedly failed to meet a core transparency standard set by the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI), a global anti-corruption body. EITI stated that these companies have declined to publicly disclose payments made to governments in countries that are not EITI members, despite having board seats on the organization. This lack of transparency contrasts with European-based oil companies like BP, Shell, and Total, which do disclose such payments.

title: Cheniere Energy's Sabine Pass Train 6 closer to service
summary: Cheniere Energy's Sabine Pass Train 6 is moving closer to operation after the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved the introduction of feed gas. The liquefied natural gas unit is now expected to come online in the first quarter of next year, earlier than initially anticipated. Cheniere also recently announced its first stock dividend of 33 cents per share, payable on November 17.

title: Sasol maps out its future
summary: Sasol, once criticized for its environmental impact, is undergoing a significant transformation towards sustainability, aiming for net-zero emissions by 2050. CEO Fleetwood Grobler revealed ambitious targets, including a 30% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from South African operations by 2030 compared to 2017 levels, and a halt to all new coal-based projects. The company plans to shift to natural gas, renewable energy, and green hydrogen, committing to reinvent itself while maintaining financial sustainability and delivering competitive returns.

title: ExxonMobil added as defendant in High Court case calling for closure of Guyana operations
summary: ExxonMobil's local subsidiary, Esso Exploration and Production Guyana Limited (EEPGL), has been added as a defendant in a High Court case in Guyana. Two Guyanese citizens are seeking to close ExxonMobil's operations, alleging that petroleum agreements with the company violate their constitutional right to a safe environment due to the large quantities of greenhouse gases that will be produced. The High Court has set timelines for document submission and adjourned the case until June 2022 for case management.

title: The growing dilemma of oil refiners: Move to biofuels or stick with what they know?
summary: Oil refiners are facing a dilemma: continue refining petroleum and risk climate change fallout, or shift to biofuels made from agricultural products, which are subject to supply volatility due to weather events. While companies like Phillips 66, Valero, and Exxon Mobil are investing in renewable fuel facilities, others like CVR Energy have postponed conversions due to soaring feedstock prices. The article highlights the pros and cons of this transition, including cleaner burning fuels versus competition with food supplies and the need for advanced biofuels from non-food sources to truly reduce emissions.

title: Shell sells Permian Basin oil and gas assets to ConocoPhillips for $9.5 billion
summary: Royal Dutch Shell has sold its Permian Basin assets to ConocoPhillips for $9.5 billion, a move aimed at maximizing cash distribution for investors rather than increasing production. The deal includes 225,000 acres and 600 miles of pipelines, with a production capacity of 175,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. ConocoPhillips stated the acquisition will strengthen its cash flow and grow its footprint in the Permian Basin, while also committing to increased greenhouse gas emission reductions.

title: Great Lakes gets $139M contract for next phase of Port of Corpus Christi's channel project
summary: Great Lakes Dredge & Dock Co., LLC has been awarded a $139 million contract for the third phase of the Port of Corpus Christi's Ship Channel Improvement Project. This phase involves deepening and widening the channel west of the La Quinta Junction through the Chemical Turning Basin and is expected to be completed by June 2023. The overall project aims to deepen the channel to 54 feet and widen it to 530 feet to improve safety and efficiency for vessels.

title: BP expands production from one of Gulf's largest oil fields
summary: BP has announced the expansion of its Thunder Horse south expansion project in the Gulf of Mexico, which is projected to boost oil and gas output by an average of 25,000 barrels per day. This move is part of the company's strategy to fund its growing renewable energy business and achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, by extracting low-cost, low-emissions crude. The Thunder Horse field is one of BP's largest discoveries in the Gulf, and the company holds a 75 percent working interest in the project.

title: Oil companies discourage climate action, study says
summary: A Harvard study reveals that major oil companies like ExxonMobil have systematically misled the public about climate change for decades. Initially, this involved outright denial of climate science, but has since evolved into more subtle forms of propaganda aimed at delaying climate action. The research indicates that while ExxonMobil knew about the dangers of global warming internally since the 1970s, their public communications consistently promoted doubt and shifted blame towards individual consumer demand rather than fossil fuel production.

title: Exxon Mobil has been lobbying against parts of Democrats' big social and climate spending bill
summary: Exxon Mobil has been actively lobbying against components of the Democrats' budget bill, which aims to boost working-class families and combat climate change. The company spent $275,000 on Facebook ads targeting proposed tax hikes and its spokesperson confirmed their efforts against a tax burden that could disadvantage U.S. businesses. The article also highlights lobbying efforts by other energy-related groups and the political significance of centrist senators like Joe Manchin in passing the bill.

title: Washington's King County drops climate lawsuit against oil companies
summary: King County in Washington state has voluntarily dropped its lawsuit against five major oil companies, including BP, Chevron, and Exxon Mobil, which accused them of contributing to climate change. This makes King County the first among two dozen municipal and state plaintiffs to end such a case, with legal experts suggesting it might indicate an evolving legal strategy focusing on marketing claims rather than public nuisance. Exxon indicated the lawsuit was a waste of taxpayer money, while the county sought damages and funding for abatement programs to address climate change impacts.

title: Bristow Names Guyana Area Manager
summary: Bristow, an offshore helicopter group, has appointed Courtney Byrne as its Area Manager for Guyana. Byrne will be responsible for managing day-to-day operations, ensuring safety, and fostering customer and community relationships as Bristow expands its services in the region. He brings 28 years of military aviation experience from the Guyana Defence Force Air Corps and extensive flight time.

title: Exxon offers new proposal to locked-out Texas refinery workers
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp offered a new contract proposal to its locked-out refinery workers in Beaumont, Texas, including some seniority protection. However, leaders of the United Steelworkers union local 13-243 stated that the offer still falls short, arguing that key proposals detrimental to workers' safety, seniority, and security remain. If ratified by November 1st, workers would receive a $500 bonus.

title: Nikola and OPAL Fuels Sign MoU to Co-Develop and Construct Hydrogen Fueling Stations and Related Infrastructure
summary: Nikola Corporation and OPAL Fuels LLC have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to collaborate on the development, construction, and operation of hydrogen fueling stations in North America. This partnership aims to accelerate the adoption of heavy-duty zero-emission fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEV) by combining Nikola's FCEV technology and planned bundled lease offers with OPAL Fuels' expertise in building and operating fueling stations and its renewable natural gas (RNG) supply. The initiative will initially focus on private fleets ("Behind the Fence") and explore public access stations, leveraging RNG to reduce the carbon intensity of hydrogen.

title: Hall of Fame Lawyer Limelight: Donald Godwin
summary: This article profiles Donald Godwin, a Hall of Fame trial lawyer, focusing on his career-defining lead litigation defense for Halliburton in the Deepwater Horizon oil spill case. It delves into his journey from tax law to litigation, his entrepreneurial decision to start Godwin Bowman, and his extensive experience in diverse legal areas, including significant asbestos negotiations and high-stakes family law. Godwin also shares insights on negotiation, leadership, and advice for aspiring lawyers.

title: New opportunities and issues after the end of single-use plastics in the EU
summary: The EU's directive banning single-use plastics presents both challenges and opportunities. While the COVID-19 pandemic complicated plastic waste issues, the directive pushes for a shift to more recyclable materials. The article highlights market fragmentation among EU member states in implementing the ban and explores the growing market for eco-alternatives, featuring innovative startups in Southeast Europe and various support programs for green businesses.

title: Eni Rovuma Basin and Standard Bank launch the entrepreneurship support program iCreate
summary: Eni Rovuma Basin, on behalf of the Area 4 Partners, and in partnership with Standard Bank, has launched iCreate, its first entrepreneurship support program. The 12-week program aims to strengthen the capacity of 25 selected Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) that have high growth potential, making them more competitive and sustainable. It includes training, mentoring, business consultancy, and exposure to market and financing opportunities as part of the Coral South Project's local content plan.

title: Colombia’s Black Gold Re Moody’s rating affirmed
summary: Moody's has affirmed the Baa3 insurance financial strength rating for Black Gold Re Limited, the Bermuda captive of Colombia's largest oil and gas producer, Ecopetrol S.A. However, Black Gold Re's outlook has been changed from stable to negative, mirroring Ecopetrol's outlook change due to the strong credit alignment between the captive and its parent company. The affirmation is based on Ecopetrol's support, Black Gold Re's integration into group risk management, adequate capitalisation, and consistent earnings, while the negative outlook reflects the close financial ties to its parent.

title: Upstart activist Engine No. 1 takes stake in GM, supports EV transition plan
summary: Activist investor firm Engine No. 1 has acquired a stake in General Motors, signaling support for the automaker's electric vehicle transition plans. The firm believes GM's aggressive approach to EVs, including a commitment to exclusively electric vehicles by 2035, positions it for significant growth and potential stock tripling within five years. This investment contrasts with their previous hostile campaign against Exxon, as Engine No. 1 praises GM's management for embracing future changes.

title: Royal Dutch Shell in discussion with CESL to invest $500 million
summary: Royal Dutch Shell Plc is reportedly in talks with India's state-run Convergence Energy Services Ltd (CESL) for a $500 million investment in CESL's decentralized solar sector. The potential investment signals growing interest from global oil firms in India's green economy, aligning with increasing focus on ESG standards. Other international energy giants like Thailand's PTT Group, Malaysia's Petronas, and France's Total are also making moves in India's green energy space.

title: Canada invokes 1977 pipeline treaty with U.S. over Line 5 dispute
summary: Canada has formally invoked a 1977 treaty with the United States to kickstart bilateral negotiations regarding Enbridge Inc.'s Line 5 pipeline. This escalation comes as Michigan has ordered the critical oil pipeline to shut down, citing environmental concerns, an order Enbridge has ignored, leading to a legal battle. By invoking the treaty, Canada aims to compel the U.S. federal government to intervene and resolve the dispute, which Ottawa views as a potential "political catastrophe" if Line 5 were to close.

title: How to Invest in Companies That Are Actually Helping the Environment
summary: ESG funds have gained popularity as investors seek to align their money with environmental concerns, but their effectiveness is debated due to broad definitions and limited regulation. This article explores how to identify truly sustainable investments, highlighting the vetting processes of fund managers and criteria for companies genuinely commitmed to environmental progress, urging investors to scrutinize reports and core business practices.

title: ICE Exchange Curbs U.K. Gas Trading Amid Wild Market Swings
summary: ICE Futures Europe temporarily limited trading on UK natural gas futures due to a 39% price surge, indicating an overheated market. The exchange used its Interval Price Limit mechanism to create a circuit-breaker, restricting trades within a specified range to manage extreme price fluctuations. This measure highlights the volatility in the natural gas market.

title: Crews containing crude oil gushing out of tank at Marathon refinery
summary: Crews at Marathon Petroleum Corp's Galveston Bay Refinery in Texas City, Texas, were working to contain a crude oil leak from a storage tank. No injuries were reported, and the crude oil was being contained within an earthen berm. An investigation will be conducted to determine the cause of the release, and regulatory notifications have been made.

title: La política de Macri con YPF
summary: This article criticizes the Macri government's energy policy, particularly regarding YPF, alleging that it favored private companies over the state-owned oil firm. It highlights the appointment of a former Shell CEO as Minister of Energy and the subsequent marginalization of YPF, leading to decreased investment and production. The article also details the detrimental impact of labor flexibilization policies on oil workers.

title: Nabors Announces World's First Fully Automated Land Rig Has Successfully Drilled Its First Well
summary: Nabors Industries Ltd. announced that its PACE®-R801, the world's first fully automated land drilling rig, successfully drilled its first horizontal well for ExxonMobil in the Permian Basin. This rig combines proprietary automated drilling software with robotics to create an unmanned rig floor, enhancing safety, efficiency, and environmental performance. The technology showcased in PACE®-R801 aims to drive the next wave of performance gains in the energy industry, with insights gained informing future innovations.

title: Exclusive Analysis: In U.S. TV Ads, Chevron Motors Past Its Big Oil Competition in Boasting of Sustainability Accolades
summary: Chevron significantly outspent its major oil competitors (BP, Exxon Mobil, Shell) in U.S. television advertising between June 2020 and August 2021, airing nearly 30,000 ads focused heavily on sustainability. While other companies aired far fewer ads or focused on traditional oil and gas messaging, 80% of Chevron's airings featured sustainability-focused language, despite external skepticism about the industry's green transition claims. This advertising strategy contrasts with its competitors' more limited or product-focused ad campaigns during the same period.

title: Transformer Oil Market Size, Growth and Key Companies – Nynas AB, Ergon Inc., Petrochina Company Limited, APAR Industries Limited, Calumet Specialty Products Partners, L.P.
summary: The Transformer Oil Market is projected to reach USD 3,630.7 Million by 2027, growing at a CAGR of 4.79% from 2020. Key players identified in the market include Nynas AB, Ergon Inc., Petrochina Company Limited, and APAR Industries Limited. The report segments the market by type (Bio-based, Silicone oil, Mineral Oil), application (Distribution Transformers, Power Transformers, Instrument Transformers), and end-use (Transmission & Distribution, Power Generation, Railways & Metros).

title: First fully automated land rig drills its first well
summary: Nabors Industries Ltd, headquartered in Hamilton, announced that its PACE-R801 rig, the world’s first fully automated land drilling rig, successfully completed its inaugural well for ExxonMobil in the Permian Basin. This rig integrates proprietary automated drilling software with robotics to eliminate human presence in high-risk "red-zone" areas, enhancing safety and drilling efficiency. The technology, which also promises reduced drilling emissions, represents a significant step towards achieving ESG goals in the oil and gas industry.

title: BW Energy Gets Hold of Two Offshore Blocks in Gabon
summary: BW Energy has been provisionally awarded operatorship of two offshore blocks, G12-13 and H12-13, in Gabon's 12th Offshore Licensing Round, pending finalization of production sharing contracts. These blocks are adjacent to BW Energy's existing Dussafu licence and will be operated by BW Energy (37.5%) in a consortium with VAALCO Energy (37.5%) and Panoro Energy (25%). The consortium plans to drill exploration wells and conduct 3D seismic acquisition, aiming to leverage existing infrastructure for potential rapid value creation.

title: Chevron commits to net zero operational emissions by 2050
summary: Chevron Corp (CVX.N) has announced a target to achieve net zero operational emissions by 2050, aligning with increasing pressure from investors and governments on energy companies to combat climate change. This commitment focuses on upstream and indirect emissions from its own operations. Unlike some European peers, Chevron's goals do not include greenhouse gases from all fuel products sold, but it plans to pivot towards low-carbon businesses and triple investments to reduce its carbon footprint.

title: Chart: Gas prices hit a new high. Here's how much a gallon costs now.
summary: The average price of a gallon of gas in the United States reached a seven-year high of $3.26 this month, according to GasBuddy. Prices are even higher in states like California and parts of the Pacific Northwest, topping $4. Experts attribute the increase to pandemic-related supply issues and Hurricane Ida, and they forecast continued rising energy prices.

title: First Fully Automated Land Rig Drills First Well
summary: Nabors Industries Ltd. announced that the world's first fully automated land drilling rig, PACE®-R801, successfully drilled its first well for ExxonMobil in the Permian basin, reaching a total measured depth of 19,917 feet. This rig combines Nabors' Smart Suite software with Canrig® robotics, aiming for enhanced safety, efficiency, and environmental performance with a crew primarily focused on supervision, service, and maintenance. ExxonMobil lauded the collaboration as a step towards optimizing drilling through advanced technologies.

title: Locked-out Texas refinery workers to vote on Exxon contract proposal -union
summary: Workers locked out of Exxon Mobil Corp's Beaumont, Texas refinery for nearly six months will vote on the company's latest contract proposal on October 19. This vote comes after a petition to remove the United Steelworkers' union was submitted to the U.S. National Labor Relations Board. The union had previously rejected Exxon's proposals over issues like job seniority and the elimination of lead operator positions.

title: Exxon says union removal vote to go forward at Texas refinery hit by lockout
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced that a vote to remove the United Steelworkers union (USW) from its Beaumont, Texas, refinery will proceed regardless of an upcoming contract ratification vote by locked-out workers. The USW sees the contract vote and the decertification vote as separate issues, while Exxon maintains the decertification process will continue as per NLRB guidelines. The union has filed a complaint against Exxon with the NLRB regarding the decertification materials.

title: P&G dogged by controversy on forests, human rights at annual meeting for third year in a row
summary: Environmental advocacy groups protested Procter & Gamble's annual general meeting for the third consecutive year, raising concerns about the company's supply chain issues, particularly its sourcing of pulp from Canadian boreal forests and palm oil from Indonesian and Malaysian tropical forests. Activists called for greater accountability regarding forest destruction, human rights, and climate change, with shareholders voting to keep board member Angela Braly despite pushback. The groups emphasize that pressure on P&G will continue until substantial improvements are made in its sourcing practices and policy.

title: Big Oil Takes a Beating, but Its Investors Are Riding High (Published 2021)
summary: Major oil companies like Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Royal Dutch Shell have faced significant setbacks recently due to climate change pressures from shareholders, courts, and a landmark report. Despite these public battles, the energy sector has seen soaring stock prices and oil demand, making it the best-performing sector in the market this year for investors. This paradox highlights the complex interplay between increasing climate pressure and rising energy demands as the economy recovers.

title: Exxon tells Texas refinery workers lockout will end if contract approved or union removed
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp informed workers at its Beaumont, Texas, refinery that their six-month lockout would end if they either ratified the company's contract offer or voted to remove the United Steelworkers union (USW) as their representative. Workers are scheduled to vote on the contract offer, while the U.S. National Labor Relations Board is reviewing a petition for a vote to decertify the USW Local 13-243. The USW has urged workers to reject the contract and has filed a complaint alleging the lockout's purpose is to remove the union.

title: Will heating bills increase? How the global price surge in gas & oil could affect Michigan
summary: As winter approaches, concerns are rising about increasing heating bills due to a global surge in oil and gas prices. While the U.S. Energy Information Administration predicts a 30% rise in natural gas costs for many households, Michigan residents may be largely protected. Thanks to the state's extensive natural gas storage capabilities, utility companies like DTE Energy and Consumers Energy anticipate stable or even lower prices for their customers, having secured much of their supply during the summer.

title: Schlumberger Technology Innovation Recognized at 2021 World Oil Awards
summary: Schlumberger received six awards at the 2021 World Oil Awards for its technological innovations across various categories in the upstream oil and gas industry. The recognized technologies include solutions for stimulation, formation testing, drilling fluids, well integrity, well intervention, and seismic mapping. These innovations were praised for their ability to improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, and significantly lower the carbon footprint of oil and gas operations.

title: Rabbis arrested demanding climate action by Wall Street giant’s Jewish CEO
summary: Three rabbis and six Jewish teenagers were arrested during a climate protest at BlackRock's Manhattan headquarters, demanding the investment firm stop funding the fossil fuel industry. The demonstration was organized by the Jewish Youth Climate Movement and GreenFaith, targeting BlackRock's CEO Larry Fink to align his investment strategies with his stated commitment to mitigating climate risk and Jewish values. This action was part of a global "Faiths 4 Climate Justice" campaign ahead of the COP26 conference.

title: Chad ExxonMobil Unit Shuts In Production Site Over Labor Dispute
summary: An Exxon Mobil Corp. unit in Chad temporarily ceased production due to an attack on its facilities stemming from a labor dispute. Workers are negotiating their remuneration package with Esso Exploration and Production Chad Inc. ahead of a planned sale of the business to Savannah Energy.

title: Valaris to reactivate drillship for new Petrobras contract
summary: Offshore driller Valaris has secured a new contract with Petrobras for its 2010-built drillship, Valaris DS-4, to operate offshore Brazil. The contract is for a minimum of 548 days and is set to commence in the second quarter of 2022. The drillship, currently stacked in the UK, will undergo reactivation in the Canary Islands before mobilizing to Brazil.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Exxon Debates Abandoning Some of Its Biggest Oil and Gas Projects
summary: Exxon Mobil's newly reconstituted board of directors is reportedly debating the future of several major oil and gas projects, including a $30 billion liquefied natural gas development in Mozambique and a multi-billion dollar project in Vietnam. This reconsideration comes as the company reevaluates its investment strategy amidst a shifting energy landscape. The board, which includes new members nominated by an activist investor, has expressed concerns about these particular projects.

title: TechnipFMC Third Quarter 2021 Earnings Call Presentation
summary: TechnipFMC announced the availability of its Third Quarter 2021 Earnings Call Presentation in connection with its teleconference scheduled for October 21, 2021. The presentation is accessible on the company's website. TechnipFMC, a leading technology provider in energy industries, also uses its website as a channel for distributing material company information.

title: Exxon board debates dropping several major oil and gas projects
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp's board is reportedly debating whether to proceed with several major oil and gas projects, including a $30 billion liquefied natural gas development in Mozambique and a multibillion-dollar gas project in Vietnam. This deliberation comes amid investor pressure for fossil fuel companies to prioritize cost-consciousness and green energy. The discussions are part of a review of Exxon's five-year spending plan, with a board vote expected at the end of the month.

title: Exxon reduces production at Chad oilfield following worker protests
summary: ExxonMobil has temporarily reduced production at its Chad oilfield and scaled back staffing due to worker protests. The workers are protesting a proposed sale of Exxon's stake in the Doba oilfield and the Chad-Cameroon oil transportation pipeline to Savannah Energy, demanding severance guarantees. The Doba field produced an average of 33,700 barrels of oil per day last year.

title: Marathon is committed to meet current, future needs
summary: Marathon Petroleum Corp. details its commitment to meeting today's energy demands while simultaneously investing in a sustainable and energy-diverse future, particularly at its Detroit refinery. The company highlights its efforts in emissions and water-use reduction, community engagement through grants and volunteer work, and investment in emerging technologies. This piece emphasizes the dual focus of providing current essential petroleum products and developing sustainable practices for the future.

title: Tsakos: A life in shipping
summary: Dr. Nikolas Tsakos, founder, CEO, and president of Tsakos Energy Navigation (TEN), discusses his life in shipping, the legacy of his family, and his vision for the future of the tanker industry. Despite a challenging year for tankers, Tsakos is optimistic about a comeback and emphasizes the importance of owner communication and sustainable practices, advocating for improved existing fuel infrastructure over radical new solutions for decarbonization. The article highlights his early career, the founding of TEN, and his views on industry challenges like decarbonization and the fragmentation of the tanker sector.

title: Valero Says Gasoline Sales Near Pre-Pandemic Levels, Natural Gas-to-Oil Switching Imminent
summary: Valero Energy Corp. reported strong third-quarter results, with gasoline sales nearing pre-pandemic levels and diesel sales exceeding 2019 figures. The company attributes its favorable outlook to low global product inventories, recovering demand, and anticipated natural gas-to-oil switching in Europe and Asia due to high gas prices. Valero is also significantly investing in its renewable diesel business, with expansion projects underway in Louisiana and Texas, and progressing on a carbon capture and sequestration project.

title: Exxon Mobil reportedly to close 2 office towers in The Woodlands
summary: Exxon Mobil is reportedly closing two office towers in The Woodlands, moving approximately 1,400 employees to its main Houston-area campus. This move could impact the tax incentives Exxon Mobil was previously supposed to maintain by employing a certain number of workers in the Hughes Landing district. The relocation follows reports from Bloomberg.

title: Exxon Mobil keen to build carbon storage hubs in SE Asia, similar to Houston project
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp plans to establish carbon capture storage (CCS) hubs in Southeast Asia, mirroring its Houston project, and has initiated discussions with countries offering potential CO2 storage sites. The company identifies Singapore as a hub given its refining-petrochemical center, intending to transport captured CO2 to storage locations in countries like Indonesia and Malaysia, where significant CO2 storage capacity exists. For these projects to be viable, ExxonMobil emphasizes the necessity of a transparent carbon price across countries to attract investment and reduce emissions effectively.

title: Despite Cutbacks, ExxonMobil Continues to Fund Climate Science Denial
summary: Despite public statements about climate change, ExxonMobil continues to fund climate science denier groups. A former top lobbyist admitted the company financed these groups to protect investments and maximize profits. While ExxonMobil reduced reported grants in 2020 and changed reporting thresholds, it still contributed significant amounts to organizations like the US Chamber of Commerce, American Enterprise Institute, and GWU Regulatory Studies Center, which actively work against climate action and renewable energy.

title: Houston-based Hilcorp to operate Alaska gas field, taking over for Exxon Mobil
summary: Houston-based Hilcorp Energy Co. will take over operational responsibility for the Point Thomson field in Alaska, succeeding Exxon Mobil Corp. This move signifies another step in Hilcorp's expansion within Alaska.

title: Oil Executives to Face Congress on Climate Disinformation (Published 2021)
summary: Executives from major oil and gas companies, including Exxon Mobil, Shell, Chevron, and BP, are set to testify before a congressional committee regarding allegations of a decades-long disinformation campaign on climate change. This hearing marks the first time these executives will address under oath accusations that their companies misled the public about the scientific consensus on fossil fuels' impact on global warming. House Democrats are drawing parallels between this inquiry and the 1990s tobacco hearings, which exposed how tobacco companies concealed the health dangers of smoking.

title: Valaris on Call to Bolster Angola’s Rig Count
summary: Valaris Limited has secured a two-year contract with Esso Exploration Angola, an ExxonMobil affiliate, for its drillship VALARIS DS-9. The rig will be reactivated in the Canary Islands and mobilized to Angola by June 2022, increasing Angola's active drilling rig count, which currently stands at nine and supports the country's 1.1 million barrels of oil per day production. This move highlights Valaris's contribution to Angola's robust oil exploration activities alongside other major players.

title: Suncor doubles dividend as oil price surge powers profit
summary: Suncor Energy Inc doubled its dividend after posting a third-quarter profit, benefiting from a rebound in crude prices. The Canadian oil and gas producer generated strong free cash flow due to soaring energy prices and growing global fuel demand, reinstating its dividend to pre-pandemic levels. The company's production and refinery throughput also saw significant increases compared to the previous year.

title: Exxon CEO accused of lying about climate science to congressional panel
summary: ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods faced accusations of lying to Congress during a hearing on the oil industry's long-standing efforts to downplay climate change. Congresswoman Carolyn Maloney likened the executives' responses to those of the tobacco industry, alleging a cover-up despite internal scientific warnings. While executives denied misrepresenting science, they declined to make specific pledges or cease lobbying against climate initiatives.

title: Eastman Chemical Co. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Eastman Chemical Co. stock (EMN) rose 4.25% to $110.04, outperforming the broader market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average on a strong trading day. This rise ended a two-day losing streak for the company's shares. Eastman Chemical Co. also outperformed competitors such as Exxon Mobil Corp., 3M Co., and FMC Corp., with its trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

title: Oil giants urged to cut off funds to climate-change denial groups
summary: US lawmakers have urged major oil companies like Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Shell, and BP to cease funding groups that cast doubt on climate science and to withdraw from the American Petroleum Institute. This demand was made during a congressional hearing where executives were questioned about their knowledge of global warming and efforts to undermine climate-protection initiatives. The hearing aimed to increase public pressure on the fossil fuel industry amid President Biden's struggles to pass climate policies and ahead of a key climate summit.

title: Exxon CEO denies spreading disinformation on climate change
summary: ExxonMobil's CEO, Darren Woods, denied accusations of spreading climate change disinformation during a House hearing. He asserted that the company's statements on climate are truthful and consistent with science, despite congressional Democrats alleging a decades-long campaign by the oil industry to mislead the public about the dangers of fossil fuels. Other oil executives from Chevron, BP America, and Shell also testified, with Democrats criticizing their actions as a "greenwashing" effort.

title: Exxon Mobil lost $22 billion in 2020, its worst performance in four decades. (Published 2021)
summary: Exxon Mobil reported a $22.4 billion loss in 2020, marking its worst performance in four decades, primarily due to the pandemic's impact on energy demand and significant write-downs of U.S. natural gas assets. Despite the substantial losses, the company noted signs of recovery in the fourth quarter and is focusing on high-return opportunities and new ventures like carbon capture and sequestration. CEO Darren W. Woods stated that the challenging year ended with a "stronger company" with a "flexible capital program."

title: Exxon posts strongest results since 2017, vows to resume share buybacks
summary: Exxon Mobil reported its strongest quarterly results since 2017, with net income of $6.75 billion, driven by surging fossil fuel demand and higher refining profits. The company announced plans to resume its share repurchase program in 2022, intending to spend up to $10 billion through 2023, while also increasing spending on carbon reduction initiatives. These developments follow a period of shareholder dissatisfaction and a successful proxy battle that led to new board members.

title: Oil and gas rally boosts Chevron's quarterly profit to 8-year high
summary: Chevron Corp reported its highest quarterly profit in eight years, reaching $6.11 billion, driven by surging oil and gas prices, increased output, and recovering motor fuel demand. The strong financial performance resulted in a significant increase in cash flow and boosted the company's shares. Chevron plans to continue its focus on oil production, adding drilling rigs and aiming for annual output increases through 2025.

title: How Artificial Intelligence is Fueling the Energy Transition
summary: This article discusses how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is crucial for the energy transition to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 while meeting increasing energy demands. It highlights AI's role in improving efficiency across traditional oil and gas operations and developing new clean energy sources. Companies like Shell are leveraging AI to reduce emissions, cut costs, and enhance safety through predictive maintenance, optimized operations, and development of low-carbon solutions.

title: NEWS: Profitable Exxon, Chevron emerge as global economy rebounds
summary: Exxon Mobil and Chevron Corp. have reported significant profits in the third quarter, reversing losses from the previous year, as the global economy rebounds and demand for crude oil increases. Exxon posted a $6.75 billion profit, exceeding Wall Street expectations, with production volumes rising in the Permian Basin. Both companies benefited from higher oil prices after pandemic-induced production cuts, though they continue to face scrutiny over climate change.

title: Robert Darnall Obituary (2021) - Englewood, FL - Chicago Tribune
summary: Robert J. Darnall, former Chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Industries, passed away at age 83. He had a distinguished career in the steel industry and served on numerous corporate and philanthropic boards, including the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago. He is survived by his wife, Marletta, and their two children and grandchildren.

title: ExxonMobil states non-union employees get higher pay at Beaumont refinery
summary: ExxonMobil informed locked-out union workers at its Beaumont, Texas, refinery that non-union employees at comparable sites receive 5% to 7% higher pay and similar benefits. This message comes ahead of a decertification vote for the United Steelworkers union Local 13-243, which represents 585 workers locked out since May 1. Exxon has stated the lockout will end if the union either accepts its proposed contract or is decertified, with the company aiming for changes to enhance competitiveness.

title: Argentina bets on natural gas despite climate commitments
summary: Argentina is prioritizing the expansion of natural gas production and its pipeline network from the Vaca Muerta fields, despite its climate commitments to reduce emissions. President Alberto Fernández's government views natural gas as a key fuel for energy transition and export, aiming to save money on imports and boost the economy. Environmental organizations, however, argue that these plans contradict emission reduction targets and could lead to stranded assets, while highlighting environmental and social risks for local communities.

title: Eco (Atlantic) Oil and Gas Ltd Announces Operational Update and Notice of AGM
summary: Eco (Atlantic) Oil & Gas Ltd. provided an operational update, including details on the JHI well drilled by ExxonMobil in Guyana, progress on defining drilling targets in the Orinduik Block, and Eco's new role as Operator on PEL 99 in Namibia. The company also announced advancements in its solar business through its subsidiary Solear Ltd., and issued a notice for its upcoming Annual and Special Meeting.

title: Oil majors won’t ride to the rescue as world faces energy shortages
summary: Major oil companies like Exxon Mobil Corp., Royal Dutch Shell Plc, and Chevron Corp. are prioritizing share buybacks and dividends over significantly increasing capital expenditures for new oil and natural gas supplies, despite current energy shortages. This approach reflects lessons from past overproduction and addresses shareholder demands for better returns and reduced climate risk. Consequently, consumers facing high energy prices and shortages in Europe and Asia should not expect these companies to rapidly boost traditional fossil fuel production.

title: BP Says Oil Demand Is Back Above 100 Million Barrels a Day
summary: Global oil demand has recovered to over 100 million barrels a day, a level last seen before the Covid-19 pandemic, according to BP Plc. This resurgence in fossil fuel consumption is happening despite international efforts to combat climate change and is driving oil prices to multiyear highs. The increased demand and constrained energy supplies are threatening the world's economic recovery.

title: Exxonmobil exploring carbon capture storage in Indonesia
summary: ExxonMobil and Indonesia's state-owned PT Pertamina signed a memorandum of understanding to evaluate the potential for large-scale carbon capture storage (CCS) in Indonesia. This agreement, made during the COP26 summit, aims to explore low-carbon technologies as Indonesia seeks to accelerate its net-zero emissions target. While advocates view CCS as crucial for decarbonization, critics argue it prolongs the use of fossil fuels.

title: These are the Fortune 500 companies that call Irving home
summary: Irving, Texas, is home to eight Fortune 500 company headquarters, with a total of 53 Fortune 500 companies maintaining offices in the city. The article highlights the reasons for Irving's appeal to corporations, such as its central location, amenities, and business-friendly policies. It then lists detailed information for each of the eight Fortune 500 companies headquartered in Irving, including their ranking, industry, number of employees, and revenue.

title: BlackRock's Larry Fink warns that oil assets will shift to private hands to avoid scrutiny --- and that's 'greenwashing'
summary: Larry Fink, CEO of BlackRock, cautioned that an overemphasis on publicly traded companies' climate actions could lead to fossil fuel operations going private to evade scrutiny. He described this potential shift as a significant "capital-market arbitrage" and labeled it "greenwashing." Fink advocated for a comprehensive approach to climate disclosure to ensure uniform standards across all businesses.

title: Trudeau promised to cap emissions, but Canada’s oil and gas companies have different plans
summary: A new analysis by Environmental Defence Canada and Oil Change International reveals that the climate plans of eight major Canadian oil and gas producers are "wholly out of line" with Canada's climate goals, despite Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's pledge to cap and cut emissions from the sector. The report highlights that these companies plan to expand production, rely on unproven technologies like carbon capture, and largely ignore significant "scope three" emissions from product use. Critics argue that these plans lack credibility and governments must intervene to achieve climate targets.

title: Exxon, union met Monday to discuss Texas refinery lockout
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and the United Steelworkers union met on Monday to discuss the ongoing lockout of nearly 600 refinery workers in Beaumont, Texas, but reported no progress. Exxon presented a revised offer that removed a signing bonus and 2021 pay raises, which the union had previously rejected. Workers are slated to vote in November on whether to remove Local 13-243 from the refinery, following a lockout initiated in May over a contract dispute concerning job seniority.

title: Objetivos de descarbonización de BBVA: ¿Qué significan y cuál es su alcance?
summary: BBVA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, encompassing both direct and indirect emissions from its clients. The bank has established intermediate decarbonization targets for 2030 across various high-emission sectors, including electricity generation, automotive, steel, cement, petroleum and gas, aviation, maritime transport, aluminum, and real estate, and aims to expand coverage further. BBVA uses methodologies like PACTA and PCAF, referencing 1.5ºC scenarios from the IEA and ISF NZ, to align its lending portfolios with the Paris Agreement and support clients in their transition to a sustainable future.

title: Corporate Climate Pledges Often Ignore a Key Component: Supply Chains (Published 2021)
summary: Many corporate climate pledges are incomplete because they fail to account for emissions generated within their supply chains, which can constitute up to 95 percent of a company's total greenhouse gas contributions. Companies like Bristol Myers Squibb, Caterpillar, and Exxon Mobil have set ambitious neutrality goals, but often overlook these indirect yet significant sources of pollution. Experts emphasize that without measuring the entire value chain, companies cannot effectively address their full environmental impact.

title: Photos: Get a rare look inside this Mid-County oil and gas terminal
summary: The article provides a rare look inside Energy Transfer's Nederland Terminal through a series of photographs and detailed descriptions. It highlights the terminal's historical significance, its current role in storing and exporting crude oil and various natural gas liquids, and its expansion efforts. The piece also touches on discussions around infrastructure spending and the oil and gas industry's role in advocating for new technologies and energy independence.

title: Oklahoma’s Harold Hamm among world’s richest oil men
summary: Harold Hamm of Continental Resources is ranked as the third richest oilman globally with a net worth of $14.8 billion, a significant increase of 191% in the past year. This increase is largely due to his company's shares soaring by 199.4%. Other notable Oklahomans on the billionaires list include Lynn Schusterman, known for her philanthropic efforts and energy investments, and Carl Icahn, an activist shareholder with investments in several energy companies.

title: Howard Hughes, The Woodlands officials search for tenants to replace Exxon in Hughes Landing
summary: As ExxonMobil plans to vacate its offices in the Hughes Landing mixed-use district in The Woodlands, Howard Hughes and The Woodlands officials are actively seeking new tenants to fill the void. This move by Exxon will see its workers relocate to its main Houston-area campus, prompting a search for new companies to occupy the significant office space. The departure impacts The Woodlands' office market, necessitating efforts to attract different businesses to the area.

title: Phillips 66 to begin repairs next week on two units at shut Louisiana refinery -sources
summary: Phillips 66 plans to start repairs next week on a catalytic reformer and a hydrotreater at its storm-damaged Alliance, Louisiana, refinery, which has been shut since Hurricane Ida. Repairs for other major units, including the crude distillation unit and fluidic catalytic cracking unit, are slated for January. The company is also evaluating options for the refinery's future, including a potential sale or closure.

title: Exxon warns some assets may be at risk for impairment due to climate change
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced that some of its oil and gas assets could face impairment due to climate change, a first such acknowledgment in a securities filing. The company's board, recently overhauled after a proxy battle, will now test assets for climate-related impairments as part of its annual review.
