This shift comes as Exxon plans to increase spending on carbon emission reduction technologies and faces pressure to address its climate strategy.

title: Sempra Infraestructura Launches in Mexico
summary: Sempra Infraestructura, a subsidiary of the US energy company Sempra, has officially launched in Mexico, demonstrating Sempra's ongoing commitment to the Mexican energy market. This new entity resulted from the merger of IEnova and Sempra LNG, retaining all their previous projects and assets, including pipelines, wind parks, refineries, and a natural gas regasification terminal. The company aims to integrate its businesses further to capitalize on new investment opportunities and meet North American energy demands sustainably, while also focusing on social and environmental initiatives like providing energy access to vulnerable communities.

title: Brazil becomes the great opportunity for Exxon Mobil Corp.
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. sees Brazil as a significant opportunity to reduce carbon emissions, aiming for a 10-15% reduction by 2025 and net-zero by 2050, driven by offshore investments. The company's focus on high-quality, lower-emission offshore production in Brazil is a strategic move to address investor pressure regarding climate change. Brazil's robust oil and gas production projections and upcoming oil rounds further solidify its importance for Exxon Mobil.

title: Speakers see opportunities in energy transition
summary: Speakers at the Executive Oil Conference in Midland, Texas, assert that oil and gas will be essential for decades, despite calls for a low-carbon future. ConocoPhillips and Devon Energy executives highlighted the Permian Basin's crucial role in U.S. energy production, emphasizing the need for technology and innovation to reduce emissions while meeting growing global energy demand, especially for populations experiencing energy poverty. They see opportunities in the energy transition for the industry and adjacent businesses.

title: Why John Hickenlooper didn’t join ‘Manchinema’
summary: Senator John Hickenlooper, once known for balancing fossil fuel interests with environmental concerns, has grown disillusioned with the oil and gas industry's climate policy stances. His shift in perspective, particularly after an Exxon lobbyist's undercover video, indicates a decreased likelihood he will align with more conservative Democrats like Senator Joe Manchin. This change reflects broader political shifts in Colorado and a growing impatience among Democrats regarding corporate climate action.

title: With 17 rigs now booked, Borr hopes to fully contract fleet by 2022
summary: Offshore drilling contractor Borr Drilling has 17 out of its 23 rigs contracted or committed, aiming for full fleet utilization by 2022 due to strong demand. The company secured new contracts for three rigs and converted several letters of award/intent into firm contracts, adding significant backlog. Borr reported increased operating revenues and an improved net loss in Q3 2021, with CEO Patrick Schorn anticipating rapid improvement in utilization levels from the strengthening market.

title: Climate change: The US state taking on an oil giant for greenwashing
summary: The US state of Massachusetts is pursuing a landmark lawsuit against ExxonMobil for alleged greenwashing, accusing the oil giant of misleading consumers and investors about its climate change efforts. The state argues that while ExxonMobil promotes green initiatives, its primary business remains oil and gas exploitation, causing real-world impacts like those experienced by local fishermen. This case, if successful, could set a global precedent for holding fossil fuel companies accountable for climate disinformation.

title: Oil prices are up, but do not expect a gas-like crunch
summary: Oil prices are hovering above $80 per barrel due to OPEC+'s supply tightening, but a full-blown energy crisis is unlikely as economic growth is not strong enough to sustain high prices long-term. Despite the current tightening market and recovery in demand, the article argues that the primary driver of high oil prices is OPEC+'s political decision to restrict production rather than robust, sustained economic expansion. The abundance of OPEC spare capacity suggests that a "gas-like crunch" is not imminent, as long-term price developments hinge on true economic growth rather than temporary stimulus-driven recovery.

title: NextEra Energy Stock Forecast: Sunny and Windy
summary: This article provides an in-depth forecast for NextEra Energy (NEE), positioning it as a leading renewable energy stock that offers both growth and dividend income. It highlights NextEra Energy's dual business model as the world's largest utility company (FPL) and largest generator of renewable energy (NextEra Energy Resources), and discusses how it stands to benefit from the $1.2 Trillion Infrastructure Bill and global shifts towards nuclear and wind energy. The article also benchmarks NEE's performance against various indices, concluding that its future looks bright given current market and political landscapes.

title: EOG Eyeing ‘Incredible Value’ for LNG Exports from Permian, Eagle Ford and Dorado
summary: EOG Resources Inc. plans to focus on returning value to shareholders rather than boosting production volumes, despite higher commodity prices. The company sees "incredible value" in exporting natural gas as LNG from its Permian, Eagle Ford Shale, and Dorado assets, and is also piloting a carbon capture and storage venture to reduce emissions. EOG reported sharply higher profits and production in 3Q2021, increased its dividend, and approved share repurchases.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Exxon Escalates Dispute With Russia Over Barred Exit From Giant Oil Project
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has notified Russian officials of its intent to sue the government unless it is allowed to exit the Sakhalin-1 oil-and-gas project. A Kremlin decree from early August has barred Exxon from transferring operatorship and selling its 30% stake, despite the company's prior efforts to transition operations following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Exxon considers Russia's actions a violation of its rights and an impediment to a safe exit from the project.

title: 7 of the Best High-Yield Dividend Stocks for 2022 to Buy Now
summary: This article identifies seven high-yielding dividend stocks that are positioned to offer stable income and help build portfolios in 2022. Amid concerns of inflation and potential slowdowns, these stocks — including Sunoco, Exxon Mobil, and AbbVie — are highlighted for their strong dividend yields, consistent payouts, and resilient business models. The analysis provides a brief overview of each company, detailing their financial performance, market position, and reasons for their inclusion as top dividend picks.

title: Lilly resumes political contributions to Republicans who voted against certifying election
summary: Eli Lilly and Co. has resumed political contributions to 14 Republican lawmakers who voted against certifying the 2020 election results, including three Indiana representatives to whom giving was previously suspended. This reversal comes after the pharmaceutical giant had initially paused donations to these individuals following the January 6th Capitol attack, citing a commitment to democratic processes. The company stated that its LillyPAC supports candidates focused on the "pharmaceutical ecosystem," but did not elaborate on the change in its stance.

title: US becomes world’s top LNG exporter for first time ever
summary: The United States became the world's top exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in December for the first time, surpassing Qatar due to increased deliveries to Europe and new production units. This achievement follows a significant surge in U.S. natural gas production and investments in liquefaction facilities over the past decade. However, the top spot might be short-lived given strong competition from Qatar and Australia, and Qatar's plans for a major export project in the late 2020s.

title: Maya Mia! - How Mexico's Plan to Phase Out Crude Oil Exports May Impact U.S. Refineries
summary: Mexico's state-owned oil company, Pemex, plans to drastically cut its crude oil exports in 2022 and eliminate them entirely by 2023. This strategy is based on Pemex's anticipation of increased utilization of its existing refineries and the start-up of a new facility, requiring all domestically produced crude. Despite initial concerns about the potential impact on U.S. refineries, the article suggests that the actual effects might be less significant than they appear, given Pemex's declining production and refinery utilization trends.

title: Iraq to acquire Exxon Mobil's stake in West Qurna oilfield -minister
summary: The Iraqi government has approved the Iraqi National Oil Company's acquisition of Exxon Mobil Corp's stake in the West Qurna 1 oilfield. This decision follows Exxon's reported intention to sell its 32.7% stake for $350 million. The West Qurna 1 field is a significant asset in southern Iraq, boasting over 20 billion barrels of recoverable reserves.

title: N.Y. governor backs nation’s first statewide gas ban
summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has announced her support for the nation's first statewide ban on natural gas in new buildings, a move that would require all new constructions to use zero-emissions heat sources by 2027. This initiative, part of her 2022 policy blueprint, aims to electrify 2 million homes by 2030 and targets buildings as a major source of greenhouse gas emissions. While the proposal faces potential opposition from the gas industry and some environmentalists who argue for an earlier implementation, it aligns with broader state goals for a carbon-free grid by 2040 and net-zero emissions by 2050, as outlined in the Climate Action Council's draft "scoping plan."

title: 3 ConocoPhillips Trades As Energy Prices Rise And Stock Sees Multi-Year Highs
summary: ConocoPhillips (NYSE: COP) shares have surged by more than 90% since early 2021, fueled by rising energy prices and optimistic OPEC+ announcements. The article details potential investment strategies for COP, including buying dips, considering energy ETFs, or utilizing cash-secured put options for those anticipating continued highs. Analysts generally rate COP as "outperform" with a significant upside, despite potential short-term volatility around upcoming earnings and OPEC+ meetings.

title: Insight: Harmful soot unchecked as Big Oil battles EPA over testing
summary: A deadly form of soot pollution from U.S. refineries, known as condensable fine particulate matter, has gone unregulated for decades due to a dispute between the U.S. oil industry and federal environmental officials over measurement methods. This delay has led to significant unchecked emissions, with regional regulators in California attempting to crack down, sparking litigation from oil refiners like Chevron Corp and PBF Energy Inc. The EPA acknowledges issues with its current testing method but continues research, while environmental scientists warn against further delays in regulation.

title: YPF presentó el estudio de impacto ambiental para explorar un nuevo bloque offshore en el Mar Argentino
summary: YPF, in partnership with Equinor, has submitted an environmental impact study for 3D seismic acquisition in the CAN 102 block of the North Argentina Basin, located off the coast of Buenos Aires province. This block is an ultra-deepwater area and requires an investment of $23.8 million for seismic studies. Additionally, YPF, Total, and Equinor plan to proceed with 3D seismic studies in the MLO 123 block in the Malvinas West Basin later this year, with an estimated investment of $44.6 million.

title: Commodities Notched Their Best Year Since 2009, Despite Precious Metals Weakness
summary: Commodities experienced their best year since 2009, with the Bloomberg Commodity Spot Index gaining 27% in 2021, driven largely by energy prices. Precious metals, however, were the worst-performing category, with gold down 3.6% blamed on expectations of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates. The article highlights the resurgence of fossil fuels due to increased demand and discusses various market trends across emerging markets, energy, and digital currencies.

title: COLUMN | Drilling Update: Borr, Vantage/ADES, Stena/Samsung, Adnoc Drilling, Maersk, and Standard not Drilling [Offshore Accounts]
summary: This article provides a drilling update for several offshore companies, detailing financial maneuvers, contract awards, and strategic shifts. Borr Drilling continues to defer debt repayments and secured new contracts, while Vantage Drilling sold three jackups to ADES to reduce its long-term debt. Stena Drilling is considering acquiring an abandoned drillship from Samsung, Adnoc Drilling expands its fleet, and Maersk Drilling's CEO faced a warning, while Standard Drilling is rebranding to Standard ETC, reflecting a change in investment strategy.

title: Canadian oil is getting cleaner
summary: This article examines the historical greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions intensity of the Canadian upstream oil sector, distinguishing between oil sands and conventional oil subsectors. It highlights that the overall GHG emissions intensity of Canadian oil production has decreased by over 10% since 2000, with the oil sands subsector seeing a nearly 23% reduction and conventional oil a more than 32% decrease. The report concludes that Canada's upstream oil sector is becoming cleaner on an emissions-per-barrel basis, reinforced by the country's high ESG ratings among major oil-producing nations.

title: EXCLUSIVE Exxon Mobil launches sale of U.S. shale gas properties -marketing document
summary: Exxon Mobil is selling shale gas properties spanning 27,000 acres in Ohio's Appalachian basin, including 61 wells that produced approximately 81 million cubic feet per day of natural gas last year. This divestment is part of an ongoing effort to sell U.S. assets and could value the properties at around $200 million. The company is focusing its development on brighter prospects in Guyana, offshore Brazil, and Texas's Permian Basin.

title: Imperial Oil to market Montney, Duvernay assets in Alberta
summary: Imperial Oil announced its intention to market its significant Montney and Duvernay oil and gas-producing assets in central Alberta, held jointly with ExxonMobil Canada through XTO Energy Canada. The decision is part of Imperial Oil's strategic review of its unconventional portfolio, aiming to focus on its key oilsands assets. The company clarified that a definitive sale decision has not yet been made.

title: Exxon, Imperial Oil to market up to $1 billion in Canadian assets
summary: Exxon Mobil and its affiliate Imperial Oil Ltd are planning to sell shale oil and gas properties in Western Canada, which could fetch between $500 million and $1 billion. This divestiture would make oil sands their largest Canadian onshore production business and is part of a broader effort by Exxon to sell smaller operations to pay down debt. XTO Energy Canada, jointly owned by Exxon and Imperial Oil, currently pumps about 9,000 barrels of liquids and 140 million cubic feet of natural gas per day in Canada.

title: Australia’s gas future – the Scarborough project
summary: The Scarborough gas project in Western Australia, valued at $16bn, faces legal disputes and environmental opposition due to concerns about its climate impact. While the Australian government supports the project as a "shot in the arm" for the economy and a transitional fuel, environmental groups argue it contradicts emission reduction targets and the Paris Agreement. The project highlights the ongoing conflict between fossil fuel development and environmental sustainability in Australia's energy future.

title: AT&T Shares Deserve a Return Call
summary: AT&T is considered significantly undervalued despite an expected dividend cut, offering an attractive yield after refocusing on its core communications business. The planned spin-off of WarnerMedia into Warner Bros. Discovery provides shareholders with shares in a new media company while allowing AT&T to invest heavily in its wireless and fixed-line networks. Investors relying on the current dividend may be disappointed, but the strategic shifts position the company for future growth and a competitive dividend yield even post-cut.

title: W&T Offshore expands in Gulf of Mexico with $47M acquisition
summary: W&T Offshore is expanding its operations in the Gulf of Mexico through a new $47 million acquisition. CEO Tracy Krohn stated that the current environment for acquisitions in the Gulf remains favorable. This move highlights the company's continued investment and growth strategy in the region.

title: DI People: JCPenney, 7-Eleven, Recode Therapeutics, Hawkeye, PCCI, and Others Make Moves
summary: This article details numerous executive appointments and promotions across various companies in North Texas, including JCPenney, 7-Eleven, Recode Therapeutics, Hawkeye, and PwC. Key moves include new CEOs for Hawkeye, Harver, and Recode Therapeutics, and significant leadership changes in e-commerce, technology, and operations at other notable firms, reflecting a dynamic period of innovation and growth in the region.

title: Exxon plans to shut Baytown, Texas, crude unit by late next week -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp plans to shut down the 135,000-bpd Pipestill-7 crude distillation unit (CDU) at its Baytown, Texas refinery by late next week for a planned overhaul. This comes as the refinery, Exxon's largest in the U.S., continues to operate at reduced levels following a December 23 explosion.

title: Beyond Local: Imperial Oil continues to innovate bitumen extraction while reducing environmental impact
summary: Imperial Oil is advancing its bitumen extraction methods at its Cold Lake Operations to improve environmental performance. The company is implementing technologies like LASER and SA-SAGD to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and water usage, with the first phase of the SA-SAGD expansion project expected to produce 15,000 barrels per day by 2023. These innovations aim to increase efficiency and reduce the environmental impact of heavy oil recovery.

title: Beyond Local: Imperial Oil continues to innovate bitumen extraction while reducing environmental impact
summary: Imperial Oil is advancing its bitumen extraction methods at its Cold Lake Operations to both increase productivity and reduce environmental impact. The SA-SAGD (Solvent Assisted Steam Assisted Gravity Drainage) expansion project, anticipated to be operational by 2023, aims to produce 15,000 barrels per day while significantly cutting down water usage and greenhouse gas emissions. This new technology utilizes lighter oils and less steam compared to conventional methods.

title: More STACK drilling projects approved
summary: The article details the approval of numerous new oil and gas drilling permits in Oklahoma's STACK region and surrounding counties. Companies like Citizen Energy III LLC, Devon Energy, Ovintiv USA Inc., and others are planning new wells, indicating a significant trend in continued exploration and development within the state. The permits specify locations across various counties including Canadian, Blaine, Kingfisher, Alfalfa, Custer, Ellis, Dewey, Stephens, Love, and Carter, targeting different geological formations.

title: ExxonMobil aims for net zero greenhouse gas emissions from operations by 2050
summary: ExxonMobil has announced its commitment to achieving net zero greenhouse gas emissions from its operations by 2050. This decision comes amid increasing pressure on the oil giant to reduce its carbon footprint. The company's report outlines over 150 potential steps, including efforts to limit methane leaks, to reach this goal.

title: Transocean's Offshore Drilling Rig to Drill Carbon Injection Well in Norway
summary: Transocean's drilling rig, the Transocean Enabler, will be used by Equinor to drill a carbon injection well in Norway for the Northern Lights Carbon Capture Storage Project. This project is a joint venture by Equinor, Shell, and TotalEnergies, aiming to establish Europe's first cross-border CO2 transport and storage network to mitigate emissions. Transocean highlighted its participation as an example of leveraging its core competencies for renewable and alternative energy projects.

title: Gas wells among Oklahoma completions
summary: Two significant gas wells in Oklahoma have been completed, with Continental Resources Inc. reporting a well in Blaine County producing 10,784 Mcf of natural gas per day. Calyx Energy III LLC also completed a gas well in Hughes County with an initial production of 9,746 Mcf per day. Additionally, Mewbourne Oil Company filed a completion report for an Ellis County oil well, yielding 162 barrels of oil and 278 Mcf of natural gas daily.

title: Presbyterian committee recommends denominational divestment from five energy companies
summary: A Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) committee, concerned about climate change and socially responsible investing, has unanimously recommended divestment from five energy companies: Chevron, ExxonMobil, Marathon Petroleum, Phillips 66, and Valero Energy. The Committee on Mission Responsibility Through Investment (MRTI) will ask the 2022 General Assembly to authorize this divestment, citing insufficient progress by these companies in addressing global warming and their poor records on environmental, social, and governance factors. This move is part of broader efforts within the PC(USA) to respond to climate change, with other proposals also heading to the General Assembly, including an overture for complete divestment from the fossil fuel industry.

title: Experts slam oil giant ExxonMobil's net-zero 'ambition'
summary: Exxon Mobil announced an "ambition" to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions in its operations by 2050, focusing only on Scope 1 and 2 emissions. Experts, however, criticized this pledge as insufficient and "too little, too late" because it excludes Scope 3 emissions, which account for about 90% of an oil company's total emissions stemming from the consumption of its products. Environmental advocates argue that the announcement is a distraction, allowing business as usual, and does not align with the urgent need for a drastic reduction in fossil fuel reliance to meet critical climate goals.

title: Imperial Oil to reduce 30 per cent oil sands emission intensity by 2030
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd (IMO-T) plans to cut greenhouse gas emissions intensity from its oil sands operations by 30% by 2030, compared to 2016 levels, through new technologies, efficiency improvements, and carbon capture. The Calgary-based company also affirmed its goal of achieving net-zero Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions in its oil sands operations by 2050, aligning with other Canadian oil sands producers and majority owner Exxon Mobil's similar pledges.

title: Adams Natural Resources Fund Announces 2021 Performance
summary: Adams Natural Resources Fund, Inc. announced strong investment returns for 2021, achieving a 47.7% return on its net asset value, outperforming its benchmark of 46.4%. The fund provided a 6.3% annual distribution rate to shareholders, exceeding its 6.0% minimum commitment. The article details comparative returns, net asset value, and top equity holdings, alongside sector weightings for the year.

title: $10B Exxon-SABIC JV petrochemical plant near Corpus Christi starts operations
summary: Exxon Mobil and SABIC announced the start-up of their $10 billion Gulf Coast Growth Ventures petrochemical plant near Corpus Christi, Texas, in December. The plant features the world's largest ethane steam cracker, capable of producing 1.8 million metric tons of ethylene annually. This joint venture represents a significant new addition to the South Texas petrochemical industry.

title: Camuzzi solicitó un aumento de la tarifa de gas del 79%
summary: Camuzzi Gas Pampeana has requested a 79% increase in gas tariffs, stating that for low-consumption users, this would mean a monthly increase of $104. Transportadora de Gas del Sur (TGS) proposed a cumulative increase of 105% for 2022, applied in two stages. Consumer defense organizations emphasize the importance of considering citizens' income and ensuring that tariff decisions are reasonable and transparent.

title: Residents share mixed feelings over state’s largest proposed renewable energy plant in Dane County
summary: Residents in Dane County, Wisconsin, expressed mixed feelings about the proposed Koshkonong Solar Energy Center, the state's largest renewable energy plant. While some landowners and environmental groups supported the project for its economic and environmental benefits, others raised concerns about its impact on property values, rural aesthetics, and potential health effects. The $649 million project, developed by Invenergy and to be acquired by WEC Energy Group and Madison Gas and Electric, aims to provide 465 megawatts of solar power and contribute to carbon-neutral goals.

title: Why the Sustainable Investment Craze Is Flawed - WSJ
summary: This article questions the effectiveness of sustainable investments (ESG funds) in truly making the world a better place, despite claims from the financial industry and the large sums of money flowing into them. The author argues that selling off "dirty" assets often just shifts ownership without reducing environmental impact, and that the rise of private capital without public reporting exacerbates this issue. This is the first in a series of columns exploring the flaws and potential solutions within ESG investing.

title: U.S. oil CEOs offer opposing views on crude output growth
summary: CEOs from Occidental Petroleum and ConocoPhillips presented differing forecasts for U.S. crude oil output growth at a recent conference, despite surging oil prices reaching seven-year highs. ConocoPhillips CEO Ryan Lance anticipates U.S. output to grow by 800,000 bpd this year and eventually surpass the 2019 record, while Occidental CEO Vicki Hollub expects production to exceed 12 million bpd but fall short of the all-time record. The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) predicts an average of 11.8 million bpd in 2022 and 12.4 million bpd in 2023, with increasing capital expenditure anticipated from producers due to rising prices.

title: Oilfield giant Halliburton revenue surges on rising oil prices
summary: Halliburton reported better-than-expected quarterly and annual revenue, driven by soaring crude oil prices and increased demand for its services. The company's revenue reached $4.3 billion for Q4 2021 and $15.3 billion for the full year, surpassing market predictions. This growth comes as WTI crude prices surged, leading to increased drilling activities in the US.

title: Chesapeake Energy's $2.6 billion deal adds gas assets
summary: Chesapeake Energy announced a $2.6 billion deal to acquire Chief E&D Holdings, strengthening its position in the Marcellus shale gas basin. Concurrently, the company is selling its assets in Wyoming's Powder River Basin for $450 million. These transactions reflect a broader consolidation trend in the U.S. shale patch.

title: Hess Corp. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Hess Corp. (HES) saw its stock advance by 3.11% to $91.50 on Tuesday, despite a generally dismal trading session for the broader market. The company closed just $3.01 below its 52-week high and outperformed some competitors like Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Royal Dutch Shell PLC ADR Cl A (RDS.A) on a day when the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced declines.

title: Continental to buy Chesapeake Energy's Powder River Basin oil, gas assets for $450 million
summary: Continental Resources will acquire Chesapeake Energy's Powder River Basin oil and gas assets for $450 million, expanding Continental's presence in the basin. The deal includes 172,000 net acres and 19,000 boe/d of production. Simultaneously, Chesapeake Energy is set to acquire Chief E&D Holdings' Marcellus assets for $2 billion and 9.44 million shares, bolstering its natural gas portfolio.

title: Chevron shares touch record high ahead of Q4 results
summary: Shares of U.S. oil major Chevron Corp touched an all-time high intraday on Wednesday, boosted by a strong stock market rally and rising oil prices, ahead of its fourth-quarter financial results. Oil prices reached $90 a barrel for the first time in seven years, leading to a surge in major producers' stocks. Analysts anticipate Chevron to report earnings per share of $3.12 for the fourth quarter.

title: Hess plans big spending on oil exploration, production in Guyana & US basin
summary: Hess Corp plans a 37% increase in capital spending for exploration and production in 2022, allocating $2.6 billion, primarily focusing on its operations in Guyana and the U.S. Bakken shale basin. This comes as global crude prices have risen significantly, prompting oil companies to boost exploration and drilling. The company expects net production to average 330,000 to 340,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, excluding Libya.

title: ExxonMobil management fails to manage environment, climate issues
summary: ExxonMobil is facing criticism and lawsuits in Guyana for its ongoing practice of gas flaring, which is illegal and causes significant environmental damage. Despite promises of good corporate citizenship and pledges to curb emissions, the company has accumulated numerous violations, leading to shareholder lawsuits and questions about CEO Darren Woods' leadership. The article highlights that ExxonMobil's managerial issues extend beyond environmental compliance to operational aspects like reserve valuations and drilling strategies.

title: How NextEra is gearing up to be the energy giant of tomorrow
summary: NextEra Energy, led by Jim Robo, aims to become the world's largest, cleanest, and most profitable clean energy provider, leading the decarbonization of the U.S. economy. Originally a traditional utility, NextEra transformed by investing heavily in wind, solar, and battery storage, leveraging tax credits and strategic acquisitions. Despite its green ambitions, the company still relies significantly on natural gas and faces scrutiny over its methane emissions and opposition to "net zero" targets, focusing instead on carbon intensity reduction.

title: Chevron kicks off oil industry's Q4 results with a miss
summary: Chevron (CVX.N) reported fourth-quarter profits that missed Wall Street estimates and provided a weak outlook for this year's oil and gas production, causing its shares to drop. The company's earnings of $2.65 per share were below the $3.12 per share forecast, largely due to weaker output, downstream margins, and a hit from timing of bookings in its LNG business. Despite this, Chevron achieved its best annual earnings since 2014, driven by spending cuts, and announced increased shareholder returns including a share buyback and a dividend hike.

title: ExxonMobil Streamlines Structure to Enhance Effectiveness, Grow Value, Reduce Costs
summary: ExxonMobil is streamlining its business structure by combining chemical and downstream companies and centralizing technology and engineering, along with other support services, to improve customer support, enhance performance, and grow value. This restructuring, effective April 1, will organize the company into three business lines: ExxonMobil Upstream Company, ExxonMobil Product Solutions, and ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions, supported by a single technology organization. The company also plans to relocate its corporate headquarters to its campus north of Houston by mid-2023 to foster closer collaboration and accelerate value delivery.

title: Exxon to combine chemical, refining business in major cost-cutting reorganization
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced a major reorganization to cut costs by combining its chemicals and refining divisions and moving its headquarters to Houston. The oil giant will realign into three business lines starting April 1. This news led to a slight increase in Exxon's stock ahead of its fourth-quarter earnings report.

title: ExxonMobil Exiting Irving HQ for Houston Megacampus
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced it will be moving its corporate headquarters from Irving, Texas, to its megacampus in the Houston area as part of a larger business restructuring. The relocation is anticipated to be finished by mid-2023. The Houston campus spans 385 acres and previously housed over 10,000 Exxon employees.

title: Exxon Mobil to move headquarters out of Irving
summary: Exxon Mobil is moving its corporate headquarters from Irving to Houston, a decision announced as part of the company's plan to streamline its business structure by combining its chemical and downstream operations. This move means that North Texas will lose its second-largest public company upon completion next year.

title: BP Turned a ‘Blind Eye’ to Corruption in Prize Azerbaijan Gas Project
summary: Leaked documents reveal that two Azerbaijani state-owned companies were set to embezzle over $1.7 billion from the Shah Deniz 2 gas project, a venture crucial for the Southern Gas Corridor to Europe, which involved BP. Despite repeated alerts about corruption, BP reportedly took no action as these companies allegedly inflated contracts and charges, with much of the funds being paid before reaching Azerbaijan's state budget. The director of one of the implicated state companies acquired lavish properties in Miami during this period, raising further questions about the flow of funds amidst a government crackdown on civil society.

title: ExxonMobil in Houston: Oil and gas giant announces headquarters are relocating from Irving, Texas to Spring
summary: ExxonMobil is relocating its headquarters from Irving, Texas, to its Spring campus in the Houston area, effective mid-2023. This move is part of a larger business restructuring aimed at enhancing teamwork, streamlining operations, and reducing costs by an estimated $6 billion. Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner welcomed the relocation, highlighting its potential to bring a strong workforce and resources to the city, which is already collaborating with ExxonMobil on carbon capture projects.

title: Exxon announces cost-cutting restructure, plans to move headquarters
summary: Exxon Mobil announced a sweeping restructuring of its global operations, combining its refining and chemicals businesses and elevating its energy transition unit to align with its other core operations. This move is part of the company's ongoing cost-cutting efforts, influenced by activist investors, and is expected to deliver greater shareholder returns. Additionally, Exxon will relocate its corporate headquarters from Irving, Texas, to its campus north of Houston by mid-2023.

title: Exxon unveils sweeping restructuring in latest cost cutting move
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced a major restructuring of its global operations, combining refining and chemicals, and elevating its energy transition business. This aligns with a broader cost-cutting effort initiated after activist investors joined its board. The company aims to cut $6 billion from operating costs by next year and anticipates no job cuts as a result of the changes.

title: Darling Ingredients VP Melissa Gaither to Retire and Suann Guthrie to Succeed
summary: Darling Ingredients Inc. announced that Melissa Gaither, Vice President of Investor Relations, Sustainability, and Global Communications, will retire on April 29 after 33 years of service. Suann Guthrie has been named as her successor, effective January 31, bringing over 20 years of experience in strategy development, media, investor relations, and corporate communications from the tech and energy sectors.

title: Exxon to move HQ to Houston, merge refining and chemicals
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced it will relocate its corporate headquarters from suburban Dallas to the Houston area by mid-2023, combining its chemical and refining divisions. This move is part of a broader shake-up aimed at reducing costs, reorganizing the company into three main business lines, and accelerating its cost-cutting drive to achieve $6 billion in savings by 2023. The reorganization seeks to enhance collaboration and shareholder value through the energy transition.

title: Exxon moves headquarters, reorganizes company
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced a reorganization and plans to move its headquarters to Spring, Texas, near Houston, to streamline operations and cut costs. The revamp includes making its low-carbon division one of its three main business lines and aims to save the company $6 billion compared to 2019. This move follows pressure from a hedge fund to focus on new forms of energy.

title: Imperial Oil misses profit estimates as cold weather hits output
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd reported fourth-quarter profits that narrowly missed estimates due to a hit in oil sands production caused by extreme cold weather in December and January. Although production fell by 3.3%, higher commodity prices and increased demand for motor fuels offset the decline. The company also raised its first-quarter dividend by 26% to 34 Canadian cents per share.

title: Exxon Mobil reports a $8.9 billion fourth-quarter profit as oil prices soar.
summary: Exxon Mobil reported strong fourth-quarter earnings of $8.9 billion, its highest in seven years, driven by soaring oil and natural gas prices. The company also announced it would resume its stock buyback program, repurchasing $10 billion in shares over the next two years, marking its first repurchase since 2016. For the full year, Exxon earned $23 billion, a significant turnaround from a $22.4 billion loss in 2020.

title: ExxonMobil to streamline its business structure
summary: ExxonMobil is streamlining its business structure by combining its chemical and downstream companies and centralizing technology and support services, effective April 1, 2022. The company will be organized into three business lines: ExxonMobil Upstream Company, ExxonMobil Product Solutions, and ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions, all supported by a single technology organization. This restructuring aims to enhance customer service, improve performance, grow value, and achieve over $6 billion in structural cost savings by 2023.

title: Exxon Mobil has deep roots in Houston area
summary: Exxon Mobil's decision to move its headquarters to the Houston area solidifies its long history in the region, which dates back to the 1901 Spindletop oil discovery and the founding of Humble Oil & Refining Co., its predecessor. Over the decades, the company established major refineries and campuses in the Houston area, evolving into Exxon and later merging with Mobil. This move consolidates its operations and reinforces its extensive presence and impact on Houston's energy sector.

title: Exxon Mobil restructures into three divisions and packs up for Houston
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is relocating its corporate headquarters from suburban Dallas to the Houston area by mid-2023 and reorganizing into three main business lines: upstream, product solutions, and low-carbon. This major shake-up aims to reduce costs, with the company on track for $6 billion in savings by 2023. This reorganization will bring top executives to the company's Houston-area campus, fostering closer collaboration and a streamlined business model.

title: Oil companies, union to continue talks on worker contract
summary: Negotiators for major oil companies and the United Steelworkers union met but failed to reach an agreement on a new labor contract covering 30,000 U.S. workers. Both sides agreed to continue talks at a later date, with the union having rejected a 9% pay raise offer over three years. This comes after the union and Marathon Petroleum averted a potential strike by agreeing to a 24-hour extension of the existing contract.

title: Enbridge pipeline extension produces hours of impassioned testimony
summary: A public hearing regarding Enbridge's proposed Line 5 pipeline reroute in northern Wisconsin generated over 10 hours of impassioned testimony. Environmental advocates and some tribal officials expressed concerns about potential ecological harm and climate impact, while supporters highlighted economic benefits and the need for energy resources. The DNR is currently reviewing a draft environmental impact statement and accepting public comments.

title: Oil tops $90, 7-year high
summary: U.S. crude oil surged past $90 per barrel, reaching a 7-year high, with Brent crude hitting $91 per barrel. This rise comes as OPEC declined requests to increase production and national average gas prices hit $3.41 per gallon, leading some experts to predict a potential rise to $4. Geopolitical tensions between Russia and Ukraine are also contributing to the price pressure.

title: Cheniere Completes Train 6 Expansion at Sabine Pass LNG Export Terminal
summary: Cheniere Energy Inc. has completed the commissioning of the sixth liquefaction train at its Sabine Pass LNG terminal in Louisiana, boosting the facility's production capacity to 30 million metric tons/year. This project was completed ahead of schedule and on budget, enhancing Cheniere's position as a major global LNG exporter. The company is also planning an expansion project at its Corpus Christi terminal, and the U.S. is expected to become the world's largest LNG exporter once new projects, including this one, come online.

title: Shell (SHEL) Stock Price, News & Analysis
summary: This article provides a detailed analysis of Shell (NYSE: SHEL) stock, covering its current price, key statistics, company overview, analyst ratings, earnings, valuation, dividend information, and recent news. It highlights Shell's position as a global integrated energy company focusing on both traditional hydrocarbons and developing lower-carbon solutions, emphasizing its "Moderate Buy" consensus rating and a 4.06% dividend yield. The report also includes FAQs about share performance, earnings, buybacks, subsidiaries, major shareholders, and how to buy shares.

title: Price of Diesel Soars 10.5¢ a Gallon to $3.951
summary: The national average price for diesel surged 10.5 cents to $3.951 a gallon, marking a significant increase of 33.8 cents over five weeks and $1.15 more than the previous year. This rise is part of a broader petroleum wave leading to increased costs for fleets, affecting not just fuel but also related components like tires. The price hike is attributed to factors like geopolitical risks and global supply struggling to meet post-pandemic demand, despite efforts by OPEC+ and U.S. shale explorers.

title: Phillips 66 stock rises Monday, outperforms market
summary: Shares of Phillips 66 (PSX) rose 1.63% on Monday, outperforming the mixed market performance where the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained slightly and the S&P 500 Index fell. The stock closed near its 52-week high, marking its second consecutive day of gains. Phillips 66's performance was mixed compared to competitors like Exxon Mobil Corp., Chevron Corp., and Marathon Petroleum Corp., all of which also saw increases.

title: Exxon Mobil, LyondellBasell, others partner with city of Houston to boost plastic recycling
summary: Exxon Mobil, LyondellBasell, and other partners are collaborating with the city of Houston to enhance plastic recycling efforts. This initiative aims to increase the supply of plastic feedstock for ExxonMobil's Baytown facility, diverting plastic from landfills and into recycling streams. Dave Andrew of ExxonMobil Chemical Co. highlights that the main challenge is access to plastic feed, not investment.

title: Federal blue hydrogen incentives: No reliable past, present or future
summary: An IEEFA analysis challenges the economic and environmental viability of "blue" hydrogen, which is produced from natural gas with carbon capture and sequestration (CCS). The analysis concludes that decades of failed CCS experiments and the high emissions from natural gas production (methane) make blue hydrogen an unreliable and environmentally unsound investment. It asserts that blue hydrogen will struggle to compete with renewable energy, electrification, and green hydrogen in the future market.

title: Civitas Grabs Bigger DJ Foothold with Takeover of Bison Oil
summary: Civitas Resources Inc., the largest oil and natural gas producer in the Denver-Julesburg Basin, has acquired Bison Oil & Gas II LLC in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $346 million. This acquisition will add 102 gross locations and increase Civitas' production by 9,000 boe/d, further solidifying its dominant position in the DJ Basin. The transaction involves Bison's private equity sponsor, Carnelian Energy Capital, receiving 2.3 million shares of Civitas and $45 million cash, with Civitas assuming $176 million of Bison's debt.

title: (02/09/22) 11 Drip Stocks You Can Add to Your IRA
summary: This article discusses the challenges and workarounds for investing in Dividend Reinvestment Plans (DRIPs) within an Individual Retirement Account (IRA). It highlights that traditional IRA custodians often don't support DRIPs directly but offers solutions through brokerage firm reinvestment plans or company-sponsored DRIPs that include IRA options. The author then recommends 11 specific DRIP stocks suitable for long-term IRA investing, including companies from the energy, telecommunications, utilities, tobacco, and consumer sectors, noting their yields and market prospects.

title: S&P Global Platts Launches LNG-Fueled TCEs, Newcastlemax Weighted Index
summary: S&P Global Platts has introduced the world's first LNG-fueled Newcastlemax time charter equivalent (TCE) assessments and a ton-mile weighted average index called NMAX GT4, effective February 3, 2022. This initiative addresses the shipping industry's growing need for alternative fuels to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, with LNG offering significant reductions in various pollutants. The new assessments provide market participants with pricing transparency for LNG-fueled dry bulk ships on six key routes, reflecting the industry's shift towards decarbonization.

title: Canadian energy could become a hot commodity, outgoing Petronas Canada CEO says
summary: Outgoing Petronas Energy Canada CEO Mark Fitzgerald believes Canadian natural gas will become a hot commodity due to its potential to be branded based on ESG measures, environmental protections, respect for Indigenous rights, and social policies. He argues that Canada, already a low-cost producer, can differentiate its natural gas from competitors by highlighting these factors, and that the industry needs to educate both global and Canadian audiences about its strong ESG performance. Fitzgerald also asserts that Canadian natural gas will be crucial as a transition fuel in the global move toward a low-carbon future.

title: Singapore Airlines to buy ExxonMobil's sustainable fuel in push to cut emissions
summary: Singapore Airlines, with support from Singapore's civil aviation authority and Temasek, will purchase sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from Exxon Mobil Corp for a year-long pilot program. This initiative aims to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 2,500 tonnes, using 1.25 million litres of neat SAF supplied by Neste Oyj and blended at Exxon Mobil's facilities in Singapore. The move reflects efforts to make air travel more environmentally friendly by leveraging SAF, which produces significantly less carbon than traditional fossil fuels.

title: Glencore moves crude oil trading leader to head LNG division
summary: Glencore has appointed Maxim Kolupaev, formerly the head of its crude oil trading team, to lead its liquefied natural gas (LNG) business division. This move signals a potential new push into the LNG market for Glencore, building on its existing portfolio and recent contracts with Cheniere Energy Inc. and Novatek. Kolupaev brings over five years of experience in crude oil trading to his new role, which also encompasses natural gas and electric power markets.

title: ConocoPhillips to weigh $1 billion Permian assets sale
summary: ConocoPhillips is considering selling over $1 billion in Permian Basin assets, working with an adviser to run an auction process. This potential sale follows its $9.5 billion acquisition of Shell's Permian operations and aligns with its strategy to high-grade its asset base and return cash to shareholders, encouraged by surging oil prices. The company had previously raised its asset sale target to between $4 billion and $5 billion by 2023, with proceeds expected primarily from the Permian Basin.

title: Exxon Mobil expands oil futures, products trading in Europe
summary: Exxon Mobil is reinvesting in its European oil trading division after previous budget cuts and an exodus of staff, with new hires and an expansion into speculative oil futures trading beyond hedging its own production. This move follows the company's biggest profit in seven years during the fourth quarter of 2021.

title: ConocoPhillips considers sale of $1bn worth of Permian basin assets in US
summary: ConocoPhillips is reportedly considering selling over $1 billion worth of its assets in the Permian Basin, specifically in the Delaware region of West Texas and New Mexico. This move follows its $9.5 billion acquisition of Shell's Permian operations in late 2021 and is part of a strategy to high-grade its portfolio and raise between $4 billion and $5 billion through asset sales by 2023. The divestment comes as global oil and gas companies seek to reduce debt and capitalize on surging oil prices.

title: Guyana May Choose to Develop Future Oil Prospects on Its Own
summary: Guyana is considering forming a national oil and gas company to manage its future exploration efforts rather than holding an offshore drilling auction this year. This decision could impact how the country develops its significant oil discoveries. Vice President Bharrat Jagdeo indicated that a choice between an auction or a national company would be made by the third quarter of the year.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise set to move into its new global headquarters in Spring
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is opening its new global headquarters in Spring, north of Houston, as construction on its 440,000 square-foot campus wraps up. Employees have begun voluntarily moving into the space, which is expected to serve as a collaborative cultural center for its 2,200 Houston-area employees. This move from California, announced in December 2020, solidifies City Place as a growing corporate hub with significant ongoing residential and commercial development.

title: Norway's oil firms hike 2022 investment plans
summary: Norway's oil and gas companies are set to increase their 2022 investments to nearly $18 billion, higher than initially forecast, taking advantage of pandemic-era tax incentives. This financial boost, however, is likely to draw criticism from environmental groups concerned about continued fossil fuel spending amid global warming efforts. Despite this, Norway aims to continue fossil fuel production due to ongoing global demand while also investing heavily in cleaner energy.

title: Facing Texas pushback, BlackRock says it supports fossil fuels
summary: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, is emphasizing its support for the fossil fuel industry to counter potential exclusion from Texas state pension funds. This move comes as Texas comptroller Glenn Hegar is mandated to create a list of financial companies boycotting fossil fuels, which could impact BlackRock's significant investments within the state. Despite its past focus on climate change and ESG factors, BlackRock asserts it will continue to invest in and back energy companies, highlighting its existing large holdings in Texas-based fossil fuel firms.

title: Energy Transfer joins in rush to build Permian gas pipeline
summary: Energy Transfer LP is joining other energy companies in the competitive race to construct a new pipeline that will transport natural gas from the Permian Basin to Gulf Coast export hubs. The company aims to complete its project within two years of a final investment decision, utilizing existing assets, and analysts consider their proposal to be a highly economic option for the region. Energy Transfer is also progressing with other major projects, including the Gulf Run pipeline in Louisiana and its own LNG export facility at Lake Charles.

title: Irving-based chemicals firm Celanese strikes $11 billion deal for DuPont business
summary: Irving-based chemicals company Celanese Corp. is acquiring the majority of DuPont de Nemours Inc.’s mobility and materials business for $11 billion in cash, marking one of the largest chemicals deals since 2020. This acquisition will significantly expand Celanese's engineered materials capabilities, particularly for future mobility, connectivity, and medical uses. Celanese expects the deal to add $4 or more per share to its earnings by 2026 and double its total free cash flow within five years.

title: Hubba Hubba: Appalachia Sees Continued Investment in Carbon Capture and Storage
summary: Appalachia is seeing continued investment in carbon capture and storage (CCS) with a new hydrogen and carbon capture hub planned for Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia by a coalition of major energy, petrochemical, and steel companies. This initiative aims to reduce emissions across various industries, create jobs, and drive innovation, modeling an integrated low-emission energy and production system. The region's abundant natural gas resources are key to producing blue hydrogen, a process that separates hydrogen from natural gas with the resulting carbon dioxide stored underground, showcasing Appalachia's role in a lower carbon future.

title: Skadden, Kirkland lead DuPont’s $11 bln sale of unit to Celanese
summary: DuPont has engaged Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom for its $11 billion sale of its mobility and materials business to Celanese Corp. Celanese, in turn, is being advised by Kirkland & Ellis and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher for the acquisition and its financing. This deal marks DuPont's largest transaction since its separation from DowDuPont, as it continues to streamline its portfolio.

title: Roy Fuller Obituary - Dallas, TX
summary: Roy Lee Fuller, born March 25, 1927, passed away peacefully on February 20, 2022, at the age of 94. He had a notable career trajectory from Geophysical Services Inc. (GSI) to Texas Instruments, followed by an energetic retirement involving hardware store ownership, chamber of commerce leadership, and rural land investments. Fuller, a veteran of WWII and a gifted musician, is survived by his wife Pat, children, stepchildren, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren.

title: The Top Carbon ETF’s of 2022: Investing Ideas for Canadians
summary: This article identifies the top carbon ETFs for Canadian investors in 2022, highlighting newly available options on Canadian exchanges like Horizons Carbon Credits ETF (CARB) and Ninepoint Carbon Credit ETF (CBON). It also discusses the U.S.-based KraneShares Global Carbon Strategy ETF (KRBN) and Carbon Streaming Corporation (NETZ) as significant investments in the carbon market. The piece emphasizes the growing accessibility of carbon-related investments due to global decarbonization efforts.

title: ‘Clear signs of recovery’ – Sasol CEO
summary: Sasol reported strong operational results for the first half of its 2022 financial year, with adjusted Ebitda increasing 71% to R31.8 billion and cash flow up 60% to R27.9 billion. Despite these positive figures and "clear signs of recovery" to pre-pandemic levels, the company is retaining interim dividends due to high macroeconomic uncertainty. Sasol continues to prioritize debt reduction, aiming to repay R18.2 billion in outstanding debt by November 2022.

title: Alta do petróleo turbina arrecadação dos governos e lucros da Petrobras enquanto gasolina e diesel sobem no posto
summary: The article discusses how the rising price of oil has significantly boosted the revenue of the Brazilian federal, state, and municipal governments, as well as the profits of Petrobras, despite increasing fuel costs for consumers. In the last three years, the federal government alone accumulated at least R$123 billion from royalties, special participations, and Petrobras dividends. States and municipalities also saw substantial increases in their coffers from oil-related revenues, leading to discussions in Congress about using these extraordinary gains to mitigate the impact of higher fuel prices on consumers.

title: Marathon Petroleum Corp: What are oil workers fighting against?
summary: This article details the struggles of US oil refinery workers against Marathon Petroleum Corp. and the United Steelworkers union. It highlights Marathon's substantial profits, the impact of federal bailouts and layoffs on workers, and the demand for a nationwide refinery strike amidst stagnant wage offers and ongoing exploitation.

title: Exxon, PNG sign deal to clear way for P'nyang gas field
summary: Exxon Mobil and its partners have signed a deal with the Papua New Guinea (PNG) government to develop the P'nyang gas field, ending years of uncertainty. Gas from P'nyang will supply Exxon's LNG plant in PNG after current sources are depleted. This agreement, which secures a 63% government take, is considered a significant win for PNG and sets a new benchmark for future negotiations.

title: Texas oil refinery workers ratify Exxon labor contract offer
summary: Unionized workers at Exxon Mobil's Beaumont, Texas, refinery voted to accept a new labor contract, ending a nearly 10-month lockout. The new agreement grants Exxon the right to determine plant assignments, a key company demand, and adds Martin Luther King Jr. Day as a paid holiday. Despite the contract's approval, the United Steelworkers union plans to continue pursuing an unfair labor practices complaint against Exxon.

title: Newpark Resources settles conflict with activist investor, expands board
summary: Newpark Resources has settled a conflict with activist investor Brad Radoff, who had advocated for the company to sell off its fluid systems business. As part of the agreement, Newpark Resources will expand its board. Radoff's main concern was that the fluid systems business, which primarily serves the upstream oil and gas industry, did not turn a profit in 2021.

title: Opinion: As the stock market struggles, look at these ‘hard-asset’ commodity funds
summary: Amidst stock market struggles and escalating geopolitical tensions, "hard-asset" commodity funds are presented as a potential haven for investors. These assets, including metals, fossil fuels, and agricultural goods, are benefiting from inflationary pressures and offer a degree of stability compared to more volatile investments like small-cap growth stocks or cryptocurrencies. The article suggests that these funds could be a strategic investment during periods of market uncertainty.

title: Iraq to develop oil and gas in the Western Desert in collaboration with Halliburton Co., Saudi Aramco
summary: Iraq plans to collaborate with Halliburton Co. and Saudi Aramco to develop oil and gas reserves in its Western Desert, specifically in the Anbar province and the Akkas natural gas field. This initiative aims to reduce Iraq's dependence on oil for electricity and achieve gas self-sufficiency by 2025. The Iraqi government will cover development costs, with potential investment from Saudi Aramco.

title: El Gobierno autoriza ajustes para distribuidoras y transportadoras de gas a partir de marzo
summary: The Argentine government has authorized gas tariff adjustments for distributors and transporters, resulting in an average 20% increase for residential users and 15% for SMEs starting in March. This measure was implemented through Decree 91/2022 after public hearings and aims to reduce state subsidies that covered the difference caused by a three-year tariff freeze. The decree ratifies agreements between the Ministry of Economy, the Enargas, and gas companies, impacting factures with adjustments based on gas price, transport, distribution, and taxes.

title: Exxon's workforce falls by 9,000 in 2021 amid cost cuts
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced a reduction of 9,000 global employees in 2021 as a result of a comprehensive cost-cutting program initiated after the COVID-19 pandemic. This workforce reduction contributed to the company's best annual profit in seven years in 2021, following a historic loss in 2020. The company plans further restructuring, including combining refining and chemicals businesses and cutting $6 billion from operating costs by next year.

title: ExxonMobil Makes First Commercial Sale of Certified Circular Polymers
summary: ExxonMobil announced its first commercial sale of certified circular polymers, produced using its Exxtend™ advanced recycling technology, to Berry Global for food-grade packaging. The company's Baytown, Texas facility has processed over 4 million pounds of plastic waste and plans to significantly increase its global annual advanced recycling capacity to 1 billion pounds by 2026 to meet growing market demand for sustainable plastics. This move aims to expand the range of recyclable plastic materials and support a more circular economy.

title: Over the Hedge: The Best Commodities To Invest in
summary: This article explores the best commodities to invest in, including energy, metals, and agriculture, as a hedge against inflation and stock market volatility. It delves into the pros and cons of commodity investing, specific opportunities within each category like oil & gas, lithium, gold, copper, silver, palladium, hemp, and coffee, and various methods for gaining exposure to these markets. The author emphasizes diversification and understanding market factors, geopolitical risks, and extraneous events like weather.

title: Where are Houston’s Fortune 500 companies? Downtown still reigns.
summary: Downtown Houston remains the primary location for Fortune 500 companies, housing ten of the 25 located in the greater Houston area. North Houston has recently gained two major Fortune 500 headquarters with Exxon Mobil and Hewlett Packard Enterprise relocating there, while other concentrations of these companies are found in West Houston, Energy Corridor, Memorial City, Katy, and the Galleria area. The article details the specific companies and their locations, highlighting the diverse geographical distribution of Houston's top businesses.

title: Exxon, union reach tentative return-to-work deal for locked-out refinery workers -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and the United Steelworkers union (USW) have reached a tentative agreement for nearly 600 workers locked out of a Beaumont, Texas, refinery to return to work starting in March. The USW Local 13-243 is scheduled to vote on the agreement, which would end the lockout that began in May 2021. The agreement outlines the return of workers while an investigation by the U.S. National Labor Relations Board into alleged unfair labor practices continues.

title: Oil companies, union reach deal on U.S. refinery workers pact
summary: Oil companies, led by Marathon Petroleum, and the United Steelworkers union have reached a new national contract for 30,000 U.S. refinery, chemical plant, and pipeline workers. The four-year agreement includes a 12% pay increase and provisions for union health and safety representatives at each facility. Negotiations stalled earlier but resumed after union protests, leading to the new agreement.

title: bp to exit Rosneft shareholding | News and insights | Home
summary: BP announced its decision to exit its 19.75% shareholding in Rosneft due to Russia's aggression against Ukraine. Both BP-nominated directors, Bernard Looney and Bob Dudley, will resign from Rosneft's board, leading to a material non-cash charge in BP's Q1 2022 results. BP's financial framework and distribution guidance remain unchanged, but it will no longer report Rosneft's results.

title: Exxon Texas refinery lockout to end on March 7
summary: Exxon Mobil announced that a 10-month lockout of union workers at its southeast Texas refinery will end on March 7, following the United Steelworkers union's acceptance of a return-to-work agreement. The agreement allows nearly 600 locked-out workers to return, after a new six-year contract was ratified that gives Exxon control over job assignments. The union's long-term presence at the refinery remains subject to a pending NLRB investigation regarding the lockout and a vote to remove the union.

title: Shell Is Leaving Joint Ventures With Russia's Gazprom
summary: Shell announced its decision to withdraw from joint ventures with Russia's Gazprom and related entities. This move follows Russia's invasion of Ukraine and aligns with similar actions taken by other companies like BP. The departure signifies a significant response from the energy sector to the geopolitical conflict.

title: The Energy Sector: 6 Things To Know
summary: This article discusses the energy sector, highlighting its evolving nature beyond traditional oil and gas to include clean energy sources. It emphasizes the sector's continued ties to oil prices, especially in light of geopolitical events like the Russia-Ukraine crisis, and explores various investment avenues, including individual stocks, ETFs, and both traditional and renewable energy options.

title: Halliburton Opens Saudi Chemical Research Plant
summary: Halliburton has officially opened a new chemical reaction plant in Saudi Arabia. This facility will manufacture a wide range of chemicals for the oil and gas industry, as well as other sectors, and will expand Halliburton's research into specialty chemicals for oilfield stimulation and production. This investment reinforces Halliburton's commitment to Saudi Arabia and supports the local In-Kingdom Total Value Add program.

title: Exxon Mobil to exit major Russian venture, will not invest in new developments
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced it is halting operations of its Sakhalin-1 oil and gas venture in Russia and taking steps to exit the project. This decision comes in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Exxon Mobil stated its support for the people of Ukraine, deplored Russia’s military action, and affirmed compliance with all sanctions.

title: Exxon Mobil says it plans to leave its last remaining Russian project. (Published 2022)
summary: Exxon Mobil announced its withdrawal from its last Russian oil and gas project, Sakhalin-1, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This decision comes after similar moves by BP and Shell, marking the end of an era for Western oil companies in Russia. Exxon cited humanitarian reasons and safety obligations for its phased exit from the project, in which it holds a 30% stake.

title: Exxon to Shut Down Oil Production in Russia After Ukraine Attack
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced it is halting operations at a multibillion-dollar oil and gas project in Russia and will cease further investments in the country due to its invasion of Ukraine. The U.S. oil giant is preparing to shut down production from the Sakhalin Island development, where it holds a 30% stake alongside Russian, Japanese, and Indian partners, and plans to exit the consortium. This decision follows similar moves by other major energy companies like BP and Shell.

title: Chevron CEO points to 'difficult decisions' by competitors to leave Russia
summary: Chevron CEO Michael Wirth expressed concern over the situation in Ukraine, acknowledging the difficult decisions competitors made regarding operations in Russia. He highlighted Chevron's limited exposure to Russia and emphasized the importance of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium for world oil supply. Wirth also discussed increasing cybersecurity spending and plans for Chevron to boost oil output in the Permian shale basin and Kazakhstan.

title: Exxon Mobil to discontinue operations at Russia's Sakhalin-1
summary: Exxon Mobil announced it is beginning the process to discontinue operations and exit the Sakhalin-1 venture in Russia. The company also stated it would not be investing in any new developments in Russia. This decision follows escalating international pressure on companies to divest from Russia.

title: H2U Technologies Closes $11M in Series A Funding from Jericho Energy Ventures, Freeflow Ventures, VoLo Earth Ventures, and Hess Corporation
summary: H2U Technologies has successfully closed an oversubscribed $11 million Series A funding round, led by Jericho Energy Ventures, Freeflow Ventures, VoLo Earth Ventures, and Hess Corporation. The company plans to use the proceeds to advance its innovative electrolyzer designs and build its proprietary Catalyst Discovery Engine™, which utilizes AI to identify non-Platinum Group Metal (PGM) PEM catalysts for green hydrogen production. This development aims to significantly reduce the cost and reliance on rare earth metals for clean hydrogen, thereby accelerating the energy transition and decarbonization efforts.

title: Kinross Gold suspending Russian mining operations amid Ukraine invasion
summary: Kinross Gold Corp. has decided to suspend its mining operations and all development work in Russia due to the ongoing military invasion of Ukraine. Russia accounted for 23% of Kinross's production last year, with the Kupol mine being its most profitable operation. The company cited the safety of its 2,000+ employees and adherence to sanctions as reasons for the decision, which comes amidst broader corporate withdrawals from Russia and existing political risk concerns for Kinross's stock.

title: SNC-Lavalin, Kinross Gold among Canadian players with Russian dealings
summary: Despite sweeping sanctions against Russia following its invasion of Ukraine, several prominent Canadian companies, including SNC-Lavalin and Kinross Gold, continued to have business dealings and investments in Russia. The article details the specific ventures of these companies within Russia's resource and manufacturing sectors, highlighting their efforts to distance themselves or comply with evolving sanctions. It also touches on Canadian government responses and the broader impact of sanctions on high-profile Russian oligarchs and their Canadian connections.

title: Alberto Fernández confirmó que el aumento del 20% en las tarifas es solo el comienzo
summary: President Alberto Fernández announced that the 20% increase in utility rates for electricity and gas is just the beginning of continuous price hikes, aligning with IMF demands. These increases, tied to salary indices, are criticized for disproportionately affecting informal workers and for not clarifying the real costs of production and distribution. The government's decision to prioritize capitalist profits and pass the burden of reduced energy subsidies onto the population is expected to lead to further mobilization from workers.

title: Exxon to exit Russia, leaving $4 bln in assets
summary: Exxon Mobil announced its decision to exit Russian oil and gas operations and halt new investments due to Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, impacting over $4 billion in assets and putting a proposed LNG facility on Sakhalin Island in doubt. This move follows similar actions by other Western companies, though Exxon's Russian business is considered relatively small within its wider enterprise. The company had been under pressure to sever ties and is now evacuating U.S. employees from the region.

title: Exxon Deplores Ukraine Attack, Begins Russia Exit, CEO Says
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has started the process of exiting its Russian operations, including its stake in the Sakhalin-1 oil development, due to international sanctions and Russia's actions in Ukraine. CEO Darren Woods stated this would be a "complicated" process. The Sakhalin-1 asset is valued at approximately $4 billion and contributes 1% to 2% of Exxon's earnings.

title: Exxon Mobil plans to exit Russian operations following Ukraine invasion
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced its plan to exit operations in Russia, including its stake and operator position in the Sakhalin-1 oil field, and reverse future investments in the country. This decision comes in response to the Ukraine invasion, with the company's Russian assets valued at over $4 billion.

title: Oil Prices Drop as Iran Deal is Renegotiated
summary: Oil prices dropped to $110 per barrel after the prospect of Iranian crude returning to the market emerged amidst renegotiations of the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. The U.S. and other nations are in talks to restore the agreement, which could bring Iranian oil back, potentially offsetting Russian supply. This development has implications for funds like the Invesco DB Oil Fund (DBO), which tracks crude oil market value without direct commodity exposure.

title: Insurance giant AIG joins movement against financing Arctic oil development
summary: Insurance giant American International Group (AIG) announced it will no longer support new Arctic energy exploration, coal-fired plants, or coal mines as part of its commitment to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. This decision has received mixed reactions in Alaska, with environmental groups like The Wilderness Society commending AIG for protecting Indigenous communities and addressing climate change, while industry alliances express disappointment, viewing the move as politically motivated and hindering responsible resource development. AIG joins other insurance companies and banks in taking similar stances against Arctic drilling.

title: Halliburton opens first-of-its-kind chemical plant in Saudi Arabia
summary: Halliburton has opened a new chemical plant in Jubail, Saudi Arabia, marking a significant investment in the country. This facility is part of the $1 billion Halliburton has invested in Saudi Arabia over the last decade. Executives from Aramco and Halliburton CEO Jeff Miller were present at the inauguration.

title: Canadian Natural Resources reports Q4 profit up, raises quarterly dividend
summary: Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. reported a significant increase in its fourth-quarter profit and raised its quarterly dividend by 28%, despite the volatile oil market exacerbated by global geopolitical events. The company emphasized a prudent, longer-term perspective on oil prices, highlighting its focus on sustainable dividend increases and strong debt reduction, with net debt decreasing by $1.9 billion. CNRL's revenue soared to $9.21 billion in Q4, and its full-year earnings reached $7.66 billion.

title: First U.S. refiner suspends purchases of Russian crude for Hawaii refinery
summary: Par Pacific Holdings Inc. has announced it will suspend purchases of Russian crude oil for its Hawaii refinery, becoming the first U.S. refiner to publicly do so after sanctions imposed due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The company plans to source crude from North and South America and was the fifth largest U.S. importer of Russian crude in 2021. This move comes as other Western companies halt Russian operations and the U.S. considers further sanctions on Russia's oil sector.

title: Exxon sues U.S. over taxes related to gas project in Qatar
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has filed a lawsuit against the U.S. government seeking a partial refund of $2.1 billion in taxes and penalties. The taxes are related to a gas project in Qatar, with Exxon alleging overpayment of income taxes and misclassification of agreements. The company claims the U.S. erroneously collected taxes for tax years 2010 and 2011 and has not respected the partnership's decision to finance its venture with debt.

title: Commodity funds post hefty gains over the past week
summary: Commodity mutual funds and ETFs experienced significant gains over the last week due to rising crude oil and metal prices, intensified by the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Key performers included ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil, United States Oil Fund LP, and iShares S&P GSCI Commodity-Indexed Trust, with oil prices reaching 2008 highs and other commodity futures also soaring. This surge led to a net inflow of $7.9 billion into commodity funds in February, marking the largest influx since August 2020.

title: U.S. OKs 2,700,000 bbls of crude oil from SPR to ExxonMobil -statement
summary: The U.S. Department of Energy has approved the release of 2.7 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to ExxonMobil Corp. This action is part of the Biden administration's broader initiative, authorized in November 2021, to enhance the U.S. fuel supply.

title: The Scale of Shell's Global AI Predictive Maintenance Program
summary: Shell has successfully scaled its AI-driven predictive maintenance program to monitor over 10,000 pieces of equipment globally, significantly reducing operating costs, preventing downtime, and improving safety and environmental outcomes. This achievement, made possible through a partnership with C3 AI and Microsoft Azure, involves ingesting 20 billion rows of data weekly and running over 10,000 machine learning models. Shell is now making its predictive maintenance solutions commercially available through the Open AI Energy Initiative to accelerate the energy transition across the industry.

title: How BlackRock, Vanguard, and UBS Are Screwing the World
summary: This article argues that major asset management firms like BlackRock, Vanguard, and UBS, despite controlling trillions in wealth, are hindering progress on climate change. They are heavily invested in fossil fuel and agribusiness companies, and also profit from unjust responses to crises through investments in private prisons and border security. The author contends that their business model prioritizes short-term returns and fee generation over genuine climate sustainability, necessitating comprehensive regulatory strategies and public investment to achieve climate justice.

title: GE Turbines Will Power New 2-GW Gas-Fired Plant in China
summary: GE Gas Power and Harbin Electric announced that Chinese utility Shenzhen Energy Group Corporation Co. has ordered three GE 9HA.01 gas turbines for its new 2-GW Guangming combined cycle power plant in China. This plant, expected to be operational by late 2023, will help replace the electricity output from the retiring Guangdong Shajiao coal-fired complex. The project highlights China's move towards gas-fired power generation to support its energy transition and emissions reduction goals.

title: Exxon Mobil CEO says oil companies were in tough position before Ukraine-Russia war
summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods stated that oil companies were challenged to ramp up production to meet demand even before the Ukraine crisis due to underinvestment during the COVID-19 pandemic and reduced government support. Woods also highlighted the global energy security needs exposed by the conflict and Exxon's efforts to increase production despite also halting operations in Russia. The article touches on rising oil prices, the U.S. government's deliberation on banning Russian oil imports, and the interconnectedness of the energy industry.

title: Dow slides nearly 800 points as oil hits $120 a barrel while Russia conflict rattles investors
summary: Global stocks, including the Nasdaq, dropped significantly as oil prices surged to $120 a barrel. This market reaction was driven by investor concerns over potential sanctions on Russian crude oil and the broader economic implications of the conflict in Ukraine.
