title: ExxonMobil Guyana Advances Fifth Offshore Guyana Development
summary: ExxonMobil has made a final investment decision for the Uaru development, its fifth project offshore Guyana, following government approvals. This project is expected to add approximately 250,000 barrels of daily capacity starting in 2026, representing a $12.7 billion investment. ExxonMobil aims to have six Floating Production Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessels online by the end of 2027, increasing Guyana's production capacity to over 1.2 million barrels per day.

title: Eni mulls second floating LNG platform in Mozambique
summary: Italian energy company Eni SpA is considering building a second floating liquefied natural gas (LNG) platform in Mozambique's Rovuma Basin, aiming to replicate the success of its Coral Sul project. This move would leverage Mozambique's vast gas reserves and strategic location to contribute significantly to European energy security and global energy needs, while maintaining a competitive edge in emissions performance.

title: Questions over accounting and inclusion mar Guyana’s unprecedented carbon scheme
summary: Guyana has launched an unprecedented carbon credit scheme, selling credits from its vast, intact forests to Hess Corporation for $750 million, with 15% allocated to Indigenous communities. However, the initiative faces scrutiny from climate experts who question the methodology used to calculate emissions reductions for forests already under low threat of deforestation, arguing the credits are overstated. Additionally, disputes have arisen among Indigenous groups regarding the adequacy and legality of consultations prior to including their lands in the carbon market.

title: Imperial Oil hoping Cold Lake carbon capture project will be running before 2030
summary: Imperial Oil announced plans for its Cold Lake carbon capture project to be operational before 2030, ahead of the larger Pathways Alliance carbon capture and storage network. The company reported strong first-quarter earnings of $1.25 billion and increased its quarterly dividend. This initiative is a key part of the oilsands majors' commitment to achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, despite industry concerns about the federal government's 2030 emissions reduction targets.

title: Exxon delivers record first-quarter profit on higher output
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp reported a record first-quarter profit, surpassing analyst estimates due to increased oil and gas production, which also pushed its shares to an all-time high. Despite softening energy prices, robust output from its Permian Basin operations, Guyana fields, and the Beaumont refinery expansion contributed to a significant rise in net profit. The company's cash balance reached $32.7 billion, with executives focusing on organic growth rather than acquisitions, while anticipating even higher cash reserves in the future.

title: Curtiss-Wright signs subsea canned motor pump agreement with Shell
summary: Curtiss-Wright Corp has secured an agreement with Shell Exploration & Production Company to manufacture, test, and provide operational support for an Electro-Submersible Pump (ESP) for an offshore platform in the Gulf of Mexico. This initiative aims to demonstrate Curtiss-Wright's canned motor technology as a reliable alternative to current subsea pump technologies, reducing outages. A test facility will also be constructed to demonstrate the pump's capability before deployment, with the first ESP expected to be ready for delivery by year-end.

title: Energy ETFs to Bet on Solid Q1 Earnings From Exxon, Chevron
summary: Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX) reported strong first-quarter profits, surpassing analyst estimates, despite a decline in oil and natural gas prices compared to the previous year. These robust earnings are expected to positively impact energy ETFs that heavily allocate to these two oil majors. The article highlights several such ETFs, including Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE), iShares U.S. Energy ETF (IYE), Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE), Fidelity MSCI Energy Index ETF (FENY), and Strive U.S. Energy ETF (DRLL), detailing their holdings, expense ratios, and risk outlooks.

title: Exxon Mobil not quitting exploration in Brazil
summary: Exxon Mobil clarified that it is not abandoning oil exploration in Brazil, contrary to recent reports. Alberto Ferrin, the company's Brazil country chief, stated during the Offshore Technology Conference that Exxon is actively looking for exploration opportunities in the country due to its favorable conditions, similar to its successful ventures in Guyana. The company maintains an 89% success rate in Guyana and sees Brazil as offering similar exploration enablers.

title: BCI calling for increased climate disclosure at Imperial Oil, Caisse pre-leasing Chilean mixed-use development
summary: The British Columbia Investment Management Corp. (BCI) is advocating for increased climate disclosure from Imperial Oil Ltd. by filing a shareholder proposal requesting greater transparency on climate risks and liabilities. Separately, the real estate arm of Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec, Ivanhoé Cambridge, is pre-leasing a mixed-use development called Somma Asturias in Santiago, Chile. This development, a joint venture with Greystar Real Estate Partners, includes apartments, office space, and retail facilities.

title: State Street CEO: Divestment Will Slow Clean Energy Transition
summary: State Street CEO Ron O’Hanley stated that pressuring large asset managers to divest from polluting companies will hinder the clean energy transition by politicizing the issue and cutting off necessary investment for these industries to innovate. He argues that polluting industries require continued investment to facilitate their shift towards cleaner energy and reduce carbon emissions. O'Hanley's comments come amidst criticism from environmentalists urging financial firms like State Street to divest from oil and gas producers.

title: Welcome to the DIG Drilling Intelligence Group moves into new space
summary: ConocoPhillips' Drilling Intelligence Group (DIG) officially moved into its new, redesigned space in Midland, transforming a former storage area into an advanced technology center. The new facility, named the DIG, allows directional drillers, operations personnel, and engineers to monitor drilling activity, analyze data, and provide real-time support to enhance overall drilling performance and leverage rig-automation capabilities. The space was designed for future growth, with plans to integrate more disciplines to further improve learnings and performance.

title: World’s first oil tanker shipping ETF starts trading in New York
summary: John Kartsonas-led Breakwave Advisors has launched the world’s first tanker shipping exchange traded fund (ETF) on the New York Stock Exchange. The Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF (BWET) offers exposure to the crude oil tanker shipping market using near-dated futures contracts. This launch capitalizes on high demand for oil transportation, limited vessel orderbooks, and geopolitical disruptions affecting oil markets.

title: 5 Biggest Oil Companies in Texas
summary: This article discusses the top oil companies based in Texas, highlighting their revenue, hedge fund interest, and operational specifics. The initial entry covered is EOG Resources Inc. (NYSE:EOG), emphasizing its financial performance, production capabilities, and commitment to shareholder returns.

title: Strive Asset Management fills leadership vacuum created by CEO's run for president
summary: Matt Cole has been appointed CEO of Strive Asset Management, taking over from co-founder Vivek Ramaswamy who resigned to pursue a presidential bid. Cole, previously CIO, will continue Strive's mission to prioritize shareholder value over stakeholder value, emphasizing an "anti-woke" approach to investing and proxy voting. Strive has launched eight ETFs totaling over $700 million and aims to offer an alternative to traditional ESG-focused asset managers.

title: The Alaskan gambit: $44 billion LNG project decades in the making
summary: A planned $44 billion natural gas project in Alaska, decades in the making, aims to pipe gas from the North Slope to an LNG terminal near Anchorage for export to Asian markets. This initiative, supported by the Biden administration, seeks to revitalize Alaska's declining oil and gas industry and provide a reliable energy source to allies like South Korea and Japan, despite environmental concerns and financing challenges. The project faces questions about its necessity amidst a flood of Gulf Coast LNG projects and the long-term demand for natural gas as nations shift to renewables.

title: Formal investigation into Kearl oil sands leaks begins
summary: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) has launched a formal investigation into the tailings leaks at the Kearl oil sands project, co-owned by Imperial Oil and ExxonMobil Canada. This follows accusations from the Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation that Alberta regulators covered up the spill and failed to alert downstream Indigenous communities for a year. The Alberta Energy Regulator (AER) confirmed the presence of naphthenic acids in a lake feeding into the Firebag River, as Imperial Oil implements mitigation systems and asserts drinking water safety.

title: MODEC Confirms Its First FPSO Order in Guyana
summary: MODEC has secured its first FPSO order in Guyana for the Uaru project, following a final investment decision by ExxonMobil. The FPSO, named ‘Errea Wittu’, will be the fifth in Guyana and MODEC's first for the country, with the company also providing operation and maintenance services for 10 years. This project marks a significant return to working with ExxonMobil for MODEC, showcasing their continued collaboration in major offshore developments.

title: Elliott Target Suncor's New CEO Plans Long Stay at Helm
summary: Rich Kruger, Suncor Energy Inc.'s new CEO, has come out of retirement to lead the struggling Canadian oil producer, with input from activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP. Kruger has expressed his commitment to the role for the long term, even selling his Texas home to relocate to Calgary. His priorities include improving Suncor's safety record, though he does not plan to revisit selling the company's Petro-Canada retail business, a previous recommendation by Elliott.

title: B.C. innovators charting routes to greener fuel options for the global marine industry
summary: B.C. companies, including Methanex Corp., Atlas Corp. (Seaspan), and Robert Allan Ltd., are leading the charge in developing greener fuel options for the global marine industry. Methanol and LNG are frontrunners in the transition to low-carbon shipping, with a mix of fuels expected to be the long-term solution. These innovators are addressing the challenge of decarbonizing the international shipping fleet through technological advancements and strategic partnerships.

title: LNG is surging. Can FERC reviews keep up?
summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) faces challenges in reviewing natural gas export projects, with legal observers noting ambiguous directives and a lack of clear guidance in the Natural Gas Act, which governs FERC's oversight of LNG. This ambiguity creates debate among lawmakers pushing for quicker approvals and environmental advocates concerned about the climate impact and thoroughness of assessments. The issue is critical as U.S. LNG exports surge, driven by European demand for alternatives to Russian fuel.

title: CRC Goes Big on Carbon
summary: California Resources Corp. (CRC) is investing heavily in carbon capture and storage, with plans to spend $2.5 billion over five years to inject carbon dioxide back into the earth, particularly in mature oil fields like Elk Hills. This strategy is a response to environmental pressures and aims to demonstrate the oil industry's commitment to carbon neutrality while continuing operations, and potentially pre-empting stricter state regulations on carbon capture projects. The company has already secured several agreements to sequester over 600,000 metric tons of CO2 annually and is seeking permits for significantly more storage capacity.

title: Indonesia’s coal gasification plans hit as Air Products withdraws
summary: Air Products and Chemicals withdrew from a $15bn coal gasification investment in Indonesia, including a $2.3bn plant, less than two years after the project was announced. This withdrawal signals deteriorating financial prospects for coal-to-chemicals projects, further complicated by rising US interest rates and questionable economic viability without massive government subsidies. Attention now turns to whether a Chinese company might step in, despite concerns about environmental impacts, increased debt, and the potential for stranded assets.

title: Govt may mandate 1% green jet fuel in all commercial flights by '25: Puri
summary: India's Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister, Hardeep Singh Puri, announced plans to mandate 1% sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) blending in all domestic commercial flights by 2025, potentially increasing to 5% in the following years. This initiative aims to boost local SAF production to meet India's de-carbonization goals and prepare for global carbon offsetting schemes in international aviation starting in 2027. State-owned IOCL is planning a large-scale SAF production plant with Praj Industries' technology to support this mandate.

title: Guyana approves Local Content Annual Plans for ExxonMobil, Halliburton, TechnipFMC, Saipem and Baker Hughes - BNamericas
summary: Guyana's Ministry of Natural Resources approved the 2023 Local Content Annual Plans for five major oil companies: ExxonMobil, Halliburton, TechnipFMC, Saipem, and Baker Hughes. These plans outline procurement, employment, and capacity development efforts aimed at ensuring local content investment. The companies also received Certificates of Compliance, marking the first time these certificates have been issued under Guyana's Local Content Act.

title: Chord Energy acquires Williston basin assets for $375 million
summary: Chord Energy Corporation has acquired assets in the Williston basin from XTO Energy Inc. and affiliates, subsidiaries of Exxon Mobil Corporation, for $375 million. The deal includes approximately 62,000 net acres with 123 estimated net 10,000-foot equivalent locations and current high-margin production, funded by existing cash on hand. This acquisition expands Chord's inventory, enhances capital and operating efficiencies, and is expected to be accretive to shareholders.

title: Chord Energy Announces Strategic Acquisition of Williston Basin Assets
summary: Chord Energy Corporation announced the strategic acquisition of Williston Basin assets from XTO Energy Inc., a subsidiary of Exxon Mobil Corporation, for $375 million. This acquisition adds approximately 62,000 net acres, primarily undeveloped, and current high-margin production to Chord's portfolio. The company expects the transaction to be accretive to cash flow, free cash flow, and return metrics, while extending its inventory life.

title: Exxon Mobil subsidiaries selling Williston Basin assets to Chord Energy
summary: Chord Energy Corp. is set to acquire approximately 62,000 net acres in the Williston Basin from Exxon Mobil subsidiaries, including XTO Energy Inc. This acquisition comes after Chord Energy was formed through the merger of Oasis Petroleum Inc. and Whiting Petroleum Corp., aiming to create a leading operator in the Williston Basin.

title: This Ultra-High-Yield Stock's Deal With ExxonMobil Could Drive Its Dividend Higher
summary: Chord Energy has agreed to acquire 62,000 acres in the Williston Basin from ExxonMobil for $375 million, a strategic move expected to boost Chord's cash flow, free cash flow, and potentially increase its dividend payments. ExxonMobil is selling these assets as they no longer align with its focused upstream investment strategy, allowing it to reallocate capital to its core, high-return assets in other regions and strengthening its financial position for future strategic acquisitions. This asset sale is seen as a win-win, benefiting Chord Energy's dividend capacity and ExxonMobil's long-term investment goals.

title: ExxonMobil Sells Williston Assets
summary: Chord Energy Corp. has entered a definitive agreement to acquire hydrocarbon development areas in the Williston Basin from ExxonMobil Corp. for $375 million, adding approximately 62,000 net acres. The acquisition will be funded through cash on hand and is expected to close in June, significantly expanding Chord's inventory runway in the low-cost, tier-one asset region. This deal follows Chord's previous acquisition of Diamondback Energy Inc.’s assets in the Williston Basin and comes as Chord also divests non-core assets.

title: Canadian oil sands output expected to reach 3.7 million barrels per day by 2030, S&P Global says
summary: S&P Global forecasts that Canadian oil sands production will reach 3.7 million barrels per day by 2030, an increase of 140,000 barrels per day from its previous outlook, marking the first such upward revision in five years. This growth is attributed to an "era of optimization" where production focuses on high-potential areas near existing developments. Although record production is anticipated, growth is expected to slow in the mid-2020s and decline in the early 2030s due to the flat production profile of oil sands assets.

title: Norway's Wealth Fund Sides With Activists Against Exxon, Chevron
summary: Norway's $1.4 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest, has announced its support for shareholder proposals at ExxonMobil and Chevron's annual general meetings. These proposals aim to introduce emissions targets, marking a significant stance against Big Oil companies by a major institutional investor. This move follows similar climate activist victories and protests despite a previous shift in investor sentiment favoring energy security.

title: Italian citizens and organisations sue fossil fuel company ENI for human rights violations and climate change impacts
summary: Twelve Italian citizens, Greenpeace Italy, and ReCommon have filed a lawsuit against the fossil fuel company ENI, alleging human rights violations and climate change impacts. The lawsuit also targets ENI’s main shareholders, the Ministry of Economy and Finance and Cassa Depositi e Prestiti S.p.A., accusing them of complicity in policies that violate the Paris Agreement. Plaintiffs, from regions severely affected by climate change, are seeking for ENI to revise its industrial strategy to reduce emissions by at least 45% by 2030.

title: Equinor Delays Bay du Nord Canada Oil Project up to 3 Years Over Rising Costs
summary: Norway's Equinor ASA has announced a delay of up to three years for its Bay du Nord Canadian offshore oil project due to rising costs and volatile market conditions. This decision impacts one of Canada's most significant oil projects, despite prior support from Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's government. The company plans to re-evaluate the project for further optimizations, while environmental groups like Sierra Club Canada hope for its cancellation.

title: ExxonMobil Clinches CCS Deal for Nucor’s Steelmaker Site in Louisiana
summary: ExxonMobil's low-carbon business has secured its third carbon capture and storage (CCS) deal in seven months, contracting with Nucor Corp. to manage up to 800,000 metric tons/year of CO2 from Nucor's Louisiana steelmaking facility. This agreement, along with previous deals, brings ExxonMobil's total CCS commitments to approximately 5 million metric tons/year. The Nucor project is scheduled to begin operations in 2026 and will connect to the CO2 storage infrastructure being developed for the CF Industries project in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana.

title: Chevron produces first gas from Gorgon Stage 2 development off Western Australia
summary: Chevron announced it has commenced gas production from its Gorgon Stage 2 development project off Western Australia. This expansion enhances the existing subsea gas gathering network of the Gorgon Project, which supplies liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Asia and domestic gas to Western Australia. The Stage 2 development involved adding 11 wells and related subsea infrastructure to maintain gas supply for the processing facilities on Barrow Island.

title: 2 Alabama-based companies make the Fortune 500
summary: Two Birmingham-based companies, Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials, have been included in Fortune's 2023 list of the nation's largest corporations. Regions Financial ranked 483rd with $7.5 billion in revenue, while Vulcan Materials placed 494th with over $7.3 billion in revenue. The Fortune 500 list, which ranks companies by their 2022 fiscal year revenue, features 52 companies led by women CEOs, an all-time high.

title: Governments Must Start Walking the Talk on Fossil Fuel Subsidies Phase-out
summary: This article argues that governments must move beyond pledges and actively phase out fossil fuel subsidies to combat climate change, especially as the UN assesses global climate progress. It highlights that current indicators are poor, with fossil fuel subsidies reaching USD 1.1 trillion in 2022, far outweighing clean energy investments. The author suggests concrete steps for governments, including improving transparency, strengthening global commitments, withdrawing all public support from fossil fuels, planning at the national level, and building public support for reforms, all of which are crucial for accelerating the transition to climate-compatible economies.

title: Exposing Texas’ Excess Emissions Problems
summary: Texas industrial facilities have released an estimated 1.1 billion pounds of pollution beyond their permit limits since 2002, largely categorized as "excess emissions" that often go unpunished. This investigation highlights how these emissions, exacerbated by extreme weather and increasing industrial activity, disproportionately affect nearby communities and reveals loopholes in reporting and enforcement. Despite federal rulings deeming these exemptions illegal, state regulators often fail to penalize companies, and firms sometimes downplay emission events to avoid violations.

title: Regions Financial, Vulcan Materials make Fortune 500
summary: Two Birmingham-based companies, Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials, have been named to the Fortune 500 list, ranking 483rd and 494th respectively. Regions generated $7.5 billion in revenue, while Vulcan amassed $7.3 billion during the 2022 fiscal period. Vulcan Materials was also recognized as one of the top 200 Best Companies to Work For by U.S. News and World Report.

title: ACB Earnings Infographic: Aurora Cannabis Q3 2023 revenue up 27%
summary: Aurora Cannabis (NASDAQ: ACB) reported a net loss of C$87 million for Q3 2023, despite a 27% year-over-year increase in total revenues to C$64 million. The company achieved adjusted EBITDA of C$0.31 million, a significant improvement from a C$10.03 million loss in the prior-year quarter. CEO Miguel Martin highlighted approximately $400 million in annualized cost savings from business transformation initiatives, which led to a reduced cash use in operating activities.

title: Recent decision leaves ExxonMobil responsible for only part of Guyana oil spill costs, leaving Guyanese people on the hook for the rest
summary: A recent court decision regarding oil spill cleanup costs in Guyana has limited ExxonMobil's liability to $2 billion, transferring the remaining financial responsibility to the Guyanese people. This decision, which overturns a lower court ruling that demanded full insurance coverage from ExxonMobil, allows drilling to continue but raises significant concerns about the nation's financial exposure to potential oil spills. Critics argue that the Guyanese government and EPA are prioritizing oil revenue over environmental protection and the public interest.

title: As San Miguel Corp posts bumper profits, Filipino communities demand end to its fossil fuel financing
summary: Ahead of San Miguel Corporation's annual stockholder's meeting, fisherfolk and farmer groups are urging the conglomerate to stop its fossil fuel investments, despite the company posting record profits in 2022. They argue that SMC's energy arm, SMC Global Power, is a major coal financier whose operations harm health and the environment, and warn shareholders of the financial risks associated with continued fossil fuel reliance amid global supply volatility and depletion of domestic gas reserves.

title: A corrida entre Brasil, China, EUA e países da Europa para explorar ‘novo pré-sal’
summary: Petroleum companies from seven countries are investing in the exploration of the "Equatorial Margin," a region between the coast of Rio Grande do Norte and Amapá in Brazil, which the Minister of Mines and Energy calls the "new pre-salt." This region is believed to hold significant oil and natural gas reserves, potentially comparable to those found in Guyana, Suriname, and Africa. The exploration faces environmental challenges, as seen with Ibama's denial of a license for Petrobras to drill in the Foz do Amazonas basin, sparking a debate within the Brazilian government.

title: iShares Global Energy ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (IXC)
summary: The iShares Global Energy ETF (IXC) has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy" based on 328 analyst ratings covering 15 companies, which comprise 53.8% of its portfolio. The aggregate price target for IXC holdings is $40.97. The article provides a detailed breakdown of the consensus ratings and potential upside for the top 15 holdings within the ETF, including major energy companies like Exxon Mobil and Chevron.

title: Vaca Muerta: el gas comienza su viaje hasta el AMBA
summary: The first valve of the Néstor Kirchner gas pipeline in Vaca Muerta is set to open, beginning the journey of gas to the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area (AMBA). The gas will travel 570 kilometers from Tratayén, Neuquén, to Salliqueló, Buenos Aires, over approximately 20 days as segments are progressively enabled. This project, owned by state company ENARSA and operated by TGS, aims to achieve energy independence for Argentina by replacing imported gas with domestic production.

title: Gasoducto Néstor Kirchner: "Es un orgullo para TGS operar y mantener el caño"
summary: Transportadora Gas del Sur (TGS) celebrates its role in operating and maintaining the Néstor Kirchner gas pipeline for the next five years. The company won a private bid from Energía Argentina (Enarsa) to manage the gas pipeline's first 573-kilometer section, along with the Tratayén and Saturno plants. This operation is considered a significant achievement for TGS, highlighting its commitment to Argentina's energy development.

title: Exclusive: Exxon, Guyana in talks to return unexplored offshore oil areas
summary: Exxon Mobil and Guyana are in discussions regarding the return of 20% of unexplored offshore areas to the government, as mandated by their 2016 contract. This move aims to attract new operators to the nascent oil nation and accelerate economic development, reducing Exxon's dominance. The relinquished areas, including portions of the Stabroek block and two others, could be re-marketed through auctions or bilateral agreements.

title: Oregon County Sues Fossil Fuel Companies Over 2021 Heat Dome (Published 2023)
summary: Multnomah County in Oregon has filed a lawsuit against several fossil fuel companies, including Exxon Mobil, Shell, and BP, along with their partners, seeking over $1.5 billion in damages. The county alleges these companies are responsible for the deadly 2021 heat dome in the Pacific Northwest, claiming their greenhouse gas emissions played a significant role and that the companies knew their products were harmful. This litigation is part of a growing trend of climate lawsuits globally, with Multnomah County's case being one of the first to seek damages related to a specific weather event like a heat dome.

title: Scaling up carbon capture and community investments in Louisiana
summary: ExxonMobil has announced significant contributions totaling $600,000 to the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, aiming to foster STEM education for local high school students and support energy-related outreach. These investments are linked to ExxonMobil's carbon capture and storage project in Vermilion Parish, which seeks to reduce CO2 emissions from industrial facilities in Louisiana. The initiative highlights the company's commitment to both environmental goals and community development through education.

title: 1,100 barrel a day oil well in Garvin County
summary: Marathon Oil Company completed an oil well in Garvin County, Oklahoma, producing 1,100 barrels of oil and 1,100 Mcf of natural gas per day. Another well, completed by EOG Resources Inc. in McClain County, produced 322 barrels of oil and 293 Mcf of natural gas daily. These reports detail the production capabilities and depths of two recent oil and gas operations in Oklahoma.

title: Shell restarts Norco, Louisiana refinery after power outage, fire
summary: Shell Plc has started restarting its 227,900 barrel-per-day refinery in Norco, Louisiana, after a power outage on Saturday. The outage caused a fire, quickly extinguished, at the DU-5 crude distillation unit. Operations began resuming on Saturday, with no injuries reported.

title: Oil Refiners Pay for Clean Fuel Credits. 2 Stocks That Can Rise.
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency's new mandates require oil refiners to increase their use of low-carbon fuels or purchase credits from renewable fuel companies. This regulation is expected to benefit companies like Opal Fuels (OPAL) and Clean Energy Fuels (CLNE), which produce and distribute renewable natural gas. These companies are poised for growth due to the increased demand for clean fuel credits driven by EPA targets.

title: Exxon Mobil breaks down silos and modernizes systems as it embraces the Data Cloud
summary: Exxon Mobil, a company with over a century of operations, is undergoing a digital transformation to consolidate its extensive and siloed data by adopting Snowflake's Manufacturing Data Cloud. This move aims to modernize its IT footprint, leverage data as an asset, and prepare for advancements in machine learning and artificial intelligence. The collaboration with Snowflake helps Exxon Mobil improve supply chain performance and integrate data from various enterprise and shop floor systems.

title: Apple Is the World’s First $3 Trillion Company
summary: Apple Inc. achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first company to close with a market value above $3 trillion, demonstrating the enduring strength and resilience of the iPhone. This achievement highlights Apple’s significant growth from its origins, now valued at double Google and seven times Exxon Mobil, despite various global challenges.

title: Exxon Mobil and Tetra Team Up for the Next Big Thing in Arkansas: Lithium Mining
summary: Exxon Mobil and Tetra Technologies are partnering to develop over 6,100 acres of lithium-rich land in Arkansas, marking Exxon's second venture into battery metals for electric vehicles. This collaboration, which leverages Tetra's expertise in water treatment and Exxon's capital, aims to extract both lithium for EV batteries and bromine for flame retardants. While Exxon seeks new U.S. lithium sources, the commercial viability of the direct lithium extraction technologies needed for this project remains largely untested.

title: Manipulaciones y amenazas petroleras: se filtra documento de YPF con estrategias para ridiculizar la protesta ambiental
summary: Greenpeace Argentina has filed a legal brief regarding a leaked document, allegedly from YPF, detailing strategies to manipulate public opinion and ridicule environmental protests against offshore oil exploration in the Argentine Sea. The organization condemns the potential use of public funds to stigmatize activists and highlights the document's tactics, which include labeling environmental defenders as "environmental guerrillas" and promoting nationalist rhetoric. Greenpeace emphasizes that these actions undermine public participation, the right to information, and ultimately endanger environmental defenders, urging the state to uphold its constitutional obligation to protect a healthy environment.

title: How to Invest in Oil
summary: This article explores various ways to invest in oil, from high-risk futures contracts to lower-risk exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and direct investments in oil exploration and production companies. It discusses the volatility of oil prices, recent market trends, and considerations for investors looking to enter the oil market. The article also provides examples of specific investment vehicles and companies.

title: Report: 1,500 Big Oil Lobbyists “Double Agents” for Supposed Climate Champions
summary: A new report reveals that over 1,500 state-level lobbyists for fossil fuel companies are also working for progressive, climate, and research groups, as well as state and municipal governments. This practice exposes the pervasive and covert influence of the fossil fuel industry, even within organizations supposedly committed to combating climate change. The findings highlight the significant challenges climate advocates face in their efforts to reduce fossil fuel use.

title: 2 New Wide-Moat Stocks to Watch
summary: Morningstar's equity research team has added two new wide-moat stocks to its coverage list: Kenvue (KVUE) and Copart (CPRT). Kenvue, Johnson & Johnson's former consumer segment, is the world's largest pure-play consumer health company, while Copart is a dominant salvage vehicle auctioneer leveraging a strong network effect. Analysts have assigned Kenvue a fair value of $27.50 per share, deeming it fairly valued, and Copart a fair value of $77 per share, considering it overpriced.

title: Fertilizer companies race to US Gulf to make low-emissions ammonia
summary: Fertilizer companies are accelerating efforts to build blue ammonia production plants along the U.S. Gulf Coast, capitalizing on Inflation Reduction Act subsidies and existing export infrastructure. Key players like OCI, CF Industries, Yara, and Nutrien are investing heavily in facilities designed to capture significant carbon dioxide emissions. These projects aim to produce low-emissions ammonia, primarily for fertilizer use, with anticipated production timelines stretching out to 2028-2029.

title: NextDecade Announces Positive Final Investment Decision on Rio Grande LNG Phase 1
summary: NextDecade Corporation has made a positive final investment decision (FID) for Phase 1 of its Rio Grande LNG (RGLNG) export facility in Texas, securing $18.4 billion in project financing, the largest greenfield energy project financing in U.S. history. The company also issued a notice to proceed to Bechtel for construction of the first three liquefaction trains. This move is supported by significant financial commitments from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala Investment Company, and TotalEnergies, and aims to supply low-carbon LNG to global markets.

title: Autonomous Well Intervention
summary: SLB has developed the industry's first digital platform for autonomous well intervention, leveraging edge computing, digitalization, automation, and Neuro™ autonomous solutions to enhance operational performance in wireline, slickline, and coiled tubing operations. This platform aims to make operations safer, more efficient, and agile by enabling real-time monitoring, automated tasks, and continuous feedback loops. The Intervention and Stimulation Alliance in Norway has successfully implemented these solutions, achieving significant efficiency gains and awards for their innovative approach.

title: Want to buy a gas station? There are 21 about to be for sale
summary: Global Partners LP, a Massachusetts-based fuel distributor, is selling 21 gas station/convenience stores in Connecticut as part of a larger divestment of 54 "non-strategic" assets in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic. These stations, which sell brands like Mobil, Exxon, and Citgo, will be offered in a sealed-bid sale on August 29 through NRC Realty & Capital Advisors. The sale presents an opportunity for smaller operators, as Global Partners LP shifts its focus to fast-growing markets such as Texas.

title: Deal Diary: V&E, Davis Polk on Denbury Sale to Exxon
summary: Denbury Inc. is selling to Exxon Mobil Corp. for $4.9 billion in stock, with Vinson & Elkins LLP advising Denbury and Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP advising Exxon. Denbury chose JPMorgan Securities LLC and TPH&Co. for financial advice. This acquisition marks Exxon's largest public company purchase since 2010 and is driven by Denbury's carbon capture and sequestration capabilities.

title: Eye on Lithium: Could this tiny town be the epicentre of a US lithium boom?
summary: Exxon Mobil is reportedly planning to build one of the world's largest lithium processing facilities in Magnolia, Arkansas, with a capacity to produce 75K-100K metric tons/year of lithium. This development is attributed to the Smackover formation, a geological trend rich in saltwater brine containing lithium, prompting interest from other companies like Standard Lithium and Tetra Technologies. The article also provides an overview of daily movements in Australian lithium stocks and news from other mining companies such as Perpetual Resources, Octava Minerals, Gold Mountain, and Coolabah Metals.

title: EQT Advancing Gulf Coast LNG Strategy and Eyeing (Eventual) MVP Opportunities
summary: EQT Corp., the largest natural gas producer in the U.S., has secured an agreement to supply the proposed Lake Charles LNG project in Louisiana with 1 million metric tons/year, aligning with its strategy to deliver Appalachia production to overseas markets. The company is actively pursuing further sales and purchase agreements with international buyers and is optimistic about the long-delayed Mountain Valley Pipeline's completion, which is expected to improve price realizations and free cash flow. Despite declining sales volumes and a net loss in the second quarter, EQT is maintaining its 2023 production forecast and capital expenditures, while also focusing on greenhouse gas emission reductions.

title: Oil producer Hess beats profit estimates on U.S. production boost
summary: Hess Corp reported an 82% year-on-year decline in second-quarter profit due to lower energy prices but still surpassed Wall Street estimates, driven by increased production in the U.S. The company also announced a new oil discovery in the Gulf of Mexico and anticipates higher production from Guyana in the fourth quarter. Hess raised its annual production forecast for the second time this year, expecting 385,000 to 390,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.

title: Estatización de YPF: Argentina define en EEUU el costo a pagar a un "fondo buitre"
summary: A U.S. judge is presiding over a three-day hearing to determine the compensation Argentina must pay Burford Capital for its 2012 expropriation of 51% of YPF shares. The final amount, ranging from US$4.999 billion to US$16.1 billion, will be decided by late August or early September. The judge had previously cleared YPF of direct liability, ruling that Argentina's national government is responsible for the payment.

title: Procter & Gamble Earnings: Margins Rebuild Even as Investments Persist
summary: Procter & Gamble's fourth-quarter earnings showed significant gross margin expansion to 48.4%, driven by higher prices and productivity savings. The company continues to invest in R&D and marketing, supporting its wide economic moat. While Morningstar expects to slightly raise its fair value estimate of P&G stock, shares are currently considered unattractive, trading at a premium to their intrinsic valuation.

title: Exxon profits slump 56%, joins global peers in energy price hit
summary: Exxon Mobil's second-quarter profit plummeted 56% to $7.88 billion, missing Wall Street expectations due to a sharp decline in energy prices and lower fuel margins. Despite the significant drop from a record 2022, the company reported its strongest second quarter in over a decade when excluding last year's exceptional performance, attributed to cost cuts and asset sales. Exxon anticipates record oil demand for this year and next, potentially leading to upward pressure on energy prices in the second half of 2023.

title: Imperial Oil shares rise as company renews share buybacks
summary: Imperial Oil's shares rose as the company announced renewed share buybacks despite a 72% drop in quarterly earnings due to maintenance and lower energy prices. The company's earnings met analyst expectations, and management expressed optimism for stronger volumes in the second half of the year, leading to investor confidence in future buybacks.

title: U.S. crude helps fix world’s key oil price
summary: The inclusion of U.S. WTI Midland crude in the Dated Brent benchmark has significantly improved its liquidity and stability. This reform addresses previous issues of supply scarcity and price manipulation, making the benchmark less susceptible to sudden shifts. The increased supply has also made it harder for individual traders to corner the market and has influenced pricing dynamics for other North Sea crudes.

title: Permian Basin group adds 21st member
summary: The Permian Strategic Partnership has expanded its membership to 21, welcoming ChampionX, a global leader in chemistry solutions and other engineered equipment. This organization focuses on responsible resource development in the Permian Basin, and includes several Oklahoma-linked companies like Devon Energy and Helmerich & Payne.

title: Italy's antitrust drops fuel prices probe on Eni, Exxon and others
summary: Italy's antitrust authority has closed a probe into several energy groups, including Eni and Exxon Mobil's ESSO Italiana unit, regarding alleged fuel price violations, without imposing sanctions. The companies have agreed to take actions to address competition concerns. However, a separate investigation into an alleged cartel over the sale of transport fuel, involving many of the same companies, was opened earlier this month.

title: Alberta crude oil production falls to seven-year low amidst oil-sands mines maintenance
summary: Alberta's crude oil production dropped to a seven-year low in June, primarily due to maintenance at oil-sands mines and the partial exclusion of Suncor Energy Inc.'s output from regulatory data. Total oil output fell 21% to 2.71 MMbpd, with oil-sands mines experiencing a 48% decline. This dip was exacerbated by a cyber incident at Suncor, which affected the reporting of its production figures.

title: Press release: Members of Canada’s Public Service Pension Plan ask Cabinet to remove Imperial Oil director from their pension’s board of directors
summary: Working and retired federal public servants have sent a letter to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and his Cabinet, requesting the removal of Imperial Oil Director Miranda Hubbs from the Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSPIB) due to her role in Imperial Oil's environmental transgressions, including significant oil sands tailings leaks. They argue that her position at Imperial Oil, which is under investigation for "environmental racism," compromises her ability to ethically oversee climate-related financial risks for the PSPIB. This request comes as other major Canadian pension funds also voted against Hubbs' re-election to Imperial Oil's board, citing a lack of oversight regarding Indigenous communities and climate risk.

title: Corporate governance
summary: ExxonMobil's corporate governance framework focuses on upholding high ethical standards, promoting transparency, and ensuring long-term growth. This is achieved through a robust board of directors providing strategic oversight, detailed policies, and a commitment to managing risks and opportunities associated with its business. The company also outlines its approach to sustainability and advancing climate solutions as key strategic priorities.

title: Diamondback Sees Permian Cost Relief as Natural Gas, Oil Activity Slows
summary: Diamondback Energy Inc. anticipates a reduction in oilfield services (OFS) costs due to a slowdown in Lower 48 activity and a reluctance among E&P firms to increase spending. Despite cost relief expectativas, the company's full-year 2023 capital expenditures are projected to increase slightly, eyeing 335-350 gross wells and significant production targets. Diamondback also detailed its second-quarter earnings, reporting a decrease in net income and revenue compared to the previous year, while highlighting its M&A discipline and hedging strategy.

title: MGV: #1 Holding Berkshire Powers Vanguard's Mega-Cap Value ETF (NYSEARCA:MGV)
summary: The Vanguard Mega Cap Value ETF (MGV) has outperformed the broad market, significantly driven by its largest holding, Berkshire Hathaway, which recently reported strong Q2 earnings. MGV focuses on undervalued stocks, offers a low expense ratio of 0.07% and an attractive yield of 2.45%, making it a strong option for diversified portfolios. Other significant holdings include Exxon, Johnson & Johnson, Broadcom, Procter & Gamble, and Chevron.

title: LyondellBasell Earnings: Weak End-Market Demand Will Constrain Performance Through Year-End
summary: LyondellBasell's second-quarter performance mirrored peers with a 31% year-over-year sales drop and flat EBITDA margins, attributed to weak demand across end markets. This soft demand is expected to continue through year-end, driven by economic uncertainty and slow recovery in China. Despite near-term challenges, Morningstar maintains a narrow moat rating and a $124 fair value estimate, anticipating a recovery in demand for polyolefin products in 2024.

title: Oil Services Stocks Could Energize This Energy ETF
summary: Energy stocks have shown modest gains this year, but the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Energy ETF (RSPG) is outperforming its cap-weighted rivals. The ETF, with over half its holdings in value stocks, could be further boosted by the performance of oil services providers, which constitute 14.10% of its portfolio. Analysts are highlighting buy-rated oil service stocks like Baker Hughes and Schlumberger due to increased spending from oil-rich nations and improved financial transparency.

title: How to Share Infrastructure on the North Slope
summary: This article discusses the challenges and benefits of sharing infrastructure on Alaska's North Slope, focusing on the historical success of the Trans Alaska Pipeline System (TAPS) as a common carrier. It also details an ongoing dispute between Santos and ConocoPhillips Alaska regarding the use of the Kuparuk River Unit road system, highlighting differing views on private property rights versus access for development. The resolution of this dispute is expected to provide greater clarity for future North Slope operations.

title: Exxon Awarded $77 Million in Claim Against Venezuela
summary: The World Bank's arbitration court has awarded $77 million to Exxon Mobil Corp. in a claim against Venezuela stemming from the 2007 nationalization of crude projects. This award follows a protracted legal battle where the International Center for Settlement of International Disputes (ICSID) determined that much of the original compensation sought by Exxon had already been paid through a separate claim. Exxon stated that while they would not comment on specifics, "on balance, ICSID ruled in our favor."

title: Global Helium Market to Reach $3.4 Billion by 2030, Fueled by Rising Demand in Cryogenics and Welding Applications
summary: The global helium market, valued at US$2.3 Billion in 2022, is projected to grow to US$3.4 Billion by 2030, exhibiting a CAGR of 5%. This growth is driven by increasing demand in various applications, particularly cryogenics and welding. The report highlights significant market expansion in regions such as China, Japan, and Canada, with key players including Air Liquide, Linde Plc, and Exxon Mobil Corporation.

title: SFL - New $100 Million Contract for Semi-Submersible Rig Hercules
summary: SFL Corporation Ltd. announced a new $100 million contract for its harsh environment semi-submersible rig Hercules with a subsidiary of Equinor ASA in Canada. The contract, commencing in Q2 2024, is for approximately 200 days and includes an optional well. This agreement secures continuous employment for the rig until Q4 2024, adding to SFL's revenue backlog and highlighting the strengthening market for advanced harsh environment semi-submersibles.

title: SFL secures $100m contract
summary: Bermudian-based SFL Corporation Ltd has inked a $100 million drilling contract with Equinor ASA for its harsh environment semi-submersible rig, Hercules. This contract, for one well with an option for another, is set to begin in the second quarter of 2024 and spans approximately 200 days including transit. This new agreement brings SFL's revenue backlog for the Hercules rig to about $200 million, securing its employment until the fourth quarter of 2024.

title: Cisco (CSCO) reports Q4 results: Here’s all you need to know
summary: Cisco Systems Inc. reported strong fourth-quarter 2023 results, with revenues up 16% year-over-year to $15.2 billion and earnings per share increasing to $1.14. The company's Secure, Agile Networks division significantly contributed to its top-line growth, and Cisco provided positive guidance for the first quarter of 2024. CEO Chuck Robbins highlighted solid customer demand, market share gains, and innovation in AI, security, and cloud as key drivers of confidence for future opportunities.

title: Two Dallas energy giants strike deals to strengthen oil patch plays
summary: Dallas energy giants Energy Transfer and HF Sinclair have made significant moves to consolidate their positions in the oil patch. Energy Transfer is acquiring Houston-based Crestwood Equity Partners for $7.1 billion, expanding its asset base in key oil and gas basins. Separately, HF Sinclair is buying the remaining stake in its limited partnership, Holly Energy Partners, to streamline its corporate structure and integrate petroleum production and distribution.

title: Remezón en la alta gerencia de Ecopetrol para enfrentar retos de la transición energética
summary: Ecopetrol has announced significant changes in its senior management to address the challenges of energy transition. Four vice presidents are leaving their positions, and new appointments have been made in areas such as Finance, Low-Emission Solutions, Compliance, and Science, Technology, and Innovation. These changes aim to integrate a new team to support the company's president, Ricardo Roa, in navigating the evolving energy landscape.

title: Atención: Ecopetrol anunció la salida de cuatro vicepresidentes. ¿Crisis dentro de la empresa?
summary: Ecopetrol, the Colombian state-owned oil company, announced the departure of four vice presidents following a board meeting on August 16, 2023. This unexpected change has sparked speculation about the company's direction and stability amid a challenging energy industry landscape. While new leaders have been appointed to fill the vacant roles, analysts are concerned about a significant drop in investment and the potential impact on Ecopetrol’s financial performance and market perception.

title: Suncor is turning its back on a clean energy future, let’s turn our backs on them
summary: Suncor's new CEO, Rich Kruger, has signaled a return to prioritizing oil sands profits over clean energy transition, following similar moves by Shell and BP. The article argues that this decision, influenced by fluctuating oil prices, means Big Oil is abandoning its commitment to clean energy. It calls for shifting support to other sectors and entrepreneurs driving the low-carbon economy and excluding traditional oil companies from climate decision-making tables.

title: Guyana's Oil Boom Grabs Bigger Share of European Market
summary: Guyana has significantly increased its share of the European oil market this year, with exports rising to 215,000 barrels per day, or 63% of its total output. This surge is attributed to increased production by an ExxonMobil-led consortium and strong European demand for light sweet crude following sanctions on Russian oil. The country's growing oil sector is set to make it one of Latin America's top producers by 2027.

title: Pantera enters the Smackover- Next to $435BN “lithium hopeful” … uhhh Exxon Mobil?
summary: Pantera Minerals (ASX:PFE) has acquired a 35% interest in Daytona Lithium, a private company that holds leased acreage in the lithium-rich Smackover Formation in Arkansas, strategically located next to Exxon Mobil's recent acquisitions. This move places PFE among major players like Exxon, Albemarle, and Standard Lithium in a rapidly developing lithium land rush. The article highlights the potential of the Smackover Formation for lithium extraction from brines using Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technology, despite associated risks, and positions PFE for potential re-valuation as it progresses its project.

title: Transco Partnering with Duke to Monitor Natural Gas Methane Emissions in North Carolina
summary: Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Co. (Transco) is collaborating with Duke Energy Corp. on a methane monitoring project in North Carolina, backed by $1 million from the U.S. Department of Energy. This initiative aims to expand Duke's existing monitoring system to include interstate natural gas assets like Transco's, using advanced technologies such as satellites, drones, and aerial light detection to measure and reduce methane emissions throughout the supply chain. The project also involves testing and refining these technologies and is part of a broader push to manage methane emissions, with other companies and institutions also receiving funding for similar efforts.

title: XOMO - YieldMax XOM Option Income Strategy ETF Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides a detailed quote and financial data for the XOMO - YieldMax XOM Option Income Strategy ETF. It includes current stock price, performance metrics, dividend information, fund characteristics, and recent news announcements related to YieldMax ETFs. The fund aims for current income and indirect exposure to Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM) through a synthetic covered call strategy.

title: Equinor Builds in U.S. by Joining Chevron, Talos in Texas Carbon Capture Project
summary: Equinor ASA has acquired a 25% stake in the Bayou Bend CCS LLC project, a carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) initiative on the Texas coast. This partnership with Chevron Corp. and Talos Energy Inc. strengthens Equinor's low carbon solutions portfolio, aiming to develop 15-30 million metric tons of CO2 transport and storage capacity annually by 2035. Bayou Bend is poised to become one of the largest CCUS projects in the U.S., offering a decarbonization option for major industrial emitters in the region.

title: Vivek Ramaswamy's 'anti-woke' investment firm now manages assets worth more than $1 billion
summary: Vivek Ramaswamy's "anti-woke" investment firm, Strive Asset Management, which was founded in 2022 to counter ESG-focused investing, has grown to manage over $1 billion in assets. The firm's success comes despite challenges, including a lawsuit from former employees, and its focus is on encouraging companies to prioritize excellence over ESG concerns. Ramaswamy has also criticized major investment firms like BlackRock for pushing ESG agendas.

title: US researchers developing autonomous robot for subsea oil & gas pipeline inspection
summary: The University of Houston is developing an autonomous robot called SmartTouch for subsea oil and gas pipeline inspection. This robot, equipped with stress wave-based sensors, video cameras, and scanning sonars, aims to identify potential leaks and structural failures, particularly in flange bolts. The project, funded by a $960,493 grant from the U.S. Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement, involves collaboration with Oceaneering International and Chevron to reduce inspection costs and risks, enhance safety, and mitigate environmental damage from corrosion.

title: Suncor refineries reach new EPA settlement over gasoline, agrees to buy electric lawn equipment
summary: Suncor's Commerce City refinery has reached a new settlement with the EPA concerning violations related to gasoline that failed to meet air pollution standards. As part of the agreement, the Canadian oil company will purchase electric lawn equipment for communities surrounding the refinery. This settlement follows previous federal penalties and ongoing concerns about Suncor's operations and air quality impact in the Denver area.

title: Nigerian State Oil Company Raises Reservations With Eni Sale
summary: Nigeria's state oil company, NNPC, has expressed reservations about Eni SpA's sale of a subsidiary with a 20% stake in four onshore oil and gas blocks to local producer Oando Plc. The NNPC claims Eni failed to obtain prior authorization for the sale, constituting a "grave breach" of their joint venture agreement, though it clarifies it's not an objection to the transaction but rather a demand to adhere to clauses protecting the deal. Eni, however, denies any breach, stating that while NNPC has pre-emption rights, it had no obligation to inform them before the announcement, and that all necessary procedures and consents will be followed.

title: YieldMax Writes Call Options on JPMorgan Chase With JPMO ETF
summary: YieldMax has launched the YieldMax JPM Option Income Strategy ETF (JPMO), an actively managed fund that aims to generate monthly income by writing call options on JPMorgan Chase & Co. Corp. (JPM). The fund seeks to harvest compelling yields with capped participation in JPM's price gains and is managed by ZEGA Financial with an expense ratio of 0.99%. This new ETF expands YieldMax's growing suite of option income strategy ETFs.

title: What exactly is green hydrogen and what can it be used for?
summary: Green hydrogen, produced by splitting hydrogen from other elements using renewable energy, is being promoted as a clean energy solution for high-emitting sectors. While it holds potential for industries like steelmaking, manufacturing, and transport, critics express concerns regarding its viability at scale, efficiency compared to direct electrification, high production costs, and transport limitations. Despite these challenges, Louisiana is emerging as a hub for green hydrogen production with several major projects underway.

title: Russia imports Halliburton equipment worth $7.1 mln despite announcement to end operations in country, customs records show; incl. co. comments
summary: Customs records indicate that Halliburton equipment worth over $7.1 million has been imported into Russia since the company announced the end of its Russian operations in September 2022. While initial shipments came from Halliburton subsidiaries, later imports were made by unrelated companies from Turkey, with the majority supplied to Halliburton's former Russian operation, BurService. Halliburton asserts it fully complied with sanctions and no longer operates in Russia.
